Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disc and $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$ the unit circle. For a non-constant analytic function $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$, a point $\zeta\in\mathbb{T}$ is said to be a point at which $f$ has an asymptotic value if there exist a value $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$ and a continuous path $\gamma:[0,1)\to\mathbb{D}$ with $\gamma(t)\to\zeta$ as $t\to1^-$ such that $f(\gamma(t))\to\alpha$ as $t\to1^-$. Define the MacLane class $\mathcal{A}$ to be the set of non-constant analytic functions $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ such that the set of points of $\mathbb{T}$ at which $f$ has an asymptotic value is dense in $\mathbb{T}$.

Say that $f$ has an arc tract if there exist a sequence of arcs $\{\gamma_n\}$ with $\gamma_n\subset\mathbb{D}$ and a non-degenerate subarc $\gamma\subset\mathbb{T}$ such that $\gamma_n\to\gamma$ (in the Hausdorff sense) and $\min\{|f(z)|:z\in\gamma_n\}\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$.

Question: Does there exist a function $f\in\mathcal{A}$ that has an arc tract and whose derivative $f'$ does not vanish anywhere in $\mathbb{D}$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem, originally posed by MacLane in 1970, asks whether a locally univalent function in the MacLane class $\mathcal{A}$ can have an arc tract. A 2017 paper by Barth, Rippon, and Sixsmith ("The MacLane class and the Eremenko–Lyubich class") explicitly states that the question remains open and provides partial results, including a strengthening that replaces the non-vanishing-derivative (local univalence) hypothesis with the more general assumption of bounded critical values. No subsequent resolution has been found.

Let $n\geq 3$ and let $B^n=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:|x|<1\}$ denote the open unit ball. A continuous map $f:B^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is called proper if $f^{-1}(K)$ is a compact subset of $B^n$ for every compact set $K$ contained in $f(B^n)$. Assume in addition that $f$ is quasiregular (i.e., $f$ belongs to the Sobolev space $W^{1,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$, is non-constant, and there exists a constant $K\geq 1$ such that $|Df(x)|^n\leq K\, J_f(x)$ for almost every $x\in B^n$, where $J_f$ is the Jacobian determinant). Let
$$B_f=\{z\in B^n:f\text{ is not a local homeomorphism at }z\}$$
denote the branch set of $f$. Suppose that $B_f$ is compact. Must $f$ be injective on $B^n$?

(Note: the planar winding map $f(z)=z^2$ on $B^2$ shows the analogous statement fails when $n=2$; and the case $f(B^n)=B^n$ for $n\geq 3$ is known.)

Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disc. A Blaschke product is a function of the form
$$B(z) = z^m \prod_{n} \frac{|a_n|}{a_n}\,\frac{a_n - z}{1 - \overline{a_n} z},$$
where $m \in \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and $\{a_n\} \subset \mathbb{D}\setminus\{0\}$ is a (possibly empty, finite, or infinite) sequence satisfying the Blaschke condition $\sum_n (1-|a_n|) < \infty$. A holomorphic function $f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ is said to be a Bloch function if
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{B}} := \sup_{z \in \mathbb{D}} (1 - |z|^2) |f'(z)| < \infty.$$

It is known that there exists a Blaschke product $B$ with $B(0) = 0$ such that the function
$$F(z) = \frac{1 + B(z)}{1 - B(z)}$$
is a Bloch function on $\mathbb{D}$.

Problem: Give an explicit construction of such a Blaschke product $B$ (i.e., specify its zero sequence, or equivalently a closed-form expression) for which $B(0) = 0$ and $\dfrac{1 + B(z)}{1 - B(z)}$ belongs to the Bloch space.

is a Bloch function on $\mathbb{D}$.

Let $A_n$ denote the universal real Clifford algebra generated by an orthonormal basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ subject to the relations $e_i e_j + e_j e_i = -2\delta_{ij}$. By a classical construction of Ahlfors, every Möbius transformation of $\mathbb{R}^n \cup \{\infty\}$ can be written in the form $x \mapsto (ax+b)(cx+d)^{-1}$, where $a,b,c,d \in A_n$ satisfy the Ahlfors–Vahlen conditions (each of $a,b,c,d$ is a product of nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $ad^* - bc^* = \pm 1$, and the elements $ac^*$, $bd^*$, $c^*a$, $d^*b$ lie in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where $*$ denotes the principal Clifford involution). Let $D = \sum_{j=1}^n e_j \partial_{x_j}$ be the Euclidean Dirac operator on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

It is known that the linear differential equations on Clifford-algebra-valued functions whose solution spaces are conformally invariant are precisely those of the form $D^k f = 0$ for $k \in \mathbb{N}$, where conformal invariance is realized by an intertwining transformation
$$f(x) \;\longmapsto\; J_k(cx+d)\, f\bigl((ax+b)(cx+d)^{-1}\bigr),$$
with conformal weight
$$J_k(cx+d) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{(cx+d)^*}{|cx+d|^{\,n+1-k}} & \text{if } k = 2p-1,\\[1ex] \dfrac{1}{|cx+d|^{\,n-k}} & \text{if } k = 2p. \end{cases}$$

Address the following:

(1) Determine all non-linear differential equations on Clifford-algebra-valued functions $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to A_n$ whose solution spaces are invariant under the action of the Möbius group of $\mathbb{R}^n \cup \{\infty\}$ (acting via some intertwining factor as above).

(2) Decide whether the conformal weights of such non-linear equations can also be expressed as explicit functions of $cx+d$, analogous to the formula for $J_k$ above, and describe the precise relationship between their solutions and the solutions of the linear conformally invariant equations $D^k f = 0$.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disc. Recall that for a sequence $\{a_n\}\subset\mathbb{D}$ satisfying the Blaschke condition $\sum_n(1-|a_n|)<\infty$, the associated Blaschke product is
$$B(z,\{a_n\})=\prod_n \frac{|a_n|}{a_n}\cdot\frac{a_n-z}{1-\overline{a_n}z}.$$
A meromorphic function $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ is called normal if the family $\{f\circ\varphi:\varphi\in\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})\}$ is normal in the sense of Montel as a family of meromorphic functions; equivalently, the spherical derivative
$$f^{\#}(z)=\frac{|f'(z)|}{1+|f(z)|^2}$$
satisfies $\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}(1-|z|^2)f^{\#}(z)<\infty$. A sequence $\{a_n\}\subset\mathbb{D}$ is called an interpolating (Carleson) sequence if for every bounded sequence $\{w_n\}\subset\mathbb{C}$ there exists $f\in H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ with $f(a_n)=w_n$ for all $n$.

Given two Blaschke sequences $\{a_n\},\{b_n\}\subset\mathbb{D}$, form the quotient
$$R(z)=\frac{B(z,\{a_n\})}{B(z,\{b_n\})},$$
which is meromorphic of bounded characteristic in $\mathbb{D}$. It is known that when both $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$ are interpolating sequences, $R$ is a normal meromorphic function on $\mathbb{D}$ if and only if the union $\{a_n\}\cup\{b_n\}$ is also an interpolating sequence.

Problem. Find necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the geometry of the sequences $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$ in $\mathbb{D}$, for the quotient $R$ to be a normal meromorphic function on $\mathbb{D}$, without the assumption that $\{a_n\}$ or $\{b_n\}$ is an interpolating sequence.

For $R>0$, let $\mathbb{D}_R = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < R\}$. A domain $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ is called hyperbolic if $\mathbb{C} \setminus D$ contains at least two points; in this case $D$ carries a unique complete conformal metric $\lambda_D(z)\,|dz|$ of constant Gaussian curvature $-1$, called its hyperbolic metric (equivalently, $\lambda_D$ is determined by pulling back the Poincaré metric $|dw|/(1-|w|^2)$ through any holomorphic universal covering $\mathbb{D}\to D$, up to the standard normalization).

Let $D_1, D_2$ be hyperbolic domains contained in $\mathbb{D}_R$ such that $D_1 \cap D_2$ is nonempty and hyperbolic, and let $\lambda_1(z)\,|dz|$, $\lambda_2(z)\,|dz|$, and $\lambda(z)\,|dz|$ denote the hyperbolic metrics of $D_1$, $D_2$, and $D_1 \cap D_2$, respectively.

Determine the smallest constant $A = A(R)$, depending only on $R$, such that
$$\lambda(z) \le A\bigl(\lambda_1(z) + \lambda_2(z)\bigr)$$
holds for every $z \in D_1 \cap D_2$ and for every admissible choice of $D_1, D_2 \subset \mathbb{D}_R$.

A 2026 preprint addresses Fuchs's additive intersection problem for the hyperbolic metric. It shows that the supremum of $\lambda_{D_1\cap D_2}(z)/(\lambda_{D_1}(z)+\lambda_{D_2}(z))$ over all hyperbolic domains is $+\infty$, while if $D_1, D_2$ are restricted to be simply connected the sharp upper bound is $1$ (via Murai's subadditivity). The infimum of the ratio is $1/2$, attained iff $D_1=D_2$. Thus the question of the least constant $A(R)$ valid for arbitrary hyperbolic domains in $\mathbb{D}_R$ is essentially resolved (no finite universal $A$ exists), with sharp constants known under the simply-connected restriction.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc, and let $H^\infty=H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{D}$. Suppose $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ is univalent (i.e. holomorphic and injective) and zero-free on $\mathbb{D}$. It is known that for each $p\in(0,\tfrac{1}{2})$ there exist holomorphic functions $B_p,F_p$ on $\mathbb{D}$ such that
$$f = B_p\,(F_p)^{1/p},$$
where $B_p\in H^\infty$, $1/B_p\in H^\infty$, and $\operatorname{Re} F_p>0$ on $\mathbb{D}$.

Recall that a holomorphic function $g:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to be subordinate to a holomorphic function $h:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ (with $h$ univalent) if $g(\mathbb{D})\subset h(\mathbb{D})$ and $g(0)=h(0)$; equivalently, there is a holomorphic self-map $\omega:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{D}$ with $\omega(0)=0$ and $g=h\circ\omega$. By a "slit plane" we mean a domain of the form $\mathbb{C}\setminus L$ where $L$ is a closed half-line.

Question: Is it always possible to take the limit $p\to\tfrac{1}{2}$ in the above factorisation? More precisely, can every univalent zero-free $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ be factored as
$$f = B\cdot G,$$
where $B\in H^\infty$ with $1/B\in H^\infty$ and $G$ is subordinate to a conformal map of $\mathbb{D}$ onto a slit plane?

Let γ denote the analytic capacity on the complex plane: for a compact set E ⊆ ℂ,
   γ(E) = sup{ |f'(∞)| : f : ℂ∖E → ℂ bounded analytic, ‖f‖_∞ ≤ 1 },
where f'(∞) = lim_{z→∞} z(f(z) − f(∞)). For a non-compact set A ⊆ ℂ, define the inner analytic capacity by γ(A) = sup{ γ(L) : L ⊆ A, L compact }.

Prove or disprove each of the following statements.

(a) If E ⊆ ℂ is compact and φ : ℂ → ℂ is a C¹-diffeomorphism, then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0. (It is known that the analogue fails when φ is merely a homeomorphism, or merely a quasiconformal mapping.)

(b) If E ⊆ ℂ is compact and φ ∈ GL(2, ℝ) acts as a real-linear automorphism of ℂ ≅ ℝ², then γ(E) = 0 if and only if γ(φ(E)) = 0.

(c) There exists an absolute constant K > 0 such that for all compact E, F ⊆ ℂ,
   γ(E ∪ F) ≤ K(γ(E) + γ(F)).
In particular, can one take K = 1?

(d) If K ⊆ ℂ is compact with γ(K) = 0, then γ(E ∖ K) = γ(E) for every compact E ⊆ ℂ, where γ(E ∖ K) is interpreted as the inner capacity defined above. A particularly interesting special case is when K is the "corner quarters" planar Cantor set (the Garnett set).

Part (c), the semiadditivity of analytic capacity, was proved by X. Tolsa (Acta Math. 190 (2003), 105–149) with some absolute constant K, settling Vitushkin's semiadditivity question; whether K = 1 is admissible remains open. Tolsa also established bilipschitz invariance of analytic capacity, which yields part (b) (linear maps are bilipschitz). Part (a) for general C¹-diffeomorphisms appears still open in the literature, and part (d) (the "subtraction of null sets") remains an open problem in general, including the Garnett set special case.

Let $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a finite interval and let $m$ denote Lebesgue measure. Two measurable functions $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are called rearrangements of one another if
$$m\{x \in I : g(x) < y\} = m\{x \in I : f(x) < y\} \quad \text{for every } y \in \mathbb{R}.$$

(a) Characterize all (sufficiently smooth) functions $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ with the property that $f'$ is a rearrangement of $f$ on $I$. Examples include $f(x) = k e^{x}$ on any finite interval and $f(x) = k \sin x$ on $[0, \tfrac{1}{2}\pi]$; determine whether there are essentially different examples and give a complete description.

(b) More generally, study "differential rearrangement" relations: for which functions $f$ and which differential operators $D$ (other than $D = d/dx$) is $Df$ a rearrangement of $f$?

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $\mathrm{BMOA}$ denote the space of analytic functions on $\mathbb{D}$ whose boundary values lie in $\mathrm{BMO}$ on the unit circle $\partial\mathbb{D}$. For $f\in\mathrm{BMOA}$, define
$$\|f\|_h \;=\; \inf_{g}\;\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}\,\bigl|f(z)+\overline{g(z)}\bigr|,$$
where the infimum is taken over all functions $g$ analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ (so that $\overline{g}$ ranges over conjugate-analytic functions). It is known that $\|\cdot\|_h$ is an equivalent norm on $\mathrm{BMOA}$.

Question: For every $f\in\mathrm{BMOA}$, does there exist an analytic function $g$ in $\mathbb{D}$ such that
$$\bigl|f(z)+\overline{g(z)}\bigr| \;=\; \|f\|_h \qquad \text{for almost every } z \text{ with } |z|=1\,?$$

(It is known that the answer is affirmative whenever $f$ is a rational function. The problem asks whether the same holds for arbitrary $f\in\mathrm{BMOA}$.)

Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a domain and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic. A point $z_0 \in G$ is called a MacLane point of $f$ if there exists an open neighborhood $N \subseteq G$ of $z_0$ such that the family of restrictions of successive derivatives
$$\{ f^{(n)}|_N : n \in \mathbb{N} \}$$
is a normal family on $N$ (in the sense of Montel: every sequence has a subsequence converging locally uniformly on $N$, possibly to $\infty$). Let $M(f) \subseteq G$ denote the set of MacLane points of $f$. It is straightforward that $M(f)$ is open in $G$.

Determine what further can be said about the set $M(f)$. In particular:

(a) Must $M(f)$ always be connected?

(b) If $G$ is simply connected, must $M(f)$ be simply connected?

(c) Conversely, can every open subset $U \subseteq G$ be realized as $U = M(f)$ for some analytic $f$ on $G$?

Investigate the analogous questions for functions meromorphic on $G$, and also for the variant in which the normalized derivatives $\{ f^{(n)}(z)/n! : n \in \mathbb{N} \}$ are used in place of $\{ f^{(n)}(z) \}$.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. Let $(n_k)_{k\ge 0}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative integers satisfying the Hadamard gap condition
$$\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k}\ge \lambda > 1 \qquad (k\ge 0),$$
and let $(a_k)_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence of complex numbers such that the lacunary power series
$$f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k z^{n_k}$$
defines a holomorphic function on $\mathbb{D}$. Define the maximum term
$$m_0(r,f) := \max_{k\ge 0} |a_k| r^{n_k},$$
and assume that $m_0(r,f)\to\infty$ as $r\to 1^-$. Define
$$E := \Big\{ \theta\in[0,2\pi) : \liminf_{r\to 1^-}\frac{|f(re^{i\theta})|}{m_0(r,f)} > 0\Big\}.$$
Prove or disprove: the set $E$ has Lebesgue measure zero.

Let $H^\infty$ denote the Banach space of bounded analytic functions on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$, equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|$, and let $(H^\infty)^*$ denote its continuous dual. A function $\varphi\in H^\infty$ is called inner if $|\varphi(e^{i\theta})|=1$ for almost every $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ (using non-tangential boundary values). Let $I\subset H^\infty$ denote the class of all inner functions.

Suppose $\{\Lambda_n\}\subset (H^\infty)^*$ is a sequence of bounded linear functionals on $H^\infty$ such that, for every inner function $\varphi\in I$, the sequence of complex numbers $\{\Lambda_n(\varphi)\}_{n\ge 1}$ is bounded; that is, there exists a constant $C(\varphi)<\infty$ (possibly depending on $\varphi$) with
$$|\Lambda_n(\varphi)|\le C(\varphi)\qquad\text{for all } n\ge 1.$$

Prove or disprove: $\sup_{n\ge 1}\|\Lambda_n\|_{(H^\infty)^*}<\infty$.

In other words, decide whether the class $I$ of inner functions is a uniform-boundedness (Banach–Steinhaus) set for the dual of $H^\infty$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

The question appears to have been resolved affirmatively. H. S. Shapiro proved a uniform boundedness principle concerning inner functions (Journal d'Analyse Mathématique), establishing that the class of inner functions is a uniform-boundedness (UBD) set in $H^\infty$ with the weak-* topology. S. Hui's "An extension of a theorem of J. Fernández" (Bull. London Math. Soc. 20 (1988), 34–36) further extended these results. Search snippets explicitly state that "inner functions are a UBD-set in $H^\infty$".

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. Suppose
$$f(z)=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n z^n$$
is holomorphic in $\mathbb{D}$, has positive real part in $\mathbb{D}$ (i.e. $\operatorname{Re} f(z)>0$ for all $z\in\mathbb{D}$), satisfies $a_n\ge 0$ for every $n\ge 1$, and is a Bloch function, meaning
$$\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}(1-|z|^2)|f'(z)|<\infty.$$
Question: Must it follow that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n^2<\infty$?

Equivalently, let $\mu$ be a probability measure on the unit circle belonging to the Zygmund class $\Lambda_*$ (i.e. $\mu([x-h,x+h])$ as a function of $x$ has Zygmund modulus of continuity, or equivalently the harmonic extension $u(re^{i\theta})$ of $\mu$ satisfies $(1-r)|\nabla u|$ bounded), and suppose its Fourier coefficients
$$\hat\mu(n)=\int_0^{2\pi}e^{-inx}\,d\mu(x)$$
are nonnegative for all $n\in\mathbb{Z}$. Is it true that $(\hat\mu(n))_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\in\ell^2$?

If the answer is negative, does there nevertheless exist some $p>4$ such that for every such $f$ one has $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|a_n|^p<\infty$?

Let $\Pi$ denote the upper half-plane in $\mathbb{C}$, and let $G$ be a finitely-generated Fuchsian group of the first kind acting on $\Pi$ (i.e., a discrete subgroup of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ whose limit set on $\partial\Pi=\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ is all of $\partial\Pi$, and which has a finite-sided fundamental domain).

A homeomorphism $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called quasi-symmetric if there is a constant $M\geq 1$ such that $\frac{1}{M}\leq \frac{f(x+t)-f(x)}{f(x)-f(x-t)}\leq M$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $t>0$. By the Beurling–Ahlfors extension, such $f$ extends to a quasiconformal homeomorphism $F:\Pi\to\Pi$. Call $F$ $G$-invariant if for every $g\in G$ there exists a Möbius transformation $g'$ preserving $\Pi$ with $F\circ g = g'\circ F$. Call $F$ totally singular if its boundary values $f$ map a set of full measure on $\mathbb{R}$ onto a set of measure zero (equivalently, $f$ is singular as a function).

Let $S_G$ denote the space of Schwarzian derivatives $S_h$ of all univalent meromorphic functions $h$ on the lower half-plane $\Pi^*$ that are $G$-compatible (i.e., for each $g\in G$ there is a Möbius transformation $g'$ with $h\circ g = g'\circ h$ on $\Pi^*$), regarded as a subset of the Banach space of bounded holomorphic quadratic differentials for $G$ on $\Pi^*$. Let $T_G\subset S_G$ denote the Teichmüller space of $G$, consisting of those Schwarzians $S_h$ where $h$ admits a quasiconformal extension to $\mathbb{C}$.

Answer the following:

(a) Is every $G$-invariant quasi-symmetric homeomorphism $F:\Pi\to\Pi$ totally singular?

(b) Is $T_G$ dense in $S_G$?

where $m$ and $N$ denote the usual Nevanlinna proximity and counting functions.

Prove or disprove: under these assumptions, $\delta(w,f)=0$ for every finite complex number $w\in\mathbb{C}$.

For a domain $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, let $H(G)$ denote the ring (under pointwise addition and multiplication) of complex-valued holomorphic functions on $G$. It is classical that for two domains $G_1, G_2 \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, the rings $H(G_1)$ and $H(G_2)$ are isomorphic (as rings) if and only if $G_1$ and $G_2$ are conformally or anticonformally equivalent.

Two rings $R_1$ and $R_2$ are said to be elementarily equivalent if they satisfy the same first-order sentences in the language of rings (i.e., $R_1 \equiv R_2$ in the sense of model theory).

Problem: Characterize, in geometric/analytic terms, those pairs of domains $G_1, G_2 \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ for which the rings $H(G_1)$ and $H(G_2)$ are elementarily equivalent. In particular, determine whether elementary equivalence of $H(G_1)$ and $H(G_2)$ implies conformal or anticonformal equivalence of $G_1$ and $G_2$, and if not, give a complete description of the elementary-equivalence classes among such rings.

$$\mathcal{D}_\alpha=\{\,f\ge 0\text{ measurable on }\mathbb{R} : \exists\,\mu\text{ finite positive Borel with } f(x)\le p_\mu(x)\text{ for all }x\,\}.$$

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $A^2=A^2(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space of all holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|_{A^2}^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. For $f\in A^2$, set
$$\mathcal{P}f=\{pf : p\text{ is a polynomial}\}\subset A^2.$$
A function $f\in A^2$ is called cyclic (for the operator of multiplication by $z$) if $\mathcal{P}f$ is dense in $A^2$.

(a) Suppose $f\in A^2$ and $1/f\in A^2$ (so in particular $f$ has no zeros in $\mathbb{D}$). Must $\mathcal{P}f$ be dense in $A^2$?

(b) More generally, suppose $f\in A^2$ and there exist constants $a,c>0$ such that
$$|f(z)|\ge c\,(1-|z|)^a\quad\text{for all }z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
Must $\mathcal{P}f$ be dense in $A^2$?

Borichev and Hedenmalm (J. Amer. Math. Soc., 1997, "Harmonic functions of maximal growth: invertibility and cyclicity in Bergman spaces") constructed a function $f\in A^2(\mathbb{D})$ with $1/f\in A^2(\mathbb{D})$ that is not cyclic, giving a negative answer to (a) and hence to the more general (b). Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc and let $H^\infty$ denote the algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{D}$. Call an arc $\gamma\subset\overline{\mathbb{D}}$ a non-tangential arc ending at $1$ if $\gamma\setminus\{1\}\subset\mathbb{D}$, $\gamma$ has $1$ as one of its endpoints, and $\gamma$ approaches $1$ non-tangentially (i.e., $\gamma$ is contained in some Stolz angle at $1$). For each $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$, set
$$\gamma_\theta=e^{i\theta}\gamma=\{e^{i\theta}z:z\in\gamma\},$$
which is a non-tangential arc in $\mathbb{D}$ ending at $e^{i\theta}$.

Question: Does there exist a function $g\in H^\infty$ such that, for every $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$, the limit
$$\lim_{\substack{z\to e^{i\theta}\\ z\in\gamma_\theta}} g(z)$$
fails to exist?

(It is known that if $\gamma$ is instead a tangential arc, such a function $g$ does exist.)

Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ denote the unit circle. Zygmund's class $\Lambda_*$ (also denoted $A_*$) consists of all continuous functions $f: \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfying the smoothness condition
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb{T},\, h>0} \frac{|f(x+h) + f(x-h) - 2f(x)|}{h} < \infty.$$
A finite complex Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{T}$ is said to belong to $\Lambda_*$ if its indefinite integral $F(x) = \mu([0,x])$ belongs to $\Lambda_*$, equivalently if there is a constant $C$ such that $|\mu(I)| \le C\,|I|$ for every arc $I \subset \mathbb{T}$ and the appropriate symmetric second-difference condition holds. The Fourier–Stieltjes coefficients of $\mu$ are
$$\hat{\mu}(n) = \int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{-in\theta}\, d\mu(\theta), \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z}.$$
A measure $\mu$ is called singular if it is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{T}$.

Question: Does there exist a singular (finite, positive or signed) measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{T}$ belonging to Zygmund's class $\Lambda_*$ such that $\hat{\mu}(n) \ge 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$?

Let $\mathbb{T}$ denote the unit circle and $L^2(\mathbb{T})$ the Hilbert space of square-integrable functions on $\mathbb{T}$ with respect to normalized Lebesgue measure. Let $H^2 = H^2(\mathbb{T})$ be the Hardy space, identified with the closed subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{T})$ spanned by $\{e^{ink}: n \geq 0\}$, and let $P_+ : L^2(\mathbb{T}) \to H^2$ be the orthogonal (Riesz) projection. For a symbol $\varphi \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T})$ (or more generally a suitable distribution on $\mathbb{T}$), the Hankel operator $H_\varphi : H^2 \to (H^2)^\perp$ is defined by
$$H_\varphi f = (I - P_+)(\varphi f), \qquad f \in H^2.$$
Recall that a bounded linear operator $T$ on a separable Hilbert space is said to belong to the trace class $S_1$ if $\sum_n s_n(T) < \infty$, where $\{s_n(T)\}$ are the singular values of $T$.

Problem: Give an intrinsic characterisation of those symbols $\varphi$ for which the Hankel operator $H_\varphi$ on $H^2$ is of trace class.

Peller (1980), who showed that a Hankel operator $H_\varphi$ on $H^2$ belongs to the Schatten–von Neumann class $S_p$ ($0 < p < \infty$) if and only if its symbol (modulo analytic part) lies in the Besov space $B^{1/p}_{p,p}$. In particular, $H_\varphi$ is of trace class ($p=1$) iff the symbol belongs to the Besov class $B^1_{1,1}$. This is now a foundational theorem in the theory of Hankel operators.

Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n$ that are analytic and univalent in the unit disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For each integer $n\geq 1$ define
$$A_n=\sup_{f\in S}|a_n|.$$
It is known (Hayman's regularity theorem) that the limit
$$K_0=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{A_n}{n}$$
exists and is finite, and that $K_0\leq C$ for some explicit constant $C<1.243$. Determine whether $K_0=1$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of whether the Hayman regularity constant K_0 equals 1 (with the bound K_0 < 1.243 due to Milin) is listed as an open problem in the standard references on univalent functions, and no resolution appears in the searched literature. The de Branges theorem proved |a_n| ≤ n for f ∈ S, which gives K_0 ≤ 1, so the question is now whether K_0 = 1 (i.e., whether the bound is sharp asymptotically); this remains open as far as accessible sources indicate.

Let $n \geq 2$, and let $\Omega$ denote either the open unit ball $B_n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : \|z\| < 1\}$ or the open unit polydisc $D^n = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : |z_j| < 1 \text{ for } j=1,\dots,n\}$. Let $H^\infty(\Omega)$ be the commutative unital ring of bounded holomorphic functions $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}$, equipped with pointwise addition and multiplication. A commutative ring $R$ is called coherent if, for every pair of finitely generated ideals $I, J \subseteq R$, the intersection $I \cap J$ is again a finitely generated ideal of $R$.

Question: Is $H^\infty(\Omega)$ coherent? Equivalently, is it true that for every pair of finitely generated ideals $I, J$ in $H^\infty(\Omega)$, the ideal $I \cap J$ is finitely generated?

(For $n = 1$, in the ring $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit disc, the intersection of two finitely generated ideals is known to be finitely generated.)

Mortini and Wick (arXiv:1606.05568, "Noncoherent uniform algebras in C^n") prove that for n ≥ 2 the algebra H^∞ of bounded holomorphic functions on the unit ball and on the polydisc in C^n is not coherent; equivalently, there exist finitely generated ideals whose intersection is not finitely generated. This resolves the question negatively in dimensions ≥ 2.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The coefficient problem for the class Σ of univalent functions on the exterior disk is a classical long-standing problem in geometric function theory. Sharp bounds are known only for the first few coefficients (|b_1|, |b_2|, |c_2|, |c_3|, and the Garabedian–Schiffer bound for |b_3|). No sharp bounds are known in general for |b_n| or |c_n| with n ≥ 4; unlike the Bieberbach conjecture for the class S (resolved by de Branges in 1985), the analogous conjecture for Σ remains open.

Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a strictly pseudoconvex domain (i.e., a bounded domain admitting a $C^2$ defining function $\rho$ such that $\Omega = \{\rho < 0\}$, $d\rho \neq 0$ on $\partial\Omega$, and the Levi form of $\rho$ is positive definite at every boundary point). A bounded holomorphic function $f \in H^\infty(\Omega)$ is called an inner function if its boundary values $f^*$, which exist almost everywhere on $\partial\Omega$ with respect to surface measure, satisfy $|f^*(z)| = 1$ for almost every $z \in \partial\Omega$. A nonconstant inner function is called nontrivial.

Question: For every strictly pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ with $n \geq 2$, does there exist a nontrivial inner function on $\Omega$?

For the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$, the existence of nontrivial inner functions was established independently by Aleksandrov and by Hakim–Sibony / Løw around 1981–1982. Løw (Math. Z. 185 (1984), 191–210) extended this to all smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$, giving a positive answer to the problem in the standard $C^\infty$-smooth setting.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $S$ denote the class of functions $h$ that are analytic and univalent on $\mathbb{D}$, normalized by $h(0)=0$ and $h'(0)=1$. A function $h\in S$ is called convex if $h(\mathbb{D})$ is a convex domain. For two analytic functions $f(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ and $g(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n z^n$ on $\mathbb{D}$, define their Hadamard (convolution) product by
$$ (f*g)(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n b_n z^n. $$
Prove or disprove: if $f,g\in S$ are both convex, then $f*g$ belongs to $S$ and is also convex on $\mathbb{D}$.

Let $\{M_k\}_{k=0}^\infty$ be a sequence of positive numbers satisfying $M_0 = 1$ and the log-convexity-type condition
$$\frac{M_{k+j}}{M_k M_j} \ge \binom{k+j}{j} \quad\text{for all } k, j \ge 0,$$
together with the non-quasianalyticity condition
$$\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{M_k}{M_{k+1}} < \infty.$$
Let $X \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a compact set. Consider the class $A(X)$ of functions $f$ on $X$ that are limits, in the norm
$$\|g\| = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{1}{M_k}\,\sup_{X} |g^{(k)}|,$$
of rational functions with poles off $X$. Then $A(X)$ is a commutative Banach algebra under this norm.

Question: Is the maximal ideal space of $A(X)$ equal to $X$ (with the natural identification of points of $X$ with evaluation characters)?

It is known that the answer is affirmative when $X$ is the closed unit disc or a compact interval of the real line. The problem asks whether this holds for an arbitrary compact set $X \subset \mathbb{C}$.

Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$, and let $A$ denote the disc algebra, i.e., the algebra of continuous functions $f : \overline{\mathbb{D}} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the closed unit disc $\overline{\mathbb{D}} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$ that are holomorphic on the open disc $\mathbb{D}$. Identify each $f \in A$ with its restriction to $S^1$, and let $\operatorname{Re} A = \{\operatorname{Re} f|_{S^1} : f \in A\}$ denote the real part of the disc algebra, viewed as a space of real-valued continuous functions on $S^1$.

Given a homeomorphism $\psi : S^1 \to S^1$, define $\operatorname{Re} A \circ \psi = \{u \circ \psi : u \in \operatorname{Re} A\}$.

Problem. Characterize, in terms of the regularity of $\psi$, those homeomorphisms $\psi : S^1 \to S^1$ for which
$$\operatorname{Re} A = \operatorname{Re} A \circ \psi,$$
that is, those $\psi$ such that for every $f \in A$ there exists $g \in A$ with $\operatorname{Re} f = \operatorname{Re} g \circ \psi$ on $S^1$.

It is known that this equality forces $\psi$ to be absolutely continuous, and that $\psi \in C^{1+\varepsilon}$ (for some $\varepsilon > 0$) is sufficient. The problem is to determine the precise regularity condition on $\psi$ characterizing this equality.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $S$ denote the class of holomorphic univalent functions
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n$$
on $\mathbb{D}$, normalized by $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=1$. For $f\in S$, the area (counted with multiplicity, or equivalently the area of $f(\mathbb{D})$ since $f$ is univalent) of the image of $\mathbb{D}$ under $f$ is given by
$$A(f)=\pi\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n\,|a_n|^2,$$
with $a_1=1$.

For a fixed complex number $c$, define
$$\mathcal{A}(c)=\inf\{A(f): f\in S,\ a_2(f)=c\}.$$

Determine $\mathcal{A}(c)$ as a function of $c$, and identify the extremal univalent functions.

Note that one always has $A(f)\ge \pi(1+2|a_2|^2)$, with equality only if $f(z)=z+a_2 z^2$; but this polynomial fails to be univalent in $\mathbb{D}$ when $|a_2|>1/2$, so the trivial lower bound is not sharp in that range, and the problem is to find the sharp bound (in particular for $|c|>1/2$, where $|c|\le 2$ by the classical coefficient bound).

Note that one always has $A(f)\ge \pi(1+2|a_2|^2)$, with equality only if $f(z)=z+a_2 z^2$; but this polynomial fails to be univalent in $\mathbb{D}$ when $|a_2|>1/2$, so the trivial lower bound is not sharp in that range, and the problem is to find the sharp bound (in particular for $|c|>1/2$, where $|c|\le 2$ by the classical coefficient bound).

The minimal area problem posed by H. S. Shapiro was studied by D. Aharonov and H. S. Shapiro in the early 1970s and was finally resolved roughly 25 years later with major contributions by A. Solynin. The sharp bound $A(f)\ge (27\pi/7)(2-\alpha)^{-2}$ holds for all $f\in S$ with $|f''(0)|=2\alpha$ and $1/2<\alpha<2$ (and the trivial bound $\pi(1+2|a_2|^2)$ is sharp for $|a_2|\le 1/2$), giving a complete solution. The work also produced quadrature domains as a notable byproduct.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $f$ be analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ with Taylor expansion
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n,$$
and assume that
$$\operatorname{Re}\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\ \ge\ \frac{1}{2}\qquad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb{D}$$
(i.e. $f$ is starlike of order $1/2$). Determine the largest number $r_0\in(0,1]$ with the property that every such $f$ is convex on the disc $\{|z|<r_0\}$, that is,
$$\operatorname{Re}\!\left(1+\frac{zf''(z)}{f'(z)}\right)>0\qquad\text{for }|z|<r_0.$$
Equivalently, writing $P(z)=\dfrac{2zf'(z)/f(z)-1}{1}$ scaled so that $\operatorname{Re} P(z)>0$ in $\mathbb{D}$ and $P(0)=1$ (this corresponds to setting $zf'(z)/f(z)=\tfrac{1}{2}+\tfrac{1}{2}P(z)$), find the largest $r$ such that
$$\min_{|z|=r}\ \operatorname{Re}\!\left\{\frac{P(z)}{P(z)+1}+\frac{zP'(z)}{P(z)+1}\right\}\ >\ 0$$
for every analytic $P$ in $\mathbb{D}$ with $\operatorname{Re} P>0$ and $P(0)=1$, and give the extremal function.

Let $\{p_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of positive integers satisfying
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{p_n}<\infty.$$
For a Jordan arc $\gamma\subset\mathbb{C}$, let $C(\gamma)$ denote the Banach space of continuous complex-valued functions on $\gamma$ equipped with the uniform norm. We say that the system of monomials $\{z^{p_n}\}_{n\ge 1}$ spans $C(\gamma)$ if the complex linear span of these monomials (restricted to $\gamma$) is dense in $C(\gamma)$.

Question: Does the convergence condition $\sum 1/p_n<\infty$ alone guarantee that the sequence $\{z^{p_n}\}_{n\ge 1}$ fails to span $C(\gamma)$ for every Jordan arc $\gamma$?

(It is known, by results on arcs of locally bounded rotation such as $C^1$ arcs, that the strengthened hypothesis
$$p_n\ge n L(n),\qquad 0<L(n)\uparrow\infty,\qquad \sum\frac{1}{nL(n)}<\infty,$$
already ensures non-spanning; the question asks whether the bare condition $\sum 1/p_n<\infty$ suffices for arbitrary Jordan arcs.)

Let p be a positive integer. A function f, holomorphic in the unit disc D = {z : |z| < 1}, is said to belong to the class S(p) of areally mean p-valent functions if for every w ∈ ℂ the number n(w) of roots of f(z) = w in D (counted with multiplicity) satisfies
   (1/π) ∫∫_{ℂ} n(w) dA(w) ≤ p · (area of f(D), counted with multiplicity, ≤ p · sup_{|z|<1} (1/2π) ∫_0^{2π} … ),
i.e. f is mean p-valent in the disc in the standard sense. Write the Taylor expansion
   f(z) = Σ_{n=0}^∞ a_n z^n,    z ∈ D.

Assume in addition that f is bounded in D. The question is the following coefficient-rate problem:

Show that for every bounded f ∈ S(p) one has
   |a_n| = o(n^{-1/2})    as n → ∞,
and prove that this estimate is best possible in the sense that for any positive function ε(n) tending to 0 there exists a bounded f ∈ S(p) for which the inequality |a_n| ≤ ε(n) n^{-1/2} fails for infinitely many n.

Let $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a planar domain and let $H^\infty(D)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $D$, equipped with the supremum norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. A sequence $\{z_j\}$ of distinct points in $D$ is called an interpolating sequence for $H^\infty(D)$ if for every bounded sequence $\{\alpha_j\} \in \ell^\infty$ there exists a function $F \in H^\infty(D)$ such that $F(z_j) = \alpha_j$ for all $j$.

Suppose that the sequence $\{z_j\} \subset D$ has the following weak (or "individual") interpolation property: there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for each index $j$ there is a function $F_j \in H^\infty(D)$ with
$$F_j(z_j) = 1, \qquad F_j(z_k) = 0 \text{ for all } k \neq j, \qquad \|F_j\|_\infty \leq C.$$

Question: Must $\{z_j\}$ then be an interpolating sequence for $H^\infty(D)$?

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. For a holomorphic function $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and $w\in\mathbb{C}$, let $n(w,f)$ denote the number of solutions of $f(z)=w$ in $\mathbb{D}$, counted with multiplicity. A function $f$ holomorphic in $\mathbb{D}$ is called areally mean univalent (mean $p$-valent with $p=1$) if
$$\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} n(Re^{i\theta},f)\,d\theta \le 1 \qquad \text{for a.e. } R>0.$$
Consider the class $\mathcal{F}$ of all areally mean univalent functions normalized by
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n z^n,\qquad z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
For this class one has the sharp Koebe-type bounds
$$\frac{r}{(1+r)^2}\le |f(z)|\le \frac{r}{(1-r)^2}\qquad (|z|=r<1),$$
the lower bound following from the fact (due to Garabedian and Royden) that every $f\in\mathcal{F}$ assumes in $\mathbb{D}$ each value $w$ with $|w|<\tfrac{1}{4}$.

Determine, for each $r\in(0,1)$, the sharp upper bounds
$$\sup_{f\in\mathcal{F},\ |z|=r}|f'(z)| \qquad\text{and}\qquad \sup_{f\in\mathcal{F},\ |z|=r}\frac{|f'(z)|}{|f(z)|},$$
and identify the extremal functions, if any.

Let $K$ be a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge 3$. Let $\mathcal{D}$ denote the space of $C^\infty$ test functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with compact support. For $\varphi\in\mathcal{D}$, let $D(\varphi)$ be a closed ball of least diameter containing the support $\operatorname{spt}\varphi$, let $d(\varphi)=\operatorname{diam}(\operatorname{spt}\varphi)$, and set
$$\|\varphi\|_*=\|\varphi\|_\infty+d(\varphi)\,\|\nabla\varphi\|_\infty.$$
Let $C$ denote the harmonic capacity in $\mathbb{R}^n$ associated with the Riesz kernel $r^{-n+2}$; for a Borel set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $C(E)$ is the standard Newtonian capacity.

For a continuous function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ consider the following two conditions:

(1) There exists a sequence $\{f_m\}_{m=1}^\infty$ of functions, each harmonic on some open neighborhood of $K$, such that $f_m\to f$ uniformly on $K$.

(2) There exists a function $\eta:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ with $\eta(\delta)\downarrow 0$ as $\delta\downarrow 0$ such that for every $\varphi\in\mathcal{D}$,
$$\left|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\,\Delta\varphi(x)\,dx\right|\le \eta(d(\varphi))\,\|\varphi\|_*\,C(D(\varphi)\setminus K).$$

It is known that (1) implies (2), and that (2) implies (1) when $f$ is of class $C^2$. Determine whether (1) and (2) are equivalent for arbitrary continuous functions $f$.

Let $H^\infty$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$, equipped with the supremum norm. Given $f_1, f_2 \in H^\infty$, let $I(f_1, f_2) = \{f_1 h_1 + f_2 h_2 : h_1, h_2 \in H^\infty\}$ denote the ideal of $H^\infty$ generated by $f_1$ and $f_2$.

Suppose $g \in H^\infty$ satisfies the pointwise inequality
$$|g(z)| \le |f_1(z)| + |f_2(z)| \qquad \text{for all } z \in \mathbb{D}.$$

It is known that under this hypothesis $g^3 \in I(f_1, f_2)$, while in general $g$ itself need not lie in $I(f_1, f_2)$.

Question: must $g^2 \in I(f_1, f_2)$? Equivalently, do there always exist $g_1, g_2 \in H^\infty$ such that
$$g(z)^2 = f_1(z)\, g_1(z) + f_2(z)\, g_2(z) \qquad \text{for all } z \in \mathbb{D}\,?$$

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

S. Treil resolved Wolff's $g^2$ problem negatively: there exist $f_1, f_2, g \in H^\infty$ with $|g| \le |f_1|+|f_2|$ on $\mathbb{D}$ for which $g^2 \notin I(f_1,f_2)$. Treil further showed that $g^{1+\varepsilon} \in I(f_1,f_2)$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$, so the exponent $2$ is the precise borderline failure between Wolff's $g^3$ result and Rao's counterexample for $g$.

Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f(z) = z + \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ that are analytic and univalent on the unit disk $\mathbb{D} = \{z : |z| < 1\}$. For two analytic functions $f(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ and $g(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} b_n z^n$ on $\mathbb{D}$, denote by $f * g$ their Hadamard (convolution) product
$$ (f * g)(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n b_n z^n. $$
A function $F \in S$ is called starlike (with respect to the origin) if $F(\mathbb{D})$ is starlike with respect to $0$, equivalently $\operatorname{Re}\bigl(z F'(z)/F(z)\bigr) > 0$ for $z \in \mathbb{D}$.

It is known that $f \in S$ if and only if for every pair of complex numbers $\xi_1, \xi_2$ with $|\xi_1| \le 1$ and $|\xi_2| \le 1$,
$$ \frac{z}{(1-\xi_1 z)(1-\xi_2 z)} * f(z) \ne 0 \qquad \text{for all } 0 < |z| < 1. $$
Moreover, if $F$ is analytic on $\mathbb{D}$ with $F(0) = 0$, $F'(0) = 1$, and satisfies
$$ (F * f)(z) \ne 0 \qquad \text{for all } z \text{ with } 0 < |z| < 1 \text{ and every } f \in S, $$
then $F$ is starlike. For example, $F(z) = z + z^n/n$ has this property for every integer $n \ge 2$ (this follows from the Bieberbach coefficient estimates, now de Branges' theorem).

Determine the complete class of starlike functions $F$ with the property that $(F * f)(z) \ne 0$ for $0 < |z| < 1$ whenever $f \in S$.

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation on the finite interval (0,L) with t>0:
  u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0,  0<x<L,  t>0,
together with the initial condition
  u(x,0) = φ(x),  0<x<L,
and a set of three linear boundary conditions of the form
  B_k u(t) = h_k(t),  k=1,2,3,  t>0,
where each B_k is a linear combination of the boundary traces u(0,t), u(L,t), u_x(0,t), u_x(L,t), u_{xx}(0,t), u_{xx}(L,t) chosen so that the linearized problem is well-posed.

For s∈ℝ, say the initial-boundary value problem is locally well-posed in H^s(0,L) if, for every (φ, h_1, h_2, h_3) in the natural product of H^s(0,L) and the corresponding compatible boundary trace spaces, there exist a time T>0 and a unique solution u∈C([0,T];H^s(0,L)) depending continuously on the data.

It is known that local well-posedness holds in H^s(0,L) for every s>-1.

Question: Does there exist any s ≤ -1 for which the above initial-boundary value problem is locally well-posed in H^s(0,L)? In particular, is the problem ill-posed in H^s(0,L) for every s<-1?

Let $f(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ be a function univalent (analytic and one-to-one) in the open unit disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C} : |z|<1\}$. Suppose there exist constants $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\lambda \neq 0$ and $\delta > 0$ such that
$$(1-r)^2 f(r) = \lambda + O\!\left((1-r)^{\delta}\right) \quad \text{as } r \to 1^-.$$
It is known that under this hypothesis the Taylor coefficients satisfy
$$\frac{a_n}{n} = \lambda + O\!\left(\frac{1}{\log n}\right) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.$$
Determine the optimal possible error term: to what extent can the bound $O(1/\log n)$ be improved? More precisely, find the best function $\varepsilon(n) \to 0$ such that the implication
$$(1-r)^2 f(r) = \lambda + O((1-r)^{\delta}) \implies \frac{a_n}{n} = \lambda + O(\varepsilon(n))$$
holds for every univalent $f$ as above, and exhibit extremal examples showing optimality.

Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $S$ denote the class of functions $f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ that are holomorphic and univalent on $\mathbb{D}$ and normalized by $f(0) = 0$ and $f'(0) = 1$. For $f \in S$, define the omitted set inside the unit disk by
$$O_f = (\mathbb{C} \setminus f(\mathbb{D})) \cap \mathbb{D},$$
i.e., the set of points $\omega$ with $|\omega| < 1$ that are not in the image $f(\mathbb{D})$.

Address the following questions:

(a) Characterise intrinsically those subsets $O \subseteq \mathbb{D}$ for which there exists $f \in S$ with $O_f = O$.

(b) Determine
$$A^* = \sup_{f \in S} \operatorname{Area}(O_f),$$
the maximum possible Lebesgue area of $O_f$, and find an extremal function (or describe the extremal configuration) for which the supremum is attained.

(c) Given two prescribed points $\omega_1, \omega_2 \in \mathbb{D}$, give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of $f \in S$ such that both $\omega_1, \omega_2 \in O_f$. More generally, for any finite collection $\omega_1, \dots, \omega_n \in \mathbb{D}$, give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of $f \in S$ with $\{\omega_1, \dots, \omega_n\} \subseteq O_f$.

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation on a finite interval (0,L), L>0,
    u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0,   (x,t) ∈ (0,L) × (0,T),
with initial datum
    u(x,0) = φ(x),  x ∈ (0,L),
and three (linear) boundary conditions of the general form
    B_k u(t) = h_k(t),   k = 1,2,3,  t ∈ (0,T),
where each B_k is a linear boundary operator built from the traces of u, u_x, u_{xx} at x = 0 and x = L, chosen so that the resulting initial-boundary value problem is well-posed in a suitable Sobolev space on (0,L). One or more of the boundary data h_k are designated as boundary controls.

Question. Determine, for an arbitrary admissible (well-posed) choice of boundary operators B_1, B_2, B_3 — beyond the specific Dirichlet/Neumann-type configurations classically known to be controllable — whether the system is exactly (or null) controllable: that is, whether for every pair of states (φ, ψ) in the chosen function space (with ψ sufficiently close to φ in the case of local controllability), there exist controls h_k among the boundary data such that the corresponding solution satisfies u(·,T) = ψ. Characterize, in terms of the boundary operators (B_1, B_2, B_3) and the length L, when controllability holds and when it fails.

Controllability of KdV on a finite interval has been established for several specific boundary configurations (Rosier; Cerpa; Coron; Glass–Guerrero; and others), and recent work has resolved small-time local controllability at all critical lengths for Neumann boundary control. However, no general controllability theory covering arbitrary admissible (Colin–Ghidaglia type) boundary operators has been published; recent literature on coupled KdV systems explicitly notes that controllability is highly sensitive to the boundary configuration and that general results are not available. The problem appears to remain open.

representations.normalized:
Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f$ that are holomorphic and univalent on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and normalized by $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=1$. For $f\in S$, define
$$h(z) = \bigl\{f(z^2)\bigr\}^{1/2} = z + c_3 z^3 + c_5 z^5 + \cdots,$$
the odd univalent function associated with $f$ (with the branch chosen so that $h'(0)=1$).

Robertson's conjecture asserts that for every $f\in S$ and every integer $n\geq 1$,
$$1 + |c_3|^2 + |c_5|^2 + \cdots + |c_{2n-1}|^2 \le n.$$

This inequality is known to hold whenever $f$ is starlike (i.e., $f(\mathbb{D})$ is starlike with respect to the origin).

Question: Does Robertson's inequality
$$\sum_{k=1}^{n} |c_{2k-1}|^2 \le n \qquad (\text{with } c_1 = 1)$$
hold under either of the following weaker hypotheses?
(a) $f\in S$ has real Taylor coefficients;
(b) $f\in S$ is close-to-convex (i.e., there exists a convex univalent function $g$ on $\mathbb{D}$ such that $\operatorname{Re}\bigl(f'(z)/g'(z)\bigr)>0$ on $\mathbb{D}$).

Robertson's conjecture for the full class S was established by Louis de Branges in 1985 as part of his proof of the Bieberbach conjecture: de Branges proved the Milin conjecture, which implies Robertson's conjecture for all of S, which in turn implies Bieberbach's. Hence the inequality holds for every f in S, in particular for f with real coefficients and for close-to-convex f, so the special cases asked about are subsumed by de Branges' theorem.

representations.normalized:
Let $\mathrm{CFT}_d$ be a $d$-dimensional conformal field theory and let $\mathcal{D}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a conformal boundary or a conformal defect of dimension $p<d$ that preserves the subgroup $SO(p+1,1)\times SO(d-p)$ of the conformal group. The defect data of $(\mathrm{CFT}_d,\mathcal{D})$ consist of:
\begin{itemize}
\item the bulk one-point functions $\langle \mathcal{O}_\Delta(x)\rangle_\mathcal{D} = a_\mathcal{O}/|x_\perp|^\Delta$ for bulk primaries $\mathcal{O}_\Delta$,
\item the spectrum $\{\widehat{\Delta}_i\}$ of defect primary operators and their bulk-to-defect coupling coefficients $b_{\mathcal{O}\,\widehat{\mathcal{O}}}$,
\item the defect conformal anomaly coefficients (e.g.\ for $p=2$ the central charges $b$ and $d_1,d_2$, and for $p=4$ the anomalies $a_\mathcal{D}$, $c_\mathcal{D}$, $d_{1,2}$),
\item the defect free energy / $g$-function and its monotonicity along defect RG flows.
\end{itemize}

Now suppose in addition that the bulk theory and the defect together preserve some amount of supersymmetry, so that supersymmetric-localization techniques apply (in particular, that the path integral on a suitable curved background such as $S^d$, $S^p\times \mathbb{H}^{d-p}$, or $\mathbb{HS}^d$ in the presence of $\mathcal{D}$ can be reduced to a finite-dimensional matrix integral).

Determine which of the non-perturbative defect data above can be computed exactly using supersymmetric localization in the presence of the defect $\mathcal{D}$. Concretely, formulate and answer the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For which classes of supersymmetric defects (e.g.\ BPS Wilson/'t Hooft lines, surface operators, BPS boundaries and interfaces of class $D5$/$NS5$ type, codimension-two monodromy defects) does localization on $S^d$ produce a closed-form matrix model whose observables compute defect one-point functions $a_\mathcal{O}$ of BPS bulk primaries?
\item Which defect anomaly coefficients (such as the $b$-anomaly of $2d$ defects in $4d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theories, or the $4d$ defect anomalies in $6d$ $(2,0)$ theories) can be extracted from the localized partition function or its derivatives, and through which precise formulas?
\item Can the defect free energy (or $g$-function) and the corresponding monotonicity ($b$-theorem, defect $a$-theorem) be proven non-perturbatively for supersymmetric defects via localization?
\item Can localization, possibly combined with integrability or the conformal bootstrap, determine non-protected defect CFT data such as anomalous dimensions of non-BPS defect primaries and bulk-to-defect OPE coefficients at finite coupling?
\end{enumerate}

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Substantial progress has been made: supersymmetric localization yields exact matrix-model expressions for one-point functions of BPS operators in the presence of D5-type interfaces in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, exact bulk-defect OPE data for the 1/2-BPS Wilson line (in combination with the Quantum Spectral Curve), and exact results for protected correlators in 3d $\mathcal{N}\ge 4$ defect setups. Defect $b$- and $a$-anomalies have been computed via localization in several supersymmetric examples, and a general defect $a$-theorem framework using $a$-maximization has been developed. However, a complete non-perturbative determination of all defect CFT data (including non-BPS spectra and general anomaly monotonicity theorems) via localization remains open; the broad question is therefore only partially resolved.

For two formal power series
$$f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n,\qquad g(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} b_n z^n,$$
define the operation
$$(f\otimes g)(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_n b_n}{n}\, z^n.$$

Prove or disprove the following statement: if $f,g\in S_{\mathbb R}$, then $f\otimes g\in S_{\mathbb R}$.

representations.normalized:
Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ that are analytic and univalent in the unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z:|z|<1\}$. The coefficient problem for a subclass $\mathcal{F}\subset S$ asks for the sharp bound
$$\sup_{f\in\mathcal{F}} |a_n|\quad \text{for every integer } n\ge 2,$$
together with a description of all extremal functions.

Determine the sharp coefficient bounds $\sup\{|a_n| : f\in\mathcal{F}\}$ for every $n\ge 2$, in each of the following one-parameter families of univalent functions:

(a) The class $B(\alpha)$ of Bazilevich functions, consisting of those $f\in S$ representable as
$$f(z)=\left(\alpha\int_0^z p(t)\,s(t)^{\alpha}\,t^{-1}\,dt\right)^{1/\alpha},$$
where $\alpha>0$, $p(t)=1+p_1 t+p_2 t^2+\cdots$ is analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ with $\operatorname{Re} p(t)>0$, and $s(t)=t+s_2 t^2+\cdots$ is starlike in $\mathbb{D}$ (i.e., $\operatorname{Re}(ts'(t)/s(t))>0$).

(b) The class $M(\alpha)$ of Mocanu–Reade functions, consisting of those $f\in S$ with $f(z)f'(z)/z\ne 0$ in $\mathbb{D}$ such that
$$\operatorname{Re}\left[\alpha\left(1+\frac{zf''(z)}{f'(z)}\right) + (1-\alpha)\,\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\right] > 0\quad\text{in }\mathbb{D},$$
where $0<\alpha<1$.

(c) The class $S^*(\alpha)$ of strongly starlike functions of order $\alpha$, consisting of those $f\in S$ such that
$$\left|\arg\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\right| < \frac{\alpha\pi}{2}\quad\text{in }\mathbb{D},$$
where $0<\alpha<1$.

The full coefficient problem for these one-parameter families remains open in general. Sharp bounds are known only in particular cases (e.g., $|a_5|$ for Bazilevich functions $B_1(\alpha)$ with $\alpha\ge 1$, certain low-order coefficients, logarithmic coefficient estimates for sub-families). Recent literature continues to obtain partial sharp bounds and Fekete–Szegő-type estimates, but no complete solution for all $n$ has been established.

Consider a holographic setup in which two conformal field theories CFT_+ and CFT_- are related by deformation by a double-trace scalar operator, and are joined along a codimension-one conformal interface (a "double-trace interface") realized in the bulk by imposing mixed Dirichlet–Neumann boundary conditions for a scalar field on the two sides of an asymptotically AdS geometry. Such interfaces can be analyzed by (i) solving the resulting mixed boundary-value problem for the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, and (ii) applying harmonic analysis on warped-product bulk geometries (so that the wave equation separates) to compute interface two-point functions and the operator spectrum localized on the interface.

Two parallel codimension-one interfaces of this type can be brought together and "fused" into a single effective interface. Develop a systematic framework, using the mixed boundary-value-problem and harmonic-analysis tools above, to describe the fusion of two such double-trace interfaces. Specifically:

1. Define the fusion of two parallel double-trace interfaces I_{a} and I_{b} (associated with double-trace deformation parameters a and b respectively) as the limit in which their separation tends to zero, and characterize the resulting interface I_{a*b} via its bulk boundary conditions and its action on bulk propagators and on the spectrum of interface operators.
2. Derive a closed-form fusion rule expressing the parameter (or boundary condition data) of I_{a*b} in terms of those of I_a and I_b, and verify associativity of the resulting fusion product.
3. Determine how the interface two-point functions and the spectrum of operators living on the fused interface are obtained from those of the constituent interfaces through the harmonic-analysis decomposition.

representations.normalized:
Consider a side-coupled quantum-dot model defined as follows. A one-dimensional interacting electron system in the Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid universality class, characterized by a Luttinger parameter K (with K=1 being the noninteracting point and K≠1 corresponding to repulsive or attractive electron–electron interactions), is coupled by a tunneling amplitude t to a single localized level (the quantum dot) of energy ε_d, where the dot is attached at a single point of the lead but does not interrupt the lead (side-coupled geometry). Let the partition function and free energy F(T) be defined for this Hamiltonian at temperature T, and let the specific heat per unit length of the lead, with the bulk Luttinger-liquid contribution subtracted, be denoted C_d(T) = -T ∂²F_d/∂T², where F_d is the impurity contribution to the free energy.

It is known that, in the low-temperature regime T → 0, C_d(T) admits an asymptotic expansion whose leading term is linear in T, i.e. C_d(T) ≃ γ T + (subleading corrections). A renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation n_d(T) at low temperatures yields a set of anomalous power-law exponents {α_i(K)} (functions of the Luttinger parameter K) that govern the subleading temperature dependence of n_d(T) about its zero-temperature value.

Determine explicitly the subleading correction terms to C_d(T) beyond the leading γT contribution as T → 0, expressing them as a sum of power-law terms T^{β_j(K)} with explicit coefficients depending on K, t, and ε_d. In particular, decide whether the set of exponents {β_j(K)} appearing in the specific heat coincides with the set of exponents {α_i(K)} obtained from the renormalization-group analysis of the dot occupation.

Let $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a Jordan domain with boundary curve $C$, and let $\{F_n(z)\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be the sequence of Faber polynomials associated with $D$ (so that $F_n$ is a polynomial of degree $n$ canonically determined by the exterior conformal map of $\mathbb{C}\setminus D$ onto the exterior of a disk). Let $S(D)$ denote the class of functions univalent in $D$ admitting an expansion
$$f(z) = F_1(z) + \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n\, F_n(z), \qquad z\in D,$$
and let $S^*(D) \subset S(D)$ denote the subclass of those $f \in S(D)$ that are starlike (i.e. $f(D)$ is starlike with respect to the origin).

For each integer $n \ge 2$, define the coefficient region
$$V_n(D) = \{\, a_n(f) : f \in S(D) \,\} \subset \mathbb{C},$$
and analogously $V_n^*(D)$ for the subclass $S^*(D)$.

Question. Does there exist some integer $n \ge 2$ for which the coefficient region $V_n(D)$ is geometrically similar to the boundary curve $C$ (i.e. has the same shape as $C$)? If not, does this hold at least for the starlike coefficient region $V_n^*(D)$?

(Background: when $D$ is the interior of an ellipse, it is known that for every $f$ starlike in $D$ there exist a direction $\theta_f$ and sequences $\{\lambda_n\}_{n\ge 2}$, $\{\mu_n\}_{n\ge 2}$ with $\lambda_n > \mu_n > 0$ — explicitly determined — such that each $a_n(f)$ lies in the closed ellipse centered at $0$ with semi-major axis $\lambda_n$ and semi-minor axis $\mu_n$, inclined at angle $\theta_f$ to the real axis.)

Consider the sine-Gordon field theory on the half-line x ≤ 0, with field φ(x,t) governed by the bulk equation
   ∂_t^2 φ − ∂_x^2 φ + sin φ = 0,
together with the one-parameter family of Robin boundary conditions at x = 0,
   ∂_x φ(0,t) = M sin(φ(0,t)/2),
where M ∈ ℝ is a real parameter. For generic M this boundary condition breaks the integrability of the bulk theory, and the scattering of an incoming antikink (or kink) off the boundary excites not only the soliton's translational zero mode but also a host of additional degrees of freedom (boundary-localized modes, breathers, and continuum radiation), so that the outgoing state may consist of various combinations of an antikink, a kink, and one or more breathers depending on the incident velocity and on M.

Problem. Develop an effective collective-coordinate description of antikink/kink scattering off this non-integrable boundary that quantitatively captures the observed reflection, transmission into breathers, and resonance windows. Concretely, exhibit a finite-dimensional reduction of the field dynamics — specifying a moduli ansatz φ(x,t) ≈ Φ(x; q_1(t), …, q_n(t)) and the resulting effective Lagrangian L_eff(q, q̇) — whose solutions reproduce, with controlled accuracy, the scattering outcomes of the full PDE for a wide range of M and incident velocities, including the resonant energy exchange between the soliton translational mode and the modes excited at the boundary.

For domains of finite connectivity the result is classical (Koebe). C. H. FitzGerald proved a uniqueness result for domains of countable connectivity with arbitrary angle assignments, and an existence result for arbitrary domains under the additional assumption that the continuous angle assignment has finite range, using a crossing-module extremal length tool. The full conjecture (continuous angle assignment, no finite-range hypothesis, on arbitrary plane domains) does not appear to be fully resolved.

Consider the sine-Gordon model in 1+1 dimensions, defined on the half-line $x \le 0$ by the bulk Lagrangian density
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{bulk}} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_t \phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x \phi)^2 + \frac{m^2}{\beta^2}\bigl(\cos(\beta\phi) - 1\bigr),$$
where $\phi(t,x)$ is a real scalar field, $m>0$ is a mass parameter, and $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ is the coupling. At the boundary $x=0$, impose a boundary potential
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{bdy}} = -V_{\text{bdy}}(\phi(t,0)),$$
where $V_{\text{bdy}}$ is chosen so that the resulting boundary condition does not preserve the infinite tower of higher-spin local conserved charges of the bulk theory (i.e., the boundary condition is non-integrable, lying outside the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov family $V_{\text{bdy}}(\phi) = M\cos\!\bigl(\tfrac{\beta}{2}(\phi-\phi_0)\bigr)$).

The problems are:

(a) Provide a precise quantum-field-theoretic description of this half-line sine-Gordon model with non-integrable boundary potential: specify the Hilbert space, the renormalized Hamiltonian, the spectrum of asymptotic particle states (solitons, antisolitons, breathers, and possible boundary bound states), and the appropriate notion of reflection amplitude when bulk-integrability-preserving boundary Yang–Baxter relations fail.

(b) Determine to what extent techniques developed for quantum integrability on the half-line — such as the boundary bootstrap, reflection matrices satisfying the boundary Yang–Baxter equation, the truncated conformal space approach, and form-factor perturbation theory — can be adapted to quantitatively describe the breakdown of integrability induced by such non-integrable boundary terms, including the computation of corrections to reflection amplitudes, decay widths of formerly stable boundary bound states, and the modification of finite-size spectra.

Existing literature treats integrable boundary conditions of the sine-Gordon model (Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov, boundary bootstrap, half-line reflection matrices) and develops form-factor perturbation theory for non-integrable bulk perturbations, plus an asymptotic Lagrangian framework for general non-integrable boundary QFT. However, no comprehensive QFT description of sine-Gordon with a generic non-integrable boundary, nor a complete adaptation of integrability techniques to quantify the breaking, has been established; the question remains open.

representations.normalized:
Consider two-dimensional conformal field theories defined on surfaces with boundary. Two specific fermionic/superconformal theories of interest are:

(i) the free Majorana fermion CFT (central charge c = 1/2), and

(ii) the third unitary N = 1 super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3, i.e. the unitary superconformal minimal model with central charge c = c(m) for m = 5 in the family
   c(m) = 3/2 · (1 − 8/(m(m+2))),
which is the supersymmetric analogue of a unitary Virasoro minimal model and contains fields organised under the N = 1 super-Virasoro algebra.

For each of these theories, conformal (and, where relevant, superconformal-preserving) boundary conditions can be specified by boundary states |B⟩ in the closed-string Hilbert space satisfying gluing conditions of Cardy/Ishibashi type, together with an integrality (Cardy) condition on the open-string spectrum.

Problem. Derive the complete set of (elementary) conformal boundary conditions, together with their boundary states and the corresponding annulus/open-string partition functions, for the free Majorana fermion and for the super-Virasoro minimal model SVIR3, by either:

(a) a direct first-principles construction (for example, solving the Cardy/Ishibashi gluing and integrality conditions intrinsically in the fermionic/superconformal category of representations), or

(b) an adaptation of the classifying-algebra and TFT-with-defects methodology used to construct boundary conditions for bosonic rational CFTs from a modular tensor category and a special symmetric Frobenius algebra, suitably extended to the fermionic/super setting.

Produce in either approach an explicit list of boundary states, verify the Cardy condition, and exhibit the boundary structure constants.

representations.normalized:
Let H denote the closed half-strip
   H = { z ∈ ℂ : Re z > 0, 0 ≤ Im z ≤ 1 }.
Let α : (0, ∞) → (α(0), ∞) be a homeomorphism with α(0) ≥ 0. Suppose that the identification
   x  ↔  α(x) + i,    x ∈ (0, ∞),
which glues the lower edge of H (the positive real axis) to the upper edge (the line Im z = 1) defines a "conformal sewing" of H, i.e. it produces a Riemann surface R(α) obtained by welding H along these two edges via α together with the conformal structure inherited from the interior of H. Say that α is hyperbolic if the resulting Riemann surface R(α) has a hyperbolic end at infinity (equivalently, R(α) admits a non-constant bounded harmonic function near the welded end, or carries a Green's function with a singularity at that end).

Question: If α is hyperbolic, must there exist a positive continuous function ε : (0, ∞) → (0, ∞) with the following stability property — every homeomorphism β : (0, ∞) → (β(0), ∞) (with β(0) ≥ 0) which defines a conformal sewing x ↔ β(x) + i of H and which satisfies
   |β(x) − α(x)| < ε(x)    for all x ∈ (0, ∞),
is itself hyperbolic?

representations.normalized:
Consider the four-dimensional defect conformal field theory obtained from N=4 super Yang–Mills theory with gauge group SU(N) by introducing a codimension-one defect dual to the probe D3–D7 brane intersection that preserves an SO(5) R-symmetry subgroup of SO(6). On one side of the defect, three of the six real scalars Φ_i (i=1,…,6) of N=4 SYM acquire classical, position-dependent vacuum expectation values built from a fuzzy-four-sphere construction with k units of background flux, while the remaining three scalars vanish classically; on the other side all scalars vanish.

Tree-level one-point functions of single-trace scalar operators of the form
   O(x) = tr( Φ_{i_1} Φ_{i_2} ⋯ Φ_{i_L} )(x)
in this background can be computed as overlaps between an SO(6) integrable spin-chain Bethe eigenstate of length L and a matrix product state |MPS_k⟩ encoding the classical defect solution.

Problem. Find a closed-form expression, valid for arbitrary chain length L, arbitrary set of magnon rapidities {u_j} solving the SO(6) Bethe equations, and arbitrary flux parameter k, for the overlap
   ⟨MPS_k | {u_j} ⟩ / ⟨{u_j} | {u_j}⟩^{1/2},
i.e. for the tree-level one-point functions of all scalar operators in the full SO(6) sector of the SO(5)-symmetric D3–D7 defect CFT, going beyond the chiral-primary (BPS) case for which a closed formula is already known.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For a fixed real number $M$ with $1<M<\infty$, let $S^{*}(M)$ denote the class of starlike univalent functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ that satisfy
$$f(0)=0,\qquad f'(0)=1,\qquad |f(z)|\le M\ \text{ for all }z\in\mathbb{D},$$
where, as usual, "starlike" means that $f(\mathbb{D})$ is a domain starlike with respect to the origin (equivalently, $\Re\bigl(zf'(z)/f(z)\bigr)>0$ on $\mathbb{D}$). Writing the Taylor expansion
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_{n}z^{n},\qquad z\in\mathbb{D},$$
determine the sharp value of
$$\sup\{\,|a_{3}|:f\in S^{*}(M)\,\}$$
for every $M$ in the range $e<M<5$.

Consider type IIB string theory on the AdS_5 × S^5 background with N units of self-dual five-form flux, dual to four-dimensional N=4 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory with gauge group SU(N) and 't Hooft coupling λ = g_YM^2 N. In the planar limit N → ∞ with λ fixed, four-point correlation functions of single-trace half-BPS superprimary operators (e.g., the stress-tensor multiplet superprimary O_2 of dimension 2) admit a strong-coupling expansion

⟨O O O O⟩ = G_sugra + λ^{-3/2} G_{R^4} + λ^{-5/2} G_{D^4 R^4} + λ^{-3} G_{D^6 R^4} + ⋯,

where G_sugra is the tree-level type IIB supergravity contribution on AdS_5 × S^5 and the subleading terms encode finite-string-tension (α'/L^2 ∼ λ^{-1/2}) higher-derivative stringy corrections.

Develop a systematic procedure to compute the 1/λ corrections G_{R^4}, G_{D^4 R^4}, G_{D^6 R^4}, … to four-point correlators of half-BPS operators at leading order in 1/N. Concretely: determine, in Mellin space or position space, the precise form of the holographic four-point amplitudes induced by the higher-derivative interactions (R^4 and its descendants) on AdS_5 × S^5, fix all coefficients consistently with superconformal Ward identities, crossing symmetry, and the flat-space α'-expansion of the type IIB four-graviton S-matrix, and identify the resulting anomalous dimensions and OPE coefficients of double-trace operators exchanged in the OPE.

Substantial progress has been made on incorporating 1/λ corrections to four-point correlators in AdS_5 × S^5. The leading R^4, D^4 R^4, and D^6 R^4 corrections to the stress-tensor multiplet four-point function have been computed in Mellin space using a combination of crossing symmetry, the flat-space limit, and supersymmetric localization constraints (Chester, Pufu, Yin and others). Let $\Sigma$ denote the class of univalent (i.e. holomorphic and injective) functions $f$ on the exterior disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|>1\}$ with the normalisation
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}b_n z^{-n}.$$
For a locally univalent holomorphic function $f$, let
$$S_f(z)=\left(\frac{f''(z)}{f'(z)}\right)'-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{f''(z)}{f'(z)}\right)^2$$
denote its Schwarzian derivative, and let $T_f(z)=f''(z)/f'(z)$ denote its pre-Schwarzian derivative. For a holomorphic function $g$ on $\{|z|>1\}$ define the hyperbolic sup-norms
$$\|g\|_{S}=\sup_{|z|>1}(|z|^2-1)^2|g(z)|,\qquad \|h\|_{T}=\sup_{|z|>1}(|z|^2-1)|h(z)|.$$
Suppose $f,f_1,f_2,\dots\in\Sigma$ and
$$\sup_{|z|>1}(|z|^2-1)^2\bigl|S_{f_n}(z)-S_f(z)\bigr|\longrightarrow 0\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.$$
Does it follow that
$$\sup_{|z|>1}(|z|^2-1)\left|\frac{f_n''(z)}{f_n'(z)}-\frac{f''(z)}{f'(z)}\right|\longrightarrow 0\quad\text{as }n\to\infty\,?$$
(It is known that the implication holds under the additional hypothesis that $f$ and the $f_n$ admit quasiconformal extensions to the whole plane.)

Consider a conformal field theory (CFT) defined on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^d$, obtained as the quotient of $\mathbb{R}^d$ (or $S^d$) by the antipodal involution $x \mapsto -x/|x|^2$. On such an unorientable background, one-point functions of bulk primary operators $\mathcal{O}_\Delta$ are not forced to vanish; conformal symmetry fixes them to take the form
$$\langle \mathcal{O}_\Delta(x)\rangle_{\mathbb{RP}^d} = \frac{A_{\mathcal{O}}}{(1+|x|^2)^{\Delta}},$$
and two-point functions of bulk primaries depend nontrivially on a cross-ratio invariant under the antipodal map. The "projective-space bootstrap" consists of constraints obtained by expanding such two-point functions in two distinct OPE channels (the bulk OPE and the image-point/crosscap channel) and demanding consistency, yielding equations that determine the coefficients $A_{\mathcal{O}}$ in terms of the bulk CFT data.

Problem. Extend this projective-space bootstrap program to strongly coupled or holographic conformal field theories — in particular to four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills theory placed on $\mathbb{RP}^4$, and to two-dimensional Liouville theory placed on $\mathbb{RP}^2$. Compute the crosscap one-point coefficients $A_{\mathcal{O}}$ (for example, for $\tfrac{1}{2}$-BPS operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM) and the corresponding two-point functions, and determine whether the resulting bootstrap predictions agree with the holographic computations obtained from the appropriate gravitational dual (e.g. type IIB supergravity on $AdS_5\times S^5$ with an orientifold-like involution dual to $\mathbb{RP}^4$).

Let S denote the class of functions f that are analytic and univalent in the open unit disk D = {z ∈ ℂ : |z| < 1} and normalized by f(0) = 0, f'(0) = 1. For 0 < R < 1, define
  I(R, f) = ∫₀^{2π} |f'(Re^{iθ})/f(Re^{iθ})|² dθ.
It is known that for every f ∈ S,
  I(R, f) = O((1/(1−R)) log(1/(1−R)))   as R → 1⁻,
and that the factor log(1/(1−R)) cannot be replaced by o(log(1/(1−R))) for the class S as a whole. For certain subclasses, such as the starlike functions and the functions of positive Hayman index (which include all support points of S), one has the improved estimate I(R, f) = O(1/(1−R)) as R → 1⁻.

Determine whether the improved estimate
  I(R, f) = O(1/(1−R))   as R → 1⁻
holds:
(a) for every extreme point f of the closed convex hull of S;
(b) for every close-to-convex function f ∈ S (where f is close-to-convex if there exists a convex univalent function g on D and a real number α with |α| < π/2 such that Re(e^{iα} f'(z)/g'(z)) > 0 for all z ∈ D).

Background and definitions. A quasi Riemann surface is a structure Q (in the sense of Friedan) that abstracts the properties of spaces of integral 0-currents on a Riemann surface: it carries a commutative associative addition with cancellation, a distinguished asymptotic cone of "effective" elements, a complete weak metric, and additional structure (integral j-currents for j = 0, 1, 2, 3) sufficient to define a Jacobian J(Q), namely the complex torus built from the homology in the middle dimension of Q.

For an ordinary 2-dimensional conformal space (Riemann surface) Σ, let D^int_0(Σ) denote the space of integral 0-currents on Σ (formal integer linear combinations of points, i.e. integral 0-cycles, with the topology and metric induced from currents). The space D^int_0(Σ) is a quasi Riemann surface, and its Jacobian coincides with the classical Jacobian variety of Σ.

Problem. Prove or disprove: every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic, as a quasi Riemann surface, to D^int_0(Σ) for some 2-dimensional conformal space Σ whose Jacobian J(Σ) is isomorphic to J(Q). If the statement holds, give an explicit construction of Σ from Q together with the isomorphism Q ≅ D^int_0(Σ).

Let $S$ denote the class of functions
$$f(z) = z + \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n z^n$$
that are analytic and univalent in the unit disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. Determine whether, for every $f \in S$,
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty} \bigl(|a_{n+1}| - |a_n|\bigr) \le 1.$$
It is known that this inequality holds when $f$ is an odd function in $S$, when $f$ is a function of maximal growth in $S$, and when $f$ is spiral-like. The question is whether the inequality holds for all $f \in S$.

Setup. Let M be a 2n-dimensional smooth manifold and let Q → M be a fiber bundle over M whose fiber at each point is a "quasi Riemann surface": a higher-dimensional generalization of a Riemann surface on which one can define a conformal-field-theory-like structure, namely an assignment to each point ξ of the total space Q of a field operator Φ(ξ) acting on a fixed Hilbert space, with operator product expansions and correlation functions analogous to those of a 2d CFT. A "defect" ξ ⊂ Q is a submanifold of Q; one says ξ is tiny (or pointlike) if its image in M under the bundle projection is concentrated near a single point of M, so that from the point of view of M the defect looks like an insertion at a point.

For each tiny defect ξ, define an ordinary local field on M by restricting/integrating the fields Φ(·) over ξ, producing an operator-valued distribution φ_ξ(x) on M (x ∈ M).

Question. Do the local fields {φ_ξ} obtained in this way, as ξ ranges over tiny defects, satisfy the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader axioms for a local quantum field theory on the 2n-dimensional manifold M, and if so, do they define genuinely new examples of local quantum field theories in 2n dimensions (i.e., theories not equivalent to previously known local QFTs in dimension 2n)?

Consider a compound nucleus formed at neutron-resonance energies. In the standard statistical model, each isolated resonance λ has partial gamma decay widths Γ_{λc} into many gamma decay channels c = 1, …, N (with N very large), and the total gamma decay width is Γ_λ = Σ_{c=1}^N Γ_{λc}. Under the usual hypothesis the partial widths Γ_{λc} are independent random variables, each distributed according to a Porter–Thomas distribution (i.e. Γ_{λc}/⟨Γ_{λc}⟩ is distributed as a chi-squared variable with one degree of freedom). Summing N such independent partial widths yields, for large N, a predicted distribution P_PT(Γ) of total gamma widths that is sharply peaked about its mean.

For the compound nucleus ^{96}Mo, the experimentally observed distribution of total gamma decay widths over many neutron resonances is found to be much broader than P_PT(Γ) and to be centered at substantially larger values of Γ than the statistical-model mean.

Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk. For $0 < k < 1$, let $S_k(\infty)$ denote the class of all functions $f$ that are analytic and univalent on $\mathbb{D}$, normalized by
$$f(z) = z + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 + \cdots,$$
and which admit a $k$-quasiconformal extension to the entire complex plane $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $f(\infty) = \infty$. (A homeomorphism $F$ of $\mathbb{C}$ is $k$-quasiconformal if it has locally integrable distributional derivatives satisfying $|\partial_{\bar z} F| \le k\, |\partial_z F|$ almost everywhere.)

For $0 < r < 1$, define the dilation $f_r : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ by
$$f_r(z) = \frac{f(rz)}{r}.$$

Prove or disprove: for every $f \in S_k(\infty)$ and every $r \in (0,1)$, the function $f_r$ also belongs to $S_k(\infty)$.
