Consider a future observatory that detects ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), with each detected air shower yielding an estimate of the primary particle's energy E and mass number A. Suppose the true differential flux dN/dE follows a steeply falling spectrum (with a suppression above roughly 4×10^19 eV), and that events with true energy below a threshold E_thresh are isotropically distributed on the celestial sphere, while events with true energy above E_thresh are clustered around a discrete set of astrophysical point sources. Reconstructed energies are subject to a Gaussian (or similar) event-by-event energy resolution σ_E/E, and reconstructed mass numbers are subject to a mass resolution σ_lnA. Heavier primaries are deflected by intervening magnetic fields by an angle proportional to their charge Z, broadening the apparent source spots.

Determine quantitative requirements on (i) the event-by-event energy resolution σ_E/E, (ii) the event-by-event mass resolution σ_lnA, and (iii) the total integrated exposure (in km² sr yr) such that, after applying energy and mass cuts above E_thresh, the resulting sample (a) contains less than a specified fraction f_bg of isotropic spillover events from the steeply falling sub-threshold population that pass cuts due to finite energy resolution, and (b) localizes individual point sources to within a specified angular scale despite magnetic deflections of heavier primaries, while retaining enough events above threshold to detect the sources at a prescribed statistical significance.

In particular, quantify how relaxing the energy resolution from 10% to 30% must be compensated by an increase in exposure given the steepness of the spectrum, and identify the minimum mass-resolution requirement that suppresses heavy-primary blurring of source images.

Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. For a family $\Gamma$ of curves in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the (conformal) $2$-modulus is
$$M(\Gamma)=\inf\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\rho(x)^2\,dx,$$
where the infimum is taken over all Borel measurable functions $\rho:\mathbb{R}^2\to[0,\infty]$ such that $\int_\gamma \rho\,ds\ge 1$ for every locally rectifiable curve $\gamma\in\Gamma$. For two disjoint sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $\Delta(A,B;\mathbb{R}^2)$ denote the family of all curves in $\mathbb{R}^2$ joining $A$ to $B$. Let $B^2(2)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|<2\}$ be the open disc of radius $2$, and write $\partial B^2(2)$ for its boundary circle.

Let $E\subset[0,1]$ be a compact subset of the real interval $[0,1]\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, viewed as lying on the positive real axis. Assume that $E$ has positive conformal $2$-capacity, in the sense that
$$M\bigl(\Delta(E,\partial B^2(2);\mathbb{R}^2)\bigr)>0.$$
Let $F=\mathbb{R}\setminus E$ (the complement of $E$ on the real line, regarded as a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$).

Question: Must one have
$$M\bigl(\Delta(E,F;\mathbb{R}^2)\bigr)=\infty\,?$$

Recent reviews and research papers (PDG 2024 cosmic-ray review, arXiv:2411.17881, A&A 2025 papers, and 2026 propagation studies) continue to debate whether the knee is due to Galactic source maximum energies (e.g. SNRs) or to propagation/escape effects, and whether the Galactic-to-extragalactic transition occurs at the second knee or at the ankle. No consensus has been reached, and competing ankle, dip, and mixed-composition models remain viable.

Let $n\ge 2$ and $\alpha>0$. For a Schwartz function $f\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $R>0$, define the Bochner–Riesz means $T_R^{\alpha}f$ by
$$\widehat{T_R^{\alpha}f}(\xi)=\Bigl(1-\frac{|\xi|^2}{R^2}\Bigr)_{+}^{\alpha}\hat f(\xi),\qquad \xi\in\mathbb{R}^n,$$
where $(t)_+=\max(t,0)$ and $\hat f$ denotes the Fourier transform of $f$. Extend $T_R^{\alpha}$ to $L^{2n/(n+1)}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in the natural way (when this is possible).

Question: Is it true that for every $\alpha>0$ and every $f\in L^{2n/(n+1)}(\mathbb{R}^n)$,
$$T_R^{\alpha}f(x)\longrightarrow f(x)\quad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\text{ as }R\to\infty?$$

(It is known that for $n=2$, if $\{R_j\}$ is a lacunary sequence tending to $\infty$, then $T_{R_j}^{\alpha}f\to f$ a.e. for all such $f$ and all $\alpha>0$. The question above asks for the full limit $R\to\infty$ in dimensions $n\ge 2$.)

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The almost-everywhere convergence problem for Bochner–Riesz means at the endpoint $L^{2n/(n+1)}$ is a long-standing problem in harmonic analysis. Recent work (e.g. Li–Wu 2024 on planar Bochner–Riesz means) has established a.e. convergence for $L^p$ in the optimal range $5/3\le p\le 2$ when $n=2$, which corresponds to (and surpasses) the endpoint $p=4/3=2n/(n+1)$. For $n\ge 3$ even the corresponding norm convergence problem at $L^{2n/(n+1)}$ remains open, and the full a.e. statement for all $\alpha>0$ and all $f\in L^{2n/(n+1)}$ is not known in general dimensions.

Consider the population of astrophysical objects proposed as candidate sources of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), i.e. cosmic rays with energies above roughly 10^18 eV. For a given source class, define t_emiss as the characteristic timescale over which an individual source emits cosmic rays, and t_prop as the mean cosmic-ray propagation timescale between sources reaching an observer at Earth (which depends on energy through diffusion in extragalactic and Galactic magnetic fields, on the magnetic-horizon scale, and on energy losses such as photopion production, photodisintegration and adiabatic losses). Call the source class "steady" at energy E if t_prop(E)/t_emiss ≫ 1, so that many sources contribute to the observed flux at all times, and "transient" at energy E if t_prop(E)/t_emiss ≲ 1, so that the observed flux is dominated by individual bursts.

(a) For each candidate UHECR source class (e.g. active galactic nuclei, radio galaxies, starburst galaxies, tidal disruption events, gamma-ray bursts, magnetars, binary neutron-star mergers), determine, as a function of cosmic-ray energy E and primary species, the energy ranges over which the observed UHECR flux from that class should be modeled as steady and the energy ranges over which it should be modeled as transient, taking into account magnetic-horizon suppression and energy losses. In particular, characterize source classes for which steady-state emission is achieved only on a finite energy interval, with transient behavior both below and above it.

(b) Specializing to gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), determine whether GRBs can accelerate cosmic rays with efficiency close to the Bohm limit, on what timescale this acceleration occurs during the prompt and/or afterglow phases, and whether—given these acceleration properties together with the constraints from (a)—GRBs constitute viable sources of the observed UHECR flux.

Determine the strength, spatial structure, and local-universe distribution of Galactic and extragalactic magnetic fields, and quantify their effect on the propagation of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (charged nuclei with energies above roughly 10^18 eV). Specifically:

1. Provide a model of the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) consisting of a regular (coherent) component B_reg(x) and a turbulent component B_turb(x) defined on the Milky Way volume, including disk and halo contributions, with field strengths typically of order microgauss.

2. Provide a model of the extragalactic magnetic field (EGMF) B_ext(x) on the cosmological volume out to ~100 Mpc, characterized by a coherence length λ_B and an rms strength B_rms, including its correlation with the large-scale structure of the local universe (filaments, voids, clusters).

3. For a charged particle of charge Ze, energy E, and rigidity R = E/Z propagating along a path from a source at distance D to Earth, compute:
   (a) the integrated deflection angle θ(E,Z,direction) induced by B_reg and the rms deflection induced by B_turb and B_ext,
   (b) the time delay Δt(E,Z,D) relative to rectilinear propagation at the speed of light,
   (c) the resulting smearing of arrival directions and its impact on the observed energy spectrum, mass composition, and large- and small-scale anisotropies.

4. Determine quantitatively under what combinations of (B_reg, B_turb, B_ext, λ_B, source distribution, composition) the deflections are small enough (e.g., ≲ a few degrees at the highest rigidities) for charged-particle astronomy — i.e., the unambiguous identification of individual ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray sources — to be feasible.

Let $W$ be a hyperbolic Riemann surface, and for each $\omega \in W$ let $G_\omega : W \setminus \{\omega\} \to (0,\infty)$ denote the Green's function of $W$ with pole at $\omega$, and let $G_\omega^*$ denote a (locally defined, multi-valued) harmonic conjugate of $G_\omega$. Let $\Gamma$ denote the fundamental group of $W$, with elements written as homotopy classes $[\gamma]$ of closed loops. Define the subgroup
$$\widetilde{\Gamma} = \{[\gamma] \in \Gamma : \text{for every } \omega \in W, \text{ the period of } G_\omega^* \text{ along any representative of } [\gamma] \text{ is an integer multiple of } 2\pi\}.$$
Then $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is a normal subgroup of $\Gamma$ containing the commutator subgroup $[\Gamma,\Gamma]$, so that
$$[\Gamma,\Gamma] \trianglelefteq \widetilde{\Gamma} \trianglelefteq \Gamma.$$
Conjecture: If $[\Gamma,\Gamma] \neq \widetilde{\Gamma}$, then $W$ is conformally equivalent to $V \setminus A$, where $V$ is a hyperbolic Riemann surface and $A \subset V$ is a non-empty relatively closed subset of zero logarithmic capacity. Decide whether this conjecture holds in general. (It is known to be true in the special case $\widetilde{\Gamma} = \Gamma$ with $V$ the unit disc, and it is known to fail when $[\Gamma,\Gamma] = \widetilde{\Gamma}$.)

representations.normalized:
Extensive air showers are cascades of secondary particles produced when an ultrahigh-energy cosmic ray (a primary nucleus or proton with laboratory energy above roughly 10^17 eV) interacts with nuclei in the Earth's atmosphere. The development of such a shower is simulated using hadronic-interaction generators (Monte Carlo models such as those tuned with accelerator data up to LHC energies) which predict, in particular, the number N_μ of muons reaching ground level as a function of primary energy E and primary mass A.

Multiple independent experiments measuring N_μ at primary energies E ≳ 10^17 eV consistently observe a muon content that exceeds the prediction of every contemporary hadronic-interaction model by approximately 30%–60%, depending on the experiment, the energy, and the reference model used. This systematic excess of measured ground-level muons over simulated muons is referred to as the muon puzzle.

Problem. Determine the physical origin of the muon excess in ultrahigh-energy extensive air showers. Specifically:

(a) Construct a quantitatively consistent modification of Standard Model hadronic interactions — for example, changes to the energy fraction carried by neutral pions, baryon-antibaryon pair production, strangeness enhancement, collective effects in pion–air or proton–air collisions, or other soft/forward QCD phenomena — that, when propagated through the full shower cascade, simultaneously reproduces the observed 30%–60% muon excess at ground level and remains consistent with all measured longitudinal shower observables (notably the depth of shower maximum X_max and its fluctuations) and with collider data on hadronic interactions.

(b) Decide whether such a Standard-Model-based modification is sufficient, or whether the observed muon excess necessarily requires a contribution from physics beyond the Standard Model.

A complete solution should specify the assumed hadronic-interaction modification (or new-physics mechanism), demonstrate via cascade simulation that the resulting N_μ matches measurements within experimental uncertainties across the relevant energy range, and verify compatibility with X_max measurements and accelerator constraints.

As of 2024–2025, the muon puzzle in ultrahigh-energy extensive air showers remains unresolved. Several candidate explanations have been proposed (collective/core-corona hadronization, gluon condensation, strangeness enhancement, and even Lorentz-invariance violation), but none has been confirmed as the definitive cause. In the study of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (with primary energies extending up to center-of-mass nucleon-nucleon energies of order √s ∼ 400 TeV), the inference of the mass composition of primary cosmic rays from extensive air-shower observables (such as the depth of shower maximum X_max and its fluctuations, muon content, and longitudinal profile) is limited by systematic uncertainties in hadronic-interaction Monte Carlo models. These models must extrapolate accelerator data to (i) center-of-mass energies far beyond those accessible at current colliders, (ii) forward phase-space regions (large pseudorapidity / large Feynman-x) not covered by central detectors, and (iii) projectile–target combinations not measured experimentally.

Identify and specify a concrete program of accelerator (collider), fixed-target, forward-physics, and air-shower measurements that would, if carried out, reduce these systematic uncertainties to a level sufficient for unambiguous mass-composition inference at ultrahigh energies. In particular, determine the required measurements (energy ranges, kinematic coverage, and observables — total and inelastic cross sections together with leading-secondary momentum and multiplicity distributions) for each of the following interaction channels:

1. pion–proton (π–p),
2. kaon–proton (K–p),
3. pion–light-nuclei (π–A, with A a light nucleus such as carbon, nitrogen, or oxygen),
4. kaon–light-nuclei (K–A),
5. proton–oxygen (p–O), including the feasibility and benefit of running such collisions at the LHC,
6. forward secondary-particle production (production spectra of π^±, K^±, K_L, neutrons, protons, and Λ at large Feynman-x in proton–proton, proton–nucleus, and pion–nucleus collisions).

For each channel, state the kinematic coverage (√s, x_F or pseudorapidity, p_T) needed, and quantify how the resulting reduction in uncertainty of the predicted air-shower observables would translate into improved discrimination among primary mass groups (proton, helium, CNO, iron) at energies E ≳ 10^18 eV.

representations.normalized:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ be a strictly pseudoconvex domain (a bounded domain admitting a $C^2$ defining function $\rho$ with $\Omega = \{\rho < 0\}$, $d\rho \neq 0$ on $\partial\Omega$, and the Levi form of $\rho$ strictly positive on the complex tangent space at every boundary point). Let $f$ be a holomorphic function on $\Omega$, not identically zero, and let $V = \{z \in \Omega : f(z) = 0\}$ be its zero set, regarded as a (pure $1$-dimensional) analytic subvariety of $\Omega$. Assume that $V$ has finite $2$-dimensional Hausdorff area inside $\Omega$, i.e.
$$\mathrm{Area}(V) = \int_{V_{\mathrm{reg}}} dA < \infty,$$
where $dA$ is the induced Euclidean area measure on the regular part of $V$.

Question: Must there exist a bounded holomorphic function $g \in H^\infty(\Omega)$, not identically zero, whose zero set (with multiplicities) equals $V$?

It is known that the answer is affirmative when $\Omega$ is the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^2$, and that the corresponding statement fails in strictly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^n$ for $n > 2$. Decide whether the affirmative answer extends to all strictly pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$.

representations.normalized:
Setting. Consider ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), i.e. primary particles (protons or atomic nuclei) with energies E ≳ 10^18 eV that propagate through cosmic photon backgrounds (with target photon energies ε ≪ 1 GeV) and subsequently initiate extensive air showers in the Earth's atmosphere upon interacting with atmospheric nuclei (target mass m_N ≈ 1 GeV). Standard predictions for (i) the cosmic-ray spectrum after propagation, (ii) interaction thresholds (e.g. the GZK threshold for pγ → Δ → Nπ), (iii) the average shower depth of maximum X_max, and (iv) the muon number N_μ at ground level are computed assuming exact Lorentz invariance and conventional hadronic interaction models extrapolated from accelerator energies.

Allow now for the possibility of new high-energy physics, in particular Lorentz-invariance violation (LIV) parametrized by modified dispersion relations of the form
   E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4 + ξ_n p^2 c^2 (pc/E_Pl)^n,  n ≥ 0,
for each particle species, where E_Pl is the Planck energy and ξ_n is a species- and order-dependent coefficient. Such modifications can: (a) shift or remove pion-photoproduction and pair-production thresholds in propagation; (b) open vacuum Cherenkov channels (e.g. p → p γ or e → e γ in vacuum) leading to rapid energy losses above a critical energy; (c) alter secondary-particle spectra and decay kinematics in air showers, e.g. by suppressing the fraction f_{π^0} of energy carried by neutral pions, thereby increasing the muon number N_μ; and (d) introduce sharp energy thresholds above which observables change abruptly.

Problem. Determine whether UHECR propagation in cosmic photon backgrounds and the development of UHECR-induced air showers can probe Lorentz-invariance violation (or other new physics beyond the Standard Model accessible only at large Lorentz boosts and/or center-of-mass energies √s ≳ 100 TeV), and identify a set of observable signatures—quantitatively expressed in terms of the UHECR energy spectrum, mass-composition indicators (X_max and its fluctuations σ(X_max)), muon number N_μ(E) and its energy dependence dN_μ/dE, and arrival-direction distributions—that would unambiguously distinguish genuine LIV or new-physics effects from shortcomings of conventional hadronic interaction models. In particular:

(1) Derive the constraints on the LIV coefficients {ξ_n} for protons, pions, photons, and electrons that follow from the observed continuation of the UHECR flux and from the absence of anomalous vacuum-Cherenkov cutoffs.
(2) Show whether a decrease in f_{π^0} induced by new physics can reproduce the observed excess of N_μ over hadronic-model predictions while remaining consistent with measured X_max distributions, assuming neutral pions still decay quasi-instantaneously.
(3) Identify whether a sharp, threshold-like increase of N_μ over a narrow primary-energy window is predicted by any consistent LIV or new-physics scenario, and specify the experimental sensitivity required to detect it.

Recent (2023–2025) literature continues to investigate this question without definitive resolution. New bounds on isotropic dim-5 Lorentz violation have been derived from the non-observation of vacuum Cherenkov radiation in UHE air showers and LHAASO Crab observations, while 2024–2025 work explores whether small LIV could explain the muon puzzle by suppressing the electromagnetic component of showers. No conclusive observation of LIV or definitive disentanglement from hadronic-model uncertainties has been reported, so the broader question remains open.

representations.normalized:
Let $A$ be an associative algebra over $\mathbb{R}$ with identity $1$ and a countable basis, and let $V \subseteq A$ be a finite-dimensional real subspace with basis $\{e_1,\dots,e_k\}$. Define the Dirac-type differential operator
$$D = \sum_{j=1}^{k} e_j \frac{\partial}{\partial x_j}$$
acting on differentiable functions $f : U \to A$ defined on open sets $U \subseteq V$ (with coordinates $x = \sum_j x_j e_j$). A function $f : U \to A$ is called left analytic if $Df(x) = 0$ for every $x \in U$.

It is known that there exists a generalized Cauchy integral formula
$$f(x_0) = \int_{\partial M} G(x, x_0) \sum_{j=1}^{k} (-1)^j e_j \, d\hat x_j \, f(x),$$
valid for every left analytic $f$, where $M \subset U$ is an arbitrary compact real $n$-dimensional manifold (with boundary), $x_0 \in \mathring{M}$, $d\hat x_j = dx_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge \widehat{dx_j} \wedge \cdots \wedge dx_k$, and $G(x,x_0)$ is a real-analytic $A$-valued kernel; this holds if and only if there exist elements $\{p_1,\dots,p_k\} \subseteq A$ satisfying
$$p_j e_l + p_l e_j = 2\delta_{jl} \quad (1 \le j,l \le k).$$

(a) Does the same representation formula remain valid when the kernel $G(x,x_0)$ is only assumed to be of class $C^1$ rather than real-analytic?

(b) Formulate and establish the analogue of this generalized Cauchy integral formula in the case where the algebra $A$ is allowed to be non-associative.

Consider an isotropic diffuse flux of ultra-high-energy (EeV-scale) neutrinos consisting of (i) a cosmogenic component produced by interactions of ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray protons and nuclei with the cosmic microwave and infrared backgrounds during propagation over cosmological (gigaparsec) baselines, and (ii) a possible point-source component from identified astrophysical accelerators. For such neutrinos, the observable quantities at Earth are: the energy spectrum dN/dE, the distribution of arrival directions on the sky, and the flavor composition (f_e : f_μ : f_τ) of the incoming flux after oscillations.

Assume that beyond-Standard-Model effects modify neutrino propagation and/or interactions in such a way that the deviation of an observable from its Standard-Model expectation can be parametrized in the schematic form
   Δ𝒪(E, L) ≃ κ_n · E^n · L,
where E is the neutrino energy, L the propagation baseline, n ∈ ℤ a model-dependent integer (e.g. n = −1 for neutrino decay, n = 0 for equivalence-principle violation, n ≥ 1 for Lorentz-invariance-violating dispersion relations), and κ_n a model-dependent coupling. Likewise, the neutrino–nucleon cross section σ_{νN}(E) at center-of-mass energies above those reached at terrestrial colliders may deviate from QCD extrapolations.

Develop a quantitative statistical framework that, given an assumed exposure of a future EeV neutrino observatory and assumed astrophysical priors on (a) the source spectral index and maximum energy, (b) the redshift evolution of source density, (c) the cosmic-ray mass composition feeding cosmogenic production, and (d) the flavor composition at the source, determines:

1. The minimum number of detected EeV cosmogenic and/or point-source neutrino events required to measure σ_{νN}(E) at E ∼ 10^{18} eV with a prescribed relative precision, and to distinguish Standard-Model QCD predictions from new high-energy strong-dynamics scenarios.

2. The sensitivity reach (i.e. smallest |κ_n| that can be excluded at a given confidence level) for each integer n ∈ {−1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4} from the joint analysis of spectrum, arrival-direction distribution, and flavor ratios.

3. A procedure to disentangle a putative new-physics signal in any of these observables from astrophysical degeneracies in spectral shape, source evolution, sky distribution, and flavor identification, including a quantitative criterion (e.g. an information-theoretic or likelihood-ratio criterion) under which fundamental and astrophysical effects become separable.

Provide explicit predicted bounds, identify the observable channel (spectrum, arrival directions, or flavor composition) that yields the strongest constraint for each n, and characterize the irreducible astrophysical uncertainty floor below which no improvement in detector exposure can refine the test.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

EeV-energy cosmogenic neutrinos have not yet been detected; experiments such as IceCube-Gen2, GRAND, POEMMA, RNO-G, and the Pierre Auger Observatory continue to push upper limits but no confirmed cosmogenic neutrino flux exists as of 2026. Consequently the proposed program of using EeV neutrinos to test cross sections, flavor composition, Lorentz violation, neutrino decay, and equivalence-principle violation over gigaparsec baselines remains an open research direction, with only forecast/sensitivity studies available rather than measurements.

Background. A superpartition is a pair $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$, where $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1,\dots,\Lambda_m)$ is a strictly decreasing sequence of non-negative integers and $\Lambda^s=(\Lambda_{m+1},\Lambda_{m+2},\dots)$ is a partition (weakly decreasing sequence of non-negative integers). Superpartitions index a basis of the ring of symmetric functions in superspace, which is the ring of polynomials in commuting variables $x_1,x_2,\dots$ and anticommuting variables $\theta_1,\theta_2,\dots$ that are invariant under the diagonal action of the symmetric group permuting simultaneously the $x_i$ and the $\theta_i$.

For each superpartition $\Lambda$, let $m_\Lambda$ denote the monomial symmetric function in superspace indexed by $\Lambda$. Equip the set of superpartitions of a fixed bidegree with the dominance order $\le$. The Jack symmetric functions in superspace $P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda$ (depending on a parameter $\alpha$) are the unique basis characterized by:
(i) $P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda = m_\Lambda + \sum_{\Omega<\Lambda} c_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\, m_\Omega$,
(ii) orthogonality with respect to the natural one-parameter scalar product on superspace.

Define the integral form of the Jack superpolynomial by
$$J^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda(x;\theta) := v_\Lambda(\alpha)\, P^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda(x;\theta),$$
where $v_\Lambda(\alpha)$ is the natural normalization factor (the product over the cells of the diagram of $\Lambda$ of the appropriate hook-type linear factors in $\alpha$) that generalizes the classical normalization for Jack polynomials. Expanding in the monomial basis,
$$J^{(\alpha)}_\Lambda = \sum_{\Omega \le \Lambda} v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)\, m_\Omega,$$
with $v_{\Lambda\Lambda}(\alpha) = v_\Lambda(\alpha)$.

Question. Is it true that for every pair of superpartitions $\Omega \le \Lambda$, the coefficient $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha)$ is a polynomial in $\alpha$ with integer coefficients, i.e., $v_{\Lambda\Omega}(\alpha) \in \mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$?

Let $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n$ with $n \geq 2$ be a domain of holomorphy, that is, an open connected set for which there exists a holomorphic function on $\Omega$ that cannot be holomorphically continued to any strictly larger connected open set. A holomorphic function $p : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}$ is called complex harmonic if it satisfies the complex Laplace equation
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n} \frac{\partial^2 p}{\partial z_j^2}(z) = 0 \quad \text{for all } z \in \Omega.$$
Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $\Omega$ guaranteeing the existence of a holomorphic function $p : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}$ which is complex harmonic in the above sense and which cannot be holomorphically extended across any boundary point of $\Omega$ (i.e. $\Omega$ is the natural domain of existence of $p$).

Work over the field $\mathbb{C}$. Let $N\ge 1$ and consider the superspace algebra in $N$ commuting variables $x_1,\dots,x_N$ and $N$ anticommuting (Grassmann) variables $	heta_1,\dots,	heta_N$, where $	heta_i	heta_j=-	heta_j	heta_i$ and $	heta_i^2=0$. The symmetric group $S_N$ acts diagonally by simultaneous permutation of $(x_i,	heta_i)$, and a superpolynomial $f(x,	heta)$ is called symmetric if it is invariant under this diagonal action. Denote the algebra of symmetric superpolynomials by $\mathcal{S}_N$.

A superpartition $\Lambda$ with exactly $N$ parts is a pair $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ where $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1^a>\Lambda_2^a>\cdots>\Lambda_m^a\ge 0)$ is a strict partition (the antisymmetric/fermionic part) and $\Lambda^s=(\Lambda^s_1\ge\Lambda^s_2\ge\cdots\ge 0)$ is a partition (the symmetric/bosonic part), with the total number of (allowed-zero) parts equal to $N$. Associated to $\Lambda$ are two ordinary partitions, $\Lambda^*$ obtained by reordering the concatenation $(\Lambda^a,\Lambda^s)$ into a weakly decreasing sequence, and $\Lambda^\circledast$ obtained from $\Lambda^*$ by adding $1$ to each entry of $\Lambda^a$ before reordering. For fixed integers $k\ge 1$ and $r\ge 2$, $\Lambda$ is called $(k,r,N)$-admissible if
$$\Lambda_i^\circledast - \Lambda_{i+k}^* \ge r \qquad \text{for all } 1\le i\le N-k.$$

For a parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^\times$, let $P_\Lambda^{(\alpha)}(x_1,\dots,x_N,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N)$ denote the Jack superpolynomial indexed by the superpartition $\Lambda$ (the unique simultaneous eigenfunction of the supersymmetric Calogero–Moser–Sutherland Hamiltonians with parameter $\alpha$ that is upper-triangular, in the dominance ordering on superpartitions, with respect to the basis of monomial symmetric superpolynomials, with leading monomial indexed by $\Lambda$).

Fix $k\ge 1$ and $N\ge k+1$, and set $\alpha_{k,2}=-(k+1)$. Let $F_N^{(k)}\subseteq\mathcal{S}_N$ be the ideal consisting of all symmetric superpolynomials $f(x,\theta)$ that vanish whenever $x_1=x_2=\cdots=x_{k+1}$.

Prove or disprove: the family
$$\bigl\{\, P_\Lambda^{(\alpha_{k,2})}(x_1,\dots,x_N,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N) \;:\; \Lambda \text{ is } (k,2,N)\text{-admissible}\,\bigr\}$$
forms a $\mathbb{C}$-vector space basis of $F_N^{(k)}$.

Let $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex compact symmetric body normalised so that its Lebesgue measure equals $1$. Define the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function with respect to $B$ by
$$M f(x) = \sup_{t>0} \frac{1}{t^n}\int_{tB} |f(x+y)|\, dy,$$
and its dyadic analogue by
$$\widetilde{M} f(x) = \sup_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} \frac{1}{2^{kn}}\int_{2^k B} |f(x+y)|\, dy.$$

Answer the following questions.

(a) Suppose $B$ is the Euclidean unit ball (suitably normalised). Does there exist a finite constant $C$, independent of the dimension $n$, such that for every $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and every $\lambda>0$,
$$\bigl|\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : \widetilde{M} f(x) > \lambda\}\bigr| \le \frac{C}{\lambda}\,\|f\|_1\;?$$

(b) Under the same hypothesis on $B$, does the analogous weak-type $(1,1)$ inequality
$$\bigl|\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : M f(x) > \lambda\}\bigr| \le \frac{C}{\lambda}\,\|f\|_1$$
hold with a constant $C$ independent of $n$?

(c) For $n=1$ (so $B$ is a centered interval), prove that the best constant $C$ in the weak-type $(1,1)$ inequality
$$\bigl|\{x\in\mathbb{R} : M f(x) > \lambda\}\bigr| \le \frac{C}{\lambda}\,\|f\|_1$$
equals $\tfrac{3}{2}$.

(d) For $1 < p \le \tfrac{3}{2}$, can the best constant $C_p$ in
$$\|M f\|_p \le C_p \|f\|_p$$
be chosen independent of $n$ and of the convex symmetric body $B$? In particular, can it be chosen independent of $n$ when $B = [-\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2}]^n$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Part (a) (dimension-free weak-(1,1) bound for the dyadic maximal function over Euclidean balls) is known to hold (Stein–Strömberg type results). Part (c) — the conjecture that the best weak-(1,1) constant on $\mathbb{R}$ equals $3/2$ — was disproved by Aldaz (1998), who showed the constant is strictly greater than $3/2$; the exact value was further studied by Melas. For cubes, Aldaz (Annals 2011) proved that the weak-type $(1,1)$ constants grow to infinity with the dimension, settling the cube version of (b)/(d) negatively for weak type. The strong-type dimension-free question for general convex symmetric bodies (parts (b) and (d) for $p>1$) remains a long-standing open problem; only partial progress is known (Bourgain, Carbery, Müller, and more recent work).

Setup. Work in the algebra of symmetric polynomials in $N$ commuting variables $x_1,\dots,x_N$ and $N$ anticommuting (Grassmann) variables $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N$, invariant under the diagonal action of the symmetric group $S_N$. A superpartition $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ is a pair consisting of a strictly decreasing partition $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1>\Lambda_2>\cdots>\Lambda_m\ge 0)$ (the fermionic part, of fermionic degree $m$) and a partition $\Lambda^s$ (the bosonic part). For positive integers $k,r$ with $\gcd(k+1,r-1)$ appropriate, a superpartition $\Lambda$ of length $\ell(\Lambda)\le N$ is called $(k,r,N)$-admissible if it satisfies the staircase-style separation condition
$$\Lambda_i-\Lambda_{i+k}\ge r\quad\text{whenever the corresponding parts are bosonic, with the analogous strict version for fermionic parts},$$
together with a tail condition on $\Lambda_{N-k+1},\dots,\Lambda_N$.

Jack superpolynomials $\mathcal{P}^{(\alpha)}_{\Lambda}(x;\theta)$ are the unique eigenfunctions of the supersymmetric trigonometric Calogero–Moser–Sutherland Hamiltonian which decompose triangularly (with respect to a fixed dominance order on superpartitions) on the monomial superfunctions $m_\Lambda$, normalized so that the coefficient of $m_\Lambda$ equals $1$. At the special value
$$\alpha=-\frac{k+1}{r-1},$$
let $I^{(k,r)}_N$ denote the linear span of the Jack superpolynomials $\mathcal{P}^{(\alpha)}_{\Lambda}$ indexed by $(k,r,N)$-admissible superpartitions $\Lambda$.

For $r=2$ and $k=2p-1$ (so that $\alpha=-2p/(2p-2)$ in the relevant minimal-model parametrization), consider the $N=1$ superconformal minimal model $M(2,4p)$ in the Neveu–Schwarz sector, with central charge $c=\tfrac{3}{2}\bigl(1-\tfrac{2(4p-2)^2}{8p}\bigr)$ and irreducible NS highest-weight modules $L_{r',s'}$ for the admissible Kac labels.

Problem. Establish a precise bijection between:
(i) the $(k,r,N)$-admissible superpartitions described above, and
(ii) a basis of states (e.g.\ a quasi-particle / Feigin–Stoyanovsky type basis) of the irreducible Neveu–Schwarz modules of the minimal superconformal model $M(2,4p)$,
in such a way that the corresponding admissible Jack superpolynomials $\mathcal{P}^{(\alpha)}_{\Lambda}$ at $\alpha=-(k+1)/(r-1)$ realize, in the large-$N$ limit, the basis vectors of these modules. In particular, prove that $I^{(k,r)}_N$ carries a module structure for (a suitable subalgebra of) the centerless Neveu–Schwarz (super-Virasoro) algebra and identify the resulting module with the appropriate direct sum of irreducible NS modules of $M(2,4p)$.

The connection between admissible superpartitions, Jack superpolynomials at negative rational parameter, and the Neveu–Schwarz sector of N=1 superconformal minimal models has been substantially developed: Blondeau-Fournier, Mathieu, Ridout and Wood ("Superconformal minimal models and admissible Jack polynomials", 2016) prove rationality and classify NS and Ramond modules in this framework, and earlier works construct super-Virasoro singular vectors via Jack superpolynomials. Work in the ring of symmetric functions in superspace, generated over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$ by the bosonic power sums $p_r$ ($r\ge 1$) and the fermionic power sums $\tilde p_r$ ($r\ge 0$), where superpartitions $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ have an antisymmetric part $\Lambda^a$ (a strict partition, possibly containing $0$) and a symmetric part $\Lambda^s$ (an ordinary partition). For a superpartition $\Lambda$ with $m$ fermionic parts, write $p_\Lambda=\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_1}\cdots\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_m}\,p_{\Lambda^s_1}p_{\Lambda^s_2}\cdots$, and let $z_\Lambda$ and $\omega_\Lambda=\pm1$ be the standard combinatorial constants associated to $\Lambda$ in superspace. The conjugate superpartition is denoted $\Lambda'$, with antisymmetric part $\Lambda'^a$.

Define the $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$-algebra automorphism $\hat\rho_{q,t}$ of this ring by
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}\,\frac{1-q^r}{1-t^r}\,p_r\qquad(r\ge 1),$$
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(\tilde p_r)=\sum_{\Lambda\vdash (r\mid 1)} z_\Lambda^{-1}\,\omega_\Lambda\,\prod_i\bigl(1-q^{\Lambda^s_i}\bigr)\,p_\Lambda\qquad(r\ge 0),$$
where the sum is over superpartitions of bidegree $(r\mid 1)$ (total bosonic degree $r$ with exactly one fermionic part).

Let $P_\Lambda(q,t)$ and $Q_\Lambda(q,t)$ denote the two normalizations of the Macdonald superpolynomials indexed by superpartitions $\Lambda$.

Prove or disprove: for every superpartition $\Lambda$,
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}\bigl(P_\Lambda(q,t)\bigr)=t^{|\Lambda'^a|}\,Q_{\Lambda'}(t,q).$$

For a superpartition $\Lambda$ with $m$ fermionic parts, write $p_\Lambda=\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_1}\cdots\tilde p_{\Lambda^a_m}\,p_{\Lambda^s_1}p_{\Lambda^s_2}\cdots$, and let $z_\Lambda$ and $\omega_\Lambda=\pm1$ be the standard combinatorial constants associated to $\Lambda$ in superspace. The conjugate superpartition is denoted $\Lambda'$, with antisymmetric part $\Lambda'^a$.

Define the $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$-algebra automorphism $\hat\rho_{q,t}$ of this ring by
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}\,\frac{1-q^r}{1-t^r}\,p_r\qquad(r\ge 1),$$
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}(\tilde p_r)=\sum_{\Lambda\vdash (r\mid 1)} z_\Lambda^{-1}\,\omega_\Lambda\,\prod_i\bigl(1-q^{\Lambda^s_i}\bigr)\,p_\Lambda\qquad(r\ge 0),$$
where the sum is over superpartitions of bidegree $(r\mid 1)$ (total bosonic degree $r$ with exactly one fermionic part).

Let $P_\Lambda(q,t)$ and $Q_\Lambda(q,t)$ denote the two normalizations of the Macdonald superpolynomials indexed by superpartitions $\Lambda$.

Prove or disprove: for every superpartition $\Lambda$,
$$\hat\rho_{q,t}\bigl(P_\Lambda(q,t)\bigr)=t^{|\Lambda'^a|}\,Q_{\Lambda'}(t,q).$$

For a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{C}$, let $\alpha(K)$ denote the continuous analytic capacity of $K$, defined by
$$\alpha(K)=\sup\{|f'(\infty)|:f\in C(\mathbb{C}),\ f\ \text{is holomorphic on}\ \mathbb{C}\setminus K,\ |f|\le 1\ \text{on}\ \mathbb{C}\},$$
where $f'(\infty)=\lim_{z\to\infty} z(f(z)-f(\infty))$.

Prove or disprove: if $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ is compact and $\alpha(K)=0$, then for every compact set $E\subset\mathbb{C}$,
$$\alpha(E\setminus K)=\alpha(E).$$

A case of particular interest is when $K$ is a $C^1$-arc. (The corresponding statement is known when $K$ is a $C^{1+\varepsilon}$-arc for some $\varepsilon>0$.)

Work in superspace: the polynomial ring in commuting variables x_1,...,x_N together with anticommuting variables θ_1,...,θ_N (θ_iθ_j = -θ_jθ_i). A superpartition Λ = (Λ^a; Λ^s) of fermionic degree m and total degree n consists of a strictly decreasing partition Λ^a = (Λ_1,...,Λ_m) with Λ_i ≥ 0 and a usual partition Λ^s, with |Λ^a|+|Λ^s| = n. To Λ associate the composition Λ^* obtained by reading the parts of Λ^a then Λ^s, and let w_Λ be the unique permutation of minimal length such that w_Λ·Λ^* gives the parts arranged in the canonical labeling associated with Λ.

For parameters q,t, let P_Λ = P_Λ(x_1,...,x_N; θ_1,...,θ_N; q,t) denote the Macdonald symmetric superpolynomial indexed by Λ (the unique element, up to normalization, characterized by triangularity with respect to dominance on superpartitions and orthogonality with respect to the Macdonald scalar product in superspace).

Define the specialization u_Λ on the variables x_1,...,x_N by
   x_{w_Λ(i)} = q^{-Λ^*_i} t^{i-1},   i = 1,2,...,N,
and the normalization
   ~P_Λ := P_Λ / P_Λ(u_{(δ^m;)}),
where (δ^m;) denotes the staircase superpartition (m-1, m-2, ..., 1, 0; ) of fermionic degree m. With this normalization ~P_Λ evaluated at the standard point ε_{q,t} equals 1.

Question: For every pair of superpartitions Λ, Ω of the same total degree (and the same fermionic degree), does the evaluation symmetry
   ~P_Λ(u_Ω) = ~P_Ω(u_Λ)
hold identically as a rational function of q and t?

Work in the algebra A of symmetric functions in superspace over Q(q,t), generated by the commuting power sums p_r (r ≥ 1) and the anticommuting power sums ~p_s (s ≥ 0). Symmetric functions in superspace are indexed by superpartitions Λ = (Λ^a; Λ^s), where Λ^a is a strict partition of distinct nonnegative parts (the "anticommuting" sector) and Λ^s is an ordinary partition.

Let {P_Λ(q,t)}_Λ denote the Macdonald superpolynomials, the basis of A characterized by suitable triangularity and orthogonality with respect to the (q,t)-deformed scalar product on superspace. Let h_Λ^{lo}(q,t) be the "lower-hook" normalization factor, and define the integral form
   J_Λ(q,t) = h_Λ^{lo}(q,t) · P_Λ(q,t).

Let φ_t : A → A be the Q(q,t)-algebra automorphism determined by
   φ_t(p_r) = (1 − t^r)^{−1} p_r  for all r ≥ 1,   φ_t(~p_s) = ~p_s  for all s ≥ 0,
and define the modified Macdonald superpolynomial
   H_Λ(q,t) = φ_t( J_Λ(q,t) ).

Let {s_Ω}_Ω denote the Schur superpolynomial basis of A. Expand
   H_Λ(q,t) = Σ_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) · s_Ω,
defining the (q,t)-Kostka coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) in superspace.

Prove or disprove: for every pair of superpartitions Λ and Ω, the coefficient K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) lies in N[q,t], i.e. is a polynomial in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients.

The (q,t)-Kostka positivity conjecture for Macdonald superpolynomials was formulated by Blondeau-Fournier, Desrosiers, Lapointe, and Mathieu (2012), generalizing Macdonald's classical positivity (proved by Haiman, 2001) to superspace. Searches for proofs through 2024–2025 turn up only restatements of the conjecture, partial/related results (e.g. nonnegativity of stable-limit double Macdonald (q,t)-Kostka coefficients and Schur-positivity in special cases), but no proof of the full superspace positivity statement. The conjecture appears to remain open.

[{"title": "Macdonald polynomials in superspace: conjectural definition and positivity conjectures", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.5188", "snippet": "Presents a conjectural definition of Macdonald polynomials in superspace and formulates positivity conjectures for the (q,t)-Kostka coefficients.", "claim": "Original formulation of the superspace (q,t)-Kostka positivity conjecture."}, {"title": "Double Macdonald polynomials as the stable limit of Macdonald superpolynomials", "url": "https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10801-014-0541-6", "snippet": "Validates conjectures in the stable regime and shows certain (q,t)-Kostka coefficients are q,t-analogs of dimensions of irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group.", "claim": "Partial/stable-limit results, but the full superspace positivity remains conjectural."}, {"title": "Hilbert schemes, polygraphs and the Macdonald positivity conjecture (Haiman)", "url": "https://www.ams.org/journals/jams/2001-14-04/S0894-0347-01-00373-3/viewer/", "snippet": "Haiman's proof of the classical Macdonald positivity conjecture via the n! theorem.", "claim": "Classical (non-super) analog is solved; the superspace version is the conjectural extension."}]

Does there exist a sequence $\{z_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ of pairwise distinct complex numbers satisfying both
\[ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{|z_n|} < \infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{z - z_n} \neq 0 \quad \text{for every } z \in \mathbb{C}\setminus\{z_n : n\geq 1\}? \]
(The first condition guarantees absolute convergence of the second series for $z \notin \{z_n\}$.) Equivalently, does there exist such a configuration of points in the plane so that the gradient field of the logarithmic potential $\sum_n \log|z - z_n|$ has no equilibrium (zero) point in $\mathbb{C}$? The analogous question may also be posed in $\mathbb{R}^N$ for $N \geq 3$ with the corresponding Newtonian potential.

Background. Symmetric functions in superspace are polynomials in two sets of variables: commuting variables x_1, x_2, ... and anticommuting (Grassmann) variables θ_1, θ_2, ... (with θ_i θ_j = -θ_j θ_i, in particular θ_i^2 = 0), which are simultaneously invariant under the diagonal action of the symmetric group permuting the indices i. A superpartition Λ = (Λ^a; Λ^s) consists of a strict partition Λ^a (the "fermionic" part, indexing the θ-variables) together with an ordinary partition Λ^s (the "bosonic" part).

In the algebra of symmetric functions in superspace there are two natural one-parameter-free families of Schur-like bases indexed by superpartitions, denoted {s_Λ} and {s̄_Λ}. Define the structure constants c^Λ_{ΓΩ} and c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} by the multiplication rules
   s_Γ · s_Ω = Σ_Λ c^Λ_{ΓΩ} s_Λ,    s̄_Γ · s̄_Ω = Σ_Λ c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} s̄_Λ,
where the sums run over superpartitions Λ. The skew Schur superfunctions s_{Λ/Ω} and s̄_{Λ/Ω} are defined dually and satisfy
   s_{Λ/Ω} = Σ_Γ c̄^{Λ'}_{Γ'Ω'} s_Γ,    s̄_{Λ/Ω} = Σ_Γ c^Λ_{ΩΓ} s̄_Γ,
where Λ' denotes the conjugate superpartition.

Problem. Provide a combinatorial Littlewood–Richardson rule, in the spirit of the classical Littlewood–Richardson rule for Schur functions, that computes the superspace structure constants c^Λ_{ΓΩ} and c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} as nonnegative (or otherwise explicitly described) integers counting combinatorial objects (such as suitably defined skew tableaux on superpartitions satisfying lattice/Yamanouchi-type conditions).

Setup. Fix integers $d,D\ge 2$ and $L\ge 2$. A translationally invariant Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on the $L\times L$ torus is determined by a single local tensor
$$A\in\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D},$$
with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ associated to the four lattice directions. Placing a copy of $A$ at every vertex of the torus and contracting all virtual indices along edges shared by neighbouring sites yields the PEPS vector $|\Psi_A\rangle\in(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes L^2}$.

For a square region $R\subset\mathbb{Z}_L\times\mathbb{Z}_L$ of size $n\times n$, let $\mathcal{V}_R:(\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes 4n}\to(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes n^2}$ be the linear map obtained by contracting the $n^2$ copies of $A$ inside $R$, viewing the $4n$ virtual indices on $\partial R$ as input and the $n^2$ physical indices as output. Let $\Pi_R$ denote the orthogonal projector onto $\mathrm{Range}(\mathcal{V}_R)\subset(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes n^2}$, and define the local term $h_R:=\mathbb{1}-\Pi_R\ge 0$. The parent Hamiltonian is
$$H \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in\mathbb{Z}_L\times\mathbb{Z}_L}\tau(h_R),$$
where $\tau$ acts on operators by lattice translation. By construction $H\ge 0$ and $H|\Psi_A\rangle=0$.

Problem. Determine the weakest possible conditions on the tensor $A$ together with the smallest possible side length $n$ of the square region $R$ such that, for all sufficiently large $L$, the following two properties simultaneously hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $|\Psi_A\rangle$ is the unique ground state of $H$ (so that the kernel of $H$ is one-dimensional);
\item[(ii)] $H$ has a spectral gap above its ground state that is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $L$.
\end{enumerate}
Identify the minimal hypotheses on $A$ (e.g. injectivity-type, normality-type, or strictly weaker algebraic/spectral conditions on the transfer operator of $A$) and the minimal $n$ for which (i) and (ii) can be guaranteed.

Let $\Pi_R$ denote the orthogonal projector onto $\mathrm{Range}(\mathcal{V}_R)\subset(\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes n^2}$, and define the local term $h_R:=\mathbb{1}-\Pi_R\ge 0$. The parent Hamiltonian is
$$H \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in\mathbb{Z}_L\times\mathbb{Z}_L}\tau(h_R),$$
where $\tau$ acts on operators by lattice translation. By construction $H\ge 0$ and $H|\Psi_A\rangle=0$.

Problem. Determine the weakest possible conditions on the tensor $A$ together with the smallest possible side length $n$ of the square region $R$ such that, for all sufficiently large $L$, the following two properties simultaneously hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $|\Psi_A\rangle$ is the unique ground state of $H$ (so that the kernel of $H$ is one-dimensional);
\item[(ii)] $H$ has a spectral gap above its ground state that is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $L$.
\end{enumerate}
Identify the minimal hypotheses on $A$ (e.g. injectivity-type, normality-type, or strictly weaker algebraic/spectral conditions on the transfer operator of $A$) and the minimal $n$ for which (i) and (ii) can be guaranteed.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Sufficient conditions exist (e.g. injectivity gives uniqueness; normality plus additional assumptions give a gap in 1D, and partial 2D results exist), and generalizations such as semi-injective PEPS extend the uniqueness class. However, identifying the minimal conditions on the tensor and the minimal region size that simultaneously guarantee uniqueness and a uniform spectral gap of the parent Hamiltonian on a 2D torus remains an open problem; in 2D the gap can fail even under injectivity, and no minimal characterization is known.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disc and let $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$ with normalized Lebesgue measure $dm(\theta)=d\theta/(2\pi)$. A bounded holomorphic function $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{D}$ is called inner if its radial boundary values $f^*(e^{i\theta})=\lim_{r\to 1^-}f(re^{i\theta})$ satisfy $|f^*(e^{i\theta})|=1$ for almost every $\theta$. Assume in addition that $f(0)=0$. Then $f^*$ induces a Lebesgue measure-preserving ergodic transformation of $\mathbb{T}$, and one may consider its measure-theoretic (Kolmogorov–Sinai) entropy $h(f)$.

The Nevanlinna class $N(\mathbb{D})$ consists of holomorphic functions $g$ on $\mathbb{D}$ for which
$$\sup_{0<r<1}\int_0^{2\pi}\log^+|g(re^{i\theta})|\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}<\infty.$$

Prove or disprove the following two assertions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h(f)<\infty$ if and only if $f'\in N(\mathbb{D})$.
\item Whenever $h(f)<\infty$, one has
$$h(f)=\int_0^{2\pi}\log\bigl|f'(e^{i\theta})\bigr|\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}.$$
\end{enumerate}

Let $D \geq 2$ be a positive integer and let $M_D$ denote the algebra of $D \times D$ complex matrices. A linear map $T: M_D \to M_D$ is called a quantum channel if it is completely positive and trace-preserving. Such a channel is called primitive if there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $T^n(\rho)$ has full rank for every positive semidefinite matrix $\rho \in M_D$ with $\rho \neq 0$. The smallest such $n$ is called the primitivity index $p(T)$.

Determine the exact (sharp) value of
$$ f(D) := \max\{\, p(T) : T \text{ is a primitive quantum channel on } M_D \,\}, $$
as an explicit function of $D$. That is, find the optimal upper bound on the primitivity index $p(T)$ over all primitive quantum channels acting on $M_D$, together with a matching family of examples achieving the bound.

The exact optimal upper bound is not known. The best general upper bound is $O(D^2 \log D)$ (Sanz–Pérez-García–Wolf–Cirac), and it is conjectured the optimal order is $\Theta(D^2)$. Setup. Fix integers $d\ge 2$ and $D\ge 1$. A translationally invariant matrix product state (MPS) on $n$ sites with physical dimension $d$ and bond dimension $D$ is determined by a tensor $A\in\mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes\mathbb{C}^{D\times D}$, regarded as a tuple $(A_1,\dots,A_d)$ of $D\times D$ matrices. For each integer $L\ge 1$, define the linear map
$$\Gamma_L(A):\mathbb{C}^{D\times D}\longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes L},\qquad X\mapsto \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_L=1}^{d}\operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(X\,A_{i_1}A_{i_2}\cdots A_{i_L}\bigr)\,|i_1\cdots i_L\rangle.$$
Equivalently, $\Gamma_L(A)$ is injective iff the family $\{A_{i_1}\cdots A_{i_L}\}_{i_1,\dots,i_L}$ spans the full matrix algebra $M_D(\mathbb{C})$.

The tensor $A$ is called normal if there exists some finite $L$ for which $\Gamma_L(A)$ is injective. For a normal tensor $A$, its injectivity index is
$$\iota(A)\;=\;\min\{\,L\ge 1\,:\,\Gamma_L(A)\text{ is injective}\,\}.$$

Problem. Determine the exact best possible upper bound, as a function of the bond dimension $D$ alone, for the injectivity index of a normal translationally invariant MPS. That is, find the smallest function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\iota(A)\;\le\;f(D)$$
holds for every normal tensor $A$ with bond dimension $D$ (over all physical dimensions $d$), and exhibit normal tensors achieving (or asymptotically achieving) this bound.

Setup. Let $D \geq 2$ be an integer (the bond dimension) and let $d \geq 1$ be a physical dimension. A PEPS tensor on a square lattice is a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d} \otimes (\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes 4}$ with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ (one per lattice direction). For a finite simply connected region $R$ of the square lattice, the associated linear map
$$\Gamma_R : (\mathbb{C}^{D})^{\otimes \partial R} \longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{d})^{\otimes |R|}$$
is obtained by placing a copy of $A$ at every site of $R$, contracting all virtual indices internal to $R$, and leaving the virtual indices on the boundary $\partial R$ open.

A PEPS tensor $A$ is called injective on the region $R$ if $\Gamma_R$ is an injective linear map. The PEPS is called normal if there exists some finite region $R_0$ on which $\Gamma_{R_0}$ is injective; equivalently, normality means injectivity is reached on some sufficiently large patch. The injectivity index of a normal PEPS is defined as the smallest integer $L = L(A)$ such that $\Gamma_R$ is injective for every $L \times L$ square region $R$ (or, equivalently, for every region containing an $L \times L$ square).

Question. Determine the optimal (i.e. smallest) function $f : \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2} \to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ depending only on the bond dimension $D$ such that for every normal PEPS tensor $A$ with bond dimension $D$, the injectivity index satisfies
$$L(A) \leq f(D),$$
and such that this bound is attained by some normal PEPS with bond dimension $D$. In other words, give the exact best possible upper bound, expressed solely in terms of $D$, on the injectivity index of a normal PEPS of bond dimension $D$.

Let $L=\{L_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be a non-negative increasing sequence satisfying
$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} L_k r^k < \infty \quad \text{for every } 0<r<1.$$
For functions $f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k z^k$ and $P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{n} b_k z^k$ analytic in the unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z:|z|<1\}$, denote by
$$(P*f)(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k b_k z^k$$
the Hadamard (coefficient-wise) product. For an analytic function $g$ on $\mathbb{D}$, write $\|g\|_\infty = \sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}} |g(z)|$.

Define the space $P_L$ to consist of all functions $f$ analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ for which there exists a constant $A\geq 0$ such that, for every integer $n\geq 0$ and every polynomial $P_n$ of degree at most $n$,
$$\|P_n * f\|_\infty \leq A\, L_n\, \|P_n\|_\infty.$$
Equip $P_L$ with the norm $\|f\|_{P_L} = \inf\{A : \text{the above inequality holds}\}$, under which $P_L$ becomes a Banach space.

It is known that for $L_k\equiv 1$, the space $P_L$ coincides with the space of Cauchy–Stieltjes transforms, and for any convex sequence $\{L_k\}$ (e.g. $L_k=k$), the function $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} L_k z^k$ lies in the closed unit ball of $P_L$.

Problem: Determine the relationship between the spaces $P_L$ and the classical Hardy spaces $H^p$ for $0<p<1$. Specifically, identify, for given sequences $L$, inclusions, embeddings, or equivalences between $P_L$ and $H^p$ ($0<p<1$).

Setup. A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a finite region $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ is the quantum state obtained by placing, on every edge of $\Lambda$, a maximally entangled pair of $D$-dimensional virtual particles, and then applying at each vertex $v$ a linear map $A_v : (\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4} \to \mathbb{C}^d$ that contracts the four virtual indices meeting at $v$ into a single physical $d$-level system. The resulting many-body state $|\Psi_\Lambda\rangle$ on the physical Hilbert space $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes |\Lambda|}$ is, under standard injectivity assumptions, the unique ground state of a local frustration-free "parent Hamiltonian" $H_\Lambda = \sum_R h_R$, whose terms $h_R \ge 0$ are supported on small plaquettes.

For a region $R \subset \Lambda$ with complement $R^c$, the reduced density matrix of $|\Psi_\Lambda\rangle$ on the virtual indices crossing the boundary $\partial R$ defines, via the standard PEPS isometry, a positive operator $\rho^{\mathrm{bd}}_{\partial R}$ on the one-dimensional boundary Hilbert space, called the boundary state of the PEPS on $R$.

The family of parent Hamiltonians $\{H_\Lambda\}$ is said to be gapped if there exists $\gamma > 0$ such that for every sufficiently large region $\Lambda$, the spectral gap above the ground space of $H_\Lambda$ is at least $\gamma$.

The boundary states are said to admit a short-range Gibbs description with exponentially decaying interactions if there exist constants $C, \xi > 0$ such that for every region $R$ one can write
$$\rho^{\mathrm{bd}}_{\partial R} = \frac{1}{Z}\, e^{-K_{\partial R}}, \qquad K_{\partial R} = \sum_{X \subset \partial R} \Phi(X),$$
with self-adjoint local terms $\Phi(X)$ satisfying $\|\Phi(X)\| \le C\, e^{-\operatorname{diam}(X)/\xi}$.

Question. Is it true that the parent Hamiltonian family $\{H_\Lambda\}$ of an (injective) PEPS is gapped if and only if its boundary states admit a short-range Gibbs description with exponentially decaying interactions in the above sense?

Setup. Consider a two-dimensional quantum lattice system on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space at each site. Let $H = \sum_{x} h_x$ be a translationally invariant local Hamiltonian, where each term $h_x$ acts on a bounded neighbourhood of the site $x$, and assume that $H$ has a spectral gap above its ground-state energy that is bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in the system size.

A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) of bond dimension $D$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is a translationally invariant tensor network state obtained by placing at each lattice site a tensor with one physical index (of the local Hilbert space dimension) and four virtual indices of dimension $D$, and contracting virtual indices along the edges of the lattice.

Question. Does the following 2D local approximation theorem hold? For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a bond dimension $D = g(\varepsilon)$ and a translationally invariant PEPS $|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle$ of bond dimension at most $g(\varepsilon)$ such that for every finite region $R \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$, the reduced density matrix of $|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle$ on $R$ approximates the reduced density matrix of the ground state of $H$ on $R$ to within $\varepsilon$ in trace distance (with constants possibly depending on $|R|$ in a controlled way).

Specifically:
(a) Does such a local approximation theorem exist in two dimensions?
(b) Can it be established assuming only the spectral gap hypothesis (without further assumptions such as frustration-freeness, injectivity of a parent Hamiltonian, or uniform local gap)?
(c) Can the bond-dimension bound $g(\varepsilon)$ be taken to be polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$?

Setup. Fix a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$ (the physical space) and a bond dimension $D$. A translation-invariant projected entangled pair state (PEPS) tensor on the square lattice is a tensor
$$A \in \mathbb{C}^d \otimes (\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4},$$
with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ associated with the four nearest-neighbor directions (up, down, left, right). Given a positive integer $L$, the PEPS on the $L\times L$ torus is the vector $|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle \in (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes L^2}$ obtained by placing one copy of $A$ at every site of the $L\times L$ periodic square lattice and contracting matching virtual indices along each edge.

Question. Characterize, in terms of a local algebraic relation between $A$ and $B$, the condition that two such tensors $A,B\in \mathbb{C}^d\otimes(\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4}$ satisfy
$$|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle = |\Psi_B^{(L)}\rangle \qquad \text{for every } L \ge 1.$$
That is, find necessary and sufficient local conditions (e.g., the existence of invertible "gauge" matrices acting on the virtual indices, possibly up to limits) on the pair $(A,B)$ equivalent to producing identical states on every square torus.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

A "fundamental theorem" for PEPS has been established when one requires equality of the states on all contraction geometries: in that setting, two tensors give the same state if and only if they are related by an invertible gauge on the virtual level (up to limits, via minimal canonical forms). However, restricting equality to the family of square tori is known to be substantially harder: deciding whether two tensors generate the same uniform PEPS on all periodic rectangular lattices has been shown to be undecidable (in contrast to the decidable case of all contraction graphs). Thus a clean local characterization for the torus-only case is not known and the original question remains only partially resolved.

A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a two-dimensional lattice is defined by associating to each site a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times D \times D \times D \times D}$ with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of bond dimension $D$, and contracting copies of $A$ along the edges of a finite region $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ (with chosen boundary conditions) to obtain a vector $|\Psi_\Lambda(A)\rangle$ in the physical Hilbert space $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes |\Lambda|}$.

A "Fundamental Theorem" for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of PEPS tensors is a theorem of the following form: there exists an explicit list of local "gauge" relations on tensors (such as application of invertible matrices on virtual indices, possibly together with additional structural moves) such that, for every pair $A, B \in \mathcal{C}$, one has $|\Psi_\Lambda(A)\rangle = |\Psi_\Lambda(B)\rangle$ for all sufficiently large regions $\Lambda$ if and only if $A$ and $B$ are related by a finite sequence of these gauge relations.

For one-dimensional Matrix Product States, such a fundamental theorem is known in full generality. In two dimensions, it is established for the subclass of "normal" PEPS (tensors whose associated transfer-type map becomes injective after blocking). At the other extreme, equality of PEPS for arbitrary tensors is known to be undecidable, ruling out any complete fundamental theorem for the full class.

Problem: Identify a class $\mathcal{C}$ of two-dimensional (and, more generally, $d$-dimensional with $d \ge 2$) PEPS tensors that strictly contains the normal PEPS but is as large as possible while still admitting an explicit Fundamental Theorem in the above sense, and prove the corresponding theorem for $\mathcal{C}$.

Let $\mathbb{T}$ denote the unit circle and $L^\infty(\mathbb{T})$ the space of essentially bounded measurable functions on $\mathbb{T}$. For $\varphi \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T})$ with Fourier coefficients $\hat\varphi(n) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} \varphi(e^{i\theta}) e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta$, define the Hankel operator $H_\varphi : H^2(\mathbb{T}) \to H^2_-(\mathbb{T})$ (where $H^2$ is the Hardy space and $H^2_- = L^2 \ominus H^2$) by $H_\varphi f = P_-(\varphi f)$, with $P_-$ the orthogonal projection onto $H^2_-$. Equivalently, $H_\varphi$ is represented in the standard bases by the matrix $(\hat\varphi(-n-m-1))_{n,m\geq 0}$.

Characterize completely those symbols $\varphi \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T})$ for which the associated Hankel operator $H_\varphi$ is positive (i.e., self-adjoint with $\langle H_\varphi f, f\rangle \geq 0$ for all $f$ in its domain, after appropriate identification of the spaces).

Background and setup. Fix a finite local Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$ (the physical space) and a bond dimension $D$. A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) tensor on the square lattice is a tensor $A \in \mathbb{C}^d \otimes (\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4}$ with one physical index of dimension $d$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$, one for each lattice direction (up, down, left, right).

For each integer $L \ge 1$, the translationally invariant PEPS state on the $L \times L$ torus associated with $A$ is the (unnormalized) vector
$$|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle \;=\; \sum_{\{i_v\}} \mathrm{tTr}\!\left(\bigotimes_{v \in \mathbb{Z}_L^2} A^{i_v}\right) \bigotimes_{v \in \mathbb{Z}_L^2} |i_v\rangle \;\in\; (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes L^2},$$
where $A^{i}$ denotes the rank-$4$ virtual tensor obtained by fixing the physical index of $A$ to $i \in \{1,\dots,d\}$ and $\mathrm{tTr}$ denotes the tensor network contraction on the $L \times L$ torus (i.e., contracting all neighbouring virtual indices according to the periodic square lattice). The state $|\Psi_B^{(L)}\rangle$ is defined analogously from another PEPS tensor $B \in \mathbb{C}^d \otimes (\mathbb{C}^{D'})^{\otimes 4}$.

We say that $A$ and $B$ are related by a local relation if there exists a fixed finite-radius, tensor-level transformation (for example: a gauge transformation on the virtual indices, possibly combined with blocking a finite number of sites and applying invertible matrices on the virtual bonds, or one of the standard equivalence operations on PEPS tensors that relate two tensors generating the same family of bulk states) that maps $A$ to $B$.

Problem. Suppose $A$ and $B$ are PEPS tensors for which there exist $\varepsilon > 0$ and $L_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $L \ge L_0$,
$$\bigl\| \,|\Psi_A^{(L)}\rangle - |\Psi_B^{(L)}\rangle\, \bigr\|^2 \;\le\; \varepsilon.$$
Does this asymptotic closeness in the thermodynamic limit imply the existence of a local relation between the tensors $A$ and $B$? Equivalently, must two PEPS tensors whose torus states remain uniformly close (in squared norm) for all sufficiently large system sizes be related by a local, tensor-level equivalence?

Consider supervised machine-learning models whose hypothesis class consists of functions parameterized by a tensor network of fixed structure (e.g. a matrix product state / tensor train, a tensor ring, a CP or Tucker decomposition) with bond dimension (rank) D. Concretely, fix a tensor network architecture on N sites with local physical dimension d and a uniform bond dimension D, and let H_{N,d,D} denote the associated class of real-valued classifiers (or regressors) obtained by contracting an input feature embedding against the network and reading out a scalar.

Provide explicit closed-form expressions, as functions of the bond dimension D (and of N, d), for:

(a) the Vapnik–Chervonenkis dimension VC(H_{N,d,D}) of the resulting binary classifier family, and
(b) the (empirical or population) Rademacher complexity R_m(H_{N,d,D}) of the hypothesis class on samples of size m.

In particular, determine matching upper and lower bounds in D that exhibit the exact dependence of these complexity measures on the bond dimension for matrix product state classifiers and for related tensor network classifiers.

Let $D = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disc, and let $D^n \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ denote the unit polydisc. For a holomorphic function $f$ on $D^n$ and $0 < p < \infty$, define
$$\|f\|_{H^p}^p \;=\; \sup_{0 \le r < 1}\, \int_{[0,2\pi)^n} |f(re^{i\theta_1},\dots,re^{i\theta_n})|^p \, \frac{d\theta_1\cdots d\theta_n}{(2\pi)^n},$$
and let $H^p(D^n)$ be the space of holomorphic functions on $D^n$ with $\|f\|_{H^p} < \infty$.

It is known that for $n \geq 3$ there exist functions $f \in H^1(D^n)$ that cannot be written as $f = g\cdot h$ with $g,h \in H^2(D^n)$.

Question: Does the same phenomenon occur when $n = 2$? That is, does there exist $f \in H^1(D^2)$ such that $f$ cannot be expressed as a product $f = g h$ with $g, h \in H^2(D^2)$?

A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a two-dimensional lattice is specified by placing, at each site v of an n × n square lattice, a tensor A^{(v)} with one physical index of dimension d and four virtual indices of dimension at most D (one for each lattice direction), and contracting all matching virtual indices between nearest-neighbor sites. The contraction yields a vector |ψ⟩ in the Hilbert space (ℂ^d)^{⊗ n²}.

The 2D PEPS zero-testing problem is the following decision problem:

  Input: a description of a PEPS on an n × n square lattice, given by the list of local tensors {A^{(v)}} (with rational or finite-precision complex entries) together with the bond dimension D and physical dimension d.
  Question: is the resulting global state |ψ⟩ equal to the zero vector?

Determine the exact computational complexity class of this decision problem. That is, identify a complexity class C such that 2D PEPS zero-testing is C-complete under polynomial-time (many-one) reductions, with matching upper and lower bounds.

Let G be a finite group and let H be a normal subgroup of G. For any finite group K, let D(K) denote Kitaev's quantum double model defined on a 2-dimensional lattice: the local Hilbert space on each edge is C[K], and the Hamiltonian is the standard sum of mutually commuting vertex operators (enforcing gauge invariance under K) and plaquette operators (enforcing flatness of the K-gauge connection). The ground space of D(K) realizes the topological phase whose anyon content is the Drinfeld center Z(Rep(K)).

A "low-depth noisy quantum circuit" is a quantum channel obtained by composing a number of layers, independent of the system size (or growing at most poly-logarithmically), where each layer is a tensor product of local quantum channels (CPTP maps) acting on O(1)-sized regions of qudits, possibly using ancillas and measurements with classical feed-forward.

Question: Does there exist such a low-depth noisy quantum circuit Φ that maps the quantum double phase associated to G to the quantum double phase associated to H? More precisely, does there exist a constant-depth (or poly-logarithmic-depth) local quantum channel Φ such that Φ sends any ground state of the D(G) Hamiltonian to a state in the topological phase of D(H), implementing the anyon condensation associated with the inclusion of the normal subgroup H ⊴ G?

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. For a finite positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\partial\mathbb{D}=\{e^{i\theta}:\theta\in[0,2\pi)\}$ that is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure, define the associated singular inner function
$$S_\mu(z)=\exp\!\left(-\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{e^{i\theta}+z}{e^{i\theta}-z}\,d\mu(\theta)\right),\qquad z\in\mathbb{D}.$$
Call $S_\mu$ discrete if $\mu$ is a purely atomic (discrete) measure, and continuous if $\mu$ has no atoms. Each $S_\mu$ is bounded analytic on $\mathbb{D}$ with $\|S_\mu\|_\infty=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}|S_\mu(z)|=1$, so distances are measured in the supremum norm on $\mathbb{D}$.

Question: Given a discrete singular inner function $S_\mu$, does there necessarily exist a constant $\delta=\delta(\mu)>0$ such that
$$\|S_\mu-S_\nu\|_\infty>\delta$$
for every continuous singular inner function $S_\nu$? (It is known that the analogous statement obtained by interchanging the roles of "discrete" and "continuous" — i.e., with $S_\mu$ continuous and $S_\nu$ ranging over discrete singular inner functions — fails.)

Setup. Fix a spatial dimension D ≥ 2 and consider a D-dimensional lattice (e.g., Z^D) with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space attached to each site.

(a) A projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on this lattice is defined as follows. To each edge incident to a site one assigns an auxiliary (virtual) Hilbert space of finite "bond dimension" D_b, and to each site one places a maximally entangled pair across each adjacent edge. A linear map (the local PEPS tensor) A: (C^{D_b})^{⊗(2D)} → C^d is then applied at every site, where d is the physical dimension; the resulting global pure state on the physical lattice is the PEPS. A translation-invariant PEPS is one where the same tensor A is used at every site.

(b) A quantum cellular automaton (QCA) on the same lattice is a *-automorphism α of the quasi-local C*-algebra of observables that is translation-invariant and strictly local, in the sense that there exists a finite radius r such that for every site x, α maps observables supported at x into observables supported in the ball of radius r about x. Two QCAs are considered equivalent if they differ by a finite-depth circuit of local unitaries (and ancilla stabilization).

Problem. Determine the precise mathematical relationship between the class of translation-invariant PEPS (parametrized by their local tensors and bond dimensions) and the class of QCAs in dimension D ≥ 2. Specifically:

(i) Characterize which QCAs α can be obtained as the action that maps the trivial product state to a (translation-invariant) PEPS, or equivalently arise as the entangling isometry/unitary implicit in a PEPS construction.

(ii) Conversely, characterize which translation-invariant PEPS arise from applying a QCA to a product state, and relate the bond dimension and tensor structure of the PEPS to the locality radius and equivalence class of the QCA.

(iii) Identify obstructions (such as nontrivial QCA index/invariants in D ≥ 2 and the existence of nontrivial QCAs in D = 3) that prevent a one-to-one correspondence, and provide an exact dictionary between PEPS and QCA in D ≥ 2.

Let $(M,g)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold. A geodesic net in $M$ is a finite graph immersed in $M$ whose edges are geodesic arcs and which satisfies a balancing condition at each vertex: at every vertex $v$, the sum of the unit tangent vectors of the edges emanating from $v$, counted with edge multiplicities, equals the zero vector in $T_v M$. A geodesic multinet is a geodesic net in which edges are allowed to have positive integer multiplicities and edges are allowed to self-intersect or coincide. Such a multinet is called closed if every vertex satisfies the balancing condition (i.e. there are no unbalanced "boundary" vertices). A non-trivial periodic geodesic is a closed geodesic that is not a constant map.

Question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ contain a closed geodesic multinet that does not contain any non-trivial periodic geodesic as a subset (i.e., none of the geodesic arcs traced by the multinet, with their multiplicities, decompose to include a non-trivial closed geodesic)?

Recall the Cauchy–Pompeiu formula: for a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℂ with sufficiently regular boundary Γ and a function f smooth enough on Ω̄,
   f(z) = (1/(2πi)) ∫_Γ f(ζ)/(ζ − z) dζ − (1/π) ∫∫_Ω (∂f/∂ζ̄)(ζ) · 1/(ζ − z) dξ dη  (ζ = ξ + iη),
for z ∈ Ω. The boundary integral and the value f(z) make sense for merely continuous f, but the area integral involves the distributional derivative ∂f/∂ζ̄.

For 0 < α < 1, let Lip α denote the homogeneous Lipschitz class of complex-valued functions on ℂ with seminorm
   ‖f‖_{Lip α} = sup_{z ≠ w} |f(z) − f(w)| / |z − w|^α.

For a Borel set Ω ⊂ ℂ with characteristic function χ_Ω, consider the distribution ∂χ_Ω/∂z̄ (the Cauchy transform-like derivative of χ_Ω). The pairing of this distribution with a test function f gives a distribution ⟨∂χ_Ω/∂z̄, f⟩.

Question: Characterize the Borel sets Ω ⊂ ℂ for which there exists a constant C_Ω < ∞ such that
   |⟨∂χ_Ω/∂z̄, f⟩| ≤ C_Ω ‖f‖_{Lip α}
for every f ∈ Lip α (with α > 0 fixed). Equivalently, for which Borel sets Ω does χ_Ω define a (continuous) multiplier or element acting on the homogeneous Besov space B^{α−1}_{∞,∞}(ℂ)?

Treat in particular the case where Ω is a "Swiss cheese", i.e., Ω = D̄ ∖ ⋃_{j=1}^∞ D_j, where D is an open disk and {D_j} is a sequence of pairwise disjoint open disks contained in D with ∑ radius(D_j) < ∞ and D̄ ∖ ⋃ D_j having empty interior.

A geodesic net in a Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ together with a continuous map from $G$ to $M$ that sends each edge to a (nonconstant) geodesic segment of $M$. At each vertex $v\in V$, let $\tau_1(v),\dots,\tau_{\deg(v)}(v)\in T_{f(v)}M$ denote the unit tangent vectors to the outgoing edge geodesics. The vertex $v$ is called balanced if $\sum_{i=1}^{\deg(v)}\tau_i(v)=0$. A closed geodesic net is a geodesic net in which every vertex is balanced (no unbalanced vertices).

Let $S^3$ denote the round $3$-sphere, equipped with its standard constant-curvature-$1$ metric. Classify all $3$-regular (finite, simple or multi-) graphs $G$ that arise as the underlying graph of some closed geodesic net realized in $S^3$. That is, determine exactly which $3$-regular graphs $G$ admit a continuous map $f:G\to S^3$ sending each edge to a geodesic arc such that at every vertex the three unit tangent vectors to the outgoing edges sum to zero.

Let $(M,g)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold of dimension $n \geq 3$. A geodesic net on $M$ is a finite multigraph $G$ together with a continuous map $f : G \to M$ such that:
(i) the restriction of $f$ to the interior of each edge of $G$ is a (nonconstant) geodesic arc parametrized by arc length;
(ii) at each vertex $v$ of $G$, the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$ of the geodesic edges meeting $v$ (taken with the outgoing orientation) equals zero in $T_{f(v)} M$.
Such a geodesic net is called a closed geodesic net. The theta-graph $\theta$ is the multigraph with exactly two vertices joined by three distinct edges.

Question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of dimension $n \geq 3$ admit a closed geodesic net whose underlying graph is the theta-graph $\theta$ (i.e., two vertices $p, q \in M$ together with three geodesic arcs from $p$ to $q$ such that the three unit tangent vectors at $p$ sum to zero, and the three unit tangent vectors at $q$ sum to zero)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of existence of theta-graph shaped stationary geodesic nets on general closed Riemannian manifolds appears to remain open. While there are partial results (e.g., existence on manifolds with nontrivial second homology, where a geodesic net of length at most 3·diam(M) exists but may be a closed geodesic, two loops, or a theta-graph; and existence on convex 2-spheres close to round), no general existence theorem in dimension ≥ 3 is recorded. Recent work (2025) on generic density of stationary geodesic nets explicitly notes that such nets may degenerate to unions of closed geodesics, leaving the theta-graph existence question unresolved.

Determine whether $\Sigma$ has Lebesgue measure zero in $(\mathbb{R}^2)^3 \cong \mathbb{R}^6$.

Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ be the open unit disk. A sequence $\{z_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty} \subset \mathbb{D}$ is called interpolating for bounded analytic functions if, for every bounded sequence $\{\alpha_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of complex numbers, there exists a bounded analytic function $f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z_n) = \alpha_n$ for all $n \geq 1$. Similarly, $\{z_n\}$ is called interpolating for bounded harmonic functions if, for every bounded sequence $\{\alpha_n\}$ of complex numbers, there exists a bounded (complex-valued) harmonic function $u : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ with $u(z_n) = \alpha_n$ for all $n \geq 1$.

It is known that a sequence $\{z_n\} \subset \mathbb{D}$ is interpolating for bounded harmonic functions if and only if it is interpolating for bounded analytic functions. All known proofs of this equivalence proceed by appealing to explicit geometric/analytic conditions (such as the Carleson condition, i.e. uniform separation in the hyperbolic metric together with the Carleson measure condition) that characterize interpolating sequences for bounded analytic functions.

Problem: Provide a direct proof of the equivalence "interpolating for bounded harmonic functions $\iff$ interpolating for bounded analytic functions" that does not rely on knowing or invoking any such characterizing condition for interpolation by bounded analytic functions.

Definitions. A geodesic multinet in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a finite weighted embedded graph $(G,w)$ where every edge $e$ is a straight line segment and is assigned a positive integer weight (multiplicity) $w(e)\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. A vertex $v$ of $G$ is called balanced if the weighted sum of unit tangent vectors along the edges incident to $v$ vanishes:
$$\sum_{e\ni v} w(e)\,\mathbf{u}_{e,v} = 0,$$
where $\mathbf{u}_{e,v}$ is the unit vector at $v$ pointing along the edge $e$ away from $v$. A vertex that is not balanced is called a boundary (or unbalanced) vertex.

Question. Does there exist a function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ such that for every positive integer $n$ and every geodesic multinet in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which has exactly three boundary vertices and in which every edge has multiplicity at most $n$, the number of balanced vertices is at most $f(n)$?
