Setup. Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A geodesic multinet is a finite connected graph $\Gamma$ embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose vertex set $V(\Gamma)$ is finite and whose edges are straight line segments (geodesics), with the convention that multiple edges between the same pair of vertices and isolated loops are allowed only insofar as each edge is realized as a (possibly degenerate) straight segment; each edge $e$ is assigned a positive integer multiplicity $m(e) \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

For a vertex $v \in V(\Gamma)$ and an edge $e$ incident to $v$, let $u_{v,e} \in \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the unit vector at $v$ pointing along $e$ away from $v$. The vertex $v$ is called balanced if
$$\sum_{e \ni v} m(e)\, u_{v,e} \;=\; 0,$$
and unbalanced otherwise. (Equivalently, a geodesic multinet is the 1-skeleton of a stationary integer 1-varifold in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose stationarity may fail at a prescribed finite set of vertices, the unbalanced ones.)

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to similarity of $\mathbb{R}^2$, of all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane that have exactly three unbalanced vertices. The classification should describe the combinatorial structure (graph with edge multiplicities), the possible positions of the unbalanced vertices and of any additional balanced vertices, and the resulting straight-edge embeddings.

Suppose $E \subset \partial F \cap \partial D$ and that $f$ extends continuously to $F \cup E$.

Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a Jordan arc (i.e., a homeomorphic image of the closed interval $[0,1]$). For each $j = 1, \dots, n$, let $\pi_j : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ denote the projection onto the $j$-th complex coordinate, and let $\gamma_j = \pi_j(\gamma) \subset \mathbb{C}$. Assume that each $\gamma_j$ has two-dimensional Lebesgue (area) measure zero in $\mathbb{C}$.

Let $C(\gamma)$ denote the algebra of continuous complex-valued functions on $\gamma$ with the supremum norm. Let $P(\gamma)$ denote the uniform closure on $\gamma$ of the algebra of holomorphic polynomials in the coordinates $z_1, \dots, z_n$, and let $R(\gamma)$ denote the uniform closure on $\gamma$ of rational functions in $z_1, \dots, z_n$ that are holomorphic on a neighborhood of $\gamma$.

It is known that under the above hypotheses $R(\gamma) = C(\gamma)$. Determine whether one always has
$$P(\gamma) = C(\gamma);$$
that is, whether every continuous function on such a Jordan arc $\gamma$ can be uniformly approximated on $\gamma$ by holomorphic polynomials in $z_1, \dots, z_n$.

For a positive integer $N_0$, an $N_0$-tuple $S = (p_1, \dots, p_{N_0}) \in (\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ is said to admit unboundedly complex balanced extensions if for every positive integer $N$ there exists a geodesic net $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose set of unbalanced vertices equals $\{p_1, \dots, p_{N_0}\}$ and whose number of balanced vertices exceeds $N$.

(a) Does there exist an integer $N_0 \ge 1$ and an $N_0$-tuple $S \in (\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ which admits unboundedly complex balanced extensions?

(b) If so, does the set of such $N_0$-tuples form a subset of $(\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$ of positive Lebesgue measure, or even contain a non-empty open subset of $(\mathbb{R}^2)^{N_0}$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture appears to remain open. For three unbalanced vertices, it has been proved that there can be at most one balanced vertex, ruling out unbounded complexity in that case. For four unbalanced vertices, only finite constructions are known: an irreducible geodesic net with four boundary points and 25 balanced vertices was recently constructed (raising the prior record of 16), and this work is presented as progress toward, but not a proof of, the conjecture that arbitrarily many balanced vertices are achievable. Let $n \geq 2$ and let $F$ be a closed subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Call $F$ a set of harmonic approximation if every function $f$ that is continuous on $F$ and harmonic on the interior of $F$ can be uniformly approximated on $F$ by functions harmonic on all of $\mathbb{R}^n$; that is, for every such $f$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a function $h$ harmonic on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\sup_{x \in F} |f(x) - h(x)| < \varepsilon$.

Find necessary and sufficient conditions on the closed set $F \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ in order that $F$ be a set of harmonic approximation, in the general case where $F$ need not be nowhere dense and need not be the closure of its interior.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

The problem has been resolved in special cases: Šaginjan handled nowhere dense $F$, and Gauthier–Goldstein–Ow gave separate necessary and sufficient (but not coinciding) conditions when $F$ is the closure of its interior in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Subsequent work characterized harmonic Arakelyan sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \geq 3$) and on Riemann surfaces (Goldstein–Ow 1993, Gauthier–Pouryayevali, and recent work by Fournodavlos), giving necessary and sufficient conditions in many settings, but a full general necessary-and-sufficient characterization for arbitrary closed $F \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ does not appear to be entirely settled.

A geodesic net in the Euclidean plane R^2 is a finite straight-line graph G = (V, E) embedded in R^2 such that every edge is a Euclidean line segment realizing the distance between its endpoints, with prescribed positive weights (or, equivalently, with each edge counted with multiplicity). For a vertex v ∈ V, define the imbalance vector at v by

  imb(v) = Σ_{e at v} u_e(v),

where the sum is over all edges e incident to v, and u_e(v) is the unit vector at v pointing along e away from v (multiplied by the weight/multiplicity of e). A vertex v is called balanced if imb(v) = 0, and unbalanced otherwise. The total imbalance of the net is defined as

  I(G) = Σ_{v unbalanced} ‖imb(v)‖.

Question: Does there exist a function F : Z_{≥0} × R_{≥0} → R such that, for every geodesic net G in the Euclidean plane,

  #{balanced vertices of G} ≤ F(#{unbalanced vertices of G}, I(G)) ?

In other words, can the number of balanced vertices of a planar Euclidean geodesic net be bounded above purely in terms of the number of unbalanced vertices and the total imbalance?

Let Γ ⊂ ℂ be a Jordan curve of logarithmic capacity 1, and let φ be the conformal map from the exterior of Γ onto the exterior of the unit circle satisfying φ(∞) = ∞. For each n ∈ ℕ, let z_1^{(n)}, …, z_n^{(n)} ∈ Γ be an n-th order Fekete point system, i.e. an n-tuple of points on Γ that maximizes the product ∏_{1 ≤ j < k ≤ n} |z_j − z_k|. Consider the discrete logarithmic potential

   U_n(z) = (1/n) ∑_{k=1}^{n} log |z − z_k^{(n)}|.

It is known that when Γ is sufficiently smooth, U_n(z) approximates log |φ(z)| outside Γ and 0 inside Γ with error O(1/n) uniformly on compact subsets bounded away from Γ. The same O(1/n) approximation holds in the degenerate case Γ = [−2, 2].

Prove that the analogous O(1/n) approximation holds in the case where Γ is a square (i.e. the boundary of a square in ℂ, scaled so as to have logarithmic capacity 1): show that on every compact set disjoint from Γ,

   U_n(z) = log |φ(z)| + O(1/n)   (z outside Γ),
   U_n(z) = O(1/n)               (z inside Γ).

Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold. A geodesic net on $M$ is a finite graph $G$ immersed in $M$ such that every edge is a geodesic segment parametrized by arclength. A vertex $v$ of $G$ is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the edges incident to $v$, taken in the outgoing direction at $v$, equals zero; otherwise it is called unbalanced. Let $L$ denote the total length of $G$ (sum of the lengths of its edges) and let $D$ denote its diameter (the diameter of $G$ as a metric subspace of $M$). For a point $p \in M$, let $\mathrm{inj}(p)$ denote the injectivity radius of $M$ at $p$. Define the adjusted total length of $G$ by
$$\widetilde L \;=\; \sum_{i} \int_0^{\ell(e_i)} \frac{ds}{\mathrm{inj}(e_i(s))},$$
where the sum is over all edges $e_i$ of $G$, parametrized by arclength, and $\ell(e_i)$ is the length of $e_i$.

Question: Does there exist a function $f_M : \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \times \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \times \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, depending on $M$ but invariant under rescaling of the metric of $M$, such that for every geodesic net $G$ on $M$ with total length $L$, adjusted length $\widetilde L$, diameter $D$, and exactly $n$ unbalanced vertices, the number of balanced vertices of $G$ is at most $f_M(\widetilde L,\, L/D,\, n)$?

In particular, if $M$ has positive (global) injectivity radius $\mathrm{inj}(M) > 0$, must the number of balanced vertices of any geodesic net $G$ on $M$ with total length $L$, diameter $D$, and $n$ unbalanced vertices be bounded above by $f_M(L/\mathrm{inj}(M),\, L/D,\, n)$?

Fix a circle C of radius 1 in the Euclidean plane with center O, and place seven equally spaced "outer" vertices u_0, …, u_6 on C. For a real parameter φ in a small neighborhood of 0, build a layered planar graph G_n(φ) whose vertex set is the disjoint union of layers V_0, V_1, …, V_n as follows.

• Layer V_0 consists of the seven outer vertices u_0, …, u_6.
• Layer V_1 ("inner layer") consists of seven vertices, each obtained from a corresponding outer vertex by rotating about O by an angle φ and scaling radially; the parameter φ measures the angular deviation of the inner heptagon from being concentrically aligned with V_0.
• For i ≥ 2 the layer V_i is produced from V_{i−1} by the following alternating "suspension-and-winging" rule:
   – If i is odd, perform a one-hook suspension: each new vertex v ∈ V_i is connected to its closest vertex P on the outer circle (the "hook"), forming an edge Pv.
   – If i is even, perform a two-hook suspension: each new vertex v ∈ V_i is connected through the Fermat point of the triangle ΔPvQ to its two closest outer vertices P and Q; let X denote the third vertex of the equilateral triangle erected on PQ (on the side away from v) used in the standard Fermat-point construction.

Define the suspension angle φ_i(φ) by
   φ_i(φ) = ∠OPv,   if i is odd (with P the hook used in layer V_i and v ∈ V_i),
   φ_i(φ) = ∠OXv,   if i is even (with X the auxiliary equilateral-triangle vertex described above and v ∈ V_i).

Each φ_i(φ) is a smooth function of φ near φ = 0. Consider the sequence of derivatives
   a_i := φ_i'(0),   i = 1, 2, 3, … .

Question: Is the sequence (a_i)_{i ≥ 1} nonrepeating, in the sense that a_i ≠ a_j whenever i ≠ j? Equivalently, prove or disprove that no two terms of the derivative sequence (φ_i'(0)) coincide.

Let $K$ be a compact subset of the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$, and let $f:K\to\mathbb{C}$ be a continuous function. Recall that a function $g$ defined on an open neighborhood $U$ of $K$ is said to be bianalytic on $U$ if $\bar\partial^{\,2} g \equiv 0$ on $U$, equivalently if $g(z)=a(z)+\bar z\, b(z)$ for some functions $a,b$ holomorphic on $U$; and $g$ is said to be analytic near $K$ if it is holomorphic on some open neighborhood of $K$.

Suppose there exists a sequence $\{f_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of functions, each bianalytic on some open neighborhood of $K$, such that $f_n \to f$ uniformly on $K$.

Question: Must there then exist a sequence $\{h_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of functions, each analytic (holomorphic) on some open neighborhood of $K$, such that $h_n \to f$ uniformly on $K$?

It is known that the answer is affirmative under the additional hypothesis that $f$ is Lipschitz of order $\tfrac12$ on $K$, and also under the hypothesis that $f \in W^{1,p}$ for some $p>2$. The problem is to decide whether the implication holds for arbitrary continuous $f$ with no additional regularity assumption.

Consider the following layered construction of a planar geodesic net depending on a small angle parameter $\phi$. Fix $\epsilon>0$ small. For $\phi\in(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$, build a sequence of layers indexed by $i=0,1,\dots,n$, where each layer is obtained from the previous one by a "suspension" operation: at each step, the construction is determined by an angle $\phi_i(\phi)$, computed recursively from $\phi_0(\phi)=\phi$ and the geometric rule that two incoming geodesic segments at the apex of layer $i$ are continued so that the balancing condition (the sum of unit tangent vectors of incident edges vanishes) holds at every newly created interior vertex. The resulting weighted geodesic graph is denoted $G_n(\phi)$; it has exactly $14$ designated unbalanced (boundary) vertices, and for $n$ large it has arbitrarily many balanced interior vertices.

A weighted geodesic net is a finite graph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with edges that are straight segments and positive integer weights $w_e$ on edges, such that at every balanced vertex $v$, $\sum_{e\ni v} w_e\, \mathbf{u}_{e,v} = 0$, where $\mathbf{u}_{e,v}$ is the unit vector along $e$ at $v$. An edge has weight greater than one precisely when two distinct edges of the underlying construction overlap along a common segment.

Prove or disprove: for every sufficiently small nonzero $\phi\in(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$, the finite sequence of suspension angles
$$\phi_0(\phi),\ \phi_1(\phi),\ \ldots,\ \phi_n(\phi)$$
contains no repeated value. Equivalently, show that for all such $\phi$, $G_n(\phi)$ is a geodesic net in which every edge has weight equal to one, while still possessing $14$ unbalanced vertices and (for $n$ large) arbitrarily many balanced vertices.

representations.normalized:
Consider a semiconductor in which charge carriers can occupy delocalized band-like states (conduction band electrons and valence band holes) and localized defect states inside the band gap. Non-radiative recombination is described by multiphonon transitions: a downward electronic transition between two such states releases its electronic energy by simultaneous emission of multiple phonons of the host lattice. The standard theory (Huang–Rhys / Henry–Lang formalism) computes the transition rate using configuration-coordinate diagrams in which the adiabatic potential energy surfaces of both the initial and the final electronic state are approximated by harmonic oscillators with prescribed frequencies and equilibrium-position offsets, and the electron–phonon matrix element is evaluated from overlaps of harmonic oscillator vibrational wavefunctions weighted by a linear electron–phonon coupling.

Suppose now that the host lattice has the following non-standard properties, characteristic of lead-halide perovskites: (i) the metal–halide bonds undergo large-amplitude, strongly anharmonic thermal fluctuations on a timescale comparable to or slower than electronic motion; (ii) these anharmonic fluctuations dynamically modulate the spatial overlap of the electronic wavefunctions of band states and defect states; (iii) low-frequency optical phonon modes contribute non-perturbatively to the dissipation of electronic energy.

Formulate a generalization of the multiphonon non-radiative recombination rate that replaces the harmonic-oscillator vibrational basis and linear electron–phonon coupling with a model incorporating anharmonic ionic potentials and a fluctuation-dependent electronic overlap. Specifically, derive an expression for the temperature- and energy-dependent transition rate between a band-like state and a localized defect state in which:
(a) the ionic potential along the relevant configuration coordinate(s) is a general anharmonic potential rather than quadratic;
(b) the electronic matrix element depends explicitly on the instantaneous ionic configuration through the modulation of wavefunction overlap;
(c) the resulting rate reduces to the standard harmonic multiphonon expression in the harmonic, weak-modulation limit.

Determine how this modification quantitatively changes the predicted magnitude and temperature dependence of non-radiative recombination rates compared with the harmonic-oscillator result.

Consider the Korteweg–de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval (0, L) with L > 0:
  u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0,   for 0 < x < L, t > 0,
  u(x, 0) = φ(x),   for 0 < x < L,
together with a set of (linear) boundary conditions of the form
  B_k u(t) = h_k(t),   k = 1, 2, 3,   t > 0,
where {B_k} is a triple of boundary operators (involving traces of u, u_x, u_{xx} at x = 0 and x = L) chosen so that the linearized problem is well-posed, and h_k are prescribed boundary data. Assume that the problem is locally well-posed in the Sobolev space H^s(0, L) for some s ≥ 0, with sufficiently smooth (or zero) boundary data h_k and initial data φ ∈ H^s(0, L) satisfying the natural compatibility conditions.

Question: Determine whether this initial-boundary value problem is globally well-posed in H^s(0, L) for some s ≥ 0; equivalently, decide whether every solution remains in H^s(0, L) for all t ≥ 0 or whether some solution can blow up in H^s(0, L) in finite time. In particular, establish (or disprove) a global a priori L^2 bound
  sup_{0 ≤ t < ∞} ‖u(·, t)‖_{L^2(0, L)} < ∞
for solutions of this IBVP, which would yield global well-posedness in H^s(0, L) for all s ≥ 0 in the locally well-posed range.

representations.normalization_method: unicode-preserving newline and trailing-whitespace normalization v1
representations.normalized:
Consider a heterojunction in a thin-film solar cell formed between a lead-halide perovskite absorber (e.g., CH3NH3PbI3 or a mixed-cation, mixed-halide analogue) and an adjacent organic charge-transport layer used as either an electron contact (such as PCBM or C60) or a hole contact (such as Spiro-OMeTAD or PTAA). Let S denote the effective interface (surface) recombination velocity governing nonradiative carrier loss at this interface, defined operationally through the boundary condition J_rec = q·S·Δn for excess minority-carrier density Δn at the interface.

Standard nonradiative recombination theory (e.g., multiphonon emission and Marcus–Jortner-type models) predicts that the rate of nonradiative band-to-band or trap-assisted recombination should increase when high-frequency vibrational modes are available to accept the released electronic energy. Organic semiconductors possess high-energy intramolecular vibrational modes (C–H, C–C, C=C stretches at energies on the order of 100–400 meV), which by this reasoning ought to enhance nonradiative recombination at perovskite/organic interfaces compared to perovskite/inorganic interfaces.

Empirically, however, perovskite/organic interfaces are observed to display extremely low effective surface recombination velocities (often comparable to or lower than perovskite/inorganic counterparts).

Problem: Construct a quantitative, predictive microscopic model of nonradiative interface recombination at perovskite/organic-semiconductor heterojunctions that
(i) explains the observed smallness of the effective surface recombination velocity S despite the presence of high-energy vibrational acceptor modes in the organic layer;
(ii) identifies the dominant physical parameters controlling S (e.g., interfacial electronic coupling, energy-level offsets, reorganization energies, vibrational mode spectrum, dielectric screening, density and energetics of interfacial defects); and
(iii) yields design rules that allow rational selection or engineering of organic contact materials to minimize S, rather than empirical screening of candidate contacts.

representations.normalized:
Consider a thin-film solar cell consisting of an absorber layer of thickness $d$ sandwiched between an electron transport layer (ETL) and a hole transport layer (HTL), each characterized by a surface recombination velocity $S$ (cm/s) at the absorber/transport-layer interface and contributing to a total series resistance $R_s$ (Ω·cm$^2$). Under standard one-sun illumination, the cell's current–voltage characteristic can be modeled by
$$ J(V) \;=\; J_{	ext{ph}} \;-\; J_0\!\left(\exp\! rac{q(V+J R_s)}{n k_B T}-1ight) \;-\;  rac{V+J R_s}{R_{sh}}, $$
where $J_{	ext{ph}}$ is the photogenerated current density, $J_0$ is the saturation current density (which depends on $S$ through the effective recombination at both interfaces, e.g. $J_0 \propto S$ in the surface-recombination-limited regime), $n$ is the ideality factor, $T$ the temperature, $R_{sh}$ the shunt resistance, and $q,k_B$ have their usual meanings. The open-circuit voltage is $V_{oc} = V$ such that $J(V)=0$, and the maximum-power-point voltage $V_{mpp}$ maximizes $V\cdot J(V)$. In addition, the spatial distribution of the built-in electric field across the absorber and the transport layers — determined by the dielectric permittivities, doping densities, and band offsets of ETL/HTL — modulates the effective collection efficiency $\eta_c \in (0,1]$ multiplying $J_{	ext{ph}}$, with most of the potential dropping over the transport layers when those layers are weakly doped or thick.

Formulate and solve the following optimization problem: choose the transport-layer parameters (thickness, doping density, dielectric constant, band offset, and resulting interface surface recombination velocity $S$) so as to maximize the power conversion efficiency
$$ \eta \;=\;  rac{\max_V \, V\,J(V)}{P_{	ext{in}}}, $$
subject to the trade-off that decreasing $S$ (which raises $V_{oc}$) generally increases $R_s$ and may redistribute the electric field in a way that reduces $\eta_c$ at $V_{mpp}$. Specifically: (i) derive analytic conditions characterizing the optimal $(S, R_s, \eta_c)$ triple for which $V_{mpp}\cdot J(V_{mpp})$ is maximized, and (ii) determine quantitatively how the resistive and field-distribution losses at the ETL/HTL interfaces should be balanced against the recombination losses in order to achieve the highest attainable efficiency.

Consider the pure initial value problem for the Korteweg–de Vries equation on the real line:
  u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0,  (x,t) ∈ ℝ × ℝ,
  u(x,0) = φ(x),  x ∈ ℝ.

For s ∈ ℝ, let H^s(ℝ) denote the L^2-based Sobolev space of order s. It is known that this initial value problem is locally (and globally) well-posed in H^s(ℝ) for s ≥ −3/4, and that for s < −3/4 the data-to-solution map fails to be uniformly continuous on bounded sets of H^s(ℝ).

Killip and Vișan (Annals of Mathematics, 2019) proved that the KdV equation on the real line is globally well-posed in H^s(ℝ) for all s ≥ −1, using a new method based on commuting flows of the integrable hierarchy. This extends well-posedness well below the previous s = −3/4 threshold and resolves the question of well-posedness for some s < −3/4 in the affirmative. Moreover, H^{-1}(ℝ) is sharp within the H^s(ℝ) scale, since the data-to-solution map cannot be continuously extended below s = −1.

Consider a multilayer thin-film solar cell consisting of a lead-halide perovskite absorber sandwiched between an electron-transport layer and a hole-transport layer, each in contact with a metal electrode. Under steady-state illumination at the maximum power point, define the following quantities:

1. The lumped series resistance R_s of the device, defined operationally from the current–voltage characteristic. Decompose R_s as R_s = Σ_i R_i, where each R_i is the contribution to the total series resistance arising from a single layer i (absorber, electron-transport layer, hole-transport layer, and the two electrode/interface contacts).

2. The internal quasi-Fermi level splitting Δμ_int(x) = E_{F,n}(x) − E_{F,p}(x) inside the perovskite absorber as a function of position x, where E_{F,n} and E_{F,p} are the electron and hole quasi-Fermi levels.

3. The external quasi-Fermi level splitting Δμ_ext = qV_ext at the metallic contacts at the maximum power point, where V_ext is the externally measured voltage.

Problem. Devise an experimental procedure (or combined experimental–analytical methodology) that:

(a) separately determines each layer-resolved resistance contribution R_i from in-operando measurements on a complete device, and

(b) quantitatively measures the coupling between the spatially averaged internal splitting ⟨Δμ_int⟩ in the absorber and the external splitting Δμ_ext at the maximum power point, i.e., determines the loss Δμ_loss = ⟨Δμ_int⟩ − Δμ_ext attributable to each transport/contact layer.

Prove or characterize, within a suitable drift-diffusion model of the device, that the proposed methodology uniquely recovers the set {R_i} and the splitting losses, and provide error bounds.

Consider a thin-film lead-halide perovskite solar cell modeled as a one-dimensional heterostructure consisting of: a transparent conductive electrode of indium tin oxide (ITO), a hole-transport contact layer of poly[bis(4-phenyl)(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)amine] (PTAA), a lead-halide perovskite absorber of band gap E_g ≈ 1.6 eV and thickness less than 1 μm, an electron-transport contact layer of [6,6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM), and a silver (Ag) back electrode. Define the built-in voltage V_bi of the device as V_bi = E_g − Δ_c − Δ_a, where Δ_c is the energy offset between the cathode contact work function and the perovskite conduction-band minimum and Δ_a is the offset between the anode contact work function and the perovskite valence-band maximum. Assume drift–diffusion transport with bulk minority-carrier diffusion lengths exceeding the absorber thickness, and let S denote the interfacial recombination velocity at the contacts. The minority-carrier concentrations n_min(0) at the hole contact and p_min(L) at the electron contact, and consequently the interfacial recombination current J_rec ≈ q·S·n_min, are controlled by V_bi through the equilibrium band bending.

(a) Derive, within a standard drift–diffusion model with Boltzmann statistics, an explicit expression for the dependence of the open-circuit voltage V_oc on V_bi and S that exposes how only a sufficiently large V_bi suppresses interfacial recombination by reducing the minority-carrier densities at the two contact interfaces.

(b) Construct an equilibrium band diagram (specifying the work functions of ITO and Ag, the HOMO/LUMO levels and any interfacial dipoles of PTAA and PCBM, and the perovskite band edges) that is quantitatively consistent with the experimentally observed efficient suppression of interfacial recombination in PTAA/perovskite/PCBM devices with ITO and Ag electrodes, despite the nominal work-function difference between ITO and Ag being too small to produce a V_bi close to E_g.

(c) Identify the mechanism (e.g., Fermi-level pinning, interfacial dipoles at PTAA/perovskite or PCBM/Ag interfaces, doping of the contact layers, or band bending inside the contact layers) that allows the effective V_bi seen by minority carriers to approach the value required for low interfacial recombination, and quantify the magnitude of the required dipole or pinning energy.

Let $L>0$. Consider the Korteweg–de Vries initial-boundary value problem
\[
\begin{cases}
u_t + u\, u_x + u_{xxx} = 0, & 0<x<L,\ t>0,\\
u(x,0)=\varphi(x), & 0<x<L,\\
u(0,t)=0,\quad u(L,t)=0,\quad u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t), & t>0.
\end{cases}
\]
The associated linear problem $u_t+u_{xxx}=0$ with the same boundary conditions is known to be well-posed both forward and backward in time on $L^2(0,L)$.

Question: Does there exist a real number $s$ (and an associated function space $X_T \subset C([0,T];H^s(0,L))$) such that for every initial datum $\varphi\in H^s(0,L)$ satisfying the natural compatibility conditions, there exists $T>0$ and a unique solution $u\in X_T$ of the above nonlinear problem depending continuously on $\varphi$? Equivalently, is the nonlinear initial-boundary value problem above well-posed in $H^s(0,L)$ for some $s\in\mathbb{R}$?

Consider the electroweak sector of a quantum field theory with gauge group SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y, in which electroweak symmetry is spontaneously broken to U(1)_em by the vacuum expectation value v ≈ 246 GeV of one or more complex scalar fields. Suppose a neutral CP-even scalar boson h of mass approximately 125 GeV has been observed, and that all of its currently measured couplings (to gauge bosons W, Z, to fermions, and its self-coupling where accessible) are consistent, within present experimental precision, with those predicted for the single Standard Model Higgs boson arising from a single SU(2)_L doublet Φ acquiring the vacuum expectation value v.

Address the following two questions:

(a) Is h the only fundamental scalar degree of freedom participating in electroweak symmetry breaking, i.e., does the scalar potential of the underlying theory contain only one SU(2)_L doublet whose neutral CP-even excitation is h, with no additional Higgs doublets, singlets, triplets, or other scalar multiplets contributing to electroweak symmetry breaking or mixing with h?

(b) If the scalar sector contains more than one SU(2)_L doublet (or further scalar multiplets) Φ_i with vacuum expectation values v_i satisfying Σ |v_i|^2 = v^2, is the physical mass eigenstate h exactly aligned with the direction of the total vacuum expectation value v in scalar field space — that is, is h the linear combination Σ (v_i / v) Re(Φ_i^0) with no admixture of orthogonal CP-even neutral scalar directions (the so-called exact alignment limit)?

Determine, on the basis of present and foreseeable experimental constraints together with theoretical consistency, whether (a) and (b) hold.

As of 2026, the LHC has measured Higgs couplings consistent with the Standard Model at the ~10% level, but extended scalar sectors (two-Higgs-doublet models, singlet extensions, MSSM Higgs sectors, etc.) remain viable and only constrained, not excluded. The question of whether h is the unique scalar degree of freedom and whether it is exactly aligned with v is therefore open and is an active target of HL-LHC and future-collider Higgs precision programs.

Consider the Standard Model Higgs boson h, a neutral scalar with vacuum expectation value v ≈ 246 GeV. Two hypotheses are entertained:

(a) h is a fundamental elementary scalar field.

(b) h is a composite bound state arising as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson of a spontaneously broken global symmetry of a new strongly interacting sector. In the Strongly Interacting Light Higgs (SILH) effective field theory framework, the low-energy Lagrangian for such a composite Higgs depends, to leading order, on two parameters:
   • mρ, the mass scale of the resonances of the strong sector,
   • gρ ∈ (0, 4π], the typical coupling of those resonances,
together with the dimensionless compositeness parameter
   ξ := gρ² v² / mρ².
The SILH Lagrangian predicts deviations of the Higgs couplings to Standard Model particles (e.g. to W, Z, top, bottom, photons, gluons) from their Standard Model values, with the leading deviations being functions of ξ (and, at next order, of the ratio v/mρ and gρ).

Problem.
(1) Determine whether h is elementary or composite.
(2) Assuming h is composite in the SILH sense, decide whether precision measurements of Higgs couplings — i.e. the set of ratios κi = gi^obs / gi^SM for i ranging over Standard Model particles coupling to the Higgs — suffice to identify the underlying compositeness parameters mρ, gρ, and ξ. Specifically, exhibit an explicit map from a finite set of measurable Higgs coupling ratios {κi} to (mρ, gρ, ξ), or prove that such an inversion is obstructed (e.g. by degeneracies in the leading SILH predictions), and quantify the precision required on {κi} to reconstruct ξ within a stated uncertainty.

Setting. Consider a renormalization-group (RG) flow in d-dimensional quantum field theory connecting an ultraviolet (UV) conformal field theory CFT_UV to an infrared (IR) conformal field theory CFT_IR. To such a flow one can associate:

(a) An "RG domain wall" (or RG interface): a conformal interface in the d-dimensional product theory CFT_UV × \overline{CFT_IR} (equivalently, in CFT_UV on a half-space glued to CFT_IR on the complementary half-space) obtained by triggering the relevant deformation that drives the flow only on one side and flowing to the IR there.

(b) A conformal boundary state |B⟩ of the folded theory CFT_UV × \overline{CFT_IR}, which (by the folding trick) encodes the same data as the conformal interface.

In general, given fixed UV and IR conformal endpoints, the set of conformal interfaces / boundary states between them is large and not unique: many distinct conformal boundary conditions of CFT_UV × \overline{CFT_IR} exist, and only specific ones arise as RG domain walls of an actual flow.

Question. Formulate and establish general principles (intrinsic to the data of CFT_UV, CFT_IR, and the deformation) that single out, from the full set of conformal interfaces/boundary states between CFT_UV and CFT_IR, those that are realized as the RG domain wall(s) / RG boundary state(s) of the flow. In particular, identify a characterization (e.g., variational, entropic via the boundary g-theorem, algebraic via fusion with bulk/topological defects, or representation-theoretic) that, given any candidate conformal boundary state of CFT_UV × \overline{CFT_IR}, determines whether it corresponds to the RG flow under consideration.

Question. Formulate and establish general principles (intrinsic to the data of CFT_UV, CFT_IR, and the deformation) that single out, from the full set of conformal interfaces/boundary states between CFT_UV and CFT_IR, those that are realized as the RG domain wall(s) / RG boundary state(s) of the flow. In particular, identify a characterization (e.g., variational, entropic via the boundary g-theorem, algebraic via fusion with bulk/topological defects, or representation-theoretic) that, given any candidate conformal boundary state of CFT_UV × \overline{CFT_IR}, determines whether it corresponds to the RG flow under consideration.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

No general selection principle is known. Algebraic constructions of RG domain walls have been proposed in special cases (e.g., between successive two-dimensional Virasoro minimal models, including recent work on A_2^{(p)} minimal models in 2023), and these examples reproduce conformal-perturbation-theory mixing of UV operators. However, no overarching principle determining the RG-selected interface/boundary state for general UV–IR flows has been established; the question is still listed as open in surveys of boundary and defect CFT.

Consider the Standard Model of particle physics regarded as a low-energy effective field theory valid below some high cutoff scale Λ_NP, with the Higgs boson having physical mass-squared m_h² (with m_h ≈ 125 GeV) and Planck mass-squared m_Pl² (with m_Pl ≈ 1.22 × 10^19 GeV), so that m_h²/m_Pl² ≈ 10^-34. Assume that at the scale Λ_NP there exist additional degrees of freedom coupling to the Higgs scalar; integrating them out generates radiative corrections to the Higgs mass-squared parameter of order Λ_NP², which, added to the bare parameter μ², must combine to yield the observed m_h² ≪ Λ_NP² ≤ m_Pl².

Identify and characterize a physical mechanism that naturally enforces m_h² ≪ m_Pl² without requiring a fine-tuned cancellation between the bare μ² term and the radiative contributions. The candidate mechanisms to evaluate fall into two broad classes:

(i) Symmetry-based mechanisms, in which a symmetry of the underlying theory protects the Higgs mass — for example, compositeness (the Higgs arises as a pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson of a spontaneously broken global symmetry of a new strongly coupled sector), or supersymmetry (a fermion–boson symmetry under which quadratic divergences in the scalar mass cancel between superpartners).

(ii) Dynamical mechanisms, in which the smallness of m_h² emerges from cosmological evolution — for example, a relaxion scenario in which an axion-like scalar field scans the effective Higgs mass-squared during the early universe and is dynamically stopped at a small value through a backreaction potential.

Determine whether any such mechanism is realized in nature, and identify the experimental signatures (e.g., new particles, modified Higgs couplings, or cosmological relics) that would confirm it.

Consider the Standard Model of particle physics extended, possibly, by additional degrees of freedom near the electroweak scale (around 100 GeV–1 TeV) that couple non-negligibly to the Higgs doublet Φ. In the early Universe at temperatures of order 100 GeV, the thermal effective potential V_eff(Φ, T) governs the transition between the electroweak-symmetric phase ⟨Φ⟩ = 0 and the electroweak-breaking phase ⟨Φ⟩ = v/√2 ≠ 0. Within the pure Standard Model (with the measured Higgs boson mass ≈ 125 GeV), the electroweak transition is known to be a smooth crossover.

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether the actual electroweak phase transition in the early Universe was first order, in the sense that V_eff(Φ, T_c) develops two degenerate minima separated by a barrier at some critical temperature T_c.

(b) Determine whether the transition was strongly first order in the sense
   v(T_c) / T_c ≳ 1,
where v(T_c) is the Higgs VEV in the broken minimum at T_c. (This is the standard sphaleron-decoupling condition required for successful electroweak baryogenesis, i.e., for the baryon asymmetry generated during bubble nucleation to be preserved against electroweak sphaleron washout in the broken phase.)

(c) If the transition was first order, identify the new degrees of freedom near the electroweak scale, coupled non-negligibly to the Higgs field, that are responsible for producing the barrier between the electroweak-symmetric minimum and the electroweak-breaking minimum of V_eff(Φ, T_c). Specify the mechanism (e.g., tree-level barrier from additional scalars, thermally-induced cubic terms from new bosonic states, non-perturbative dynamics from a strongly-coupled sector, or a modified Higgs potential from higher-dimensional operators) by which the barrier is generated.

Background. A boundary conformal field theory (bCFT) on a manifold with boundary is a unitary conformal field theory equipped with a conformal boundary condition. In two-dimensional bCFT, Affleck and Ludwig defined the boundary entropy g (the boundary g-function), the logarithm of the universal contribution of the boundary to the partition function on a strip; the g-theorem (proved by Friedan and Konechny) asserts that g is monotonically non-increasing along any unitary boundary renormalization group (RG) flow that preserves bulk conformal invariance, and is stationary only at boundary fixed points.

More generally, a conformal defect of dimension p in a D-dimensional CFT is a (D−p−1)-codimensional submanifold supporting a non-trivial conformal boundary condition for the ambient theory; a boundary corresponds to p = D−1.

Problem. For each pair of integers (p, D) with 1 ≤ p ≤ D−1 and (p, D) ≠ (1, 2), determine whether there exists a real-valued quantity C_{p,D}(\mathcal D), defined for every conformal defect \mathcal D of dimension p in a unitary D-dimensional CFT, such that:
(i) C_{p,D} is intrinsic to the defect (independent of the choice of bulk fixed point in any continuous family fixing \mathcal D);
(ii) C_{p,D}(\mathcal D_{UV}) ≥ C_{p,D}(\mathcal D_{IR}) for every unitary defect-localized RG flow connecting a UV defect fixed point \mathcal D_{UV} to an IR defect fixed point \mathcal D_{IR}, with equality only when the flow is trivial;
(iii) at conformal fixed points C_{p,D} reduces to a universal local quantity (e.g. a defect Weyl-anomaly coefficient, a sphere free energy, or a generalization of the boundary entropy).

In particular, for the boundary case p = D − 1 with D ≥ 3, exhibit such a monotone, or prove that no quantity satisfying (i)–(iii) exists.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Defect/boundary monotonicity theorems have been established in several cases: a defect a-theorem for 4-dimensional defects (Wang, 2021), a boundary/defect F-theorem in 3 dimensions, and more recently Casini–Salazar Landea–Torroba and Cuomo–Komargodski–Mezei–Raviv-Moshe established irreversibility of RG flows on planar defects of dimension d ≤ 4 using entanglement-entropy / QNEC methods, unifying known defect c-, F- and a-theorems. So the question is partially solved: monotones exist and are proved for defect dimensions p ≤ 4 (and conjecturally for boundaries via the b-anomaly in higher D), but a fully general all-dimensional defect c-theorem remains open.

Consider the Standard Model of particle physics extended only by allowing the Yukawa couplings of the observed Higgs boson $h$ (with mass $\approx 125\,\mathrm{GeV}$) to fermions $f$ to be complex, so that the effective Lagrangian for a fermion $f$ takes the form
$$\mathcal{L}_{hff} = -g_{hff}\,h\,\bigl[\cos(\phi_f)\,\bar f f + \sin(\phi_f)\,\bar f\, i\gamma_5 f\bigr],$$
where $g_{hff}>0$ is the magnitude of the coupling and $\phi_f\in(-\pi,\pi]$ is a CP-violating mixing angle ($\phi_f=0$ corresponds to a pure CP-even, Standard-Model-like coupling, $\phi_f=\pm\pi/2$ to a pure CP-odd coupling).

Within the framework of electroweak baryogenesis (in which the observed cosmological baryon-to-photon ratio $\eta_B \simeq 6\times 10^{-10}$ is generated at a first-order electroweak phase transition through CP-violating interactions at the bubble walls), determine the following:

(a) Can a nonzero CP-violating phase $\phi_f$ in the Higgs Yukawa couplings — in particular in the $h\tau\bar\tau$ coupling ($f=\tau$) and/or the $ht\bar t$ coupling ($f=t$) — supply a CP-violating source sufficient to generate the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe, consistently with all current experimental constraints (including bounds from the electron electric dipole moment and from LHC measurements of Higgs production and decay)?

(b) Identify experimental observables involving the CP-violating mixing angles $\phi_\tau$ and $\phi_t$ whose precision measurement at present or near-future colliders would conclusively confirm or rule out this mechanism.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question remains open. Recent analyses show that CP violation in quark Yukawa couplings is severely constrained by electron EDM bounds, but a complex τ Yukawa coupling can still by itself account for the observed baryon asymmetry within current LHC and EDM limits, while complex t or b couplings can contribute only a few percent. No experiment has yet measured a nonzero CP phase φ_τ or φ_t, and ATLAS/CMS measurements so far are consistent with φ_τ=0 with sizeable uncertainty, leaving the mechanism neither confirmed nor excluded.

Consider an extension of the Standard Model obtained by adding a single real scalar field S(x) transforming in the gauge-singlet representation (1,1)_0 under the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)_C × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y. Let H denote the Standard Model Higgs doublet, with physical Higgs mass M_h ≈ 125 GeV, and write the most general renormalizable scalar potential

  V(H, S) = μ_H^2 |H|^2 + λ_H |H|^4 + (a_1 |H|^2 S + a_2 |H|^2 S^2) + (b_1 S + b_2 S^2 + b_3 S^3 + b_4 S^4),

so that after electroweak symmetry breaking S can mix with the neutral CP-even Higgs and, if the physical singlet mass M_S satisfies M_S < M_h/2, the decay channel h → SS is kinematically open.

Address the following:

(a) Determine whether there exist light degrees of freedom that are singlets under the Standard Model gauge group — in particular, light states associated with dark matter — that mix with the Higgs sector or appear in exotic Higgs decays.

(b) Within the singlet-scalar extension above, characterize the regions of parameter space (couplings a_1, a_2, mass M_S, and Higgs–singlet mixing angle) that are compatible with current measurements of Higgs production, Higgs couplings, and direct/indirect searches for h → SS and for an additional scalar mixing with h.

(c) Identify Higgs-sector observables (signal-strength modifications, invisible or exotic Higgs branching ratios, off-shell Higgs effects, double-Higgs production) that can reveal or definitively exclude such a light singlet scalar.

Let a quantum field theory (QFT) be a conformal field theory (CFT) on a d-dimensional manifold, possibly with boundaries or with embedded submanifolds (defects). A conformal boundary condition for a CFT on a half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d-1}	imes\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is a boundary condition that preserves the subgroup of the conformal group fixing the boundary hyperplane, while a conformal defect of dimension $p<d$ is an insertion supported on a $p$-dimensional submanifold preserving the conformal subgroup fixing that submanifold.

Using modern techniques developed for boundary and defect CFT — including the conformal bootstrap (with crossing equations and unitarity bounds applied to boundary/defect channel decompositions), large-charge and large-spin expansions, the analytic structure of correlators with defects, holographic constructions of boundaries/defects in AdS, and integrability or symmetry-based constraints — address the following:

(a) Construct, or prove the existence of, previously unknown conformal boundary conditions for natural CFTs (for example, the d=3 critical Ising model, free scalar/free fermion theories in various dimensions, or four-dimensional gauge theories) beyond those already classified.

(b) Construct, or prove the existence of, previously unknown conformal defects (of various codimensions) in such theories beyond those already known.

(c) Determine whether the resulting structures (e.g., the algebra of boundaries, defects, and their fusion) suggest a qualitatively new axiomatic or constructive formulation of quantum field theory itself, distinct from the standard Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader, algebraic (Haag–Kastler), and functorial/cobordism formulations.

Produce concrete new examples or, conversely, classification/no-go results.

representations.normalized:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the Yukawa interactions between the Higgs doublet and the three generations of quarks and charged leptons give rise, after electroweak symmetry breaking, to the charged fermion mass matrices, whose diagonalization yields the observed mass eigenvalues and the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) mixing matrix V_CKM in the quark sector. The neutrino sector is described analogously by the (Majorana or Dirac) neutrino mass matrix and the Pontecorvo–Maki–Nakagawa–Sakata (PMNS) mixing matrix. Empirically:

(a) The charged fermion masses span many orders of magnitude (m_e ≪ m_μ ≪ m_τ, m_u ≪ m_c ≪ m_t, m_d ≪ m_s ≪ m_b) and the CKM mixing angles are small and hierarchical.
(b) The neutrino mass-squared splittings Δm²_{21} and |Δm²_{31}| are within two orders of magnitude of each other, and the PMNS mixing angles are all O(1) (with the exception of θ_13, which is small but not very small).
(c) Generic new physics at the TeV scale, coupling to Standard Model fermions with O(1) flavor-arbitrary couplings, would induce flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) processes (e.g., K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing, B⁰_{(s)}–B̄⁰_{(s)} mixing, μ → eγ, μ → e conversion) at rates orders of magnitude above current experimental bounds.

Provide a theoretical framework that simultaneously:

(i) Explains the smallness and hierarchical pattern of the charged fermion masses and CKM mixing angles.
(ii) Explains why the neutrino mass and mixing parameters fail to exhibit a comparable hierarchy, degeneracy, or smallness pattern.
(iii) Specifies, assuming TeV-scale new physics, the alignment and/or degeneracy mechanism by which the new physics avoids generating FCNC contributions in conflict with experimental constraints.

In addition, identify a set of observables among the Yukawa couplings y_f of the 125 GeV Higgs boson h (in particular flavor-diagonal couplings to second-generation fermions, such as h → μ⁺μ⁻ and h → cc̄) and flavor-violating Higgs decays (such as h → τμ, h → τe, h → eμ) whose measured values would discriminate among competing frameworks satisfying (i)–(iii).

Let T be the infinite unrooted binary metric tree, namely the metric graph obtained by gluing copies of the half-line so that every vertex has degree 3, and let T_o be the rooted infinite binary metric tree, where one distinguished vertex (the root) has degree 2 and every other vertex has degree 3 (all edges have length 1, say, or any fixed positive length, and the resulting graph is endowed with the natural metric and Lebesgue measure on each edge). For G ∈ {T, T_o}, let H^1(G) denote the usual Sobolev space of continuous functions on G whose restriction to each edge belongs to H^1, and define, for μ > 0, the mass-constrained space
   H^1_μ(G) := { u ∈ H^1(G) : ∫_G |u|^2 dx = μ }.
For p ∈ (2,4), define the NLS energy
   E(u, G) := (1/2) ∫_G |u'|^2 dx − (1/p) ∫_G |u|^p dx,
and the ground-state level
   L_G(μ) := inf_{u ∈ H^1_μ(G)} E(u, G).
Let
   λ_1 := inf_{u ∈ H^1(G), u ≠ 0} (∫_G |u'|^2 dx) / (∫_G |u|^2 dx)
denote the best Poincaré constant of G (which is strictly positive for both T and T_o), and define the threshold mass
   μ_G^* := max{ μ ≥ 0 : L_G(μ) = (1/2) λ_1 μ }.
Prove or disprove that μ_G^* > 0.

Let $G$ be either the rooted infinite binary metric tree $T_o$ (an infinite metric graph in which the root vertex has degree 1 and every other vertex has degree 3, with all edges of unit length) or the unrooted infinite binary metric tree $T$ (every vertex has degree 3, with unit-length edges). Functions on $G$ are defined edgewise, and $H^1(G)$ denotes the space of continuous functions on $G$ whose edgewise weak derivatives are square-integrable.

For $p \in (2,6)$ and a mass $\mu > 0$, consider the constrained minimization problem
$$L_G(\mu) := \inf\Big\{ E(u,G) : u \in H^1(G),\ \|u\|_{L^2(G)}^2 = \mu \Big\},$$
where the NLS energy is
$$E(u,G) := \tfrac{1}{2}\int_G |u'|^2\,dx - \tfrac{1}{p}\int_G |u|^p\,dx.$$
A function attaining the infimum (when finite and attained) is called a ground state of mass $\mu$.

Let $\lambda_1 = \lambda_1(G) > 0$ denote the bottom of the spectrum of the (Neumann/Kirchhoff) Laplacian on $G$, and define the threshold
$$\mu_G^* := \max\Big\{ \mu \geq 0 : L_G(\mu) = \tfrac{1}{2}\lambda_1\, \mu \Big\}.$$

Question: For the critical exponent $p = 4$, does there exist a ground state of mass $\mu = \mu_G^*$ on $G = T$ and on $G = T_o$?

Let $T_o$ be the rooted binary metric tree: a metric graph obtained by taking a root vertex $o$ and attaching, recursively, two half-edges at every vertex, so that every vertex except $o$ has degree 3 and $o$ has degree 2 (each edge is identified isometrically with an interval of $\mathbb{R}$ of fixed length). Let $T$ be the unrooted binary metric tree, in which every vertex has degree 3. For a point $x$ of $T_o$, let $|x|$ denote the geodesic distance from $x$ to $o$; for $T$, fix an arbitrary vertex $o$ and define $|x|$ analogously. A function $u \in H^1(T_o)$ (resp. $u \in H^1(T)$) is called radial if $u(x)$ depends only on $|x|$.

For $p > 2$ and a prescribed mass $\mu > 0$, consider the NLS energy
$$E(u) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\int_{T_o} |u'|^2\,dx \;-\; \tfrac{1}{p}\int_{T_o} |u|^p\,dx,$$
and the constrained minimization problem
$$\mathcal{E}(\mu) \;=\; \inf\{\, E(u) : u \in H^1(T_o),\ \|u\|_{L^2(T_o)}^2 = \mu\,\},$$
with the analogous definition on $T$. A ground state is a minimizer of this problem.

Question: Whenever a ground state exists, must it necessarily be a radial function? Equivalently, on $T_o$ or on $T$, is every NLS ground state of mass $\mu$ a function whose value at $x$ depends only on $|x|$?

Consider the sine-Gordon model on the half-line $x\le 0$ for a real scalar field $\phi(x,t)$ satisfying
$$\partial_t^2 \phi - \partial_x^2 \phi + \sin\phi = 0, \qquad x<0,\; t\in\mathbb{R},$$
with the one-parameter family of Robin boundary conditions
$$\partial_x \phi(0,t) = -2k\,\sin\!\big(\phi(0,t)/2\big), \qquad k\in\mathbb{R}.$$
For $k\notin\{0,\pm\infty\}$ this boundary condition breaks integrability (the integrable cases being the Neumann limit $k=0$ and Dirichlet-type limits).

Send in an antikink with initial velocity $v\in(0,1)$ from $x=-\infty$ and let it collide with the boundary. Record the late-time outcome (e.g.\ a reflected antikink, a kink, a kink–antikink pair, one or more breathers, breather emission accompanying a soliton, or trapping at the boundary) as a function of the pair $(v,k)$ in some chosen region of the parameter plane.

Numerical experiments reveal that the resulting outcome diagram contains regions with an extremely intricate, apparently fractal pattern of nested resonance windows.

Problem: Identify and rigorously characterize the dynamical mechanism responsible for these almost fractal structures in the late-time outcome diagram of antikink–boundary scattering for the sine-Gordon model with Robin boundary conditions. In particular, explain the origin, scaling, and self-similar organization of the nested resonance windows in terms of the internal dynamics of intermediate excitations (such as breathers or boundary-bound modes) created during the collision and their subsequent re-collision with the boundary.

Let $\mathcal{T}_o$ denote the rooted binary metric tree: a metric graph obtained by taking a root vertex $o$ and attaching, at every generation $n\ge 0$, two outgoing edges of equal length $\ell_n>0$ to each vertex of generation $n$ (so that every non-root vertex has degree $3$ and every edge length depends only on the generation). Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the unrooted binary metric tree obtained by gluing two copies of $\mathcal{T}_o$ at their roots, so that every vertex has degree $3$. In what follows let $G\in\{\mathcal{T}_o,\mathcal{T}\}$ and assume $\sum_n 2^n \ell_n=\infty$ (so $G$ is non-compact and of infinite total length).

For a function $u:G\to\mathbb{R}$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(G)$ (continuous on $G$ with edgewise weak derivative $u'\in L^2(G)$), and for a fixed exponent $p\in(2,6)$, define the NLS energy
$$E(u,G):=\tfrac12\int_G |u'(x)|^2\,dx-\tfrac1p\int_G |u(x)|^p\,dx.$$
For $\mu\ge 0$ let
$$H^1_\mu(G):=\{u\in H^1(G):\ \|u\|_{L^2(G)}^2=\mu\},$$
and call a function $u\in H^1(G)$ \emph{radial} if its value at any point $x\in G$ depends only on the distance from $x$ to the root (in the unrooted case, distance to the gluing vertex). Set
$$H^1_{\mu,r}(G):=\{u\in H^1_\mu(G):\ u\text{ is radial}\}.$$
Define the free and radial mass-constrained ground state energy levels
$$L_G(\mu):=\inf_{u\in H^1_\mu(G)} E(u,G),\qquad L_{G,r}(\mu):=\inf_{u\in H^1_{\mu,r}(G)} E(u,G).$$
The inequality $L_G(\mu)\le L_{G,r}(\mu)$ is immediate.

Question: Does the equality $L_G(\mu)=L_{G,r}(\mu)$ hold for every $\mu\ge 0$, when $G=\mathcal{T}_o$ or $G=\mathcal{T}$?

Let $\mathcal{T}_o$ denote the rooted binary metric tree: a metric graph obtained by taking a root vertex $o$ and attaching, at every generation $n\ge 0$, two outgoing edges of equal length $\ell_n>0$ to each vertex of generation $n$ (so that every non-root vertex has degree $3$ and every edge length depends only on the generation). Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the unrooted binary metric tree obtained by gluing two copies of $\mathcal{T}_o$ at their roots, so that every vertex has degree $3$. In what follows let $G\in\{\mathcal{T}_o,\mathcal{T}\}$ and assume $\sum_n 2^n \ell_n=\infty$ (so $G$ is non-compact and of infinite total length).

For a function $u:G\to\mathbb{R}$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(G)$ (continuous on $G$ with edgewise weak derivative $u'\in L^2(G)$), and for a fixed exponent $p\in(2,6)$, define the NLS energy
$$E(u,G):=\tfrac12\int_G |u'(x)|^2\,dx-\tfrac1p\int_G |u(x)|^p\,dx.$$
For $\mu\ge 0$ let
$$H^1_\mu(G):=\{u\in H^1(G):\ \|u\|_{L^2(G)}^2=\mu\},$$
and call a function $u\in H^1(G)$ \emph{radial} if its value at any point $x\in G$ depends only on the distance from $x$ to the root (in the unrooted case, distance to the gluing vertex). Set
$$H^1_{\mu,r}(G):=\{u\in H^1_\mu(G):\ u\text{ is radial}\}.$$
Define the free and radial mass-constrained ground state energy levels
$$L_G(\mu):=\inf_{u\in H^1_\mu(G)} E(u,G),\qquad L_{G,r}(\mu):=\inf_{u\in H^1_{\mu,r}(G)} E(u,G).$$
The inequality $L_G(\mu)\le L_{G,r}(\mu)$ is immediate.

Question: Does the equality $L_G(\mu)=L_{G,r}(\mu)$ hold for every $\mu\ge 0$, when $G=\mathcal{T}_o$ or $G=\mathcal{T}$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is posed as an open problem in the work introducing this framework; subsequent literature on NLS on metric trees (e.g., later works by Adami, Dovetta, Serra and collaborators on noncompact metric graphs and trees) does not appear to resolve whether the unrestricted and radial ground-state energy levels coincide on binary metric trees. No published proof of equality (or of strict inequality) was found.

Let $\{X(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ be a continuous-time, irreducible, finite-state Markov chain on a state space $S=\{1,\dots,n\}$ with generator matrix $Q$ and unique stationary distribution $\pi$. Let $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ with $\lambda_i\ge 0$ and at least one $\lambda_i>0$. Conditional on the trajectory of $X(\cdot)$, let $N(\cdot)$ be an inhomogeneous Poisson process with instantaneous rate $\lambda_{X(t)}$; the pair $(X(\cdot),N(\cdot))$ is called an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP). Let $0<T_1<T_2<\dots$ denote the event epochs of $N$, and let $T_k^\alpha=T_k-T_{k-1}$ (with $T_0=0$) denote the inter-event times under the event-stationary distribution (the Palm distribution at event epochs, equivalently the stationary distribution of the embedded chain $X(T_k-)$ at event times). Define the squared coefficient of variation
$$c^2 \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Var}(T_1^\alpha)}{(\mathbb{E}[T_1^\alpha])^2}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every irreducible MMPP, $c^2 \ge 1$.

Consider the sine-Gordon equation
  u_{tt} − u_{xx} + sin(u) = 0
posed on the quarter-plane Q = {(x,t) : x < 0, t > 0}, with prescribed initial data u(x,0), u_t(x,0) for x ≤ 0 and a boundary condition imposed at x = 0 of Robin type
  u_x(0,t) + 2 M sin(u(0,t)/2) = 0, t ≥ 0,
where M ∈ ℝ is a real parameter. For generic M the boundary condition breaks the bulk integrability of the sine-Gordon equation, while distinguished values of M (including M = 0 and the integrable Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov family) preserve infinite hierarchies of conserved quantities.

The Fokas (unified transform) method represents the solution of the sine-Gordon equation on Q via a matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem whose jump matrices are built from four spectral functions associated with the initial and boundary data, related through a global relation.

Develop the unified transform / Fokas approach to extract residual or asymptotic integrability of the sine-Gordon equation on the quarter-plane with Robin boundary conditions of the above form, and use it to analyze quantitatively how the boundary induces breaking of integrability. Specifically:
  (a) Formulate the matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem corresponding to the Robin boundary condition above and derive the corresponding global relation between the spectral functions determined by the initial data and those determined by the boundary data.
  (b) Identify, via this Riemann–Hilbert / global-relation framework, those features of the dynamics (e.g. soliton trajectories, reflection coefficients, infinite families of approximately conserved charges, long-time asymptotics on rays x/t = const) that remain controllable for general Robin parameter M, and quantify the obstruction to full integrability when M is generic.
  (c) Determine the long-time asymptotic behaviour of u(x,t) on Q for generic Robin M, including the leading dispersive contribution and any soliton/breather content reflected from the boundary.

The Fokas/unified-transform analysis of the sine-Gordon equation on the quarter-plane has been substantially developed: a Riemann–Hilbert formulation and global relation are available, nonlinear Fourier transforms and long-time asymptotics have been studied (Its, Kotlyarov, Lenells and others), and Robin-type boundary conditions breaking integrability have been analyzed perturbatively. Let $\{J(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ be an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with generator matrix $Q$ and unique stationary distribution $\pi$. Let $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ with $\lambda_i\ge 0$ and $\sum_i \pi_i\lambda_i>0$. Conditional on the trajectory of $J$, let $N$ be an inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity $\lambda_{J(t)}$ at time $t$. The pair $(J,N)$ is the (irreducible) Markov-modulated Poisson process (MMPP).

Two natural stationary initializations of the MMPP on $\mathbb{R}$ are:
- The time-stationary version: the law under which the joint process $(J(t),N)$ is invariant under time shifts; equivalently, $J(0)$ is distributed according to $\pi$. Let $T_1^\pi$ denote the time from $0$ to the first event of $N$ after $0$ under this law.
- The event-stationary (Palm) version: the law obtained by Palm-conditioning on an event of $N$ at time $0$; equivalently, $J(0)$ is distributed according to $\alpha$, where $\alpha_i = \pi_i\lambda_i / \sum_j \pi_j\lambda_j$. Let $T_1^\alpha$ denote the time from $0$ to the next event of $N$ after $0$ under this law.

Prove or disprove: for every irreducible MMPP,
$$T_1^\pi \ge_{\mathrm{st}} T_1^\alpha,$$
i.e. $\Pr(T_1^\pi > t) \ge \Pr(T_1^\alpha > t)$ for all $t\ge 0$.

Consider the tricritical Ising minimal model, the unitary Virasoro minimal model M(4,5) with central charge c = 7/10, and analogous rational two-dimensional conformal field theories that admit extended chiral or superconformal symmetry algebras (for example, an N=1 super-Virasoro algebra, a W-algebra, or a coset extension of the Virasoro algebra). A conformal defect on the cylinder is a line operator that commutes with the diagonal Virasoro generators L_n − \bar L_{-n} but need not commute with L_n + \bar L_{-n}. Such a defect is called:
  • topological if it commutes with both holomorphic and antiholomorphic stress tensors (equivalently, it is fully transmissive);
  • factorizing if it is a tensor product of a conformal boundary state with its conjugate (equivalently, it is fully reflective);
  • non-topological and non-factorizing otherwise.

Equivalently, by the folding trick, a conformal defect in a CFT C corresponds to a conformal boundary condition of the doubled theory C ⊗ \bar C, and a topological (resp. factorizing) defect corresponds to a boundary preserving the full diagonal (resp. fully decoupled) chiral algebra.

Question: Develop a systematic construction principle whereby boundary states of C ⊗ \bar C that preserve only an extended chiral or superconformal subalgebra of the full chiral symmetry — but not the full chiral algebra of C ⊗ \bar C — yield genuinely new conformal defects of C that are neither topological nor factorizing. Concretely:

(a) For the tricritical Ising model, exhibit conformal defects obtained by imposing gluing conditions for an extended (e.g. N=1 superconformal or coset) chiral algebra on the folded theory, and prove that the resulting defects are not expressible as superpositions of topological defects and factorizing defects.

(b) Compute their reflection and transmission coefficients and verify 0 < T < 1.

(c) Extend the construction to a broader family of rational CFTs (e.g. other unitary Virasoro minimal models, super-Virasoro minimal models, or WZW models) and characterize when extended-algebra-preserving boundary states of the doubled theory produce new non-topological, non-factorizing conformal defects.

Let $N = (N_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a Cox process (doubly stochastic Poisson process) on the real line, that is, a point process which, conditional on a non-negative stochastic intensity process $\Lambda = (\Lambda_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$, is an inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity $\Lambda$. Assume that $\Lambda$ is stationary and ergodic with finite, strictly positive mean rate $\lambda = \mathbb{E}[\Lambda_0] \in (0,\infty)$, together with whatever further regularity conditions (e.g.\ integrability and mixing) are needed to make the constructions below well defined.

Associated to $N$ are two canonical inter-event-time distributions:

(a) The time-stationary first inter-event time $T^\ast$: under the time-stationary (Palm-with-respect-to-Lebesgue) law, $T^\ast$ is the waiting time from an arbitrary deterministic time origin until the next event of $N$.

(b) The event-stationary inter-event time $T$: under the Palm distribution of $N$ (the law of the process as seen from a typical event), $T$ is the time between two consecutive events.

Prove or disprove the following two statements for every such Cox process satisfying the regularity assumptions:

1. The squared coefficient of variation of $T$ satisfies
$$\mathrm{CV}^2(T) \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Var}(T)}{(\mathbb{E}[T])^2} \;\geq\; 1.$$

2. The time-stationary first inter-event time stochastically dominates the event-stationary inter-event time, i.e.
$$\mathbb{P}(T^\ast > t) \;\geq\; \mathbb{P}(T > t) \qquad \text{for all } t \geq 0.$$

Consider a four-dimensional conformal field theory (specifically, a setup of AdS/dCFT type in which a half-BPS codimension-one defect supports a three-dimensional defect theory) in the presence of a flat planar boundary or codimension-one defect. In such a defect conformal field theory the basic bootstrap data include: (i) bulk one-point functions ⟨O(x)⟩ = a_O / (2 x_⊥)^{Δ_O}, where x_⊥ is the distance to the defect and Δ_O is the scaling dimension of the bulk operator O; and (ii) bulk two-point functions ⟨O_1(x) O_2(y)⟩ which, by conformal symmetry preserved by the defect, depend on a single cross-ratio and admit two channel decompositions — a bulk channel into bulk operators and a defect channel into operators living on the three-dimensional defect — whose equality gives the boundary/defect conformal bootstrap equations.

Develop a systematic framework that uses the one- and two-point function data {a_O} and the bulk-to-defect couplings as input to the boundary/defect conformal bootstrap equations, sufficient to constrain or determine the spectrum and OPE coefficients of the three-dimensional defect theory. Concretely:

(a) Identify the structural data of the three-dimensional defect CFT (operator content, symmetries, OPE coefficients, possible integrability or supersymmetry constraints) needed so that the crossing equations relating bulk and defect channels become a closed, solvable system.

(b) Show how to combine these inputs with the bulk-channel decomposition to extract nontrivial bootstrap constraints on this defect theory, and demonstrate the procedure on the half-BPS codimension-one defect in the relevant AdS/dCFT example.

Concretely:

(a) Identify the structural data of the three-dimensional defect CFT (operator content, symmetries, OPE coefficients, possible integrability or supersymmetry constraints) needed so that the crossing equations relating bulk and defect channels become a closed, solvable system.

(b) Show how to combine these inputs with the bulk-channel decomposition to extract nontrivial bootstrap constraints on this defect theory, and demonstrate the procedure on the half-BPS codimension-one defect in the relevant AdS/dCFT example.

Let L^2(R) denote the Hilbert space of square-integrable complex-valued functions on the real line, equipped with its usual norm. For ψ ∈ L^2(R) and integers j, k ∈ Z, define the dyadic dilates and integer translates

  ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k),  x ∈ R.

A function ψ ∈ L^2(R) is called an orthonormal wavelet if the family {ψ_{j,k} : j, k ∈ Z} is an orthonormal basis of L^2(R). Every orthonormal wavelet has unit L^2-norm, so the set W of all orthonormal wavelets is naturally a subset of the unit sphere of L^2(R).

Question: Is W path-connected in the L^2(R) norm? That is, given any two orthonormal wavelets ψ_0, ψ_1 ∈ W, does there exist a map Ψ : [0,1] → L^2(R), continuous with respect to the L^2 norm, such that Ψ(0) = ψ_0, Ψ(1) = ψ_1, and Ψ(t) is an orthonormal wavelet for every t ∈ [0,1]?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The path-connectivity of the set of all orthonormal wavelets in L^2(R) is a long-standing open question (often attributed to the Wutam Consortium). Partial results are known: the MSF (minimally supported frequency) wavelets and s-elementary wavelets form path-connected subsets, and path-connectivity has been established for various subclasses such as MRA wavelets and MRA Parseval wavelets. A conjecture of Rzeszotnik asserts that orthonormal wavelets with a fixed dimension function form a path-connected set, but this remains open in full generality. No proof of (dis)connectivity for the entire set W has been published.

Consider the defect conformal field theory obtained from the D3–D5 brane intersection in type IIB string theory: a stack of N D3-branes ending on a single D5-brane that wraps an AdS$_4 \times S^2$ submanifold of AdS$_5 \times S^5$, with $k$ units of background magnetic flux through the $S^2$. The dual gauge theory is $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills on $\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ with a codimension-one defect across which the gauge group rank jumps by $k$, and three of the six adjoint scalars acquire $x_3$-dependent classical expectation values determined by an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ representation of dimension $k$. Local single-trace gauge-invariant operators $\mathcal{O}(x)$ in this background have nonvanishing one-point functions of the form
$$ \langle \mathcal{O}(x) \rangle = \frac{C_{\mathcal{O}}}{x_3^{\Delta_{\mathcal{O}}}}, $$
where $\Delta_{\mathcal{O}}$ is the scaling dimension of $\mathcal{O}$.

On the string-theory side, one-point functions of $\tfrac{1}{2}$-BPS (protected) operators have been computed by evaluating classical supergravity fields, sourced by the probe D5-brane, against the appropriate bulk-to-boundary propagators. For non-protected (non-BPS) operators, however, no such gravity computation suffices, and a genuine worldsheet string computation is required.

Problem. Develop a worldsheet string-theoretic prescription, in the D3–D5 probe-brane background of AdS$_5 \times S^5$, that computes the holographic one-point function coefficient $C_{\mathcal{O}}$ for a non-protected single-trace operator $\mathcal{O}$ (for example, an operator dual to a massive string state outside the supergravity spectrum), and use it to obtain $C_{\mathcal{O}}$ at strong 't Hooft coupling for at least one such non-protected operator. Match the result, where applicable, with the integrability-based gauge-theory predictions expressed as overlaps of Bethe eigenstates with a matrix product state.

Let $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Hilbert space of square-integrable complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$ with the standard norm $\|\cdot\|_{L^2}$. For $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and integers $j,k \in \mathbb{Z}$, define the dyadic translation–dilation
$$\psi_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2}\,\psi(2^j x - k), \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}.$$
Call $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ a Parseval wavelet if the system $\{\psi_{j,k} : j,k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is a Parseval frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, i.e.
$$\sum_{j,k \in \mathbb{Z}} |\langle f, \psi_{j,k}\rangle|^2 = \|f\|_{L^2}^2 \qquad \text{for every } f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}).$$
Let $\mathcal{P} \subset L^2(\mathbb{R})$ be the set of all Parseval wavelets, equipped with the metric inherited from the $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ norm.

Question: Is $\mathcal{P}$ path connected? Equivalently, given any two Parseval wavelets $\psi_0, \psi_1 \in \mathcal{P}$, does there exist a continuous map $\gamma: [0,1] \to (L^2(\mathbb{R}), \|\cdot\|_{L^2})$ with $\gamma(0) = \psi_0$, $\gamma(1) = \psi_1$, and $\gamma(t) \in \mathcal{P}$ for all $t \in [0,1]$?

Consider the holographic dual of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills theory at large $N$, namely type IIB string theory on $\mathrm{AdS}_5\times S^5$. In the supergravity (large 't Hooft coupling) limit, four-point functions of half-BPS single-trace operators admit a $1/N^2$ expansion whose successive orders correspond to tree-level, one-loop, two-loop, ... Witten diagrams in the bulk. Three complementary techniques have been developed to access the one-loop (and higher-loop) order:

(a) An analytic conformal bootstrap approach, in which crossing symmetry, the Lorentzian inversion formula, and the structure of the double-trace anomalous-dimension spectrum are used to fix the loop-level correlators up to a finite number of contact-term ambiguities.

(b) Direct computation of one-loop Witten diagrams in $\mathrm{AdS}_5\times S^5$ using bulk Feynman rules together with the spectral/Mellin representation.

(c) Integrability-based methods (e.g. the hexagon form-factor program, octagons, and integrated correlators tied to localization), which compute correlators or specific integrated observables exactly in the planar coupling.

Problem. Develop a unified framework that combines the analytic-bootstrap method (a) with either the direct one-loop Witten-diagram computation (b) or the integrability-based approach (c), in such a way that:

  (i) the contact-term and other crossing-symmetric ambiguities left undetermined by the analytic bootstrap are fixed by inputs from (b) or (c);
  (ii) results obtained by each approach provide independent, mutually consistent checks of the others; and
  (iii) the framework extends to higher loops and to half-BPS operators of arbitrary Kaluza–Klein weight on $S^5$.

Concretely, exhibit such a combined procedure (or prove an obstruction to it) and use it to determine the one-loop four-point function of four half-BPS single-trace operators in $\mathrm{AdS}_5\times S^5$ supergravity, including all contact-term coefficients, in agreement with both bulk Witten-diagram computations and integrability/localization predictions.

$$A \sum_{n} |c_n|^2 \;\le\; \Big\| \sum_n c_n e_n \Big\|_H^2 \;\le\; B \sum_n |c_n|^2$$

Let $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ be a Parseval wavelet, that is, the family $\{\psi_{j,k} : j,k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ defined by
$$\psi_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2}\psi(2^j x - k)$$
satisfies
$$\sum_{j,k \in \mathbb{Z}} |\langle f, \psi_{j,k}\rangle|^2 = \|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})}^2 \quad \text{for every } f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}).$$
Define the space of negative dilates of $\psi$ by
$$V(\psi) := \overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\psi_{j,k} : j < 0,\ k \in \mathbb{Z}\} \subseteq L^2(\mathbb{R}),$$
and let $D : L^2(\mathbb{R}) \to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the dyadic dilation operator $(Df)(x) = \sqrt{2}\, f(2x)$. Determine whether
$$\bigcap_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} D^j\bigl(V(\psi)\bigr) = \{0\}$$
holds for every Parseval wavelet $\psi$.

Background and setup. Let M be a closed oriented Riemannian 2n-manifold. A quasi Riemann surface Q(M) is, informally, a higher-dimensional analogue of an ordinary Riemann surface built from M, in which the role of meromorphic functions is played by certain "harmonic" data on M and which is locally probed by maps from a complex disk that play the role of holomorphic curves in M. More precisely, fix the unit disk Σ ⊂ ℂ. A local quasi-holomorphic curve into Q(M) is a smooth one-parameter family of geometric data on M (for example, a family of currents, harmonic forms, or sections of an appropriate bundle over M) parametrized by Σ that satisfies a Cauchy–Riemann–type equation on Q(M), so that its pullback represents the local function theory of Q(M) as ordinary meromorphic-function theory on Σ.

Problem. Take M = S^{2n} (the round 2n-sphere, identified with ℝ^{2n} ∪ {∞}). Construct explicit families of local quasi-holomorphic curves f : Σ → Q(S^{2n}) — i.e., write down concrete representatives of such Cauchy–Riemann solutions, parametrized by the unit disk (or by the Riemann sphere) — sufficient to exhibit and study the local conformal-field-theoretic structure on Q(S^{2n}). Equivalently, give an explicit local parametrization of the quasi-holomorphic curves through a basepoint of Q(S^{2n}) and describe the induced ordinary meromorphic function theory on Σ.

  ψ_{j,k}(x) := 2^{j/2} ψ(2^j x − k),  j, k ∈ ℤ.

Call ψ a Bessel wavelet with bound d if there exists a finite constant d > 0 such that

  ∑_{j,k ∈ ℤ} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|² ≤ d ‖f‖²  for every f ∈ L²(ℝ).

  ∑_{j,k ∈ ℤ} |⟨f, ψ_{j,k}⟩|² = ‖f‖²  for every f ∈ L²(ℝ).

is a Parseval frame for L²(ℝ)?

A quasi Riemann surface is a higher-dimensional generalization of a Riemann surface designed so that two-dimensional conformal field theory data can be transported to higher-dimensional defect settings: it is equipped with analogues of complex structure, holomorphic differentials, period pairings, and a notion of conformal/biholomorphic equivalence sufficient to support correlators of local insertions and extended defects. On such a quasi Riemann surface, develop higher-dimensional analogues of the standard two-dimensional CFT constructions, namely:

(a) Orbifolding: given a CFT on a quasi Riemann surface together with a global symmetry group G acting on it, formulate a consistent gauging procedure that produces a new theory, including the prescription of twisted sectors, modular-invariant (or appropriately covariant) partition functions, and operator content; and

(b) Perturbation theory: given a CFT on a quasi Riemann surface, formulate a deformation by a (quasi-)marginal operator and prove existence of, and compute, perturbative corrections to correlators and to the spectrum of defect operators.

Show that these two constructions, when applied on quasi Riemann surfaces, generate genuinely new conformal theories describing higher-dimensional defects, and identify the resulting families of defect CFTs.

A quasi Riemann surface is a higher-dimensional generalization of a Riemann surface designed so that two-dimensional conformal field theory data can be transported to higher-dimensional defect settings: it is equipped with analogues of complex structure, holomorphic differentials, period pairings, and a notion of conformal/biholomorphic equivalence sufficient to support correlators of local insertions and extended defects. On such a quasi Riemann surface, develop higher-dimensional analogues of the standard two-dimensional CFT constructions, namely:

(a) Orbifolding: given a CFT on a quasi Riemann surface together with a global symmetry group G acting on it, formulate a consistent gauging procedure that produces a new theory, including the prescription of twisted sectors, modular-invariant (or appropriately covariant) partition functions, and operator content; and

(b) Perturbation theory: given a CFT on a quasi Riemann surface, formulate a deformation by a (quasi-)marginal operator and prove existence of, and compute, perturbative corrections to correlators and to the spectrum of defect operators.

Show that these two constructions, when applied on quasi Riemann surfaces, generate genuinely new conformal theories describing higher-dimensional defects, and identify the resulting families of defect CFTs.
