Consider linear control systems of the form
  ẋ(t) = Ax(t) + Bu(t),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach (or Hilbert) space, A : D(A) ⊂ X → X generates a strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} on X, and B ∈ L(U, X_{-1}) is a (possibly unbounded) admissible input operator with U a Banach space and X_{-1} the extrapolation space associated with A. Inputs u are taken from L^∞_loc([0,∞); U).

Such a system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that, for every x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})  for all t ≥ 0.

It is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and θ, μ ∈ K_∞ such that
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + θ(∫₀^t μ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds)  for all t ≥ 0.

Provide a complete structural characterization of the relationship between ISS and iISS for this class of linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded admissible input operators B. Specifically, determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of (A, B, X, U), under which ISS implies iISS, under which iISS implies ISS, and identify the precise gap between the two notions in this setting (going beyond isolated examples and counterexamples to a general theory).

Consider control systems of the form
  x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  x(0) = x_0,
on a Banach space X, where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup and B: U → X_{-1} is a (possibly unbounded) admissible input operator from a Banach space U of input values; admissible inputs u belong to L^∞(0,∞;U). Let β denote the class of KL-functions and let K, K_∞, P denote the standard comparison-function classes.

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that, for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})  for all t ≥ 0.

It is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL, θ ∈ K_∞ and μ ∈ K such that
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + θ( ∫_0^t μ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds )  for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous functional V: X → [0,∞) is called an ISS-Lyapunov function if it satisfies coercive bounds ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖) with ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞, and an appropriate dissipation inequality of ISS type along trajectories; an iISS-Lyapunov function satisfies analogous bounds with an iISS dissipation inequality. Every ISS-Lyapunov function is automatically an iISS-Lyapunov function.

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional control system of the above form, with an unbounded input operator B, that is integral input-to-state stable but not input-to-state stable? If such a system exists, quantify in what precise sense its existence reveals limitations of the Lyapunov-function approach to verifying ISS for systems with unbounded input operators, and characterize how severe these limitations are (e.g., whether iISS-Lyapunov functions can fail to detect the absence of ISS, and to what extent the Lyapunov method remains a complete tool for ISS in this setting).

Consider control systems of the form
  x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),  x(0) = x_0,
on a Banach space X, where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup and B: U → X_{-1} is a (possibly unbounded) admissible input operator from a Banach space U of input values; admissible inputs u belong to L^∞(0,∞;U). Let β denote the class of KL-functions and let K, K_∞, P denote the standard comparison-function classes.

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that, for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})  for all t ≥ 0.

It is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL, θ ∈ K_∞ and μ ∈ K such that
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + θ( ∫_0^t μ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds )  for all t ≥ 0.

A continuous functional V: X → [0,∞) is called an ISS-Lyapunov function if it satisfies coercive bounds ψ_1(‖x‖) ≤ V(x) ≤ ψ_2(‖x‖) with ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞, and an appropriate dissipation inequality of ISS type along trajectories; an iISS-Lyapunov function satisfies analogous bounds with an iISS dissipation inequality. Every ISS-Lyapunov function is automatically an iISS-Lyapunov function.

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional control system of the above form, with an unbounded input operator B, that is integral input-to-state stable but not input-to-state stable? If such a system exists, quantify in what precise sense its existence reveals limitations of the Lyapunov-function approach to verifying ISS for systems with unbounded input operators, and characterize how severe these limitations are (e.g., whether iISS-Lyapunov functions can fail to detect the absence of ISS, and to what extent the Lyapunov method remains a complete tool for ISS in this setting).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent literature (2024–2025) on ISS/iISS for infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators continues to develop coercive and noncoercive ISS-Lyapunov methods, generalized ISS-Lyapunov functionals, and iISS-Lyapunov constructions for parabolic/hyperbolic PDEs with boundary disturbances. None of the surveyed works exhibits an iISS but not ISS infinite-dimensional system with unbounded B, nor rules it out; the question of whether such systems exist (and what limitations of the Lyapunov method this would entail) is still treated as an open problem in current surveys and tutorials.

Consider an abstract control system $\Sigma = (X, \mathcal{U}, \phi)$ where $(X, \|\cdot\|_X)$ is a Banach space (the state space), $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed vector space of admissible input functions $u : \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \to U$ with values in a normed space $U$, and $\phi : D_\phi \subset \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \times X \times \mathcal{U} \to X$ is a transition map satisfying the usual axioms (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity).

Recall the standard comparison-function classes: $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\mathcal{L}$, and $\mathcal{KL}$.

The system $\Sigma$ is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\alpha, \gamma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for all $x \in X$, all admissible $u \in \mathcal{U}$, and all $t \geq 0$,
$$\alpha(\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X) \leq \beta(\|x\|_X, t) + \int_0^t \gamma(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds.$$

A continuous function $V : X \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $V(0)=0$ is called a coercive iISS Lyapunov function if there exist $\psi_1, \psi_2 \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ (or positive definite), and $\sigma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
$$\psi_1(\|x\|_X) \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X), \qquad \dot V_u(x) \leq -\alpha(\|x\|_X) + \sigma(\|u\|_U),$$
where $\dot V_u$ denotes an appropriate (Dini or Lie) derivative of $V$ along trajectories. Dropping the lower bound $\psi_1(\|x\|_X) \leq V(x)$ (so only $0 \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X)$ is required) yields a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function candidate.

Develop a theory of non-coercive integral input-to-state Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems of the above type. Specifically:

(a) Identify the appropriate definition (or definitions) of a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function for $\Sigma$.

(b) Establish their basic properties (existence, regularity, behaviour along trajectories, relations to coercive iISS Lyapunov functions, and converse-Lyapunov style results).

(c) Prove sufficient conditions under which the existence of a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function implies that $\Sigma$ is iISS, and identify minimal additional regularity hypotheses (e.g., on the semigroup, well-posedness, or admissibility of the input operator) needed for such an implication.

Non-coercive Lyapunov function theory for infinite-dimensional systems has been substantially developed since 2019 (Mironchenko–Wirth, JDE 2019; SIAM J. Control Optim. 2020), extending to ISS and to certain iISS/LISS settings via norm-to-integral ISS characterizations and constructions for time-varying semilinear evolution equations. However, a fully developed theory of non-coercive iISS Lyapunov functions with general converse results matching the coercive case does not yet appear in the literature; recent works (e.g., 2025 papers on coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular systems and 2025 time-varying evolution equation results) treat related but partial settings. The problem is therefore best classified as partially solved.

Consider control systems on Banach spaces of the form
  ẋ = A x + f(x, u),
where A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on a Banach space X, u is an input from a function space U, and the resulting evolution is well-posed.

Such a system is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist a class-KL function β and class-K functions α, γ such that for every initial state x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u, the solution x(·) satisfies
  α(‖x(t)‖_X) ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + ∫₀ᵗ γ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds   for all t ≥ 0.

Now consider a feedback interconnection of two (or finitely many) such infinite-dimensional iISS subsystems
  ẋ_i = A_i x_i + f_i(x_1, …, x_n, u),   i = 1, …, n,
in which the "inputs" of subsystem i include the states x_j of the other subsystems plus an external input u.

Develop a substantial theory for such interconnections of infinite-dimensional iISS systems. In particular:

(a) Formulate sharp small-gain conditions on the iISS gain functions γ_{ij} (governing the influence of x_j on x_i) that guarantee iISS of the overall interconnected system on the product space X_1 × … × X_n.

(b) Provide a systematic coupling theory for infinite-dimensional iISS subsystems, including Lyapunov-based and trajectory-based criteria, that parallels and substantially extends the existing interconnection theory available for finite-dimensional iISS systems and for infinite-dimensional ISS systems.

The task is to establish such small-gain theorems and coupling criteria with the same level of completeness already achieved for ISS interconnections in the infinite-dimensional setting.

Several partial results exist: iISS small-gain theorems for two interconnected distributed-parameter systems and constructions of iISS Lyapunov functions for interconnected parabolic PDEs have been established, and recent works extend ISS small-gain theorems to infinite networks of heterogeneous infinite-dimensional systems. Consider a bilinear control system on a Banach space $X$ of the form
$$\dot x(t) = A x(t) + B(u(t), x(t)), \qquad x(0) = x_0 \in X,$$
where $A : D(A) \subset X \to X$ is the generator of a strongly continuous semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $X$, $u \in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty); U)$ is an input from a Banach space $U$, and $B : U \times X \to X_{-1}$ is a continuous bilinear map taking values in the extrapolation space $X_{-1}$ associated with $A$ (so that $B$ is, in general, an unbounded bilinear operator with respect to the state space $X$). Mild solutions are defined in $X_{-1}$ and assumed to belong to $X$ for all $t\ge 0$.

The system is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\theta, \mu \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x_0 \in X$ and every admissible input $u$,
$$\|x(t)\|_X \le \beta(\|x_0\|_X, t) + \theta\!\left(\int_0^t \mu(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds\right), \qquad t \ge 0.$$

Develop a systematic integral input-to-state stability theory for such bilinear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded bilinear operators $B$. In particular:

(a) Provide verifiable sufficient conditions on $A$, $B$, $X$, and $U$ ensuring that the system is iISS.
(b) Characterize iISS in terms of qualitative properties such as 0-uniform global asymptotic stability and suitable Lyapunov-type functions adapted to the unbounded setting.
(c) Identify a class of admissible inputs (e.g., subspaces of $L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}$ guaranteeing well-posedness) for which the theory is consistent, and apply the resulting criteria to representative PDE examples with boundary or otherwise unbounded bilinear control.

Significant progress has been made: Hosfeld, Jacob, and Schwenninger (Math. Control Signals Systems, 2022; arXiv:1811.08470) established iISS results for unbounded bilinear control systems on Hilbert spaces, including sufficient conditions and applications such as a bilinearly controlled Fokker–Planck equation. Background and definitions. Consider an infinite-dimensional control system

  ẋ(t) = F(x(t), u(t)),  x(t) ∈ X,  u ∈ U_c,

where X is a Banach state space, U_c is a space of admissible input functions u : [0,∞) → U taking values in a normed input space U (for instance L^∞_loc([0,∞); U)), and F generates a well-posed semiflow φ(t, x, u) with φ(0, x, u) = x. Denote by K the class of continuous, strictly increasing functions α : [0,∞) → [0,∞) with α(0) = 0; by K_∞ the subclass of unbounded such functions; and by KL the class of continuous β : [0,∞)² → [0,∞) such that β(·, t) ∈ K for each t and β(r, t) ↓ 0 as t → ∞.

Recall:
• The system is input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every x ∈ X and admissible u,
  ‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)  for all t ≥ 0.
• The system is integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and α, γ ∈ K_∞ such that
  α(‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X) ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + ∫_0^t γ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds  for all t ≥ 0.
• Following the finite-dimensional definition, call the system strongly iISS if it is iISS and additionally ISS with respect to small inputs, i.e. there exist β ∈ KL, γ ∈ K, and a constant R > 0 such that for all admissible u with ‖u‖_∞ ≤ R,
  ‖φ(t, x, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_∞)  for all t ≥ 0, x ∈ X.

Problem. Develop a theory of strong iISS for such infinite-dimensional control systems. In particular:
(a) Establish equivalent Lyapunov-function characterizations of strong iISS (e.g. the existence of a smooth iISS-Lyapunov function whose dissipation rate is positive definite, together with a small-input ISS condition).
(b) Determine the precise relationship of strong iISS to ISS, iISS, and to the existence of asymptotic gains, including whether strong iISS is strictly stronger than iISS and strictly weaker than ISS in the infinite-dimensional setting.
(c) Prove or disprove that strong iISS is preserved under cascade interconnection of infinite-dimensional systems and analyze its behaviour under feedback and small-gain interconnections.
(d) Identify nontrivial classes of infinite-dimensional systems (e.g. linear systems with unbounded admissible input operators, semilinear evolution equations, bilinear control systems on Hilbert spaces) for which strong iISS can be verified, and provide checkable sufficient conditions in these classes.

Subsequent research has begun to develop strong iISS / strong ISS notions in infinite dimensions. Works on characterizations of ISS and iISS for infinite-dimensional and non-autonomous systems (e.g. Mironchenko-Wirth and follow-ups, and the 2022 characterization of integral ISS for time-varying systems of infinite dimension) have produced partial results, including Lyapunov-type characterizations and preservation under cascades, but a full systematic theory matching the finite-dimensional strong iISS framework does not yet appear complete in the literature.

Consider a control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$ where $X$ is a Banach space (the state space), $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to U$ (with $U$ a normed input-value space), and $\phi:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\times X\times\mathcal{U}\to X$ is a transition map satisfying the standard axioms of a forward-complete control system (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity in initial state). Equip the system with an output map $h:X\times U\to Y$ taking values in a Banach output space $Y$; write $H(t,x,u):=h(\phi(t,x,u),u(t))$.

Recall the standard comparison-function classes: $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\mathcal{L}$, and $\mathcal{KL}$. The system $(\Sigma,h)$ is called input-to-output stable (IOS) if there exist $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x\in X$, every $u\in\mathcal{U}$, and every $t\geq 0$,
$$\|H(t,x,u)\|_Y \;\leq\; \beta(\|x\|_X,t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}).$$

Develop a theory of input-to-output stability for such infinite-dimensional systems with outputs that parallels the finite-dimensional IOS theory. In particular, address the following:

1. (Superposition / characterization theorem.) Identify weaker stability-like properties (analogues of output asymptotic gain, output Lagrange stability, output limit property, output continuity at the equilibrium, etc.) whose conjunction is equivalent to IOS, and determine which combinations are sufficient versus insufficient in the infinite-dimensional setting.

2. (Lyapunov characterizations.) Define an appropriate notion of IOS Lyapunov function $V:X\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ involving the output norm $\|h(x,u)\|_Y$, and prove that the existence of such a function is equivalent (or, where this fails, obtain the strongest possible implications) to IOS.

3. (Structural / small-gain results.) Establish small-gain theorems for feedback interconnections and (possibly infinite) networks of IOS subsystems on Banach spaces, giving verifiable conditions on the gain operators that guarantee IOS of the interconnection.

Provide the criteria, Lyapunov tools, and structural results, and identify intrinsic obstructions specific to the infinite-dimensional case (e.g., examples showing classical finite-dimensional equivalences fail).

representations.normalized:
Background and setup. Consider control systems of the form
    x'(t) = F(x(t), u(t)),  t > 0,  x(0) = x_0,
where the state x(t) takes values in a Banach space X, the input u belongs to the space U_c := L^∞(R_+, U) of essentially bounded measurable functions with values in a normed space U, and F generates (for each fixed input) a possibly nonlinear evolution. A typical existing framework treats the semilinear case
    x'(t) = A x(t) + f(x(t), u(t)),
where A generates a strongly continuous (linear) semigroup on X and f satisfies suitable Lipschitz/boundedness conditions.

A system Σ with state space X and input space U_c is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every initial state x_0 ∈ X, every admissible input u ∈ U_c, and all t ≥ 0,
    ‖x(t; x_0, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)}),
where K denotes continuous strictly increasing functions [0,∞) → [0,∞) vanishing at 0, and KL denotes functions β(r,t) that are class-K in r and decrease to 0 as t → ∞.

The theory of nonlinear semigroups (m-accretive operators, Crandall–Liggett generation, mild solutions in the sense of Bénilan–Crandall–Pazy) provides a unified well-posedness framework for fully nonlinear evolution equations including the porous medium equation
    ∂_t ρ = Δ(ρ^m) + b(ρ, u),  m > 1,
on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^d with appropriate boundary conditions and distributed/boundary input u, and the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
    ∂_t v + (v · ∇)v = νΔv − ∇p + g(v, u),  div v = 0,
on a domain Ω with boundary conditions and an input u entering through forcing or boundary data.

Problem. Develop a general theory of input-to-state stability for fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional control systems generated by (perturbed) nonlinear semigroups on Banach spaces. Specifically:

(a) Formulate sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the nonlinear generator F (e.g., dissipativity/accretivity estimates, Lyapunov-type inequalities, or coercivity of an associated functional) and of the input dependence, that guarantee ISS of the resulting evolution with respect to inputs u ∈ L^∞(R_+, U).

(b) Apply the resulting framework to establish ISS (or appropriate variants such as integral ISS or strong ISS) for the porous medium equation and for the Navier–Stokes equations under physically meaningful classes of distributed and/or boundary disturbances.

representations.normalized:
Develop a systematic robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional control systems—particularly those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs)—based on the framework of input-to-state stability (ISS).

Setup and definitions. Consider a control system of the form
  ẋ(t) = A x(t) + f(x(t), u(t), d(t)),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach (or Hilbert) state space, A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on X (or, more generally, the dynamics are described by an evolution equation on X possibly with unbounded boundary input operators), u(·) takes values in a control space U, and d(·) ∈ L^∞(ℝ₊; D) represents an exogenous disturbance taking values in a normed space D. Boundary control is allowed: inputs may enter through boundary conditions of the underlying PDE.

The closed-loop system under a feedback law u = K(x) is said to be input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to the disturbance d if there exist a class-KL function β and a class-K function γ such that, for every x₀ ∈ X and every admissible d,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖d‖_{L^∞(0,t;D)})  for all t ≥ 0.

Problem. Provide a constructive design framework that, given a class of PDE control systems (for example, parabolic or hyperbolic PDEs in one or several space dimensions, with either distributed or boundary actuation), produces feedback laws K—possibly together with ISS-Lyapunov functionals certifying the closed-loop ISS estimate above—and that is general enough to address concrete robust control problems in which a systematic methodology is currently lacking, such as:
  (a) the drilling problem (axial/torsional vibrations modeled by wave equations with nonlinear boundary conditions);
  (b) robust stabilization of flexible aircraft structures (beam/plate equations coupled with rigid-body dynamics and uncertain aerodynamic loads).

The methodology should specify (i) the admissible classes of disturbances and uncertainties, (ii) the construction of ISS-Lyapunov functionals for the closed loop, (iii) verifiable sufficient conditions on the controller gains ensuring the desired ISS gain γ, and (iv) extensions to cases with unbounded input operators arising from boundary actuation.

The development of a systematic ISS-based robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional and PDE systems is recognized as a broad open research direction. While Lyapunov-based ISS analysis and small-gain results have advanced (e.g., for ODE-PDE interconnections and networks of infinite-dimensional systems), no comprehensive constructive design framework covering the cited application areas (drilling, flexible aircraft structures) has been established. Recent surveys and tutorials (2020–2021) continue to list robust ISS-based design as an active and largely open problem.

representations.normalized:
Setup. Let $P$ be a Poisson bi-vector on a smooth manifold $M$. In the Kontsevich graph calculus, an unoriented graph cocycle $\gamma$ (with respect to the vertex-expanding differential in Kontsevich's graph complex) determines, via the orientation map $\mathcal{O}\vec{r}$, a universal infinitesimal deformation $Q(P)=\mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)$ of Poisson structures: on every affine chart, $\dot P = Q(P)$ preserves the Jacobi identity to first order in the deformation parameter. Among the well-known cocycles in this family are:
- the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ (Kontsevich), giving the flow $Q_{1:6/2}(P) = \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_3)(P)$;
- the pentagon-wheel cocycle $\gamma_5$, giving $Q_5(P) = \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_5)(P)$;
- the heptagon-wheel cocycle $\gamma_7$, giving $Q_7(P) = \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_7)(P)$.

These flows are constructed in affine coordinates on $\mathbb{R}^d$, using polynomial differential operators in the components of $P$.

Problem. For each of the three Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetries
$$Q_{1:6/2}(P) = \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_3)(P), \qquad Q_5(P) = \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_5)(P), \qquad Q_7(P) = \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_7)(P),$$
construct a smooth-atlas globalisation: produce a well-defined infinitesimal deformation $\dot P = \tilde Q(P)$ of Poisson bi-vectors on an arbitrary smooth Poisson manifold $(M,P)$, given by an explicit recipe on each chart together with correction terms compatible with smooth coordinate changes, such that the resulting deformation agrees with the affine formula in any affine atlas and preserves the Jacobi identity (modulo the deformation parameter squared) globally on $M$.

Let G(n,k) denote the Kontsevich graph complex of equivalence classes (under sign-respecting graph automorphisms) of finite connected oriented graphs on n vertices and k edges, equipped with the standard differential d that inserts a new vertex and sums over ways of expanding an existing vertex (so coboundaries d(λ) of graphs λ on n−1 vertices land in graphs on n vertices). A graph cocycle is a finite formal linear combination γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a (with γ_a distinct equivalence classes of graphs on n vertices) satisfying d(γ) = 0, considered modulo the equivalence relation [γ] = [γ + d(λ)].

(a) Stability of combinatorial statistics. Fix n large. For a cocycle γ = Σ_a c_a · γ_a on n vertices, define the multiset-valued statistics
  • Diam(γ) = the multiset of graph diameters of the γ_a, weighted by |c_a|;
  • Val(γ) = the multiset of vertex-valency distributions of the γ_a, weighted by |c_a|.
Determine whether Diam(γ) and Val(γ) (or natural normalizations thereof) are invariants of the cohomology class [γ], i.e. whether they are preserved under all coboundary modifications γ ↦ γ + d(λ) by graph cochains λ on n−1 vertices. If not invariants, identify which features of these statistics are well-defined on cohomology classes once n is sufficiently large.

(b) Asymptotics and generating function. Let H^{n,k} denote the cohomology of this graph complex in bi-grading (n vertices, k edges). Determine the large-n asymptotic behavior of dim H^{n,k}, with emphasis on the ray k = 2n − 2 (the bi-grading relevant to symmetries of Poisson brackets). In particular, determine whether there exists a generating function F(x,y) = Σ_{n,k} dim H^{n,k} x^n y^k (or its restriction along k = 2n − 2) admitting a closed form or functional equation, and describe the growth rate of dim H^{n, 2n−2} as n → ∞.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The dimensions of Kontsevich's graph cohomology remain an active subject of computational and theoretical research. Recent work (e.g., 11-loop computations posted in 2025) extends known dimensions but no closed-form generating function or asymptotic formula along the ray (n, 2n−2) is established. The cohomological-class invariance of combinatorial statistics such as diameter and valency distributions does not appear to be settled in the literature. The problems thus appear open.

Let Gra denote Kontsevich's unoriented graph complex: the differential graded Lie algebra spanned by isomorphism classes of connected undirected graphs (with at least trivalent vertices and an ordering of edges, modulo the standard sign relations), equipped with the differential given by edge contraction and the Lie bracket given by the sum over insertions of one graph into the vertices of another. Let grt denote the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra (the graded Lie algebra of derivations of the free Lie algebra on two generators satisfying the pentagon and hexagon constraints). Willwacher's theorem provides a Lie algebra isomorphism

  grt  ≅  H^0(Gra).

Problem: For each small vertex number n ∈ {4, 6, 8, 9, 10, …} for which the cohomology H^0(Gra) has nontrivial classes, exhibit explicit graph cocycles γ_n ∈ Gra of degree zero on n vertices representing a basis (or distinguished generators) of the corresponding piece of H^0(Gra), and describe explicitly the elements of grt that correspond to them under Willwacher's isomorphism. In particular, give a concrete combinatorial-and-algebraic dictionary at vertex counts n = 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, … relating each generating cocycle (e.g. the tetrahedron at n = 4, and its higher-loop analogues) to its image in grt.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Willwacher's isomorphism grt ≅ H^0(Gra) is established, and explicit representatives are known for the lowest cases (the tetrahedron cocycle at n=4 corresponding to σ_3, and the pentagon/heptagon-like cocycles in higher loop orders studied by Willwacher–Živković, Brown, and others). Concrete dictionaries at general higher n remain only partially known: graph cocycles have been enumerated computationally for small n, but explicit identification with specific elements of grt beyond the first few generators (σ_3, σ_5, σ_7, …) is incomplete.

representations.normalized:
Consider Kontsevich's graph complex of finite undirected graphs on N vertices and 2N edges (for N ≥ 1), graded by the number of vertices and edges, equipped with the vertex-expansion differential d. A cocycle ω is an element of ker d. Along the bi-grading ray (#V, #E) = (N, 2N), the well-known wheel cocycles γ_{2ℓ+1} (the tetrahedron γ_3 at N=4, the pentagon-wheel γ_5 at N=6, the heptagon-wheel γ_7 at N=8, ...) are known to exist. For an undirected graph cocycle ω, let O→r(ω)(P) denote Kontsevich's orientation morphism producing, when no obstructions occur, an oriented graph cocycle built from wedges ←•→ which encodes an infinitesimal symmetry Ṗ = O→r(ω)(P) of any Poisson structure P on an affine manifold.

Solve the following:
(a) Determine the smallest integer N′ > 7 such that there exists a nontrivial cocycle ω ∈ ker d in the graph complex on the ray (N′, 2N′) that is not in the linear span of the previously known wheel cocycles.
(b) Determine the smallest integer N″ ≥ N′ such that some such new cocycle ω on the ray (N″, 2N″) is orientable, i.e. encounters no obstruction in passing through O→r(·) to a nonzero oriented Kontsevich graph cocycle built from wedges.
(c) Provide explicit examples of new Poisson-bracket symmetries of the form
   Ṗ = (O→r(ω)(P))^m · O→r(γ)(P),  m ≠ 0,
where γ is a known wheel cocycle and ω is a new cocycle constructed in part (b).

Setup. Let $P$ be a Poisson bivector on a finite-dimensional affine manifold, with Schouten bracket $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$, so that $[\![P,P]\!]$ is the Jacobiator (a tri-vector that vanishes on Poisson structures). Following the Kontsevich graph calculus, an oriented Kontsevich graph on $n$ "aerial" vertices encodes a poly-differential operator built from copies of $P$; a Leibniz graph is an oriented graph in which exactly one internal vertex carries the tri-vector $[\![P,P]\!]$ (with three outgoing edges, satisfying the Leibniz rule), while all other internal vertices carry $P$. Each Leibniz graph $L$ has a canonical expansion $\mathrm{Exp}(L)$ as a finite linear combination of Kontsevich oriented graphs obtained by resolving the Jacobiator vertex via the Leibniz rule.

For a Kontsevich-graph cocycle $\gamma$ producing a flow $\dot P = \overrightarrow{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)$, the Poisson-cocycle condition $[\![P,\overrightarrow{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)]\!]=\diamondsuit(P,[\![P,P]\!])$ admits in general non-unique factorisations through Leibniz graphs: one may have two distinct Leibniz-graph linear combinations $\diamondsuit_1,\diamondsuit_2$ both balancing the equation, yielding identities $\diamondsuit_2-\diamondsuit_1\equiv 0$ in the space of Leibniz graphs.

Define the Leibniz meta-graph $\mathcal{M}$ as follows: vertices of $\mathcal{M}$ are Leibniz graphs (in a given combinatorial type/order), and two Leibniz graphs $L,L'$ are joined by an edge for each Kontsevich oriented graph appearing in both $\mathrm{Exp}(L)$ and $\mathrm{Exp}(L')$ (multi-edges allowed).

Problem. For each known non-unique factorisation of the Poisson-cocycle condition through Leibniz graphs (e.g. those arising from the tetrahedral, pentagon-wheel, and heptagon-wheel cocycles), determine the topological/combinatorial structure of the resulting identities $\diamondsuit_2-\diamondsuit_1\equiv 0$. Concretely, describe the corresponding Leibniz meta-graph $\mathcal{M}$: compute or estimate its genus, diameter, typical cycle length, and other natural graph invariants. Furthermore, analyse the saturation behaviour of the iterative algorithm that generates Leibniz graphs balancing such factorisations: at which stage do newly-produced Leibniz graphs typically appear as leaves of $\mathcal{M}$ versus as handles (i.e. closing new cycles), and characterise the last Leibniz graphs to be produced before saturation.

representations.normalized:
Setup. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifold, i.e. an affine space equipped with a Poisson bivector $P \in \Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!] = 0$, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. An infinitesimal symmetry of the Poisson structure is a bivector-valued functional $Q(P) \in \Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$, polynomial-differential in the components of $P$, such that the linearized Jacobi identity holds:
$$[\![P, Q(P)]\!] = 0.$$
Such a symmetry $Q$ is called:
- universal if a single universal differential-polynomial expression in $P$ defines $Q(P)$ simultaneously for every affine Poisson manifold of every finite dimension;
- proper if it is not of the form $[\![P, X(P)]\!]$ for any vector field $X(P)$ that is itself a universal differential-polynomial in $P$ (i.e. it is nontrivial in the relevant Poisson cohomology);
- nonlinear if its expression involves at least two copies of $P$ (so that it is not linear in $P$).

Kontsevich's orientation morphism $\mathrm{O}\vec{r}$ is a linear map from the (unoriented) graph complex to the space of universal differential-polynomial bivectors on affine Poisson manifolds: to each cocycle $\gamma$ in the Kontsevich graph complex it associates a universal infinitesimal symmetry $\mathrm{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)$ of $P$, obtained by summing over all admissible orientations of $\gamma$ with two outgoing edges at a chosen vertex and decorating each oriented edge with a copy of $P$.

Question. Do there exist nonlinear, proper, universal infinitesimal symmetries $Q(P)$ of Poisson structures (universal with respect to all finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds) that do not arise as $\mathrm{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)$ for any cocycle $\gamma$ in the Kontsevich graph complex (modulo trivial symmetries)?

representations.normalized:
Setup. Let $M$ be an affine Poisson manifold of dimension $r$, that is, a manifold $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ equipped with an atlas whose transition maps are affine, together with a Poisson bi-vector field $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!]=0$ in the Schouten bracket. Let $\gamma$ be a cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex (a finite linear combination of unoriented graphs on $n$ internal vertices, modulo signs from edge orderings, that is closed under the vertex-expansion differential). Associated with $\gamma$ is the orientation morphism $\vec{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)$, a bi-vector whose coefficients are universal differential polynomials in the components of $P$, obtained by summing over all admissible orientations of $\gamma$ on two sinks and inserting a copy of $P$ at every internal vertex. Because $\gamma$ is a cocycle, the assignment $\dot P=\vec{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)$ defines an infinitesimal deformation that preserves the Poisson property to first order in a formal parameter $\varepsilon$.

Consider the formal flow
$$P(\varepsilon)=\exp\!\Big(\varepsilon\,\vec{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)\cdot\frac{\partial}{\partial \vec P}\Big)P\,\Big|_{\varepsilon=0}\;\in\;\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)[\![\varepsilon]\!],$$
viewed as a formal power series in $\varepsilon$ with coefficients that are differential-polynomial expressions in the components of $P$.

Question. For an arbitrary affine Poisson manifold $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$, does the formal power series $P(\varepsilon)$ converge—uniformly on $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$, in a suitable topology on bi-vector fields—on a nontrivial interval of values of $\varepsilon$, so that for each such $\varepsilon$ it determines a globally well-defined Poisson bi-vector field on $M$?

Because $\gamma$ is a cocycle, the assignment $\dot P=\vec{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)$ defines an infinitesimal deformation that preserves the Poisson property to first order in a formal parameter $\varepsilon$.

Consider the formal flow
$$P(\varepsilon)=\exp\!\Big(\varepsilon\,\vec{\mathrm{Or}}(\gamma)(P)\cdot\frac{\partial}{\partial \vec P}\Big)P\,\Big|_{\varepsilon=0}\;\in\;\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)[\![\varepsilon]\!],$$
viewed as a formal power series in $\varepsilon$ with coefficients that are differential-polynomial expressions in the components of $P$.

Question. For an arbitrary affine Poisson manifold $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$, does the formal power series $P(\varepsilon)$ converge—uniformly on $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$, in a suitable topology on bi-vector fields—on a nontrivial interval of values of $\varepsilon$, so that for each such $\varepsilon$ it determines a globally well-defined Poisson bi-vector field on $M$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Recent works (2024–2025) in the series "Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets" continue to list convergence of the graph-defined exponential flow on (Nambu–)Poisson bi-vectors as an open problem; no general convergence result for arbitrary affine Poisson manifolds has been established. Existing results address formal-series-level cocycle properties and specific examples, not global convergence.

Background and setup. Let $M$ be a smooth (or formal) manifold and let $P=P^{ij}(x)\,\partial_i\wedge\partial_j$ be a Poisson bi-vector on $M$, i.e. a smooth section of $\Lambda^2 TM$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!]=0$, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. A Kontsevich graph cocycle is a finite linear combination $\gamma=\sum c_\alpha \Gamma_\alpha$ of oriented graphs $\Gamma_\alpha$ on $n$ internal (aerial) vertices and two ground (sink) vertices, with two outgoing edges from each internal vertex, such that the universal bi-vector $Q_\gamma(P)$ obtained by inserting copies of $P$ at the internal vertices and contracting along the edge orientations satisfies the infinitesimal-symmetry equation
$$[\![P,Q_\gamma(P)]\!]=0\qquad\text{for every Poisson bi-vector }P.$$
Such a $\gamma$ thus determines a flow $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ on the variety of Poisson structures, where the right-hand side is a polynomial differential expression in the components $P^{ij}$ and their partial derivatives. Concrete examples include the tetrahedral flow $\dot P = Q_{\gamma_3}(P)$ and the higher graph cocycles $\gamma_5,\gamma_7,\dots$ producing nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems for the components $P^{ij}(x,t)$.

Recall that an evolutionary PDE system is called Liouville-integrable if it admits an infinite hierarchy of independent commuting symmetries (equivalently, an infinite family of Poisson-commuting conserved functionals in involution with respect to a compatible Hamiltonian structure), and super-integrable if it admits, in addition, further independent (not necessarily commuting) integrals beyond what Liouville integrability requires.

Problem. Determine the Liouville-integrability and, when applicable, the super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ associated with the known Kontsevich graph symmetries $\gamma$ of Poisson bi-vectors (in particular $\gamma_3$, $\gamma_5$, $\gamma_7$, and the linear combinations of graph cocycles producing nontrivial Poisson cohomology classes). Specifically:
(a) Exhibit, or prove the nonexistence of, an infinite hierarchy of commuting symmetries of $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$.
(b) Construct a (bi-)Hamiltonian formulation, recursion operator, or Lax representation, or prove that none exists.
(c) Decide whether any such system is super-integrable in the sense above.

Let M be a smooth manifold and let P denote a Poisson bi-vector on M, i.e. a section of Λ²TM satisfying the Jacobi identity [[P,P]] = 0, where [[·,·]] is the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. Consider an evolution equation on the space of Poisson bi-vectors of the form

  Ṗ = Q(P),

where Q(P) is a bi-vector built universally from P and its derivatives by a finite linear combination of Kontsevich-type oriented graph cocycles, and where Q(P) is required to preserve the Jacobi identity (i.e. [[P, Q(P)]] = 0 whenever [[P,P]] = 0).

Working on the infinite jet space J^∞ of the components of the Poisson bi-vector P (regarded as unknown fields), let π be a variational Poisson structure on this jet space (i.e. a Hamiltonian differential operator giving rise to a variational Poisson bracket on the corresponding space of local functionals) and let χ = χ(P) be a variational covector (a section of the appropriate horizontal cotangent bundle on J^∞).

Question: Does there exist such a pair (π, χ) so that the flow Ṗ = Q(P) admits the Hamiltonian/Poisson representation

  Q(P) = π( χ(P) ),

and, in particular, can χ be chosen as the variational derivative χ = δH/δP of a well-defined local Hamiltonian functional H of the jet of P?

On $\mathbb{R}^3$ with coordinates $(x,y,z)$, consider the two-parameter family of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets
$$\{f,g\}_{a,\rho}(x,y,z) \;=\; \rho(x,y,z)\,\det\!\Big(\tfrac{\partial(a,f,g)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\Big),$$
where $a\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is a Casimir function and $\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is a density (the bracket is Poisson, i.e. skew-symmetric and Jacobi-satisfying, for every choice of $a,\rho$). Let $P=(P^{ij})$ denote the associated Poisson bi-vector and let
$$\dot P^{ij} \;=\; Q^{ij}_{P\alpha\beta}([a],\rho)$$
be a Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry of $P$, i.e.\ a bi-vector flow built from a non-trivial cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex which preserves the Jacobi identity to first order.

Define the linear differential operator
$$\tau:(a,\rho)\longmapsto \{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho}.$$

(i) Determine whether the class $\{\,\{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho} : a,\rho\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)\,\}$ is preserved under every Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry $\dot P=Q(P)$.

(ii) For a given Kontsevich symmetry $Q$, decide whether there exists an evolutionary system in the jet space with fibre variables $a,\rho$,
$$\dot a \;=\; A([a],[\rho]),\qquad \dot\rho \;=\; R([a],[\rho]),$$
whose pushforward under the tangent map $\tau_*$ equals $Q(P([a],\rho))$, i.e.
$$\tau_*\!\big(A([a],[\rho]),R([a],[\rho])\big) \;=\; Q\big(P([a],\rho)\big).$$
Describe such $(A,R)$ explicitly when they exist.

Subsequent work has established that on $\mathbb{R}^3$ the class of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets $\{\cdot,\cdot\}_{a,\rho}$ is preserved by the known Kontsevich graph flows (tetrahedral and pentagon-wheel), with explicit evolutionary systems for $(a,\rho)$ realizing the symmetry; the corresponding deformations are trivial in second Poisson cohomology. The general statement for arbitrary Kontsevich symmetries and in higher dimensions remains under active investigation, with dimension-specific obstructions (e.g. invisible graphs) appearing in $d\geq 4$. Thus the problem is partially solved for the originally posed setting on $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Setup. Let $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ denote a finite-dimensional affine real manifold of dimension $r$, equipped with a Poisson bivector $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$. Let $\mathsf{GC}_2$ be the Kontsevich graph complex of undirected graphs (with the differential $d$ given by vertex expansion), and let $\ker d\subset\mathsf{GC}_2$ be the space of graph cocycles. The Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{grt}$ of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is known (by Willwacher's theorem) to embed into $H^0(\mathsf{GC}_2)$, and contains an infinite family of cocycles built from the $(2\ell+1)$-wheel graphs (for $\ell\geq 1$) together with all iterated Lie brackets thereof; this yields a countable family $\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}\subset\ker d$.

Let $\mathcal{O}\vec{r}\colon\mathsf{GC}_2\to\mathrm{End}(\text{Poisson bivectors})$ denote the Kontsevich orientation morphism: for a graph cocycle $\gamma$ on $n$ vertices and $2n-2$ edges, $\mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)$ is the formal sum, over all admissible orientations in which each of the $n$ original vertices is the tail of exactly two arrows, of the bivector obtained by inserting copies of $P$ at the vertices and contracting along edges. The output $\mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ is a universal infinitesimal symmetry of the Poisson structure $P$.

Question. For a fixed affine Poisson manifold $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$, determine how many elements of the countable family $\{\mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_i)(P)\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ are nonzero as global sections of $\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$, i.e. do not vanish identically on $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$.

The orientation morphism from graph cocycles to Poisson symmetries is actively studied (Buring–Kiselev–Rutten and others). Let $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ be an affine Poisson manifold of dimension $r$, that is, a smooth manifold equipped with a Poisson bivector $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ whose components in some affine atlas are polynomial (in particular, take the standard affine setting in which $P$ is given globally by polynomial coefficients). Consider the Kontsevich graph complex of unoriented finite graphs with a wedge-ordering on edges, equipped with the differential $d$ obtained by vertex-expansion. To each cocycle $\gamma\in\ker d$ one associates, via the Kontsevich orientation morphism applied to $(\gamma,P)$, a vector field $X(\gamma)=X(\gamma,P)\in\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ — called a trivialising vector field — with the property that the bivector flow $\dot P=[\![P,X(\gamma)]\!]$ realises the infinitesimal Poisson-cohomology-trivial deformation produced by $\gamma$.
\medskip

Question. Describe the size of the family
$$\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)=\{\,X(\gamma,P): \gamma\in\ker d\,\}\subset\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}}).$$
More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Is the linear span of $\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$ locally complete in $\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$, in the sense that for every point $x\in M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$, every smooth vector field on a neighbourhood of $x$ can be approximated (in the $C^\infty$ topology) by elements of this span?
\item Equivalently, do the time-one flows $\exp(tX(\gamma,P))$, as $\gamma$ ranges over $\ker d$ and $t$ over $\mathbb{R}$, generate a (pseudo)group rich enough to imitate the full diffeomorphism action on $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ preserving $P$?
\end{enumerate}
Determine, for a given $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$, whether such local completeness holds, and if not, characterise the closure of $\mathrm{span}\,\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$ inside $\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$.

Consider any quantisation of this model, consisting of a Hilbert space H of states together with an associative (typically noncommutative) algebra A of operator-valued observables that deforms the Poisson algebra of classical observables.

Question: Must there always exist a well-defined "post-quantisation response" to the classical symmetry Q — that is, a canonically associated action or transformation induced by Q on the Hilbert space H, on the operator algebra A, or on both — corresponding to the classical action of Q on {·,·}_P?

Setup. Let $P$ be a Poisson bi-vector on a smooth manifold $M$, and let
$$\star \;=\; \times \;+\; \hbar\,\{\cdot,\cdot\}_P \;+\; o(\hbar)$$
be a Kontsevich formal deformation-quantisation star-product on $C^\infty(M)[[\hbar]]$ whose leading deformation term is the Poisson bracket associated with $P$. Two such star-products $\star$ and $\star'$ are called gauge-equivalent if there exists a formal differential operator $T = \mathrm{id} + \hbar T_1 + \hbar^2 T_2 + \cdots$ such that
$$T(f \star g) \;=\; T(f) \star' T(g) \qquad \text{for all } f,g \in C^\infty(M)[[\hbar]].$$

Let $\mathsf{GC}$ denote Kontsevich's graph complex of (un)oriented graphs with the vertex-expansion differential $[\bullet\!-\!\bullet,\,\cdot\,]$. For each cocycle $\gamma \in \ker[\bullet\!-\!\bullet,\,\cdot\,]$, the orient-and-realise map produces a multivector field $Q(P) := \mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)$ that is a symmetry of the Poisson structure, in the sense that $P + \varepsilon\,Q(P) + o(\varepsilon)$ is again Poisson modulo $\varepsilon^2$.

Problem. Describe explicitly the induced action of the graph complex $\mathsf{GC}$ on the set of Kontsevich star-products. Specifically:

1. Given a graph cocycle $\gamma$ and a star-product $\star$ as above, define and compute an infinitesimal deformation $\star \mapsto \star + \varepsilon\,\delta_\gamma(\star) + o(\varepsilon)$ whose leading-order Poisson bi-vector is shifted from $\hbar P$ to $\hbar P + \varepsilon\,Q(\hbar P) + o(\varepsilon)$.

2. Determine how this action interacts with gauge equivalence $\star \rightleftarrows \star'$: in particular, decide whether gauge-equivalent star-products are sent to gauge-equivalent star-products, and identify the induced action on gauge-equivalence classes.

3. Illustrate the construction with explicit examples (e.g. using small graph cocycles such as the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ or the pentagon-wheel $\gamma_5$) on concrete Poisson manifolds.

representations.normalized:
Setup. Let $(M,P)$ be a smooth finite-dimensional Poisson manifold with Poisson bivector $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$, satisfying $[\![P,P]\!]=0$ in the Schouten bracket. Recall Kontsevich's directed graph complex: a vertex set with ordered pairs of outgoing edges per internal vertex carries a differential $d$ given by vertex expansion, and any cocycle $\gamma\in\ker d$ produces, via the Kontsevich graph orientation map, a bivector-valued differential operator $\mathcal{O}_{\vec r(\gamma)}(P)\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ such that the flow $\dot P=\mathcal{O}_{\vec r(\gamma)}(P)$ preserves the class of Poisson bivectors (i.e.\ $[\![P,\dot P]\!]=0$ on the nose). Kontsevich's formality also produces, for each $P$, an associative star product $\star=\times+\hbar\{\cdot,\cdot\}_P+o(\hbar)$ on $C^\infty(M)[\![\hbar]\!]$.

Consider the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson sigma-model: a two-dimensional topological field theory whose fields are a map $X:\Sigma\to M$ from a disk $\Sigma$ together with a $1$-form $\eta\in\Omega^1(\Sigma,X^*T^*M)$, with action
$$S_P[X,\eta]=\int_\Sigma \big(\langle\eta,dX\rangle+\tfrac12 P^{ij}(X)\,\eta_i\wedge\eta_j\big),$$
whose perturbative Feynman path-integral expansion of boundary correlators $\langle f(X(0))\,g(X(1))\rangle$ recovers the Kontsevich star product $f\star g$.

Problem.
(a) Determine how the graph-complex symmetry flows $\dot P=\mathcal{O}_{\vec r(\gamma)}(P)$, with $\gamma\in\ker d$, act on the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson sigma-model: identify the corresponding transformations of the fields $(X,\eta)$ and/or of the action $S_P$ that implement these infinitesimal deformations of $P$ as symmetries (or quasi-symmetries) of the path-integral measure, in a way compatible with the encoding of $\star$ by boundary correlators.

(b) Decide whether the Ikeda–Izawa Poisson sigma-model admits infinitesimal symmetries deforming the Poisson structure $P$ that do not arise from any graph cocycle $\gamma\in\ker d$ via the construction $\mathcal{O}_{\vec r(\gamma)}$.

Let $P$ be a Poisson bi-vector on a smooth (affine) manifold, so that the classical master equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$ holds, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten bracket on multi-vectors. A universal infinitesimal symmetry of the class of Poisson structures is a map $P\mapsto Q(P)$, built from $P$ by a universal (e.g. Kontsevich-graph) formula in the partial derivatives of the components of $P$, such that the flow $\dot P=Q(P)$ preserves the equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$, i.e. $[\![Q(P),P]\!]=0$ whenever $[\![P,P]\!]=0$.

In the Batalin–Vilkovisky framework, the classical master equation is replaced by the quantum master equation
$$i\hbar\,\Delta P + \tfrac12\,[\![P,P]\!] = 0,$$
where $\Delta$ is the BV Laplacian acting on the relevant space of (formal) multi-vectors / functionals, and $P$ is now allowed to depend formally on $\hbar$.

Question: Does every universal infinitesimal symmetry $\dot P=Q(P)$ of the classical equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$ (in particular, those produced by the Kontsevich graph construction) persist under Batalin–Vilkovisky quantisation, in the sense that the flow $\dot P=Q(P)$ — possibly after a universal $\hbar$-deformation $Q(P)\mapsto Q_\hbar(P)$ — preserves the quantum master equation $i\hbar\,\Delta P + \tfrac12\,[\![P,P]\!]=0$?

Background and setup. Let $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}, P)$ denote a finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifold, where $P = \tfrac{1}{2} P^{ij}(x)\,\partial_i \wedge \partial_j$ is a Poisson bivector, i.e. a bivector satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!] = 0$ in the Schouten algebra of polyvector fields. Kontsevich's graph construction associates, to every suitable directed graph $\Gamma$ on $n$ aerial vertices and to a Poisson bivector $P$, a polydifferential operator $\Gamma(P)$ built by placing a copy of $P$ at each aerial vertex and contracting derivations along the edges; this construction yields, in particular, the graph cocycles producing infinitesimal symmetries (flows) $\dot P = Q(P)$ of the Maurer–Cartan equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$. Denote by
\[
\mathrm{sym}\bigl([\![P,P]\!]=0\bigr) := \bigl\{ Q \;:\; [\![P,Q(P)]\!] = 0 \text{ for every Poisson } P \bigr\}
\]
the set of all such graph-encoded symmetries.

On the other hand, Kontsevich's formal noncommutative (super)geometry replaces the commutative algebra of functions by the commutative but non-associative calculus of cyclic words, equipped with the topological pair-of-pants multiplication
\[
\mu : S^1 \times S^1 \longrightarrow S^1,
\]
which, on cyclic words in noncommuting (super)variables, defines a commutative non-associative product compatible with the cyclic structure. In this framework, polyvector fields and Schouten-type brackets admit cyclic-word analogues.

Question. Does there exist a generalisation $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ of the Kontsevich graph construction from affine Poisson manifolds $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}, P)$ to the commutative non-associative calculus of cyclic words with pair-of-pants multiplication, such that $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is:

(i) well defined as an operation on cyclic words (respecting cyclic invariance and the pair-of-pants product), and

(ii) universal with respect to the full family of graph-encoded symmetries $Q \in \mathrm{sym}([\![P,P]\!]=0)$ of Poisson structures, in the sense that for every such $Q$ the noncommutative lift $\widetilde{Q}$ is simultaneously well defined and yields a symmetry of the cyclic-word analogue of the Maurer–Cartan equation?

Construct such a universal extension or prove that no such extension exists.

Consider a discrete-time temporal network on a fixed set of $N$ nodes given by a finite sequence of adjacency-matrix snapshots $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_T$, where $A_t \in \{0,1\}^{N\times N}$ records the contacts active during time step $t$. On this temporal network, run a discrete-time Markovian SIS spreading process with per-contact transmission probability $\lambda$ and per-step recovery probability $\mu$, and define the epidemic threshold $\lambda_c$ as the smallest $\lambda$ for which the disease-free state is unstable.

A standard analytic approach computes $\lambda_c$ by extending the snapshot sequence periodically, i.e., imposing the periodic boundary condition
$$A_{t+T} \equiv A_t \quad \text{for all } t \in \mathbb{Z},$$
so that the network is treated as an infinitely repeated cycle of the original $T$ snapshots, and then analyzing the spectral radius of the product $\prod_{t=1}^{T}\bigl[(1-\mu)I + \lambda A_t\bigr]$ (or an analogous transmission operator).

Repeating the snapshot sequence can create time-respecting paths $(i_0, t_0) \to (i_1, t_1) \to \cdots$ (with $t_0 < t_1 < \cdots$ and $A_{t_k}(i_{k-1}, i_k) = 1$) that do not exist within the single original window $\{1,\dots,T\}$.

Question: Does imposing the periodic boundary condition $A_{t+T} \equiv A_t$ change the epidemic threshold of the original finite temporal contact network $(A_1,\dots,A_T)$ compared to the threshold one would obtain without periodic repetition? If so, characterize quantitatively how the threshold depends on $T$ and on the structure of the snapshots, and identify conditions (e.g., a minimum period length) under which the periodic-boundary threshold faithfully recovers the threshold of the non-repeated temporal network.

Consider a temporal contact network represented as a sequence of time-stamped contacts (i,j,t) among a population of N individuals, where each contact denotes a potentially infectious interaction at time t. On such a network, run a standard compartmental spreading process (e.g., SIS or SIR) in which an infectious individual transmits along each contact independently with per-contact probability β (or rate β) and recovers at rate μ. The epidemic threshold is the critical value of β/μ above which a macroscopic outbreak occurs in the limit of large N.

Now suppose the temporal network exhibits coordinated bursts of contacts: at certain random times t_k, a large subset S_k ⊂ {1,…,N} of individuals becomes simultaneously and pairwise (or densely) in contact for a short duration Δ_k, after which contacts revert to a baseline temporal pattern. The sizes |S_k|, durations Δ_k, inter-burst intervals, and memberships may follow prescribed distributions, and these synchronized burst events are correlated across individuals (in contrast to independent per-edge burstiness).

Determine, analytically or through a tractable model, how such coordinated bursts modify (i) the epidemic threshold and (ii) the size and time course of the resulting outbreak, compared with a baseline temporal network having the same marginal contact rates but without coordinated bursts. In particular, characterize the dependence of the threshold shift on the burst-size distribution, burst frequency, and burst duration.

Consider a temporal network model in which the contact structure is described by a time-indexed sequence of graphs $\{G_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}}$ on a fixed vertex set $V$ of $n$ nodes, where each $G_t = (V, E_t)$ specifies which pairs of nodes are in contact at discrete time $t$. Assume the sequence is periodic with period $T \geq 1$, i.e. $G_{t+T} = G_t$ for all $t \geq 0$. On this temporal network, run a susceptible–infected–susceptible (SIS) (or SIR) Markovian spreading process: at each time step $t$, an infected node infects each susceptible neighbor in $G_t$ independently with probability $\beta \in (0,1]$, and each infected node recovers independently with probability $\mu \in (0,1]$. Define the epidemic threshold as the critical ratio $(\beta/\mu)_c$ above which the expected number of infected nodes does not vanish in the long-time limit (equivalently, the spectral threshold characterizing the stability of the disease-free state under the periodic time-inhomogeneous dynamics).

Problem. Determine the effect of the periodicity $T$ and the structure of the periodic sequence $\{G_t\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$ on the epidemic threshold $(\beta/\mu)_c$ and on the qualitative behavior of disease spread. In particular:

(a) Derive an analytical expression (or sharp bounds) for $(\beta/\mu)_c$ as a function of $T$ and of the sequence of adjacency matrices $A_0, A_1, \dots, A_{T-1}$, for example in terms of the spectral radius of the product $\prod_{t=0}^{T-1}\big((1-\mu) I + \beta A_t\big)$ or an analogous operator capturing one full period.

(b) Identify how the threshold compares with that of (i) the time-aggregated static network with adjacency $\bar A = \tfrac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} A_t$, and (ii) a randomly shuffled (non-periodic) version of the same sequence, and characterize regimes in which periodicity raises or lowers the threshold.

(c) Determine whether resonance phenomena can occur between the period $T$ of the contact pattern and the intrinsic time scale $1/\mu$ of the recovery process, and quantify their impact on outbreak size and on the prevalence in the endemic state.

Consider a population modeled by a temporal contact network: a vertex set $V$ together with a time-indexed family of edge sets $\{E(t)\}_{t \in T}$, encoding which pairs of individuals are in contact at each time. On this network, run a stochastic compartmental epidemic process (e.g., SIS or SIR) with infection rate $\beta$ along active edges and recovery rate $\mu$. The epidemic threshold is the critical value of $\beta/\mu$ separating extinction of the infection from a sustained outbreak.

For analytical or computational tractability, one often restricts attention to a closed temporal-network model, in which only contacts among the vertices of $V$ are represented, even though in reality individuals in $V$ also interact with individuals outside $V$. Model these unmodeled external contacts statistically: for instance, augment each vertex $v \in V$ with an independent inhomogeneous external infection process of rate $\lambda_v(t)$ (or, equivalently, attach a random time-varying boundary force of infection drawn from a prescribed distribution, possibly correlated across vertices and time).

The problem is the following: design such a statistical augmentation and a corresponding analytic framework so that one can compute (or rigorously bound) the epidemic threshold of the closed temporal-network model with external forcing, in a way that yields predictions which usefully approximate the threshold of the true open system. Concretely, identify classes of temporal networks and classes of external-interaction statistical models for which the epidemic threshold can be derived in closed form or via a tractable spectral / mean-field calculation, and quantify the error introduced by replacing the open system with the closed-plus-external-forcing surrogate.

Let G = (V, E(t)) be a temporal network on a finite vertex set V whose edge set E(t) varies with time t in a specified family of contact processes (e.g. activity-driven, switching, or empirically measured contact sequences). On G run a stochastic SIS or SIR epidemic process with per-contact transmission rate β and recovery rate μ, starting from a small set of initially infected vertices. Define an "epidemic" to be the event that the cumulative or prevalence trajectory exceeds a fixed threshold (e.g. that the fraction of ever-infected vertices exceeds some ε > 0 before extinction, or that the prevalence persists above ε for a time exceeding T).

Classically, an epidemic threshold is defined as a critical value of a control parameter λ = β/μ (or of a spectral quantity of the temporal contact structure) above which an epidemic occurs with positive probability in the large-network limit and below which it almost surely dies out.

Reformulate this notion probabilistically:

(a) Given the temporal network model G and parameters (β, μ) — possibly known only up to specified estimation errors with a prior or confidence region — develop a quantitative theory expressing the probability P_epi(β, μ, G) that an epidemic (in the above sense) occurs, as an explicit or computable function of the model parameters and of the temporal-network statistics.

(b) Replace the singular critical value by a level set {(β, μ) : P_epi(β, μ, G) = p} for p ∈ (0, 1), and characterize the geometry, scaling, and dependence on temporal-network features (degree distribution, inter-event time distribution, temporal correlations, spectral radius of suitable supra-adjacency operators) of these level sets.

(c) Using the resulting likelihood-based threshold, formulate and solve an intervention-optimization problem: given a cost functional C(I) for an intervention I that modifies (β, μ, G), and a benefit functional B measuring the reduction of P_epi achieved by I, determine intervention strategies minimizing C subject to constraints on P_epi or maximizing B − C.

Provide rigorous results — exact formulas, asymptotic expansions, or provable bounds — for at least one nontrivial family of temporal-network models, and prove that the level-set formulation reduces to the classical epidemic threshold in an appropriate limit (e.g. as p → 0 with the network size tending to infinity).

representations.normalized:
Consider a temporal network on a finite vertex set $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$, represented as a sequence of (possibly weighted) adjacency matrices $\{A_t\}_{t=1}^{T}$, where $A_t(i,j)$ encodes the strength or presence of an interaction between vertices $i$ and $j$ at discrete time $t$. On such a network run a Markovian SIS epidemic process: at each time step, an infected vertex $i$ infects a neighbor $j$ along edge $(i,j)$ at rate $\beta A_t(i,j)$, and each infected vertex recovers independently at rate $\delta>0$. The epidemic threshold $\tau^* = \tau^*(\{A_t\}, \delta)$ is the critical value of $\beta/\delta$ separating the regime where the expected time to extinction is $O(\log n)$ from the regime where it is $\exp(\Omega(n))$.

Now suppose the network is not deterministically observed but is generated from a statistical network model with latent community structure. Specifically, let $z:V\to\{1,\dots,K\}$ assign each vertex to one of $K$ communities, and let $\{A_t\}$ be drawn from a dynamic stochastic block model with community-pair interaction rates $B_t \in [0,1]^{K\times K}$, so that conditional on $z$ the entries $A_t(i,j)$ are independent Bernoulli$(B_t(z_i,z_j))$ random variables. Assume only a partial observation of $\{A_t\}$ is available (for instance edges revealed up to time $T_0<T$, or a subsample of edges).

Develop a framework producing:

(a) a definition of the epidemic threshold $\tau^*$ in this probabilistic, partially observed setting, together with a rigorous estimator $\hat\tau$ of $\tau^*$ computable from the observed portion of $\{A_t\}$ and from community labels inferred by a community-detection procedure;

(b) finite-sample concentration or consistency guarantees of the form $\hat\tau \to \tau^*$ (in probability, as $n\to\infty$ or $T\to\infty$) under stated identifiability conditions on the dynamic stochastic block model;

(c) valid uncertainty quantification (e.g.\ confidence intervals or posterior credible sets) for $\tau^*$ that incorporate both the randomness of the network model and errors arising from imperfect community recovery and from prediction of future interactions $\{A_t\}_{t>T_0}$.

Consider a temporal network on a finite vertex set $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$, represented as a sequence of (possibly weighted) adjacency matrices $\{A_t\}_{t=1}^{T}$, where $A_t(i,j)$ encodes the strength or presence of an interaction between vertices $i$ and $j$ at discrete time $t$. On such a network run a Markovian SIS epidemic process: at each time step, an infected vertex $i$ infects a neighbor $j$ along edge $(i,j)$ at rate $\beta A_t(i,j)$, and each infected vertex recovers independently at rate $\delta>0$. The epidemic threshold $\tau^* = \tau^*(\{A_t\}, \delta)$ is the critical value of $\beta/\delta$ separating the regime where the expected time to extinction is $O(\log n)$ from the regime where it is $\exp(\Omega(n))$.

Now suppose the network is not deterministically observed but is generated from a statistical network model with latent community structure. Specifically, let $z:V\to\{1,\dots,K\}$ assign each vertex to one of $K$ communities, and let $\{A_t\}$ be drawn from a dynamic stochastic block model with community-pair interaction rates $B_t \in [0,1]^{K\times K}$, so that conditional on $z$ the entries $A_t(i,j)$ are independent Bernoulli$(B_t(z_i,z_j))$ random variables. Assume only a partial observation of $\{A_t\}$ is available (for instance edges revealed up to time $T_0<T$, or a subsample of edges).

Develop a framework producing:

(a) a definition of the epidemic threshold $\tau^*$ in this probabilistic, partially observed setting, together with a rigorous estimator $\hat\tau$ of $\tau^*$ computable from the observed portion of $\{A_t\}$ and from community labels inferred by a community-detection procedure;

(b) finite-sample concentration or consistency guarantees of the form $\hat\tau \to \tau^*$ (in probability, as $n\to\infty$ or $T\to\infty$) under stated identifiability conditions on the dynamic stochastic block model;

(c) valid uncertainty quantification (e.g.\ confidence intervals or posterior credible sets) for $\tau^*$ that incorporate both the randomness of the network model and errors arising from imperfect community recovery and from prediction of future interactions $\{A_t\}_{t>T_0}$.

The problem is to construct such a framework and to prove that it yields consistent estimation and asymptotically valid uncertainty quantification of the epidemic threshold under explicit, minimal assumptions on the dynamic stochastic block model.

Let a temporal network be a sequence $G = (V, E_1, E_2, \ldots, E_T)$, where $V$ is a fixed finite set of nodes and each $E_t \subseteq \binom{V}{2}$ is the set of contacts active at discrete time step $t$. Consider a Susceptible–Infected–Susceptible (or SIR) compartmental process on $G$ with per-contact infection probability $\beta \in (0,1]$ and per-step recovery probability $\mu \in (0,1]$; the epidemic threshold is the critical value $(\beta/\mu)_c$ separating the regime where an initial infection dies out almost surely (in the large-network limit) from the regime where it persists with positive probability.

Define a "local structure" in $G$ to be a small subset $S \subseteq V$ together with the induced temporal subgraph $(S, E_1\cap\binom{S}{2}, \ldots, E_T\cap\binom{S}{2})$ exhibiting one of the following patterns: (i) an anomalously dense temporal subgraph (more contacts among $S$ across time than expected under a chosen null model), (ii) a temporal clique (a subset $S$ in which every pair is in contact at least once within a time window $\Delta$), or (iii) a temporal chain (a sequence of nodes $v_1, \ldots, v_k$ with contacts $\{v_i, v_{i+1}\}$ active at strictly increasing times $t_1 < t_2 < \cdots < t_{k-1}$).

Problem. Develop a rigorous framework that:

(a) connects algorithmic detection of local structures of types (i)–(iii) to the computation or bounding of the epidemic threshold $(\beta/\mu)_c$ on temporal networks, producing explicit upper and/or lower bounds on $(\beta/\mu)_c$ as functionals of the detected local structures; and

(b) quantifies the effect of each type of local structure on the disease dynamics — for instance, by giving asymptotic expressions, in terms of the sizes, densities and temporal arrangements of these local structures, for the expected outbreak size, the time to extinction, and the shift of the epidemic threshold relative to a randomized null version of $G$ that destroys the local structure while preserving global statistics (such as aggregate degree distribution and contact rate).

representations.normalized:
Consider a temporal network represented as a time-indexed sequence of graphs G_t = (V, E_t) for t in a discrete or continuous time domain T, where V is a fixed set of n nodes and E_t ⊆ V × V is the set of edges active at time t. On such a structure, consider a stochastic spreading process (e.g., a susceptible–infected–susceptible (SIS) or susceptible–infected–recovered (SIR) model) with per-contact infection rate β and recovery rate μ, where infections may propagate only along edges that are active at the moment of contact. The epidemic threshold is the critical value of β/μ (or analogous control parameter) above which the expected fraction of infected nodes remains bounded away from zero in the large-time and/or large-n limit.

Two distinct network-surveillance problems are defined on this setting:
(i) Surveillance of propagation on a fixed network: given a static graph G = (V, E), select a subset S ⊆ V (sensors) of bounded size that minimizes the expected detection time, or maximizes the probability of detection, of a spreading process initiated at an unknown source.
(ii) Surveillance of a changing network: given the temporal network {G_t}, select (possibly time-varying) sensors S_t ⊆ V to detect either anomalous changes in the network structure itself or propagation processes whose dynamics interact with the changing topology.

Problem. Establish precise mathematical relationships between problems (i) and (ii) and the epidemic threshold of the underlying spreading process on the temporal network. Specifically:
(a) Derive quantitative bounds linking optimal sensor placements (and their detection-time guarantees) in problems (i) and (ii) to spectral or combinatorial quantities that determine the epidemic threshold on {G_t}.
(b) Identify conditions under which solving (i) is equivalent to, reducible to, or strictly easier/harder than solving (ii), in terms of the temporal-network parameters that govern the threshold.
(c) Characterize how the epidemic threshold itself can be inferred or estimated from observations available through optimal surveillance schemes of types (i) and (ii).

representations.normalized:
Let $\mathcal{G} = (G_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ be a temporal contact network on a fixed vertex set $V$ of $n$ individuals, where each $G_t = (V, E_t)$ is a (possibly weighted) graph describing the contacts active at time $t$. Consider an SIS or SIR compartmental epidemic model on $\mathcal{G}$ with per-contact infection rate $\beta$ and recovery rate $\mu$, and let $\tau_c(\mathcal{G})$ denote the epidemic threshold of the model on $\mathcal{G}$, defined (e.g., via the dominant eigenvalue of the appropriate infection-propagation operator built from $(G_t)$) as the critical value of $\beta/\mu$ separating the regime in which an initial infection dies out almost surely from the regime in which it persists/spreads with positive probability as $n \to \infty$.

Standard threshold theory assumes that the entire trajectory $(G_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ is observed. Suppose instead that one only has access to a partial observation $\mathcal{O}$ of $\mathcal{G}$, formalized as one of the following:
(i) a temporal subsample: $G_t$ is observed only for $t$ in a random or deterministic subset $S \subseteq [0,T]$;
(ii) a vertex/edge subsample: at each observed time, only the induced subgraph on a random subset $V' \subseteq V$, or a Bernoulli-sampled subset of edges, is recorded;
(iii) a coarse aggregation: only time-aggregated graphs $\bar G_k = \bigcup_{t \in I_k} G_t$ over a partition $\{I_k\}$ of $[0,T]$ are observed.

Develop a methodology that, given $\mathcal{O}$, produces an estimator $\hat\tau_c(\mathcal{O})$ of $\tau_c(\mathcal{G})$ together with a quantitative uncertainty bound, i.e., explicit nonasymptotic or asymptotic confidence intervals
$$\Pr\big(|\hat\tau_c(\mathcal{O}) - \tau_c(\mathcal{G})| \leq \varepsilon(\mathcal{O})\big) \geq 1 - \delta,$$
where $\varepsilon(\mathcal{O})$ depends explicitly on the sampling design and intensity. Furthermore, characterize, for each epidemiological regime (e.g., short-timescale outbreaks vs. endemic dynamics; sparse vs. dense contact networks; SIS vs. SIR), the minimal class of partial observations $\mathcal{O}$ that is sufficient to guarantee a prescribed accuracy $\varepsilon$ with confidence $1-\delta$ in the threshold estimate.

Setup. In deep inelastic lepton–nucleon scattering, let $F(x,Q^2)$ denote a nucleon structure function depending on the Bjorken variable $x$ and the squared momentum transfer $Q^2$. At large $Q^2 \ge Q_0^2$, $F$ is well described by a smooth scaling curve $F_{\rm scaling}(x,Q^2)$ predicted by perturbative QCD with logarithmic ($Q^2$-dependent) evolution. At low $Q^2$, the same structure function (plotted, for example, versus the Nachtmann variable or as a function of the final hadronic mass $W$) exhibits prominent nucleon resonance peaks.

Bloom–Gilman duality is the empirical statement that:
(i) when averaged over a suitable interval in $W$ (or equivalently in $x$), the low-$Q^2$ resonance structure of $F(x,Q^2)$ reproduces the high-$Q^2$ scaling curve $F_{\rm scaling}(x,Q_0^2)$; and
(ii) as $Q^2$ increases, the locally averaged resonance curve smoothly slides down along the scaling curve, matching its slope, until the resonances dissolve into the scaling regime.

Problem. Starting from the QCD Lagrangian (quarks and gluons with the standard non-Abelian gauge interaction) alone, derive Bloom–Gilman duality from first principles. That is, prove rigorously, without postulating a hadronic spectrum or invoking phenomenological models of bound-state production, that the exact electromagnetic structure function of the nucleon defined by QCD necessarily exhibits the resonance/scaling matching and sliding behavior described in (i)–(ii).

A first-principles QCD derivation of Bloom–Gilman duality remains an open problem. In perturbative QCD, the running strong coupling $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ is governed by the renormalization-group equation
$$Q^2\,\frac{d\alpha_s(Q^2)}{dQ^2} = \beta(\alpha_s) = -\alpha_s^2\bigl(b_0 + b_1\alpha_s + b_2\alpha_s^2 + b_3\alpha_s^3 + \cdots\bigr),$$
where the first two coefficients $b_0$ and $b_1$ are universal but the coefficients $b_i$ for $i\ge 2$ depend on the chosen renormalization scheme. A typical observable used to extract $\alpha_s$ at a momentum scale $Q$ has a perturbative expansion of the form
$$\delta_{\rm QCD}(Q) = \sum_{n\ge 1} c_n\,\alpha_s^n(Q^2),$$
where the coefficients $c_n$ are conjectured to grow factorially, $c_n \sim n!\,K^n$, due to renormalon singularities in the Borel plane that reflect non-perturbative power corrections of order $(\Lambda_{\rm QCD}^2/Q^2)^p$. As a result, the series is divergent (asymptotic), and truncations carry an irreducible ambiguity of size $\sim e^{-1/(b_0\alpha_s)}$.

Problem. Devise a determination of $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ from physical observables that simultaneously
(i) eliminates or controls the scheme dependence introduced by the higher beta-function coefficients $b_i$, $i\ge 2$, and
(ii) tames the factorial $n!\,\alpha_s^n$ renormalon-driven divergence of $\delta_{\rm QCD}(Q)$ — for instance by an unambiguous prescription that subtracts renormalon contributions while consistently incorporating the associated non-perturbative power corrections — so as to yield a value of $\alpha_s(Q^2)$ whose theoretical uncertainty can in principle be reduced below the present perturbative ambiguity.
