Consider two-dimensional, two-phase composite materials in which one phase is an isotropic linearly elastic solid with bulk modulus $\kappa$ and shear modulus $\mu$, and the other phase is void (vanishing moduli). For any sufficiently regular periodic (or statistically homogeneous) microgeometry, classical homogenization assigns to the composite an isotropic effective bulk modulus $\kappa_*$ and an isotropic effective shear modulus $\mu_*$.

Restrict attention to microgeometries that simultaneously realize the two extreme constraints
$$\kappa_* = 0 \qquad\text{and}\qquad \frac{1}{\kappa} = 0,$$
that is, the composite is effectively incompressible-auxetic at the macroscopic level (zero effective bulk modulus) while the solid phase is taken in the rigid-bulk limit (infinite bulk modulus, finite shear modulus $\mu$).

Prove or disprove: under these constraints, the supremum of the effective shear modulus over all admissible isotropic microgeometries equals
$$\mu_*^{\max} = \frac{4\mu}{5}.$$

Equivalently, decide whether $\mu_* \le 4\mu/5$ holds for every such composite, with equality attainable (in a limiting sense) by some microstructure.

The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a list of open problems on composites (Milton, Phil. Trans. Roy. Soc. A, 2021). Consider a two-phase composite occupying a reference region $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ consisting of an isotropic hyperelastic solid phase and a void (empty) phase. Subject the composite to macroscopically uniform finite (not necessarily infinitesimal) deformations characterized by an average deformation gradient $\bar F$, decomposed via the polar decomposition into stretches and rotations, and expressed through invariants such as a macroscopic compressive (volumetric) deformation $\bar J = \det \bar F$ and a macroscopic shear (deviatoric) deformation. Geometric nonlinearities (large rotations and stretches) are retained, so the response cannot be captured solely by linearized infinitesimal elastic moduli.

Problem: Derive rigorous, microstructure-independent bounds that correlate the simultaneously achievable macroscopic compressive deformations and macroscopic shear deformations of such elastic-and-void composites in the regime of finite (but moderate) deformations. Equivalently, characterize the admissible region in the plane of macroscopic compressive vs. shear deformation invariants, going beyond bounds formulated only on infinitesimal linearized effective moduli.

Consider three-dimensional linearly elastic polycrystals: composite materials assembled from grains that are all copies of a single anisotropic crystal, where the grains differ only by rigid rotations of the crystal's elasticity tensor. Assume the grain geometry is such that the resulting composite is macroscopically (statistically) isotropic, so that its effective elasticity tensor is described by an effective bulk modulus κ* and an effective shear modulus μ*.

Given the elasticity tensor of a fixed single crystal, determine the set
G = { (κ*, μ*) ∈ ℝ_{>0} × ℝ_{>0} : (κ*, μ*) is realizable as the pair of effective bulk and shear moduli of some macroscopically isotropic 3D polycrystal built from rotated copies of the given crystal }.

Specifically: characterize G completely. The known sharp bounds on κ* alone, together with the known (but not generally optimal) bounds on μ*, confine G to a rectangle in the (κ*, μ*)-plane; the task is to determine the precise feasible region within (or strictly inside) this rectangle, and to exhibit microgeometries attaining each point of the boundary.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

In the planar (2D) case, a complete characterization of the achievable (κ*, μ*) pairs for polycrystals built from a single crystal was obtained by Avellaneda–Cherkaev–Gibiansky–Milton–Rudelson and refined in subsequent works (including extremal planar polycrystal constructions published in 2021). In three dimensions, the bulk-modulus bounds are sharp but the shear-modulus bounds are generally not optimal, and no complete characterization of the feasible (κ*, μ*) region appears in the literature; recent works (e.g., on Hashin–Shtrikman bounds for 3D polycrystals of arbitrary symmetry) only provide bounds, not a full characterization. The problem is thus still open in 3D.

Consider isotropic composite materials formed by mixing two isotropic linearly elastic phases in prescribed volume fractions f_1 and f_2 = 1 - f_1, where each phase i ∈ {1,2} has bulk modulus κ_i and shear modulus μ_i (with the limiting cases of one phase being rigid, μ_i = κ_i = ∞, or void, μ_i = κ_i = 0, allowed). For any such composite, the homogenized (effective) elasticity tensor is again isotropic and is characterized by an effective bulk modulus κ* and an effective shear modulus μ*. Define the attainable set

  G(f_1; κ_1, μ_1, κ_2, μ_2) = { (κ*, μ*) : (κ*, μ*) is realized by some isotropic two-phase composite with the given phase moduli and phase-1 volume fraction f_1 } ⊂ ℝ_{>0} × ℝ_{>0}.

The classical Hashin–Shtrikman–Walpole inequalities give two-sided bounds on κ* and μ* separately, and partial coupled bounds on the pair (κ*, μ*) are known.

Problem. Derive bounds on the set G(f_1; κ_1, μ_1, κ_2, μ_2) that strictly improve on the currently best-known inequalities relating κ* and μ* simultaneously, and ultimately determine the optimal (sharp, attainable) coupled bounds describing G exactly, including the cases in which one of the phases is rigid or void.

Subsequent work (e.g., Cherkaev–Gibiansky, Milton, Allaire–Kohn, Liu) has produced partial improvements via translation/quasiconvexification methods and identified extremal microstructures attaining the bulk-modulus or shear-modulus bound separately, but a complete description of the optimal G-closure for two isotropic phases (especially with rigid or void inclusions) has not been established.

Background and definitions.

A represented space is a pair (X, δ_X) where δ_X is a partial surjection from Baire space N^N onto X. A multivalued function f : ⊆ X ⇒ Y between represented spaces is Weihrauch reducible to g : ⊆ Z ⇒ W, written f ≤_W g, if there are computable functions H, K : ⊆ N^N → N^N such that whenever G is a realizer of g (i.e. G(z) is a name of some w ∈ g(δ_Z(z))), the map p ↦ H(p, G(K(p))) is a realizer of f.

A topological space X is Fréchet–Urysohn if for every A ⊆ X and every x in the closure of A, there is a sequence in A converging to x. A space is coPolish if it is the colimit of an increasing sequence of Polish subspaces with appropriate compatibility (equivalently, a quasi-Polish countably tight cb_0 space arising as a sequential colimit of Polish spaces); examples include the space of polynomials with the colimit topology of finite-dimensional subspaces.

For a represented space X, let A(X) denote the hyperspace of closed subsets represented by enumerations of basic open sets that intersect the set (the "overt" representation). The overt choice principle on X is the multivalued function
  VC_X : ⊆ A(X) ⇒ X,
sending a nonempty closed set A ∈ A(X) to any element of A.

The Weihrauch degree LPO is represented by the limited principle of omniscience
  LPO : N^N → {0,1}, p ↦ 1 if p = 0^ω, else 0.

The principle isEmpty : A(N^N) → S sends a closed subset of Baire space (given by its overt representation) to the Sierpiński-space value 1 if the set is empty and ⊥ otherwise.

It is known that for every non-Fréchet–Urysohn coPolish space X,
  LPO ≤_W VC_X ≤_W (isEmpty : A(N^N) → S).

Problem. Determine, for each non-Fréchet–Urysohn coPolish space X, the precise Weihrauch degree of VC_X. More precisely, give a classification (e.g. in terms of standard Weihrauch degrees or a topological invariant of X) that strictly improves upon the bounds LPO ≤_W VC_X ≤_W (isEmpty : A(N^N) → S).

Background and definitions.

Work in the framework of Weihrauch reducibility on multi-valued partial functions between represented spaces. For multi-valued problems f, g, write f ≤_W g for Weihrauch reducibility. Two problems are Weihrauch-equivalent (denoted ≡_W) if they reduce to each other; a Weihrauch degree is an equivalence class under ≡_W.

Define the problem AoUC ("All-or-Unique Choice on the unit interval") as follows: given a pair (a, b) of real numbers with 0 ≤ a ≤ b, AoUC outputs any real x satisfying b·x = a. (Equivalently, if b > 0 the unique solution x = a/b must be produced, and if b = 0 any real x is an admissible output.)

For a problem f, the diamond operator f^⋄ denotes the closure of f under finite (adaptively chosen) compositions: f^⋄ is, up to Weihrauch equivalence, the supremum of f, f ⋆ f, f ⋆ f ⋆ f, …, where ⋆ is the compositional product in the Weihrauch lattice. Thus AoUC^⋄ is the Weihrauch degree obtained by allowing finitely many adaptive applications of AoUC.

Problem.

Exhibit a "natural" computational problem — for instance, one arising from a standard question in linear algebra — whose Weihrauch degree is precisely AoUC^⋄, or prove that no such natural problem exists.

Setup. Work in the Baire space $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with its product topology. For a (partial) function $f:\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}\to\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, the Wadge game $G(f)$ is played as follows. In each round, Player I plays one natural number, extending an input sequence $x\in\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, while Player II plays either a natural number, extending an output sequence $y\in\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, or a "pass" symbol. After $\omega$ rounds, Player II wins if either Player I's sequence $x$ does not lie in $\operatorname{dom}(f)$, or Player II's sequence $y$ is infinite and equals $f(x)$; otherwise Player I wins. It is a classical fact that $f$ is continuous on its domain iff Player II has a winning strategy in $G(f)$, and (in the effective version) Player I has a winning strategy in $G(f)$ iff $f$ is discontinuous at some point of its domain.

Weihrauch reducibility. Given multi-valued partial functions $F,G$ on $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, one says $F\le_{\mathrm W} G$ if there exist computable functionals $H,K$ such that for every $G$-realizer $g$, the map $x\mapsto K(x,g(H(x)))$ is a realizer of $F$. The induced equivalence classes are the Weihrauch degrees.

Problem. Determine the Weihrauch degree of the multi-valued problem
$$\mathsf{WadgeDisc}\;:\;\sigma \;\mapsto\; \{x\in\operatorname{dom}(f_\sigma) : f_\sigma \text{ is discontinuous at } x\},$$
where the input $\sigma$ is (a code of) a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for some function $f_\sigma$, and the output is any point at which $f_\sigma$ is discontinuous.

It is known that whenever such a winning strategy is computable, there exists a computable point of discontinuity for $f_\sigma$; the question asks whether this passage is uniformly Weihrauch-computable, and if so to identify its precise Weihrauch degree.

Background. A multi-valued function (problem) on Baire space is a partial relation $f \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}} \times \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, where the domain consists of "instances" and, for each instance $x$, the set $f(x) = \{y : (x,y) \in f\}$ is the set of "solutions". Weihrauch reducibility $f \le_W g$ holds iff there exist computable functionals $H, K$ such that, for every instance $x$ of $f$, $K(x)$ is an instance of $g$ and, for every solution $y$ of $g$ on $K(x)$, $H(x,y)$ is a solution of $f$ on $x$. The resulting equivalence classes form the Weihrauch degrees, a lattice studied in computable analysis.

Extended Weihrauch reducibility generalises this notion by allowing the "instances" and "solutions" to be arbitrary subsets of Baire space (rather than single points), and by formulating the reduction in a realizability framework (e.g. as instance degrees in the Kleene–Vesley realizability topos). The resulting structure, the extended Weihrauch degrees, contains a canonical embedding of the ordinary Weihrauch degrees but properly extends them with additional degrees not arising from any single multi-valued function in the classical sense.

Problem. Provide a clear structural account describing how the additional degrees that occur in the extended Weihrauch degrees but not in the (image of the) ordinary Weihrauch degrees relate to the ordinary Weihrauch degrees. In particular, characterise the new degrees in terms of natural operations (such as suprema, infima, implications, or other lattice-theoretic / topos-theoretic constructions) applied to ordinary Weihrauch degrees, or otherwise describe their position within the extended Weihrauch lattice relative to the embedded copy of the ordinary Weihrauch degrees.

Background. Weihrauch reducibility compares multi-valued functions on represented spaces: for partial multi-valued functions f, g :⊆ N^N ⇒ N^N, one writes f ≤_W g if there exist computable functions H, K :⊆ N^N → N^N such that, whenever p is a name for an instance of f, K(p) is a name for an instance of g, and whenever q is a name for a g-solution to that instance, H⟨p, q⟩ is a name for an f-solution. The induced equivalence classes are the (standard) Weihrauch degrees, and they form an extensively studied lattice used to calibrate the uniform computational content of mathematical theorems.

Bauer's extended Weihrauch degrees enlarge this structure by representing problems as relations (or predicates) on Baire space rather than as multi-valued functions; in this larger structure one can also assign a degree to "problems" that have no solutions at all, including formal counterparts of false mathematical statements. The standard Weihrauch degrees embed into the extended Weihrauch degrees in a natural way, and the extended structure contains additional degrees corresponding to such empty/false problems.

Problem. Exhibit explicit and mathematically natural examples of extended Weihrauch degrees that arise from false statements (i.e. problems with empty solution set, or that otherwise fail to be realized by any function), and determine how these degrees sit relative to the embedded scaffold of standard Weihrauch degrees: identify their position with respect to standard benchmark degrees (such as the degrees of LPO, LLPO, choice principles C_N, C_{N^N}, WKL, lim, etc.), describe their behaviour under the lattice and algebraic operations (join, meet, product, parallelization, composition), and characterize structural features that distinguish "false" extended Weihrauch degrees from those induced by genuine multi-valued functions.

For a complex-valued potential $q\in L_2(0,\pi)$ that vanishes on $(0,a)$ where $a\in(0,\pi)$, and for $j=0,1$, let $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$ denote the boundary value problem
$$-y''(x)+q(x)\,y(x-a)=\lambda\,y(x),\qquad 0<x<\pi,$$
with the boundary conditions $y(0)=0$ and $y^{(j)}(\pi)=0$ (Dirichlet at $\pi$ for $j=0$, Neumann at $\pi$ for $j=1$). Let $\{\lambda_{n,j}\}_{n\ge 1}$ be the eigenvalue sequence of $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$.

Inverse Problem. Given the two spectra $\{\lambda_{n,0}\}$ and $\{\lambda_{n,1}\}$, recover $q$.

Determine, more generally, the complete classification of pairs $(a,\text{boundary-condition type})$ — where the boundary condition at $0$ and at $\pi$ are each chosen from an admissible family of separated linear conditions — for which the two spectra uniquely determine the potential $q$, and the pairs for which uniqueness fails (i.e., for which there exist iso-bispectral potentials).

Let $a\in(0,\pi)$ be a fixed delay parameter, and let $q\in L_2(0,\pi;\mathbb{C})$ be a complex-valued potential satisfying $q(x)=0$ for $x\in(0,a)$. For $j\in\{0,1\}$, let $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$ denote the boundary value problem for the functional-differential equation
$$-y''(x)+q(x)\,y(x-a)=\lambda\, y(x),\qquad x\in(0,\pi),$$
(with the convention that $y(x-a)=0$ for $x<a$), under the boundary conditions
$$y'(0)-h\,y(0)=0,\qquad y^{(j)}(\pi)+(-1)^j H\,y(\pi)=0,$$
where $h,H\in\mathbb{C}$ are fixed parameters; denote by $\sigma_j(a,q)$ the spectrum of $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$.

Two potentials $q_1,q_2$ (each vanishing on $(0,a)$) are called iso-bispectral if
$$\sigma_0(a,q_1)=\sigma_0(a,q_2)\quad\text{and}\quad \sigma_1(a,q_1)=\sigma_1(a,q_2).$$
It is known that for $a\in[\pi/2,\pi)$ the pair of spectra $\bigl(\sigma_0(a,q),\sigma_1(a,q)\bigr)$ uniquely determines $q$, while for $a\in(0,\pi/2)$ uniqueness fails: this is the degenerate regime, in which infinite families of distinct iso-bispectral potentials exist.

Problem: For every $a$ in the degenerate regime $(0,\pi/2)$, give a complete description of the class of iso-bispectral potentials, i.e., describe explicitly all complex-valued $q\in L_2(0,\pi)$ with $q|_{(0,a)}=0$ that share a given pair of spectra $\bigl(\sigma_0(a,q),\sigma_1(a,q)\bigr)$.

Non-uniqueness in the degenerate regime $a\in(0,\pi/2)$ has been established by constructing infinite families of iso-bispectral potentials: the cases $a\in[2\pi/5,\pi/2)$ and $a\in[\pi/3,2\pi/5)$ were treated first, and the remaining nonlinear case $a\in(0,\pi/3)$ was settled in a 2021 follow-up (arXiv:2102.08149) by Buterin–Vasiliev, again by constructing iso-bispectral families. The question was answered negatively: for arbitrarily small delays, the two-spectra inverse problem for the delayed Sturm–Liouville operator does not uniquely recover the potential. Consider the Sturm–Liouville-type differential equation with constant delay
\[
-y''(x) + q(x)\,y(x-a) = \lambda\, y(x), \qquad x \in (0,\pi),
\]
where the delay parameter satisfies $a \in [\pi/3, \pi)$, the complex-valued potential $q \in L_2(0,\pi)$ is supported on $[a,\pi]$, and $q(x)=0$ for $x\in[0,a)$ (so that the term $q(x)y(x-a)$ is interpreted with $y$ extended appropriately on $(-a,0)$).

For $j\in\{0,1\}$ and a fixed complex number $h\in\mathbb{C}$, let $\sigma_j(q,h)$ denote the spectrum (counted with multiplicity) of the boundary value problem
\[
-y''(x) + q(x)\,y(x-a) = \lambda\, y(x), \qquad y'(0) - h\,y(0) = 0,\quad y^{(j)}(\pi) = 0.
\]
Thus $\sigma_0(q,h)$ corresponds to the boundary condition $y(\pi)=0$ and $\sigma_1(q,h)$ to $y'(\pi)=0$.

Inverse spectral problem. Given $h\in\mathbb{C}$ and the two spectra $\sigma_0(q,h)$ and $\sigma_1(q,h)$, is the potential $q$ uniquely determined?

Question. Decide which of the following holds for $a$ in the range $[\pi/3, 2\pi/5)$ (and, more generally, for the delay ranges in $[\pi/3,\pi)$ where non-uniqueness is known to fail or to hold in the Dirichlet case $y(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0$):

(a) Construct an explicit pair of distinct potentials $q_1,q_2 \in L_2(0,\pi)$ (with the support assumption above) and a value $h\in\mathbb{C}$ such that
\[
\sigma_0(q_1,h) = \sigma_0(q_2,h) \quad\text{and}\quad \sigma_1(q_1,h) = \sigma_1(q_2,h),
\]
i.e., an iso-bispectral counterexample for the Robin-type boundary conditions; or

(b) Prove that, for every $h\in\mathbb{C}$ and every admissible $a$, the pair $(\sigma_0(q,h), \sigma_1(q,h))$ uniquely determines $q$.

The Neumann subcase $h=0$ of the Robin-type boundary condition $y'(0)-hy(0)=0$ has been resolved in the negative: a counterexample (an infinite family of iso-bispectral potentials) was constructed for delay $a\in[\pi/3,2\pi/5)$, paralleling the earlier Dirichlet ($y(0)=0$) counterexample. Fix an integer d ≥ 3. For a positive integer N, let [N] = {1, …, N}. The Erdős–Rényi d-uniform hypergraph G_d(N, 1/2) is the random hypergraph on vertex set [N] in which each of the C(N,d) possible d-element hyperedges is included independently with probability 1/2. The hypergraphic planted clique model G_d(N, 1/2, κ), with clique size κ ∈ {1, …, N}, is generated as follows: first sample G ~ G_d(N, 1/2); then pick a subset K ⊂ [N] with |K| = κ uniformly at random; then add (or keep) every d-element hyperedge whose vertices all lie in K. The hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem is the hypothesis testing problem

  H0: G ~ G_d(N, 1/2)   versus   H1: G ~ G_d(N, 1/2, κ),

with the goal of finding a test whose Type-I plus Type-II error probability tends to 0 as N → ∞.

Encode the hypergraph by its symmetric d-th order adjacency tensor A ∈ {0,1}^{N×N×…×N}. For an integer 1 ≤ k ≤ d−1, the (k, d−k)-matricization (unfolding) of A is the N^k × N^{d−k} matrix M_k(A) obtained by grouping the first k tensor indices into rows and the remaining d−k indices into columns. A "SVD-based detector on a matricization/unfolding of A" is any test that thresholds the leading singular value of M_k(A) (for some k) after appropriate centering.

Determine the following:

(a) Identify the sharp threshold function κ*(N, d) such that for κ ≫ κ*(N, d) some SVD-based test on a matricization/unfolding of A solves HPC detection (errors → 0), while for κ ≪ κ*(N, d) every such SVD-based test fails (errors → 1).

(b) Decide whether there exists a polynomial-time algorithm (not necessarily based on the SVD of a matricization) that solves HPC detection for some κ asymptotically below the threshold in (a).

Fix an integer $d \ge 2$. For a positive integer $N$, let $G_d(N, 1/2)$ denote the null model: a random $d$-uniform hypergraph on vertex set $[N]$ in which every $d$-subset of $[N]$ is included as a hyperedge independently with probability $1/2$. For an integer $\kappa = \kappa(N) \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, let $G_d(N, 1/2, \kappa)$ denote the planted-clique model: first sample a hypergraph as above, then choose a uniformly random subset $K \subseteq [N]$ of size $\kappa$ and add all $d$-subsets of $K$ as hyperedges (so $K$ becomes a $d$-uniform clique). Assume the following Hypergraphic Planted Clique (HPC) detection conjecture: if
$$\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\kappa}{\log N} \le 1-\tau\quad\text{for some }\tau>0,$$
then for every sequence of polynomial-time (in $N$) tests $\phi_N : \text{hypergraphs on }[N] \to \{0,1\}$,
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\Big(\mathbb{P}_{H_0}(\phi_N(G)=1)+\mathbb{P}_{H_1}(\phi_N(G)=0)\Big) > \tfrac{1}{2},$$
where $H_0$ is $G_d(N,1/2)$ and $H_1$ is $G_d(N,1/2,\kappa)$.

Existing rigorous evidence for this conjecture covers Metropolis-type local algorithms and low-degree polynomial tests. Provide rigorous evidence (in the form of unconditional lower bounds against detection in the regime $\log\kappa/\log N \le 1-\tau$) for the HPC detection conjecture in additional algorithmic frameworks, specifically:
(i) statistical query (SQ) algorithms,
(ii) sum-of-squares (SOS) semidefinite programming hierarchies,
(iii) belief propagation (BP),
(iv) approximate message passing (AMP).

representations.normalized:
Fix integers $d \geq 3$ and $N \geq 1$. The hypergraphic planted clique (HPC) detection problem with parameters $(N, d, \kappa)$ is the following hypothesis testing problem on $d$-uniform hypergraphs with vertex set $[N]$, encoded by their symmetric adjacency tensor $A \in \{0,1\}^{N \times \cdots \times N}$ (with zero diagonal):

- Under $H_0$, every hyperedge $\{i_1,\dots,i_d\} \subseteq [N]$ is included independently with probability $1/2$ (Erdős–Rényi $d$-uniform random hypergraph).
- Under $H_1$, a uniformly random subset $S \subseteq [N]$ of size $\kappa$ is chosen and all $\binom{\kappa}{d}$ hyperedges contained in $S$ are present; every other hyperedge is included independently with probability $1/2$.

The case $d=2$ recovers the ordinary planted clique (PC) detection problem.

There is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from HPC$(N,d,\kappa)$ to PC$(N,\kappa)$ that preserves the planted clique size: given the tensor $A$, fixing any $d-2$ indices and varying the remaining two yields an $N \times N$ adjacency matrix that constitutes a PC instance with planted clique size $\kappa$. Hence HPC detection is no harder than PC detection.

Question: In the regime $\kappa = O(N^{1/2 - \tau})$ for some fixed $\tau > 0$, does there exist a randomized polynomial-time reduction in the reverse direction, from PC$(N,\kappa)$ detection to HPC$(N,d,\kappa)$ detection (preserving the planted clique size $\kappa$), thereby establishing that the two detection problems are computationally equivalent in this threshold regime?

The problem is posed as an explicit open challenge concerning the equivalence of HPC and PC detection in the sub-square-root regime. A search for follow-up work (including reductions from PC to HPC and related tensor-PCA / hypergraph reductions through 2024–2025) did not surface a published randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC to HPC preserving the clique size $\kappa$. Existing literature establishes only the easy direction (HPC to PC) and various low-degree / SoS hardness results, but not the desired computational equivalence. The status therefore appears to remain open.

Let $I=(c,d)$ with $-\infty\le c<0<d\le\infty$, and let $w:I\to(0,\infty)$ be an admissible exponential weight in the following sense. Write $Q=\log(1/w)$ and assume:

(i) $Q$ is continuously differentiable on $I$ with $Q(0)=0$;
(ii) $Q'$ is nondecreasing on $I$, and $Q(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to c^+$ and as $x\to d^-$;
(iii) the function $T(x)=xQ'(x)/Q(x)$ ($x\ne0$) is quasi-increasing on $(0,d)$ and quasi-decreasing on $(c,0)$, and satisfies $T(x)\ge\lambda>1$ for all $x\ne 0$;
(iv) there exists $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1)$ such that $T(y)\sim T\!\left(y\bigl(1-\varepsilon_0/T(y)\bigr)\right)$ for $y\ne 0$;
(v) for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that
$$\int_{x-\delta x/T(x)}^{x+\delta x/T(x)}\frac{|Q'(s)-Q'(x)|}{|s-x|^{3/2}}\,ds\;\le\;\varepsilon\,|Q'(x)|\sqrt{T(x)/|x|}\qquad(x\ne 0).$$

For each $n\ge 1$ fix an array $\chi_n=\{x_{1,n},\dots,x_{n,n}\}\subset I$ of distinct interpolation nodes together with positive "Cotes numbers" $\{\lambda_{j,n}\}_{j=1}^n$. Let $V:I\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth weight factor that decays at the endpoints $c$ and $d$, let $0<p<\infty$, and let $\mathcal P_{n-1}$ denote the algebraic polynomials of degree at most $n-1$.

Problem. Determine sufficient (and where possible necessary) conditions on $w$, $V$, $p$, and on the arrays $(\chi_n,\lambda_{j,n})$ under which the following hold uniformly in $n$ and in $P\in\mathcal P_{n-1}$:

(a) Forward Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund quadrature estimate
$$\sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_{j,n}\, w(x_{j,n})^{-2}\,V(x_{j,n})\,|P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p \;\le\; C\int_I |P(x)w(x)|^p\,V(x)\,dx;$$

(b) Converse Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund estimate
$$\|Pw\|_{L^p(I)} \;\le\; C\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_{j,n}\, w(x_{j,n})^{-2}\,|P(x_{j,n})w(x_{j,n})|^p\Bigr)^{1/p}.$$

(c) Establish corresponding polynomial density criteria, in particular characterizing those continuous $f$ for which weighted polynomial approximation $\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\|(f-P)w\|$ tends to $0$, including endpoint-decay conditions on $fw/V$.

(d) Apply the resulting estimates to prove mean ($L^p$) and uniform convergence of Lagrange interpolation operators at the nodes $\chi_n$ and of orthogonal expansions with respect to $w^2$, and to obtain quantitative rates of convergence.

The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a survey on Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund inequalities and numerical approximation of singular integrals for exponential weights. While partial results exist for special subclasses (e.g. Freud and Erdős weights, smooth even exponential weights), a complete theory of forward/converse MZ quadrature inequalities, density criteria, and convergence of Lagrange interpolation and orthogonal expansions at the full level of generality of admissible exponential weights on an arbitrary interval $(c,d)$ has not been established.

Let $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ be a nonzero function and let $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a nonempty discrete set of bounded density, that is,
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \#\bigl(\Lambda \cap [x, x+1)\bigr) < +\infty.$$
We say that $f + \Lambda$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at level zero if
$$\sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda} f(t - \lambda) = 0 \quad \text{for almost every } t \in \mathbb{R},$$
where the series converges absolutely a.e.

The set $\Lambda$ is said to have uniform density $D(\Lambda)$ if there exists a real number $D(\Lambda)$ such that
$$\#\bigl(\Lambda \cap [x, x+r)\bigr) = D(\Lambda)\, r + o(r) \quad \text{as } r \to +\infty,$$
uniformly with respect to $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Question: Suppose $f + \Lambda$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at level zero, with $f$ and $\Lambda$ as above. Must $\Lambda$ possess a uniform density $D(\Lambda)$?

Equivalently (in Fourier-analytic form): if $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ is nonempty and of bounded density, and the Fourier transform (in the distributional sense) of the measure $\delta_\Lambda = \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda} \delta_\lambda$ vanishes on some nonempty open interval $(a, b) \subset \mathbb{R}$, does it follow that $\Lambda$ has a uniform density?

Let $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ be a nonzero function such that the set $\{x \in \mathbb{R} : f(x) \neq 0\}$ has finite Lebesgue measure. A discrete set $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ is said to have bounded density if $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \#(\Lambda \cap [x, x+1]) < \infty$. We say that $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at level $w \in \mathbb{C}$ by the translation set $\Lambda$ if
$$\sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda} f(x - \lambda) = w \quad \text{for almost every } x \in \mathbb{R},$$
with the series converging absolutely a.e. We say that $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ has a periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions
$$\Lambda = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N} (a_j \mathbb{Z} + b_j),$$
where $a_j > 0$ and $b_j \in \mathbb{R}$.

Question: Suppose $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ at some level $w$ by a translation set $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}$ of bounded density. Must $\Lambda$ necessarily have a periodic structure?

Let G = (V, E) be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. For vertices x, y ∈ V, let d_G(x, y) denote the length (number of edges) of a shortest path between x and y in G. A spanning tree T of G is called a tree 3-spanner of G if, for every pair of vertices x, y ∈ V, the distance d_T(x, y) in T satisfies d_T(x, y) ≤ 3 · d_G(x, y).

A graph is chordal if it contains no induced cycle of length at least 4. For an integer k ≥ 3, a k-sun is the graph on 2k vertices consisting of a cycle u_1, w_1, u_2, w_2, …, u_k, w_k, u_1 together with all edges of a clique on {u_1, …, u_k}, where each w_i has degree exactly 2. A graph is strongly chordal if it is chordal and contains no induced k-sun for any k ≥ 3.

The Tree 3-Spanner problem on a graph class C asks: given G ∈ C, decide whether G admits a tree 3-spanner.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that decides Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is chordal? In particular, does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm deciding Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is strongly chordal?

Let G = (V, E) be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. For vertices x, y ∈ V, let d_G(x, y) denote the length (number of edges) of a shortest path between x and y in G. A spanning tree T of G is called a tree 3-spanner of G if, for every pair of vertices x, y ∈ V, the distance d_T(x, y) in T satisfies d_T(x, y) ≤ 3 · d_G(x, y).

A graph is chordal if it contains no induced cycle of length at least 4. For an integer k ≥ 3, a k-sun is the graph on 2k vertices consisting of a cycle u_1, w_1, u_2, w_2, …, u_k, w_k, u_1 together with all edges of a clique on {u_1, …, u_k}, where each w_i has degree exactly 2. A graph is strongly chordal if it is chordal and contains no induced k-sun for any k ≥ 3.

The Tree 3-Spanner problem on a graph class C asks: given G ∈ C, decide whether G admits a tree 3-spanner.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that decides Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is chordal? In particular, does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm deciding Tree 3-Spanner when the input graph is strongly chordal?

Let $\mathbb{R}$ be the real line equipped with Lebesgue measure $\operatorname{mes}$. For a measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $0<\operatorname{mes}(\Omega)<+\infty$, let $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ denote its indicator function. Given a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ and a positive integer $w$, we say that $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ by translations along $\Lambda$ at level $w$ if
$$\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbf{1}_\Omega(x-\lambda)=w\qquad\text{for almost every }x\in\mathbb{R}.$$
The case $w=1$ corresponds to a partition (modulo measure zero) of $\mathbb{R}$ into translates of $\Omega$.

Say that a set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ has periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union
$$\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{N}\bigl(a_j\mathbb{Z}+b_j\bigr)$$
of finitely many arithmetic progressions, where $a_j>0$ and $b_j\in\mathbb{R}$. Otherwise, $\Lambda$ is said to lack periodic structure.

Question: Does there exist a measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}$ with $0<\operatorname{mes}(\Omega)<+\infty$, a positive integer $w$, and a translation set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ lacking periodic structure such that $\mathbf{1}_\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}$ along $\Lambda$ at level $w$? In particular, can this be achieved at level $w=1$?

Call a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ of tempered growth if there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $\#(\Lambda\cap(-r,r))=O(r^N)$ as $r\to\infty$. Say that $\Lambda$ has a periodic structure if it can be written as a disjoint union of finitely many arithmetic progressions, i.e. $\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{M}(a_j\mathbb{Z}+b_j)$ with real $b_j$ and $a_j>0$. Given $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ and $w\in\mathbb{C}$, we say $f+\Lambda$ is a tiling of $\mathbb{R}$ at level $w$ if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}f(x-\lambda)=w$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, with the sum converging absolutely a.e.

Prove or disprove: if $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonzero with compact support and $f+\Lambda$ is a tiling at some level $w$ for a discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}$ of tempered growth, then $\Lambda$ must have a periodic structure (and in particular bounded density).

A discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is said to have bounded density if there exists $M>0$ such that $\#(\Lambda\cap(x+B))\le M$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, where $B$ denotes the open unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For a lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ (i.e., a discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^d$ of full rank), we write $f+L$ for the tiling by the translates of $f$ along $L$.

Must there exist a lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $w'$ such that $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ at level $w'$ with translation set $L$ (i.e., $f+L$ is a tiling)?

Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple connected graph. For an integer t ≥ 1, a spanning subgraph H of G is called a t-spanner of G if for every pair of vertices u, v ∈ V the distance d_H(u, v) in H is at most t · d_G(u, v), where d_G denotes the usual shortest-path distance. A tree t-spanner of G is a t-spanner of G that is a tree (necessarily a spanning tree). The TREE t-SPANNER problem asks, given a graph G, to decide whether G admits a tree t-spanner.

A graph is called a path graph if it is the intersection graph of a family of paths in some host tree (equivalently, the vertices can be put in bijection with paths in a tree so that two vertices are adjacent iff the corresponding paths share at least one vertex). A graph is chordal if every cycle of length at least 4 has a chord. A chordal graph is strongly chordal if every cycle of even length at least 6 has an odd chord (a chord joining two vertices whose distance along the cycle is odd).

Questions:
(a) For each fixed integer t ≥ 3, determine the computational complexity of TREE t-SPANNER when the input graph is restricted to be a path graph.
(b) In particular, determine the computational complexity of TREE 3-SPANNER when the input graph is restricted to be a path graph that is also strongly chordal.

The lower bound $f(n;C_4)\ge 2^{\mathrm{ex}(n,C_4)}=2^{(1/2+o(1))n^{3/2}}$ is immediate from extremal $C_4$-free graphs, and Kleitman–Winston proved an upper bound of the form $2^{c\,n^{3/2}}$ for some constant $c$, but the matching constant $c=1/2$ remains unproven. Surveys on enumeration of $H$-free graphs for bipartite $H$ continue to list this as open: even the correct constant in the exponent for $C_4$-free graphs is not known.

Background and definitions. For an integer k ≥ 1, let b : R^k → {−1, 1} be a Borel measurable function. For a positive integer d, let C_d denote the set of d×d real correlation matrices (symmetric positive semidefinite matrices with all diagonal entries equal to 1). Given X = (X_1,…,X_d) a centered Gaussian vector in R^{kd} whose "block correlation" structure is described by a matrix Σ ∈ C_d (with each block X_i ∈ R^k standard Gaussian), define the completely correlation preserving (CCP) function associated with b by

   h_b(Σ) := ( E[ b(X_i) b(X_j) ] )_{1 ≤ i,j ≤ d}    ∈ C_d.

Restricted to the diagonal "scalar input" r ∈ [−1, 1] (the case d = 2), h_b induces a real-analytic odd function on (−1, 1), still denoted h_b, with h_b(0) = 0 in the case relevant below.

Workflow conditions. Say that b satisfies the workflow if all of the following hold:
 (H) h_b : [−1, 1] → [−1, 1] is a homeomorphism with h_b(0) = 0; in particular h_b is strictly increasing.
 (RA) The inverse g_b := h_b^{-1} admits a Taylor series expansion g_b(t) = Σ_{n ≥ 0} a_n t^n that converges absolutely on [−1, 1], i.e. Σ_{n ≥ 0} |a_n| < ∞.
 (PI(1)) Defining f_b(r) := Σ_{n ≥ 0} |a_n| r^n on [0, 1], there exists 0 < r* < 1 such that f_b(r*) = 1.

It is known that under (H), (RA), and (PI(1)), the real Grothendieck constant satisfies K_G^R ≤ 1 / r*. Two classical examples satisfying the workflow are the sign function sign : R → {−1, 1} (Grothendieck/Krivine function) and the function giving the Haagerup function in the complex case.

Problem. Exhibit an integer k ≥ 1 and a Borel measurable function b : R^k → {−1, 1}, distinct from the (one-dimensional) sign function, such that b satisfies the workflow conditions (H), (RA), and (PI(1)) above, and such that the resulting bound 1/r* is strictly smaller than the best currently known upper bound for the real Grothendieck constant K_G^R. Equivalently, find such a b that yields, via this workflow, a strict improvement of the known upper bound on K_G^R.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The exact value of the real Grothendieck constant K_G^R has been open since 1953. The CCP-function workflow framework continues to be actively studied (e.g., Oertel's 2024 Springer Lecture Notes and the related arXiv paper 2305.04428), and finding a non-sign function b : R^k → {−1, 1} satisfying all workflow conditions and yielding a strictly improved bound is highlighted as a persistent open problem with non-trivial combinatorial obstructions. While Braverman–Makarychev–Makarychev–Naor proved K_G^R is strictly smaller than Krivine's bound (non-constructively), no explicit b of the desired form delivering an improved 1/r* bound via this workflow is known.

Background and notation. Let $b\in[-1,1]$ and let $h_b:[-1,1]\to[-1,1]$ be a real, one-dimensional completely correlation-preserving (CCP) function attached to $b$, i.e. an analytic function on a neighbourhood of $0$ with $h_b(0)=0$, $h_b'(0)\neq 0$, having a power series expansion
$$h_b(\rho)=\sum_{n\ge 1}\alpha_n\,\rho^n,\qquad \alpha_1\neq 0.$$
Since $\alpha_1\neq 0$, the formal/analytic inverse $g_b:=h_b^{-1}$ exists in a neighbourhood of $0$ and admits a power series expansion
$$g_b(t)=\sum_{n\ge 1}\beta_n\,t^n.$$

Conjectured pattern. For each integer $k\ge 2$ let
$$A_k\;\subset\;\Bigl\{\mu=(\mu_2,\mu_3,\dots,\mu_n)\in\mathbb{N}_0^{\,n-1}\;:\;\sum_{l=2}^{n}l\,\mu_{l-1}=n-1+k\Bigr\}$$
be a (presently unspecified) finite set of multi-indices, and define
$$p_k(\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\dots,\alpha_n)\;:=\;\sum_{(\nu_2,\dots,\nu_n)\in A_k}\;\prod_{l=2}^{n}\alpha_l^{\,\nu_l}.$$
Suppose that for each integer $k\ge 2$ there exists an integer $m_k\in\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ such that, for every integer $n\ge 4$, the coefficients $\beta_n$ of the inverse series satisfy the identity
$$n\,\beta_n\,\alpha_1^{\,2n-1}\;=\;-n\,\alpha_1^{\,n-2}\,\alpha_n\;+\;\sum_{k=2}^{n-2}(-1)^k m_k\binom{n-1+k}{k}\alpha_1^{\,(n-1)-k}\,p_k(\alpha_2,\dots,\alpha_n)\;+\;(-1)^{n-1}\binom{2(n-1)}{n-1}\alpha_2^{\,n-1}.$$

Problem. For all integers $n\ge 4$ and all $k$ with $2\le k\le n-2$:
(a) Prove that the above representation of $n\beta_n\alpha_1^{2n-1}$ holds.
(b) Determine the index sets $A_k$ explicitly.
(c) Determine the integers $m_k\in\{1,\dots,k\}$ explicitly.
If an explicit determination is not feasible, establish what can be proved and identify the obstructions.

For integers $n\ge 1$ and $1\le k\le n$, the ordinary partial Bell polynomial in the indeterminates $x_1,x_2,\dots$ is defined by
$$
\hat B_{n,k}(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_{n-k+1}) \;=\; \sum \frac{k!}{j_1!\,j_2!\cdots j_{n-k+1}!}\, x_1^{j_1}x_2^{j_2}\cdots x_{n-k+1}^{j_{n-k+1}},
$$
where the sum runs over all tuples $(j_1,\dots,j_{n-k+1})$ of non-negative integers satisfying
$$
j_1+j_2+\cdots+j_{n-k+1}=k,\qquad j_1+2j_2+\cdots+(n-k+1)j_{n-k+1}=n.
$$
Suppose $f(z)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_n z^n$ is a formal power series with $a_1\ne 0$, and let $g(z)=\sum_{n\ge 1}\beta_n z^n$ denote its compositional inverse. By the Faà di Bruno formula one has the closed-form representation
$$
\beta_n \;=\; \frac{1}{n\, a_1^n}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(-1)^k\,\frac{(n+k-1)!}{(n-1)!}\,\hat B_{n-1,k}\!\left(\tfrac{a_2}{a_1},\tfrac{a_3}{a_1},\dots\right),\qquad n\ge 2.
$$

Develop a structural theory of the ordinary partial Bell polynomials $\hat B_{n,k}$ that is strong enough to yield closed-form, or otherwise computationally effective, descriptions of the values $\hat B_{n,k}(x_1,\dots,x_{n-k+1})$ entering the inversion coefficients $\beta_n$ above, in a generality sufficient to handle Taylor-series inversion of analytic functions whose coefficient sequences are not assumed to satisfy any complete-correlation-preservation property. Provide such a theory together with: (i) explicit recursive or closed-form identities for the family $\{\hat B_{n,k}\}$ that reduce the combinatorial complexity of the sum defining $\beta_n$, (ii) inductive frameworks (potentially stronger than ordinary induction on $n\in\mathbb{N}$, such as Noetherian induction on a suitable well-founded order on multi-indices) that allow the verification of structural statements about $\hat B_{n,k}$, and (iii) algorithmic procedures, possibly based on computer algebra, that compute $\hat B_{n,k}$ and the resulting $\beta_n$ efficiently for large $n$.

Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and define the complex Haagerup function $h:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ by
$$h(z)\;=\;\frac{\pi}{4}\,z\,\, {}_{2}F_{1}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2};\,2;\,|z|^{2}\right),$$
where ${}_{2}F_{1}$ is the Gauss hypergeometric function. Since $h$ is a smooth bijection from $\mathbb{D}$ onto its image and $h'(0)=\pi/4\neq 0$, the (formal/local) inverse $h^{-1}$ admits a power-series expansion of the form
$$h^{-1}(w)\;=\;\sum_{n\ge 0}\sum_{k\ge 0} c_{n,k}\, w^{n}\,\overline{w}^{k}$$
on a neighbourhood of $0$ (the appearance of $|z|^{2}=z\bar z$ in $h$ forces a real-analytic, rather than holomorphic, expansion).

Problem. Determine an explicit closed-form formula for the coefficients $c_{n,k}$ of the inverse $h^{-1}$, or alternatively establish structural results (e.g. recursions, generating-function identities, asymptotics, or sign/positivity properties) that characterize them. In particular, express $c_{n,k}$ in a form that avoids the combinatorial complexity introduced by the ordinary partial Bell polynomials appearing in the generic Lagrange-type inversion of two-variable real-analytic series.

Let $\Phi$ denote the standard normal cumulative distribution function and, for $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $\Sigma_2(\rho)=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$. For $p\in(0,1)$, define the bivariate Gaussian copula correlation function
$$\psi(p,p;\rho)\;=\;\mathbb{P}\bigl(X\le \Phi^{-1}(p),\ Y\le \Phi^{-1}(p)\bigr)-p^2,$$
where $(X,Y)$ is a centered bivariate Gaussian vector with covariance matrix $\Sigma_2(\rho)$ (more precisely, $\psi(p,p;\rho)$ is the standard Gaussian-copula expression that, after centering and normalizing, encodes the Pearson correlation produced by the Gaussian copula at level $p$).

For any measurable function $\chi:\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,1\}$ define
$$h_\chi(\rho)\;=\;\mathbb{E}\bigl[\chi(X)\chi(Y)\bigr],\qquad (X,Y)\sim\mathcal{N}_2(0,\Sigma_2(\rho)).$$

Question: Does there exist a parameter $p\in(0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}$ and a measurable sign-valued function $\chi_p:\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$\psi(p,p;\rho)\;=\;h_{\chi_p}(\rho)\quad\text{for every }\rho\in[-1,1]\,?$$

Equivalently, can the Gaussian-copula CCP function $\psi(p,p;\cdot)$ (for some $p\ne 1/2$) be realized as the correlation function $\rho\mapsto\mathbb{E}[\chi_p(X)\chi_p(Y)]$ of a $\{-1,1\}$-valued function of a standard normal variable?

Background and definitions.

(a) Bivariate Gaussian copula and tetrachoric series. Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be a centered Gaussian vector with $\mathbb{E}[X_i^2]=1$ and $\mathbb{E}[X_1 X_2]=\rho\in[-1,1]$. For real-valued square-integrable functions $f,g$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with respect to the standard Gaussian measure $\gamma$, expand $f=\sum_{k\ge 0}\hat f_k H_k$ and $g=\sum_{k\ge 0}\hat g_k H_k$ in the orthonormal Hermite basis $\{H_k\}_{k\ge 0}$. The Mehler/tetrachoric identity gives
$$\mathbb{E}[f(X_1)g(X_2)]=\sum_{k\ge 0}\hat f_k\,\hat g_k\,\rho^{k}.$$
For sign-valued $f,g\colon\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,+1\}$ define
$$T_{f,g}(\rho):=\mathbb{E}[f(X_1)g(X_2)],$$
which is an odd-or-even real-analytic function of $\rho$ on $[-1,1]$ with $T_{f,g}(\pm 1)\in[-1,1]$.

(b) The bivariate $\chi_p$-realization problem. For a fixed exponent $p\ge 1$, the bivariate $\chi_p$-realization problem asks: which functions $\varphi\colon[-1,1]\to[-1,1]$ admit a representation
$$\varphi(\rho)=\mathbb{E}[f(X_1)g(X_2)]$$
for some pair of measurable sign-valued functions $f,g\colon\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,+1\}$, possibly subject to $L^p$-type normalizations on the Hermite coefficients? Equivalently, which kernels $\varphi$ on $[-1,1]$ arise as completely correlation preserving (CCP) functions through Gaussian rounding, in the workflow used to derive Grothendieck-type bounds?

Problem. Let $n\ge 3$ be an integer. Let $\mathbf X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ be a centered Gaussian vector with unit variances and correlation matrix $R=(\rho_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le n}\in\mathcal{C}_n$, where $\mathcal{C}_n$ denotes the set of $n\times n$ correlation matrices.

(i) Develop the multivariate analogue of the tetrachoric/Mehler expansion: derive a closed-form Hermite-type series representation, in terms of $R$, of
$$T_{f_1,\dots,f_n}(R):=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^{n} f_i(X_i)\right]$$
for arbitrary sign-valued functions $f_i\colon\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,+1\}$, $i=1,\dots,n$, including explicit formulas for the multivariate analogues of the tetrachoric coefficients.

(ii) Formulate and resolve the $n$-variate $\chi_p$-realization problem: characterize, for $n\ge 3$ and $p\ge 1$, the class of functions $\Phi\colon\mathcal{C}_n\to[-1,1]$ that can be realized as
$$\Phi(R)=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^{n} f_i(X_i)\right]$$
for some choice of sign-valued $f_1,\dots,f_n$, and determine which such $\Phi$ arise as completely correlation preserving functions in the multivariate Gaussian rounding scheme used to obtain Grothendieck-type bounds.

Background and setup. Haagerup's identity states that for unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\,\mathrm{sign}(\langle u,Z\rangle)\,\overline{\mathrm{sign}(\langle v,Z\rangle)}\,\bigr] \;=\; \langle u,v\rangle\cdot\, _2F_1\!\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12;2;|\langle u,v\rangle|^2\right),$$
where $Z=(Z_1,\dots,Z_n)$ is a standard complex Gaussian vector (i.e.\ $Z_j$ are i.i.d.\ with $Z_j=(X_j+iY_j)/\sqrt{2}$, $X_j,Y_j$ i.i.d.\ real standard normal), and $\mathrm{sign}(w)=w/|w|$ for $w\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$.

In the real case, one has Grothendieck's identity
$$\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathrm{sign}(\langle u,g\rangle)\,\mathrm{sign}(\langle v,g\rangle)\bigr] \;=\; \tfrac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\langle u,v\rangle)$$
for unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $g$ standard real Gaussian, and this identity admits a generalization based on the Gaussian copula construction: for an arbitrary pair of one-dimensional distribution functions $F,G$ with quantile functions $F^{-1},G^{-1}$, the correlation between $F^{-1}(\Phi(\langle u,g\rangle))$ and $G^{-1}(\Phi(\langle v,g\rangle))$ (with $\Phi$ the standard normal CDF) is expressible as a function $\psi_{F,G}(\langle u,v\rangle)$ of the input correlation, providing a "completely correlation preserving" framework that reproduces Grothendieck's identity for the choice of $\pm 1$-valued marginals.

Problem. Determine whether the Gaussian-copula construction described above can be transferred to the complex setting—i.e., whether there exists a construction, based on the standard complex Gaussian distribution, that takes prescribed pairs of complex marginal laws (or unit-modulus marginals) and an input Hermitian correlation $\langle u,v\rangle\in\mathbb{C}$ and returns the corresponding output complex correlation as a fixed scalar function of $\langle u,v\rangle$. If such a transfer is possible, decide whether it produces an analogous generalization of Haagerup's identity, recovering Haagerup's formula in the special case where the marginals are taken to be uniform on the unit circle (i.e., the complex sign).

Setup. Let $\mathbb{D}_d=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<d\}$ for some $d>0$, and let $\chi_p$ denote the characteristic-function-like generator obtained as follows. Fix $p\in[1,\infty)$. For a centred jointly Gaussian random vector $(X,Y)$ with $\mathbb{E}X^2=\mathbb{E}Y^2=1$ and correlation $\rho\in[-1,1]$, set
$$h_b(\rho):=\frac{\mathbb{E}\bigl[b(X)b(Y)\bigr]}{\mathbb{E}\bigl[b(X)^2\bigr]},$$
where $b:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a fixed odd Borel function with $0<\mathbb{E}[b(X)^2]<\infty$ (the "scalar building block''). Extend $h_b$ to $\mathbb{D}_d$ by its real Taylor expansion. Consider the following workflow conditions.

(H) $h_b(0)=0$ and $h_b:\mathbb{D}_d\to\mathbb{D}_d$ is a homeomorphism.

(RA) $g_b:=h_b^{-1}:\mathbb{D}_d\to\mathbb{D}_d$ admits a representation $g_b(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\beta_n z^n$ for all $z\in\mathbb{D}_d$ with real coefficients $\beta_n\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|\beta_n|<\infty$.

(ABS) Define $f_b(z):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|\beta_n|\,z^n$ for $z\in\mathbb{D}_d$.

(PI(1)) There exists $0<r<1$ such that $f_b(r)=1$.

If (H), (RA), (ABS), (PI(1)) all hold, then the real Grothendieck constant satisfies
$$K_G^{\mathbb{R}}\;\le\;\frac{1}{r},$$
where $r$ is the value in (PI(1)).

Assume now that for the specific building block $\chi_p$ (or its $n$-variate analogue obtained by replacing $(X,Y)$ with an $n$-tuple of jointly Gaussian variables and the bivariate copula realization with its $n$-variate counterpart) the underlying copula-realization problem has a positive answer; that is, $h_{\chi_p}$ (resp. its $n$-variate version) is well-defined as a map $\mathbb{D}_d\to\mathbb{D}_d$ arising from a genuine Gaussian copula construction.

Problem. Under this assumption:
(a) Determine whether the conditions (H), (RA), (ABS), and (PI(1)) hold for $h_{\chi_p}$ (and for its $n$-variate analogue).
(b) Whenever they do hold, compute, or numerically approximate to high precision, the resulting upper bound $1/r$ for $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$, and compare it with the best known upper bounds (in particular Krivine's bound $\pi/(2\ln(1+\sqrt{2}))\approx 1.7822\ldots$).

Background. A (classical) bivariate copula is a function $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ satisfying $C(u,0)=C(0,v)=0$, $C(u,1)=u$, $C(1,v)=v$, and the 2-increasing condition $C(u_2,v_2)-C(u_1,v_2)-C(u_2,v_1)+C(u_1,v_1)\ge 0$ for all $u_1\le u_2$, $v_1\le v_2$ in $[0,1]$. By Sklar's theorem, every joint cumulative distribution function $H$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with marginals $F,G$ admits a representation $H(x,y)=C(F(x),G(y))$ for a copula $C$, so copulas encode the dependence structure of pairs of real random variables independently of their marginals.

In the quantum/non-commutative setting, pairs of "random variables" are replaced by (possibly non-commuting) self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, equipped with a state, and the joint distribution function in the classical sense is generally not defined because the spectral projections need not commute. The phenomena of entanglement, Bell-type correlation inequalities, and Tsirelson-type bounds for quantum correlation matrices are quantitatively governed by the real Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$, which is the smallest constant such that for every $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$, every real matrix $(a_{ij})$, and all unit vectors $x_i,y_j$ in a real Hilbert space,
$$\Big|\sum_{i,j} a_{ij}\,\langle x_i,y_j\rangle\Big| \;\le\; K_G^{\mathbb{R}}\;\sup\Big\{\Big|\sum_{i,j} a_{ij}\,s_i t_j\Big|:\; s_i,t_j\in\{-1,+1\}\Big\}.$$

Problem. Construct a class of mathematical objects, to be called "non-commutative copulas," together with an associated notion of "non-commutative (joint) distribution function," such that:

(i) The class reduces to the usual class of bivariate copulas (and to ordinary joint cumulative distribution functions) when restricted to pairs of commuting self-adjoint operators with a common spectral resolution.

(ii) There is an analogue of Sklar's theorem: every admissible non-commutative joint object factors through a non-commutative copula and the (one-variable) spectral distributions of its marginals.

(iii) The class supports a "non-commutative dependence" theory in which entanglement, Bell-type correlations, and Tsirelson-type quantum-correlation bounds for pairs of self-adjoint contractions on Hilbert space arise as natural functionals, with extremal/limiting quantities expressible in terms of the real Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$.

Give precise definitions of these objects, prove the analogue of Sklar's theorem in this setting, and exhibit the link to $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$.

Recall that a bounded operator $N$ on a Hilbert space is called normal if $N N^* = N^* N$, and that the classical spectral theorem provides a projection-valued measure on the spectrum $\sigma(N) \subset \mathbb{C}$ representing $N$. For a finite tuple $(N_1, \dots, N_d)$ of pairwise commuting normal operators there is a joint projection-valued measure on $\mathbb{C}^d$, which underlies a multivariate functional calculus. In the classical (commutative) probabilistic setting, tail-dependence measures (such as upper and lower tail-dependence coefficients of a copula) quantify the asymptotic probability that one coordinate of a random vector takes an extreme value given that another coordinate does.

The problem has two intertwined parts:

Background. Grothendieck's inequality states that there exists a finite universal constant K (depending on the scalar field F = R or C) such that for every integer n ≥ 1, every n × n matrix (a_{ij}) with scalar entries, and every choice of unit vectors x_1,…,x_n, y_1,…,y_n in a Hilbert space H over F,

   |Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} ⟨x_i, y_j⟩| ≤ K · sup{ |Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} s_i t_j| : |s_i|, |t_j| ≤ 1, s_i, t_j ∈ F }.

The smallest such K is the Grothendieck constant K_G^F. A standard route to the inequality realizes the inner product ⟨x_i, y_j⟩ via expectations of the form E[f(⟨x_i, g⟩) f(⟨y_j, g⟩)] for a standard Gaussian vector g and a suitable function f, and an equivalent "trace-inequality" formulation expresses the bound in terms of correlation matrices arising from such Gaussian expectations.

Problem. Investigate whether the underlying Gaussian probabilistic structure used in proofs of Grothendieck's inequality, over both F = R and F = C, can be replaced by another class of probability distributions while still yielding an inequality of the same form with a finite constant. Specifically:

(a) Can the Gaussian distribution be replaced by a tail-dependent distribution function — for example, a generalized extreme value (GEV) distribution (Gumbel, Fréchet, or Weibull type) — in such a way that the resulting inequality continues to hold with a finite universal constant?

(b) Can it be replaced more generally by an infinitely divisible probability distribution on R^d (or C^d), so that an analogue of Grothendieck's inequality is obtained?

(c) If such replacements are possible, can the resulting framework yield improved upper bounds, or improved lower bounds, on the Grothendieck constants K_G^R and K_G^C compared with the bounds known from the Gaussian approach?

(d) In any such non-Gaussian replacement, determine whether the trace-inequality reformulation of Grothendieck's inequality can still be expressed purely in terms of correlation matrices, or whether one must instead use a strictly larger class of dependence objects (e.g., copulas or general joint distribution functions encoding tail dependence).

Let $n \geq 2$ and $\lambda \geq 0$, $v > 0$ be fixed constants. Suppose that $(M_i^n, g_i, p_i)$ is a sequence of pointed complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds satisfying the uniform lower Ricci curvature bound
$$\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i} \geq -\lambda$$
together with the noncollapsing condition
$$\mathrm{Vol}(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0,$$
and that $(M_i^n, g_i, p_i)$ converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space $(X, d, p)$. The regular set $\mathcal{R}(X)$ consists of those $x \in X$ for which every tangent cone at $x$ is isometric to Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, and the singular set is $\mathcal{S}(X) = X \setminus \mathcal{R}(X)$. It is known that $\mathcal{S}(X)$ has Hausdorff codimension at least $2$ in $X$.

Question: Does there exist a closed subset $S \subset X$ with $\dim_{\mathcal{H}}(S) \leq n-2$ such that $X \setminus S$ is bi-Lipschitz homeomorphic to a smooth $n$-dimensional manifold? Equivalently, is $X$ bi-Lipschitz to a manifold away from a set of codimension two?

Let $n\ge 2$, $\lambda\ge 0$, and $v>0$ be fixed. Suppose $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ is a sequence of pointed complete Riemannian $n$-manifolds satisfying
\[\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i}\ge -\lambda\,g_i\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathrm{Vol}(B_1(p_i))>v,\]
and that $(M_i^n,g_i,p_i)$ converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric space $(X,d,p)$ (a noncollapsed lower-Ricci limit).

For $x\in X$, a tangent cone at $x$ is any pointed Gromov–Hausdorff limit of rescalings $(X,r_i^{-1}d,x)$ with $r_i\downarrow 0$. A pointed metric space $(Y,d_Y,y)$ is called $k$-symmetric if it is isometric to $(\mathbb{R}^k\times C(Z),d_{\mathrm{prod}},(0,o_C))$ for some compact metric space $Z$, where $C(Z)$ is the metric cone over $Z$ with vertex $o_C$. Define the Federer-type stratification
\[S^k(X)\;=\;\{x\in X:\text{no tangent cone at }x\text{ is }(k+1)\text{-symmetric}\},\qquad k=0,1,\dots,n-1.\]

A map $\varphi:B_1(0^k)\subset\mathbb{R}^k\to X$ is bi-Hölder if there exist $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $C>0$ such that
\[C^{-1}|u-v|^{1/\alpha}\le d(\varphi(u),\varphi(v))\le C\,|u-v|^{\alpha}\qquad\text{for all }u,v\in B_1(0^k).\]

Decide whether the following statement holds for every such limit $(X,d,p)$ and every $0\le k\le n-1$: there exists a countable collection of bi-Hölder maps $\varphi_i:B_1(0^k)\to X$ such that, setting
\[\widehat S^k(X)\;=\;\bigcup_i \varphi_i(B_1(0^k)),\]
one has
\begin{enumerate}
\item $S^k(X)\subseteq \widehat S^k(X)$, and
\item for every $x\in \widehat S^k(X)$, every tangent cone of $X$ at $x$ is at least $k$-symmetric.
\end{enumerate}

Consider any pointed complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(M^n, g, x)$ satisfying the lower Ricci curvature bound $\mathrm{Ric}_g \geq -\lambda\, g$ and the noncollapsing volume bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B_1(x)) > v$, where $B_1(x)$ denotes the open geodesic ball of radius $1$ about $x$. Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $C = C(n, \lambda, v) > 0$, depending only on $n$, $\lambda$, and $v$, such that
$$\int_{B_1(x)} R_g \, d\mathrm{vol}_g < C$$
for every such $(M^n, g, x)$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is a noncollapsing version of Yau's conjecture on local L^1 bounds for scalar curvature under a lower Ricci bound. It is widely cited as an open conjecture in recent surveys and research on Ricci limit spaces; web searches in 2024–2025 turn up related results (e.g., L^2 curvature bounds under two-sided Ricci bounds, integral Ricci bounds for collapsed spaces) but no proof or disproof of this specific noncollapsed L^1 scalar curvature conjecture. It appears to remain open.

Let n ≥ 3, and let (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) be a sequence of pointed complete Riemannian manifolds satisfying the lower Ricci curvature bound Ric_{g_j} ≥ −λ for some constant λ ≥ 0, together with the noncollapsing condition Vol_{g_j}(B_1(x_j)) ≥ v > 0. Assume (M_j^n, g_j, x_j) converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric space (X, d, x), and that the scalar curvature measures R_{g_j} dvol_{g_j} converge as Radon measures on X to some limit measure μ.

It is known that on X there exists a subset of full (n−2)-dimensional Hausdorff measure on the top singular stratum on which the tangent cone at each point y is unique and isometric to ℝ^{n−2} × C(S^1_{r_y}), where C(S^1_r) denotes the metric cone over a circle of length 2πr and r_y ∈ (0,1] is the corresponding radius (so 2π(1 − r_y) is the cone angle defect). Denote this radius function by r_·.

Prove or disprove the following energy-identity decomposition: as measures on X,
   R_{g_j} dvol_{g_j} ⟶ R_X · 𝓗^n + 2 θ · 𝓗^{n−1}⌞Σ + 2π(1 − r_·) · 𝓗^{n−2}⌞S,
where:
 (i) R_X : X → ℝ is locally integrable with respect to 𝓗^n and bounded below;
 (ii) Σ ⊂ X is an (n−1)-rectifiable set and θ : Σ → (0, 1] is a Borel density satisfying θ ≤ 1;
 (iii) S is the top stratum of the singular set Sing(X), the third term is an (n−2)-rectifiable measure supported on S, and r_· is the radius function described above.

Setup. Fix integers n ≥ 2 and a constant λ ≥ 0. Consider a sequence of pointed complete n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) satisfying the lower Ricci curvature bound Ric_{g_i} ≥ −λ, equipped with their renormalized volume measures ν_i (i.e., ν_i = Vol_{g_i}/Vol_{g_i}(B_1(p_i))). Assume that

  (a) (M_i^n, g_i, ν_i, p_i) converges in the pointed measured Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric measure space (X, d, ν, p), and
  (b) the sequence is collapsing in the sense that Vol_{g_i}(B_1(p_i)) → 0.

By a theorem of Cheeger–Colding and Colding–Naber, there exists a unique integer k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n such that X is k-rectifiable; that is, ν-almost every point of X has a unique tangent cone equal to ℝ^k, and X can be covered up to a ν-null set by countably many bi-Lipschitz images of subsets of ℝ^k.

Question. Is the Hausdorff dimension dim_H(X, d) of the limit space necessarily equal to this rectifiable dimension k?

status_assertions.value: open_status:solved

Pan and Wei (Geometric and Functional Analysis, 2022; arXiv:2106.03967) resolved the question negatively. They constructed explicit collapsing Ricci limit spaces (universal covers of certain doubly warped products [0,∞) ×_f S^{p−1} ×_h S^1 with h(r) ~ r^{−β}) for which the Hausdorff dimension equals 1+β and can be a non-integer strictly larger than the rectifiable dimension k. Hence Hausdorff dimension need not equal the rectifiable integer k.

Setting. Let $n\ge 2$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $(X,d,\nu)$ be a metric measure space arising as a (pointed) measured Gromov–Hausdorff limit of a sequence of complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(M_i^n,g_i,\mathrm{vol}_{g_i}/\mathrm{vol}_{g_i}(B_1(p_i)))$ with $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i}\ge -(n-1)\lambda$ (a Ricci limit space of dimension $\le n$). Call $X$ noncollapsed if it is a noncollapsed Ricci limit, equivalently if $\nu=\mathcal{H}^n$ up to a constant.

For $x\in X$ and $r>0$, write $B_r(x)$ for the open metric ball of radius $r$ around $x$, and let $\nu(B_r(x))$ denote its measure.

Let $\gamma:(-2,2)\to X$ be a unit-speed minimizing geodesic.

Question. Prove or disprove the following two statements.

(1) (Lipschitz volume-ratio bound) There exists a constant $C=C(n,\lambda)>0$ such that for all $r\in(0,1)$ and all $s,t\in(-1,1)$,
$$\frac{\nu(B_r(\gamma(s)))}{\nu(B_r(\gamma(t)))}\le 1+C(n,\lambda)\,|t-s|,$$
i.e. the function $s\mapsto \nu(B_r(\gamma(s)))$ is, up to ratios, Lipschitz along $\gamma$ with constants depending only on $n$ and $\lambda$.

(2) (Constant infinitesimal density) If in addition $X$ is noncollapsed, then for all $s,t\in(-1,1)$,
$$\lim_{r\to 0^+}\frac{\nu(B_r(\gamma(s)))}{\nu(B_r(\gamma(t)))}=1.$$

The question has been resolved in the negative. Work by Brué, Naber, and Semola (arXiv:2308.03909, "Lower Ricci Curvature and Nonexistence of Manifold Structure," published in Geometry & Topology, 2025) constructs collapsed Ricci limit spaces, arising as Gromov–Hausdorff limits of smooth manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, that are k-rectifiable but contain no open subset homeomorphic to a topological manifold; in fact every open subset is non-contractible.

Consider the Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites at fixed particle density ρ ∈ (0,1): each site holds at most one particle, and every particle independently attempts jumps to each neighboring site at rate 1, the jump being performed only if the target site is empty. Let K(t) denote the dynamical activity, i.e. the total number of jumps performed by the system up to time t, and define the scaled cumulant generating function (SCGF) of the activity by

  ψ_K^SSEP(s) = lim_{t→∞} (1/t) log E[ e^{-s K(t)} ].

The "diffusive" (Edwards–Wilkinson) regime corresponds to scaling s = λ/L² with λ fixed; in this regime ψ_K^SSEP(s) is well understood, including a hyperuniform phase for sufficiently negative λ. The problem concerns the complementary regime where s is of order one with s > 0 (beyond the diffusive scaling).

A formal mapping relates ψ_K^SSEP(s) to the SCGF ψ_Q^ASEP(µ) of the integrated current Q in the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) with forward/backward hop rates p, q on the same ring at the same density, via

  ψ_K^SSEP(s) = (2/(p+q)) · ψ_Q^ASEP(µ),    with    e^{-2µ} = p/q,    e^{-s} = cosh(µ).

Expanding ψ_Q^ASEP(µ) as a cumulant series in µ produces, on the SSEP side, a series in s whose coefficients diverge whenever q/p approaches a root of unity, preventing a direct termwise interpretation for s > 0.

Determine ψ_K^SSEP(s) for s > 0 with s = O(1) as L → ∞. Equivalently, find a resummation or analytic transformation of the ASEP cumulant series that resolves the root-of-unity singularities, and produce a parametric representation of ψ_K^SSEP(s) valid for s > 0 analogous to the parametric representation known for s < 0, thereby describing the hyperuniform phase beyond the diffusive regime.

Recent work on large deviations of activity/current in SSEP and ASEP (e.g. SciPost Phys. 17.2.033 and follow-up studies on topological phases in SSEP dynamics) continues to discuss the hyperuniform phase and the diffusive Edwards–Wilkinson regime, but no resummation of the ASEP cumulant series yielding ψ_K^SSEP(s) for s = O(1) > 0, nor a parametric representation valid for positive s, appears to have been obtained. Consider the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic XXZ Hamiltonian on a chain
$$H = J_0 \sum_{k} \big(\sigma^x_k \sigma^x_{k+1} + \sigma^y_k \sigma^y_{k+1} + \Delta\, \sigma^z_k \sigma^z_{k+1}\big),$$
restricted to the sector of fixed total magnetization with average value $\bar m \in (-1,1)$. In the massless (gapless) phase $-1 < \Delta \le 1$, the ground-state connected longitudinal correlation function admits the large-distance expansion
$$\langle \sigma^z_0 \sigma^z_n\rangle_c = \frac{c_1(\Delta,\bar m)}{n^2} + (\text{subleading oscillatory terms}),$$
where $c_1(\Delta,\bar m)$ is the universal amplitude of the non-oscillating $1/n^2$ part.

Determine whether, for every fixed $\bar m \in (-1,1)$, the amplitude satisfies the asymptotic equivalence
$$c_1(\Delta,\bar m) \;\underset{\Delta \to -1^+}{\sim}\; -\frac{1}{\pi}\sqrt{\frac{1-\bar m^2}{2(1+\Delta)}}.$$
That is, prove or disprove that this limiting form (which generalizes the known half-filling result $\bar m = 0$) holds as $\Delta$ approaches $-1$ from above for arbitrary fixed magnetization in $(-1,1)$.

Consider the symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a one-dimensional lattice (e.g., a ring of L sites) with hard-core particles each attempting jumps to nearest-neighbor sites at rate 1, with the move accepted only if the target site is empty. The dynamics is reversible with respect to the uniform Bernoulli measure. The dynamical activity over a time interval [0,T] is defined as the total number of particle jumps performed by the system, K_T. Studying the large deviations of K_T/T together with finite-size (in L) corrections reveals, on one side of a dynamical phase transition for the activity, scaling exponents and a limit shape characteristic of the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class.

Independently, KPZ-type scaling (with dynamical exponent z=3/2 and KPZ scaling functions) has been identified in the equilibrium spin-spin autocorrelations of:
(a) the classical isotropic Heisenberg (SO(3) symmetric) lattice spin dynamics, and
(b) the one-dimensional isotropic quantum Heisenberg magnet at high temperature.

Problem. Determine whether there is a precise mathematical relationship between the KPZ scaling that governs the activity large deviations of the time-reversal-symmetric SSEP and the KPZ scaling observed in the spin transport of the classical SO(3) Heisenberg spin dynamics and the quantum isotropic Heisenberg magnet. Specifically, identify a common underlying structure (such as an exact mapping, shared limiting nonlinear stochastic equation, or shared random matrix / Bethe-ansatz mechanism) that explains the appearance of KPZ universality in all three settings, or alternatively prove that the KPZ behaviors arise from genuinely distinct mechanisms.

Consider the one-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites at half filling. Let A_t denote the total time-integrated activity (the number of particle jumps, in either direction, up to time t), and consider its scaled cumulant generating function (SCGF)

  ψ(λ) = lim_{t→∞} (1/t) log E[ exp(λ A_t) ].

Introduce the rescaled fugacity s = λ / L^2. There are two relevant regimes:

(a) Diffusive (Edwards–Wilkinson, EW) regime: λ fixed and L → ∞ (equivalently s → 0). In this regime, ψ(λ) admits a leading EW scaling form, and Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) techniques and their extensions are known to produce systematic large-λ corrections to this leading EW scaling.

(b) Finite-s (KPZ) regime: s held fixed as L → ∞. In this regime, ψ admits a small-s expansion of KPZ type, with computable subleading coefficients beyond the leading order.

Question: Develop TBA methods (and their generalizations) to compute the corrections to the EW activity-fluctuation scaling at large λ in the diffusive regime, and prove that, upon expressing both expansions in the common variable s = λ/L^2, the resulting large-λ TBA corrections in the diffusive regime match, term by term, the next-to-leading orders of the small-s expansion of ψ in the finite-s KPZ regime.

representations.normalized:
Consider the symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites: each site is either empty or occupied by at most one particle, and each particle attempts, at rate 1, to jump to a uniformly chosen nearest neighbor, the move being accepted only if the target site is empty. The (time-integrated) dynamical activity K_t is the total number of particle jumps (in either direction) performed in the time interval [0,t]. Tilting the dynamics by a parameter s, one defines the scaled cumulant generating function

  ψ(s) = lim_{t→∞} (1/t) log E[ exp(s K_t) ],

which can be obtained as the largest eigenvalue of the tilted Markov generator

  (M_s f)(η) = Σ_{⟨i,j⟩} [ e^{s} η_i (1-η_j) f(η^{ij}) − η_i (1-η_j) f(η) ],

where η^{ij} denotes the configuration with the occupations at sites i and j swapped. The tilted generator is integrable and can be diagonalized by the coordinate Bethe Ansatz, giving ψ(s) and the corresponding eigenstate as functions of Bethe roots solving a coupled system of algebraic equations on the ring.

Two scaling regimes are known for activity fluctuations in the limit L → ∞:

  (i) Edwards–Wilkinson (EW) regime: s = λ/L² with λ fixed; here ψ(s) scales diffusively, consistent with EW universality.
  (ii) Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) regime: s held fixed of order one with L → ∞; here ψ(s) exhibits KPZ-type scaling.

Problem. Starting from the coordinate Bethe Ansatz equations for the SSEP tilted by s, determine analytically how the structure of the Bethe roots and the resulting scaled cumulant generating function ψ(s,L) interpolates between these two regimes as the scaling of s with L is varied. In particular, identify an appropriate crossover scaling variable interpolating between s ∼ L^{-2} (EW) and s = O(1) (KPZ), and derive the corresponding crossover scaling function for ψ together with the asymptotic behavior of the Bethe roots in this crossover.

Consider the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on a one-dimensional periodic lattice of L sites with hard-core particles that hop right with rate p and left with rate q, subject to the exclusion rule that each site contains at most one particle. For a long time window [0,T], let Q_T denote the time-integrated current (number of right jumps minus left jumps across a fixed bond, or summed over all bonds) and K_T the time-integrated activity (total number of jumps, regardless of direction). Define the joint scaled cumulant generating function

  ψ(λ, μ) = lim_{T→∞} (1/T) log ⟨ exp( λ Q_T + μ K_T ) ⟩,

which can be obtained as the largest eigenvalue of the tilted (deformed) Markov generator W(λ, μ) acting on configuration space. It is known that there exists a similarity transformation W'(λ', μ') = U W(λ, μ) U^{-1} relating the tilted generators of two ASEPs with possibly different hopping rates and tilting parameters, thereby producing an exact mapping between their joint current–activity scaled cumulant generating functions, and in particular relating current large deviations in the ASEP to activity large deviations in the symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP).

Question: Can this similarity-transform mapping between joint current–activity scaled cumulant generating functions of ASEP-type models be derived from, or otherwise put into precise correspondence with, the previously established mappings between current large-deviation functions of exclusion processes (such as those relating ASEP and zero-range or related processes via gauge-type transformations) and the mappings used in the analysis of steady-state large deviations of exclusion processes (e.g., via matrix-product or additivity-principle techniques)?

Consider the one-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a periodic ring of L sites: each site is occupied by at most one particle, and every particle attempts to jump to each neighboring site with rate 1, the move being executed only if the target site is empty. The activity over a time window is defined as the total number of particle jumps (in either direction) performed during that window. Tilting the continuous-time Markov generator by a parameter s conjugate to the activity yields the deformed (non-stochastic) matrix M(s), whose largest eigenvalue gives the scaled cumulant generating function of the activity and whose subleading spectral gap Δ_M(L,s) controls finite-time relaxation of activity-biased trajectories.

Consider also the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on a ring of L sites with biased hopping rates, and the deformed generator W(s') obtained by tilting with a parameter s' conjugate to the integrated particle current. There exists a similarity/parameter mapping that identifies the spectra of M(s) (SSEP, activity-biased) and W(s') (ASEP, current-biased) outside the diffusive regime.

Questions:
(1) Can the spectral gap of the deformed evolution operators M(s) and W(s') be computed by the Bethe Ansatz in the vicinity of dynamical phase transitions and at nonzero values of the Legendre conjugate parameter s (respectively s')?
(2) Using the mapping between M and W, does the gap of M(s) satisfy
   Δ_M(L,s) ~ C(s) · L^{-3/2}  as L → ∞,
for all sufficiently large |s|, thereby establishing that the dynamical exponent governing SSEP activity large deviations beyond the diffusive regime equals 3/2 (in contrast with the value 2 of the diffusive regime)?

Consider the open weakly asymmetric simple exclusion process (WASEP) on the lattice {1, 2, ..., L} defined as follows. Each site is either occupied by a single particle or empty. In the bulk, a particle at site i attempts to jump to site i+1 at rate p and to site i-1 at rate q (jumps are rejected if the target site is occupied), with the weak asymmetry scaling p/q = exp(2ν₁/L) for a fixed real parameter ν₁. At the left boundary, particles are injected at site 1 (when empty) at rate consistent with reservoir density ρ_L = 1/2 and ejected from site 1 at the corresponding rate; the right boundary at site L is coupled analogously to a reservoir of density ρ_R = 1/2.

Let K_t denote the total number of particle jumps (in either direction, summed over all bonds, including the boundary bonds) up to time t — i.e., the dynamical activity. Tilt the path measure by the activity by introducing a bias parameter s = λ/L² with λ ∈ ℝ, weighting trajectories by exp(-s K_t). In the joint limit t → ∞ followed by L → ∞, the typical (most probable) density profile ρ*(x), x ∈ [0,1], conditioned on this activity bias can be characterized via a hydrodynamic large deviation principle.

The model has a particle-hole symmetry: replacing the occupation η_i by 1 - η_i (together with reversing the asymmetry direction) leaves the dynamics with ρ_L = ρ_R = 1/2 invariant. The symmetric flat profile ρ*(x) ≡ 1/2 is always a critical point of the rate functional. One says that particle-hole symmetry is dynamically broken at parameters (ν₁, λ) if the optimal profile ρ*(x) achieving the activity large deviation is non-flat (i.e. ρ*(x) ≢ 1/2).

It is known (via a real-parameter mapping to a current-conditioned WASEP) that for λ ≤ ν₁²/2 the symmetry-breaking question is settled within an explicit parameter range. The problem is:

Determine whether, for λ > ν₁²/2, particle-hole symmetry is broken in the activity-conditioned open WASEP described above — i.e., decide whether the optimal density profile ρ*(x) ceases to be the flat profile 1/2 in this regime, and if so, characterize the transition.
