Let $E/F$ be a quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero, with nontrivial Galois automorphism $c$. Fix a nontrivial additive character $\psi: F \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ and a character $\mu$ of $E^\times$ whose restriction to $F^\times$ is the quadratic character associated to $E/F$.

For each positive integer $m$, there are exactly two isomorphism classes of non-degenerate $m$-dimensional skew-Hermitian spaces over $E$; denote representatives by $V$ and $W$. For any skew-Hermitian space $X$ over $E$, let $U(X)$ denote its unitary group and let $\omega_{X,\psi,\mu}$ denote the associated Weil representation of $U(X)$ (with respect to the splitting data $(\psi,\mu)$) on the doubled space, viewed as a smooth representation.

Let $\pi$ be a tempered irreducible smooth representation of $U(V)$, and let $\mathrm{Sp}(\pi,2)$ denote the generalized Steinberg representation of $U(V \oplus V)$ (respectively $U(V \oplus W)$) associated to $\pi$, defined as the unique irreducible quotient (Langlands quotient) of the parabolically induced representation $\mathrm{Ind}_{P}^{U(V \oplus V)}(\pi |\det|^{1/2})$ for the Siegel-type parabolic $P$, normalized so that it generalizes the Steinberg representation when $\pi$ is the trivial character.

Prove that for every such $\pi$ and for both isomorphism classes $V$ and $W$,
$$\mathrm{Hom}_{U(V\oplus V)}\!\big(\mathrm{Sp}(\pi,2),\; \omega_{V\oplus V,\psi,\mu}\big) = 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \mathrm{Hom}_{U(V\oplus W)}\!\big(\mathrm{Sp}(\pi,2),\; \omega_{V\oplus W,\psi,\mu}\big) = 0.$$

Equivalently, establish this vanishing in all dimensions $m = \dim V = \dim W \geq 1$ (the case $m=1$ being known).

Let $E/F = \mathbb{C}/\mathbb{R}$. For an integer $n \geq 1$ and integers $p,q \geq 0$ with $p+q = n$, let $V_{p,q}$ denote the $n$-dimensional skew-Hermitian space over $\mathbb{C}$ of signature $(p,q)$, and let $U(V_{p,q})$ be its unitary group.

Fix the additive character $\psi(x) = e^{2\pi i x}$ of $\mathbb{R}$. Let $\alpha \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z} \setminus \mathbb{Z}$ be a half-integer that is not an integer, and define the character
$$\mu : \mathbb{C}^\times \to \mathbb{C}^\times, \qquad \mu(z) = (\bar z / z)^{\alpha}.$$
Associated to $(V_{p,q}, \psi, \mu)$ there is a Weil (oscillator) representation $\omega_{V_{p,q},\psi,\mu}$ of $U(V_{p,q})$ (the splitting of the metaplectic cover being determined by $\mu$).

Let $B \subset GL_n$ be the Borel subgroup of upper-triangular matrices. For $j = 1, \dots, n$, let $r_j \in \mathbb{C}$ and $k_j \in \mathbb{Z}$, and define the characters
$$\chi_j : \mathbb{C}^\times \to \mathbb{C}^\times, \qquad \chi_j(z) = |z|^{r_j} (z/\bar z)^{k_j/2}.$$
Assume that the (normalized) principal series representation
$$\Pi = \mathrm{Ind}_{B(\mathbb{C})}^{GL_n(\mathbb{C})}(\chi_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes \chi_n)$$
is irreducible and generic.

Prove that, among all signatures $(p,q)$ with $p+q = n$, the space of $U(V_{p,q})$-equivariant continuous linear maps
$$\mathrm{Hom}_{U(V_{p,q})}\bigl(\Pi,\ \omega_{V_{p,q},\psi,\mu}\bigr)$$
is nonzero if and only if
$$p = \#\{\, j : k_j > \alpha\,\} \qquad \text{and} \qquad q = \#\{\, j : k_j < \alpha\,\} = n - p.$$

Let $\pi$ be an irreducible admissible representation of $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ whose Arthur parameter has the form
$$M_A = \bigoplus_i M_i \boxtimes \mathrm{Sym}^{d_i}(\mathbb{C}^2),$$
where each $M_i$ is a tempered representation of the appropriate Weil–Deligne group and $\mathrm{Sym}^{d_i}(\mathbb{C}^2)$ denotes the $(d_i+1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$. Write $M_A^\sigma$ for the $\sigma$-conjugate parameter, and call a pair $(M_A,\mu\cdot M_A^\sigma)$ "relevant" if it satisfies the combinatorial relevance condition formulated for the twisted GGP setting (i.e., the parameter decomposes as a tempered piece plus summands of the form $N_i\boxtimes \mathrm{Sym}^{d_i}(\mathbb{C}^2)\oplus \mu\cdot N_i^\sigma\boxtimes \mathrm{Sym}^{d_i-1}(\mathbb{C}^2)$, with each $N_i$ tempered).

$$N_i\boxtimes \mathrm{Sym}^{d_i}(\mathbb{C}^2)\;\oplus\;\mu\cdot N_i^\sigma\boxtimes \mathrm{Sym}^{d_i-1}(\mathbb{C}^2),$$
equivalently, $M_A$ and $\mu\cdot M_A^\sigma$ are relevant.

Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $E$ and $K$ be two distinct quadratic field extensions of $F$. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional skew-Hermitian space over $E$, and set $V_K = V \otimes_F K$, regarded as a skew-Hermitian space over the compositum $EK$ relative to the involution induced from $E/F$. Denote by $U(V)$ and $U(V_K)$ the corresponding unitary groups, and view $U(V) \hookrightarrow U(V_K)$ via the natural embedding.

Fix a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of $F$ and a conjugate-symplectic character $\mu$ of $E^\times$. Let $\omega_{V,\psi,\mu}$ denote the Weil representation of $U(V)$ associated with $(\psi,\mu)$. For $\pi \in \mathrm{Irr}(U(V_K))$, define the multiplicity
$$m_V(\pi,\mu) = \dim \mathrm{Hom}_{U(V)}(\pi, \omega_{V,\psi,\mu}).$$

Let $M$ be a generic $L$-parameter of $U(V_K)$, with local Vogan $L$-packet $\Pi_M$ (over the set of pure inner forms indexed by isomorphism classes of skew-Hermitian spaces $V$ of the given dimension), and let $A_M$ denote its local component group. Prove the following assertions:

Setup. Let $E/F$ be a quadratic extension of number fields with adèle ring $\mathbb{A}_E$, and let $L/E$ be a further quadratic extension such that $K := L \otimes_E F$ is a field (the "$E\neq K$" case, where $K/F$ is also quadratic). Fix a continuous character $\mu : \mathbb{A}_L^\times / L^\times \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ whose restriction to $\mathbb{A}_E^\times$ is trivial (so $\mu$ cuts out the extension $L/E$ in the appropriate sense).

Let $V$ be a Hermitian space over $E$ and let $V_K := V \otimes_E K$, viewed as a Hermitian space over $K$ with respect to the involution induced by $\mathrm{Gal}(L/E) \times \mathrm{Gal}(K/F)$. Let $\mathrm{U}(V)$ and $\mathrm{U}(V_K)$ be the associated unitary groups, viewed as reductive groups over $F$, and let $H := \mathrm{U}(V) \hookrightarrow G := \mathrm{Res}_{E/F}\mathrm{U}(V_K)$ be the natural embedding arising from the twisted Gan–Gross–Prasad setting.

Let $\Pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $G(\mathbb{A}_F)$ which is tempered and everywhere locally generic, occurring in the discrete spectrum. For a factorizable cusp form $\varphi = \otimes_v \varphi_v \in \Pi$, define the global period
$$P(\varphi) := \int_{[H]} \varphi(h)\, \mu(\det h)\, dh,$$
where $[H] = H(F)\backslash H(\mathbb{A}_F)$ and $dh$ is the Tamagawa measure on $H(\mathbb{A}_F)$, decomposed as $dh = \prod_v dh_v$ via a fixed factorization. Let $\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{Pet}} = \prod_v \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_v$ be a corresponding factorization of the Petersson inner product on $\Pi$.

Let $S_\Pi$ denote the global component group attached to $\Pi$ by the relevant Langlands parametrization, and let $|S_\Pi|$ be its cardinality. Let $M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V)}$ and $M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V_K)}$ be the motives dual to the motives of Gross attached to $\mathrm{U}(V)$ and $\mathrm{U}(V_K)$, respectively, with associated completed $L$-values $L(1, M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V)})$ and $L(1, M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V_K)})$. Let $L(s, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E} \times \mu^{-1})$ be the twisted Asai $L$-function of $\Pi$ relative to $L/E$ twisted by $\mu^{-1}$, and let $L(s, \Pi, \mathrm{Ad})$ be the adjoint $L$-function of $\Pi$. For each place $v$ of $F$, define the normalized local integral
$$I_v^{\#}(\varphi_v, \varphi_v') := \frac{L(1, M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V),v})}{L(1, M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V_K),v})} \cdot \frac{L(1, \Pi_v, \mathrm{Ad})}{L(1/2, \Pi_v, \mathrm{As}_{L/E}\times \mu^{-1})} \cdot \int_{H(F_v)} \langle \Pi_v(h_v)\varphi_v, \varphi_v'\rangle_v\, \mu_v(\det h_v)\, dh_v.$$

Problem. Prove the following refined global identity: for all factorizable $\varphi, \varphi' \in \Pi$,
$$P(\varphi)\,\overline{P(\varphi')} \;=\; \frac{1}{|S_\Pi|} \cdot \frac{L(1, M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V_K)})}{L(1, M^\vee_{\mathrm{U}(V)})} \cdot \frac{L(1/2, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E}\times \mu^{-1})}{L(1, \Pi, \mathrm{Ad})} \cdot \prod_v I_v^{\#}(\varphi_v, \varphi_v').$$

Setting. Recall Arnold's framework: given a (possibly infinite-dimensional) Lie group $G$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a (weak) right- or left-invariant Riemannian metric induced by an inner product on $\mathfrak{g}$, the geodesic equation on $G$ reduces to an evolution equation on $\mathfrak{g}$ called the Euler–Arnold equation. Equivalently, it is the Hamiltonian equation on the dual $\mathfrak{g}^{*}$ with respect to the Lie–Poisson structure and the Hamiltonian induced by the metric. This framework realizes the Euler equations of an ideal incompressible fluid as the geodesic flow on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and the rigid body equations as a geodesic flow on $SO(3)$.

A Lie groupoid is a small category $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M$ whose objects form a manifold $M$, whose morphisms form a manifold $\mathcal{G}$, and whose source, target, identity, inverse, and composition maps are smooth, with source and target submersions. Its infinitesimal counterpart is a Lie algebroid $A \to M$ with anchor $\rho: A \to TM$ and a Lie bracket on sections of $A$, and the dual bundle $A^{*}$ carries a natural linear Poisson structure generalizing the Lie–Poisson structure on $\mathfrak{g}^{*}$. Given a fibrewise inner product on $A$, one obtains a sub-Riemannian or Riemannian structure on $\mathcal{G}$ that is invariant under groupoid multiplication, and the associated geodesic flow descends to a Hamiltonian system on $A^{*}$, which is the Euler–Arnold equation on the groupoid. Known examples in fluid dynamics include geodesic descriptions of generalized (multiphase) flows and of vortex-sheet motions as Hamiltonian systems on appropriate diffeomorphism groupoids.

Problem. Develop a geodesic and Hamiltonian Euler–Arnold formalism on a suitable Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M$ (with associated Lie algebroid $A \to M$, anchor $\rho$, invariant fibrewise metric, and Lie–Poisson structure on $A^{*}$) such that the resulting equations describe systems of continuum elasticity theory. More precisely:

(a) Identify a Lie groupoid (or family of groupoids) generalizing the diffeomorphism group setting, together with an invariant (possibly degenerate) fibrewise inner product on its Lie algebroid, whose induced geodesic equations on $\mathcal{G}$ recover the equations of motion of elastic continua (for instance nonlinear elastodynamics of a hyperelastic body, with stored-energy function playing the role of a kinetic-like term, or a Lagrangian/Hamiltonian system on a configuration space of embeddings).

(b) Write down the corresponding Euler–Arnold equation on $A$ (or its dual $A^{*}$) as the reduction of the geodesic flow, identify the Lie–Poisson Hamiltonian, and verify that the unreduced geodesic equation on $\mathcal{G}$ coincides with the elasticity equations of motion.

(c) Establish the analogue of Arnold's stability and curvature theory in this groupoid setting and apply it to stability questions for elastic media.

Goal: produce a framework that simultaneously encompasses the known groupoid descriptions of multiphase fluids and vortex sheets and the equations of elasticity theory.

Its infinitesimal counterpart is a Lie algebroid $A \to M$ with anchor $\rho: A \to TM$ and a Lie bracket on sections of $A$, and the dual bundle $A^{*}$ carries a natural linear Poisson structure generalizing the Lie–Poisson structure on $\mathfrak{g}^{*}$. Given a fibrewise inner product on $A$, one obtains a sub-Riemannian or Riemannian structure on $\mathcal{G}$ that is invariant under groupoid multiplication, and the associated geodesic flow descends to a Hamiltonian system on $A^{*}$, which is the Euler–Arnold equation on the groupoid. Known examples in fluid dynamics include geodesic descriptions of generalized (multiphase) flows and of vortex-sheet motions as Hamiltonian systems on appropriate diffeomorphism groupoids.

Problem. Develop a geodesic and Hamiltonian Euler–Arnold formalism on a suitable Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M$ (with associated Lie algebroid $A \to M$, anchor $\rho$, invariant fibrewise metric, and Lie–Poisson structure on $A^{*}$) such that the resulting equations describe systems of continuum elasticity theory. More precisely:

(a) Identify a Lie groupoid (or family of groupoids) generalizing the diffeomorphism group setting, together with an invariant (possibly degenerate) fibrewise inner product on its Lie algebroid, whose induced geodesic equations on $\mathcal{G}$ recover the equations of motion of elastic continua (for instance nonlinear elastodynamics of a hyperelastic body, with stored-energy function playing the role of a kinetic-like term, or a Lagrangian/Hamiltonian system on a configuration space of embeddings).

(b) Write down the corresponding Euler–Arnold equation on $A$ (or its dual $A^{*}$) as the reduction of the geodesic flow, identify the Lie–Poisson Hamiltonian, and verify that the unreduced geodesic equation on $\mathcal{G}$ coincides with the elasticity equations of motion.

(c) Establish the analogue of Arnold's stability and curvature theory in this groupoid setting and apply it to stability questions for elastic media.

Goal: produce a framework that simultaneously encompasses the known groupoid descriptions of multiphase fluids and vortex sheets and the equations of elasticity theory.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is stated as an open research direction in a recent survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics. Related groupoid approaches to geometric mechanics and to generalized/multiphase fluid flows exist (e.g., Fusca's thesis and the Izosimov–Khesin paper on generalized fluid flows), but no published work appears to carry out the Euler–Arnold groupoid program for elasticity theory. The problem appears to remain open.

Consider now the Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G}$ of multiphase (generalized) volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$: objects are measurable partitions (or, more generally, generalized configurations / Young-measure-like states) of $M$ preserving the total volume, and morphisms are diffeomorphism-like maps that intertwine such configurations while preserving the relevant volume forms. Equip $\mathcal{G}$ with the source-wise right-invariant $L^2$ metric, so that geodesics correspond to multiphase fluid flows (homogenized vortex sheets, generalized flows in the sense of Brenier, etc.).

Problem: Develop the differential geometry of $\mathcal{G}$ with respect to this source-wise right-invariant $L^2$ metric. Specifically:
(a) compute the sectional curvatures of $\mathcal{G}$ in terms of pairs of tangent vectors at identity bisections;
(b) compute the Ricci curvature in admissible directions;
(c) describe the locus and structure of conjugate points along geodesics,
in a manner analogous to Arnold's description for $D_\mu(M)$.

representations.normalized:
Consider a system of finitely many (or, more generally, a continuum of) material particles moving in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d>1$. The particles are assumed to obey the sticky-collision rule: whenever two or more particles occupy the same position at the same time, they merge into a single particle whose mass equals the sum of the masses and whose momentum equals the sum of the momenta of the colliding particles, after which the merged particle continues to move and obey the same rule. The macroscopic continuum limit of such systems is expected to describe weak (in particular shock) solutions of the multidimensional pressureless dynamics
$$\partial_t \rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho v)=0,\qquad \partial_t(\rho v)+\nabla\cdot(\rho v\otimes v)=0,$$
including the case where $v$ is the gradient of a potential (modeling the multidimensional inviscid Burgers equation $\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v = 0$) as well as the non-potential case.

Problem: Construct a variational principle (i.e., an action functional on a suitable class of admissible mass-flow / trajectory configurations, together with appropriate admissibility/entropy-type constraints) whose minimizers, critical points, or otherwise variationally selected solutions coincide with sticky-particle dynamics for arbitrary finite particle configurations in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d>1$), and which, in the continuum limit, describes the formation and subsequent evolution of shock waves for the multidimensional Burgers equation, in both the potential and non-potential settings. The formulation must be intrinsically multidimensional (not reducible to a one-dimensional construction along characteristics) and must remain meaningful through and beyond the first time of mass concentration.

Let $(M,g)$ be a closed oriented Riemannian manifold with Riemannian volume form $\mu$, and let $D_\mu(M)$ denote the group of smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, regarded as an infinite-dimensional Lie group with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{X}_\mu(M)$ of smooth divergence-free vector fields. The $L^2$ inner product on $\mathfrak{X}_\mu(M)$ is
$$\langle u,v\rangle_{L^2} = \int_M g(u,v)\,\mu.$$
Extending this inner product by left translations yields a left-invariant weak Riemannian metric on $D_\mu(M)$: for $\eta \in D_\mu(M)$ and tangent vectors $U,V \in T_\eta D_\mu(M)$,
$$\langle U,V\rangle_\eta^{\text{left}} = \langle (TL_{\eta^{-1}})U,(TL_{\eta^{-1}})V\rangle_{L^2} = \int_M g\bigl((d\eta^{-1})U,(d\eta^{-1})V\bigr)\,\mu.$$
(By contrast, the analogous right-invariant $L^2$ metric on $D_\mu(M)$ is Arnold's classical metric whose geodesics are solutions of the incompressible Euler equations.)

Tasks:
(a) Exhibit a mechanical or continuum/fluid-type system whose configuration space is $D_\mu(M)$ and whose kinetic energy is given by $\tfrac{1}{2}\langle \dot\eta,\dot\eta\rangle_\eta^{\text{left}}$, so that the resulting Euler–Lagrange equations are the geodesic equations of this left-invariant $L^2$ metric.

(b) Derive the corresponding Euler–Arnold (geodesic) equation on $\mathfrak{X}_\mu(M)$ in terms of the right-logarithmic derivative, and interpret it physically.

(c) Determine whether there exist physically meaningful systems (in fluid dynamics, elasticity, plasma physics, or otherwise) that exhibit this type of left-invariance, as opposed to the usual right-invariance associated with material/spatial frame interchange.

representations.normalized:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $n \ge 2$):
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0, \qquad u(0,\cdot)=u_0,$$
for the velocity field $u:[0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ and pressure $p$.

For $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, the inhomogeneous Besov space $B^{s}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is defined via a Littlewood–Paley decomposition $(\Delta_j)_{j\ge -1}$ as the space of tempered distributions $f$ with finite norm
$$\|f\|_{B^{s}_{\infty,q}} = \Big\| \big(2^{js}\|\Delta_j f\|_{L^\infty}\big)_{j\ge -1}\Big\|_{\ell^q}.$$
It is known that $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$ embeds into $C^1$, which embeds into the Lipschitz class, which embeds into the Zygmund class $B^{1}_{\infty,\infty}$; and for $1<q<\infty$ the spaces $B^{1}_{\infty,q}$ interpolate between $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$ and $B^{1}_{\infty,\infty}$. Local ill-posedness of the Euler equations is already established in the endpoint critical spaces $C^1$, $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$, and $B^{1}_{\infty,\infty}$.

Determine, for each $q$ with $1<q<\infty$, whether the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations is locally ill-posed in $B^{1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ (e.g. in the sense of failure of continuous dependence of the solution map on the initial data, or instantaneous norm inflation).

Recent work has established ill-posedness for the incompressible Euler equations in the endpoint critical Besov spaces $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$ (Bourgain–Li, and subsequent refinements) and in $B^{s}_{p,\infty}$ spaces (with third index $\infty$, including the Zygmund-type endpoint). Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $s > 2$. Denote by $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ the group of orientation-preserving, volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$. This group carries a smooth Hilbert manifold structure, and equipping its tangent space at the identity $e$ — the space of divergence-free $H^s$ vector fields on $M$ tangent to $\partial M$ — with the $L^2$ inner product $\langle u, v\rangle_{L^2} = \int_M \langle u(x), v(x)\rangle\, d\mu(x)$ and extending by right-translation yields a smooth weak Riemannian metric on $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ whose geodesics correspond (via Arnold's theorem) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $\exp_e : T_e \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M) \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the associated Riemannian exponential map at the identity.

Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ be arbitrary.

(i) (Surjectivity Problem.) Determine whether there exists a divergence-free $H^s$ vector field $v$ on $M$ such that $\exp_e v = \varphi$.

(ii) (Variational Problem.) Determine whether there exists a curve $\gamma : [0,1] \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with $\gamma(0) = e$ and $\gamma(1) = \varphi$ that minimizes the energy functional
$$E(\gamma) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1 \|\dot\gamma(t)\|_{L^2}^2\, dt$$
among all such $H^1$ paths in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$.

Equip $\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$ with the right-invariant weak Riemannian metric induced at the identity by the $L^2$ inner product on divergence-free vector fields,
$$\langle u, v \rangle_{L^2} = \int_M \langle u(x), v(x)\rangle\, d\mathrm{vol}(x).$$
Geodesics of this metric correspond to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations of an ideal fluid on $M$. For a smooth path $\eta:[0,1]\to\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$ with fixed endpoints, consider the kinetic energy (action) functional
$$E(\eta) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1 \langle \dot\eta(t), \dot\eta(t)\rangle_{L^2}\, dt.$$
Question: Does $E$, viewed on a suitable Hilbert/Sobolev completion of the space of paths in $\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$ with fixed endpoints, satisfy the Palais–Smale condition? That is, does every sequence $\{\eta_n\}$ along which $E(\eta_n)$ is bounded and $\|dE(\eta_n)\|\to 0$ admit a convergent subsequence?

Let $M$ be either a closed (compact, boundaryless) smooth surface of genus $g\ge 2$, or a smooth bounded planar domain with at least two holes (i.e. whose boundary has at least three connected components), equipped with a smooth area form $\mu$. For an integer $s>\dim(M)/2+1$, let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of orientation- and volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$ (in the planar case, additionally fixing the boundary). It is a smooth infinite-dimensional Hilbert manifold and a topological group, and it carries the right-invariant weak Riemannian metric induced at the identity by the $L^2$ inner product
$$\langle u,v\rangle_{L^2} \;=\; \int_M \langle u(x),v(x)\rangle\, d\mu(x)$$
on divergence-free tangent vector fields. A geodesic of this metric corresponds to a solution of the incompressible Euler equation on $M$.

Question. Does there exist a non-constant closed geodesic of this $L^2$ metric in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, i.e. a smooth curve $\eta:\mathbb{R}\to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ which is a geodesic and satisfies $\eta(t+T)=\eta(t)$ for some $T>0$ and all $t$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question of existence of a closed $L^2$ geodesic in the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group on higher-genus surfaces or multiply-connected planar domains appears to remain open. Recent work by Drivas and Torres de Lizaur (generalizing earlier results of Ebin) shows that geodesics on such groups cannot have transverse self-intersections—any returning geodesic must be periodic—but this only rules out non-periodic recurrence and does not produce or exclude closed geodesics. No source found that constructs such a closed geodesic or proves its non-existence in the stated setting.

Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary) endowed with a smooth volume form $\mu$, and let $D_\mu(M)$ denote the group of smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$. Equip $D_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant weak Riemannian metric obtained by right-translating the $L^2(\mu)$ inner product on divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$ (the Arnold metric, whose geodesics correspond to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations).

Recall that an infinite-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(N,g)$ is called locally symmetric if every point $p\in N$ admits a neighborhood on which the geodesic central reflection $\sigma_p$ (sending $\exp_p(v)\mapsto \exp_p(-v)$) is a local isometry; equivalently, the curvature tensor $R$ is parallel, $\nabla R\equiv 0$.

(a) Determine in what precise analytic and geometric sense $(D_\mu(M),\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{L^2})$ fails to be an infinite-dimensional locally symmetric Riemannian space. In particular, identify obstructions to $\nabla R = 0$ and to the geodesic reflections $\sigma_e$ at the identity being isometries of the right-invariant $L^2$ metric, and quantify "how far" $D_\mu(M)$ is from local symmetry (e.g.\ via $\nabla R$, via the failure of $\sigma_e$ to preserve the metric, or via the holonomy algebra).

(b) Use this failure of local symmetry to explain the apparent paradox arising for the parallel sinusoidal steady flow with stream function $\psi(x,y)=\cos(ky)$ on the flat two-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^2$: Arnold's theorem asserts that the sectional curvature of $D_\mu(\mathbb{T}^2)$ is non-positive (and negative for most) two-planes containing the direction of $\psi$, which in a locally symmetric setting would suggest Lagrangian (and hence Eulerian) instability of the flow; yet such parallel flows can be Eulerian-stable (e.g.\ those with convex velocity profiles on sufficiently short tori). Reconcile this discrepancy by showing how the deviation of $D_\mu(M)$ from local symmetry breaks the symmetric-space heuristic linking negative sectional curvature to exponential divergence of geodesics, and thereby clarify the relationship between sign of curvature, Lagrangian instability, and Eulerian (hydrodynamic) stability.

Consider the incompressible Euler equations
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = -∇p,   div u = 0,
on a smooth Riemannian manifold M (possibly with boundary ∂M), with the no-penetration condition u·ν = 0 on ∂M. Given a sufficiently regular initial velocity u_0, let X(t,x) denote the Lagrangian flow map defined by
  d/dt X(t,x) = u(t, X(t,x)),   X(0,x) = x.

(a) Determine whether, in every spatial dimension d ≥ 2, the particle trajectories t ↦ X(t,x) are real-analytic functions of time on their interval of existence, for the case M = ℝ^d (no boundary).

(b) For fluids on a manifold M with boundary, determine how the time-analyticity of particle trajectories depends on the regularity of ∂M: in particular, whether analyticity of trajectories holds when ∂M is merely smooth (non-analytic) versus when ∂M is real-analytic.

(c) In the Yudovich class on a two-dimensional bounded domain (initial vorticity ω_0 ∈ L^∞ giving rise to a unique global weak solution with a continuous flow), it is known that particle trajectories are Gevrey regular in time, with the Gevrey order depending on the regularity of the boundary. Decide whether such Yudovich-class trajectories are in fact real-analytic in time.

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Time-analyticity of Lagrangian particle trajectories is established in ℝ^d for d = 2, 3 (Serfati, Shnirelman, Frisch–Zheligovsky and follow-ups), and is generally believed to extend to higher dimensions without fundamentally new difficulties, but a complete published treatment for all d and for general boundary cases is not standard. For Yudovich solutions in bounded 2D domains, results establish Gevrey regularity of trajectories (with Gevrey order depending on boundary regularity) but full real-analyticity in the Yudovich class remains unresolved. Thus the problem is partially solved.

Let $M$ be a two-dimensional compact analytic Riemannian manifold with analytic boundary. Let $\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, and consider the space of divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$. The Yudovich space $YU(M)$ is the space of divergence-free vector fields $u$ on $M$ tangent to $\partial M$ whose vorticity $\operatorname{curl} u$ lies in $L^\infty(M)$. A steady (stationary) solution of the incompressible Euler equation on $M$ is a vector field $u$ such that the pair $(u,p)$ satisfies $\nabla_u u = -\nabla p$ and $\operatorname{div} u = 0$ for some pressure function $p$. A generalized minimal flow on $M$ is, by definition, a vector field $u \in YU(M)$ that minimizes the $L^2$ kinetic energy $\tfrac{1}{2}\int_M |v|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}$ within its coadjoint orbit (equivalently, within the isovortical class consisting of all vector fields obtained from $u$ by the action of measure-preserving homeomorphisms preserving the vorticity distribution), where the minimum is taken over the closure of this orbit inside $YU(M)$. Let $GM(M) \subset YU(M)$ denote the set of all such generalized minimal flows on $M$.

Prove that $GM(M)$ is nonempty and is a proper subset of $YU(M)$.

Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a domain M ⊂ ℝ² (or a two-dimensional Riemannian manifold), governing a velocity field u(x,t) that is divergence-free and satisfies
  ∂_t u + (u · ∇) u + ∇p = 0,  div u = 0.
A generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) is a weak solution u(x,t) of these equations obtained as a limit of approximate minimizers of the action functional
  A[u] = ½ ∫₀^T ∫_M |u(x,t)|² dx dt
on the space of incompressible flows realizing a prescribed pair of initial and final configurations (i.e. of measure-preserving transformations of M), in the sense of generalized incompressible flows minimizing kinetic energy between two volume-preserving diffeomorphisms.

Let ω(x,t) = curl u(x,t) denote the scalar vorticity associated with such a GM-flow u.

Prove that for every GM-flow u(x,t), and every regular value c of ω(·,t), the vorticity level set
  { x ∈ M : curl u(x,t) = c }
is a union of real-analytic curves in M, for every fixed time t in the interval of definition.

Consider steady solutions of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a compact analytic surface (or a planar domain) M with velocity field u and vorticity ω = curl u. A "generalized minimal (GM) flow" is a steady Euler flow that arises as a long-time weak limit of solutions to the 2D Euler equations and admits a decomposition M = B₀ ⊔ (⨆ᵢ Bᵢ), where the Bᵢ ("blob regions") are open sets bounded by streamlines, and B₀ ("background region") is the complement, with vorticity organized so that the level sets of ω inside each blob are real-analytic curves.

Prove the following structural statement: for any GM-flow, the vorticity ω = curl u is constant on the background region B₀. Equivalently, every level set of ω in M is either a real-analytic curve or coincides with the entire background region B₀.

representations.normalized:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations for an ideal fluid on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (or on a smooth $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold), $d \ge 2$:
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla) u + \nabla p = 0,\qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
where $u(t,x)$ is the velocity field and $p(t,x)$ the pressure.

Motivated by the observation that physical fluid flows often exhibit much higher smoothness along streamlines (integral curves of $u$) than transverse to them — for example, vorticity tends to be analytic along level lines while only finitely smooth in the transverse direction — carry out the following program:

(a) Define a scale of anisotropic function spaces $X = X(\Omega)$ on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (or on a manifold) in which regularity is measured separately in the direction tangent to the flow lines of a given divergence-free vector field $u$ and in the directions transverse to those flow lines, with strictly higher (e.g., analytic or Gevrey) regularity required tangentially and only finite (e.g., Hölder or Sobolev) regularity required transversally. Provide a precise definition of $X$ that is intrinsic, invariant under volume-preserving diffeomorphisms compatible with the flow structure, and well adapted to the transport operator $u\cdot\nabla$.

(b) Prove local-in-time existence and uniqueness theorems for the Euler system above with initial data in $X$, in any dimension $d \ge 2$, establishing that the solution map $u_0 \mapsto u(t,\cdot)$ is well-defined and continuous in the topology of $X$ on some nontrivial time interval.

representations.normalized:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold (for concreteness, take $M = [0,1]^n$ with $n \ge 2$, or the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^n$). Denote by $\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$ the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$. Given two volume-preserving maps $\eta_0, \eta_1 \in \mathrm{SDiff}(M)$, consider the variational problem of minimizing the kinetic action
$$\mathcal{A}(\eta) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1\!\!\int_M |\partial_t \eta(t,x)|^2 \, dx\, dt$$
over paths $t \mapsto \eta(t,\cdot)$ joining $\eta_0$ to $\eta_1$. In general no classical minimizer exists, and one is led to Brenier's relaxation: a generalized minimal flow (GM-flow) is a probability measure $\mu$ on the space of continuous paths $\Omega = C([0,1], M)$ that is incompressible (the time-$t$ marginal of $\mu$ equals normalized volume for every $t \in [0,1]$), that satisfies the prescribed endpoint coupling $(e_0, e_1)_\# \mu = (\mathrm{id} \times \eta_1)_\# \mathrm{vol}$, and that minimizes the action
$$\mathcal{A}(\mu) \;=\; \int_\Omega\!\!\int_0^1 \tfrac{1}{2}|\dot\gamma(t)|^2\,dt\, d\mu(\gamma)$$
among all such measures. The associated pressure field $p$ is the Lagrange multiplier in the dual problem, and is known to be a distribution on $(0,1)\times M$ with limited Sobolev/BV regularity in space–time.

Problem. Introduce anisotropic function spaces $X^{s,s'}$ on $(0,1)\times M$ adapted to the geometry of flow lines — that is, spaces in which regularity is measured separately in directions tangent to the typical Lagrangian trajectories of the GM-flow and in directions transverse to them — and determine the sharp regularity, expressed by sharp exponents $(s, s')$, of:

(i) the pressure field $p$ associated to a GM-flow, and
(ii) the conditional law of trajectories $\gamma \mapsto \gamma(t)$ of $\mu$ along flow lines,

within these anisotropic spaces. The goal is to identify the optimal anisotropic Hölder/Sobolev/Besov scale on which GM-flows possess regularity strictly better than the known isotropic bounds.

Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian three-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$, for $s>\tfrac{n}{2}+1=\tfrac{5}{2}$. Equip $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant $L^2$ (kinetic energy) metric; its geodesics correspond, via the Arnold interpretation, to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $\exp_e: U \subset T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M) \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ be the associated Riemannian exponential map at the identity.

It is known that, in contrast to the two-dimensional case, $\exp_e$ generally fails to be a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero when $\dim M = 3$: there exist explicit initial velocity fields $v_0 \in T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ along whose geodesics the derivative $d\exp_e$ is not Fredholm.

Problem: Quantify this failure of the Fredholm property. For instance, for a geodesic with initial velocity $v_0$, determine the essential spectrum of the derivative $d\exp_e|_{tv_0}$ (viewed as a bounded operator on $T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$), or otherwise provide a precise measure of its non-compactness. Specifically, decomposing $d\exp_e$ in the form $A + K_r$ where $A$ is an invertible operator and
$$K_r w \;=\; (1-\Delta)^{-r/2}\, P_e\!\left(\iota_w\, d\,(1-\Delta)^{r/2} v_0^{\flat}\right)$$
(with $P_e$ the Hodge projection onto divergence-free fields, $\flat$ the metric musical isomorphism, and $r=0$ corresponding to the $L^2$ case), determine whether and how badly $K_0$ fails to be compact, and compute (or estimate) the essential spectrum of $d\exp_e$ along three-dimensional Euler geodesics.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Existing literature establishes that the L^2 exponential map on the volumorphism group is nonlinear Fredholm of index zero in dimension two but fails to be Fredholm in dimension three, with explicit non-Fredholm examples on three-manifolds (e.g., solid torus). A decomposition of the derivative into an invertible part plus a remainder K_r is available for H^r metrics with r>0, suggesting the L^2 failure is borderline, but no published work appears to quantify the failure (e.g., compute the essential spectrum) for compact Riemannian 3-manifolds. The problem appears to remain open.

Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold with (possibly nonempty) boundary, and let $D^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of Sobolev-class $H^s$ (with $s > \dim M/2 + 1$) volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric whose geodesics through the identity correspond to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations. Given an $L^2$ geodesic $\eta(t)$ in $D^s_\mu(M)$ with $\eta(0)=\mathrm{id}$, a point $\eta(t_0)$ is called a conjugate point along $\eta$ if the differential of the Riemannian exponential map $\exp_e$ at $t_0\dot\eta(0)$ fails to be a linear isomorphism; its order is the dimension of the kernel of $d\exp_e$ at that point (with appropriate notions of mono- and epi-conjugacy in the infinite-dimensional setting).

(a) Determine the order of the first conjugate point along any $L^2$ geodesic in $D^s_\mu(M)$ starting at the identity. In particular, decide whether this order is always strictly greater than one.

(b) A stationary flow of an ideal fluid on $M$ is Arnold (Lyapunov) stable if the quadratic form given by the second derivative of the kinetic energy, restricted to the coadjoint orbit of the corresponding vorticity, is either positive definite or negative definite. Determine whether the existence of conjugate points along the $L^2$ geodesic in $D^s_\mu(M)$ generated by a stationary flow is related to the failure of Arnold's stability criterion for that flow; in particular, decide whether every Arnold-stable stationary flow on $M$ generates a geodesic with no conjugate points.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Partial results are known but the general questions remain open. Preston (2006) showed that on the volumorphism group the differential of the exponential map at a first conjugate point is never Fredholm, and conjugate points must be either epiconjugate-but-not-monoconjugate or monoconjugate of infinite order, yet the precise order along a general L2 geodesic is not determined. For part (b), non-existence of conjugate points has been verified along Arnold-stable steady states on simple two-dimensional domains (disk, annulus, channel), and the Misiołek curvature criterion provides a sufficient condition, but a general equivalence/relationship between Arnold stability and absence of conjugate points has not been established.

For a Sobolev exponent $s > n/2 + 1$, denote by $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$. For a curve $\gamma:[0,T]\to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, define its absolute complexity $C(\gamma(t))$ to be the total spatial complexity accumulated by $\gamma$ up to time $t$ (for instance, measured by the growth of an appropriate geometric quantity such as the length of the image of a generic submanifold, or equivalently a measure of the intricacy of the configuration $\gamma(t)$ relative to the identity).

$$ C(\gamma(t)) \;\le\; a\, \exp\!\bigl(b\, t\, \|\dot\gamma(0)\|_{H^s}\bigr) $$
for all $t$ in the interval of existence of $\gamma$.

representations.normalized: Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold. Arnold's classical framework realizes solutions of the Euler equations of an ideal incompressible fluid on $M$ as geodesics on the group $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ (or $\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$) equipped with the right-invariant $L^2$ kinetic-energy metric, and realizes the inviscid Burgers equation as the geodesic equation on $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ with this metric. For smooth potential initial data, Burgers solutions correspond to one-parameter families of diffeomorphisms; however, generic solutions develop shock waves in finite time, at which point the family of maps ceases to be a diffeomorphism and the geodesic in $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ terminates. Let $\mathrm{Map}(M)$ denote the semigroup of suitably regular maps $M \to M$, containing $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ and allowing non-injective maps that model particle fusion inside shocks. Problem: Construct an extension of Arnold's geodesic framework from $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ to $\mathrm{Map}(M)$ (or an appropriate completion such as the semigroup of polymorphisms / generalized flows) endowed with a geometric structure generalizing the right-invariant $L^2$ metric, such that the resulting generalized geodesics: (i) coincide with classical smooth solutions of Burgers-like and compressible Euler equations on $M$ as long as those solutions remain smooth, and (ii) continue in a canonical way past the formation of shock waves, with continuations describing generalized/entropy solutions in which characteristics may merge. Specify the geometry (metric, connection, or variational principle), prove existence of such generalized geodesics, and show that they recover the standard shock-admissible weak solutions of the Burgers and compressible fluid equations.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is posed as an open problem in geometric hydrodynamics. Partial progress exists: Khesin–Misiolek related Burgers shocks to focal points and curvatures on the diffeomorphism group, and a flow completion via the semigroup of polymorphisms has been proposed. Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary (e.g.\ a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ or the periodic channel $\mathbb{T}\times(0,a)$), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving Sobolev diffeomorphisms of $M$ of class $H^s$ (with $s>n/2+1$). The tangent space at the identity may be identified with the space of divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$,
$$T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)=\{u\in H^s(M;TM):\ \operatorname{div} u=0,\ u\cdot\nu|_{\partial M}=0\},$$
on which the incompressible Euler equations
$$\partial_t u+(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla p,\qquad \operatorname{div} u=0,\qquad u\cdot\nu|_{\partial M}=0 \tag{$\ast$}$$
define a (local) flow $u(t,\cdot)$.

Construct a continuous functional ("Lyapunov function")
$$L:T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}$$
with the following two properties:

(i) For every solution $u(t,\cdot)$ of $(\ast)$, the map $t\mapsto L(u(t,\cdot))$ is monotone nondecreasing, i.e.\ $\frac{d}{dt}L(u(t,\cdot))\ge 0$ for all $t$ for which the solution is defined.

(ii) The set of velocity fields $u\in T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ at which equality $\frac{d}{dt}L(u(t,\cdot))=0$ may hold is a "slim" subset of $T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ — for instance, of infinite codimension.

Such a functional should quantify the heuristic "aging"/regularity-deterioration phenomenon for ideal incompressible fluids and, in particular, should not be supported only near $\partial M$ (i.e.\ examples with support in the interior of the fluid domain are sought). Does such a Lyapunov function exist?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem of constructing a global Lyapunov function on divergence-free velocity fields that is monotone along Euler evolution outside a slim set is listed as an open problem in the geometric-hydrodynamics open-problems survey (Khesin et al., 2022). No interior-supported global Lyapunov function quantifying aging is known.

Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a periodic channel $\Omega = \mathbb{T} \times [0,1]$ (with $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$), written in vorticity form
$$\partial_t \omega + u\cdot\nabla \omega = 0, \qquad u = \nabla^\perp \psi, \qquad -\Delta \psi = \omega,$$
with impermeable boundary conditions $u\cdot n = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Let $U(y)$ be a smooth plane-parallel shear profile whose vorticity $\Omega(y) = -U'(y)$ is strictly monotone in $y\in[0,1]$, so that the level sets of $\Omega$ are the horizontal lines $\{y = \text{const}\}$.

Let $\omega_0$ be a smooth initial vorticity on $\Omega$ that is a small perturbation of $\Omega(y)$ in a suitable topology, and suppose that exactly one level set $\Gamma_0 = \{\omega_0 = c_0\}$ of $\omega_0$ is a simple closed curve (in the channel) which is smooth away from a single point $p_0$ where it has a corner — a "kink" — i.e. the curve $\Gamma_0$ has two distinct one-sided tangent directions at $p_0$, while all other level sets of $\omega_0$ are smooth.

Let $\omega(t,\cdot)$ be the solution of the Euler equation with initial data $\omega_0$, and let $\Gamma_t = \{\omega(t,\cdot) = c_0\}$ be the corresponding level set transported by the flow.

Prove that the kink persists for all time: there exists a point $p_t \in \Gamma_t$ (depending continuously on $t$) at which $\Gamma_t$ has a corner singularity, and in particular the level set $\Gamma_t$ does not become $C^1$-smooth at any time $t>0$.

Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space (or a Hilbert space) and let $M\subset X$ be a compact subset equipped with a Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported on $M$. For $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, consider the following entropy-type quantities.

(i) The $\varepsilon$-entropy of the set $M$:
$$H_\varepsilon(M)=\log_2 N_\varepsilon(M),$$
where $N_\varepsilon(M)$ is the minimal number of closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ needed to cover $M$.

(ii) The measure $\varepsilon$-entropy: choose a minimal $\varepsilon$-cover of $M$ by balls and let $\{C_j\}$ be the associated partition of $M$ into measurable pieces of diameter $\le 2\varepsilon$; set
$$H_\varepsilon(\mu)=-\sum_j \mu(C_j)\log_2\mu(C_j).$$

(iii) The $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-entropy $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\mu)$: the logarithm (base $2$) of the minimal number of $\varepsilon$-balls needed to cover a subset of $M$ of $\mu$-measure at least $1-\delta$.

(iv) The variants $\widetilde H_\varepsilon$ and $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ in which coverings are replaced by packings (maximal collections of pairwise disjoint balls of radius $\varepsilon$ centered in $M$, with the analogous measure-restricted version for $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$).

Problem. Investigate the properties of, and establish the precise relations between, the four entropy functions $H_\varepsilon$, $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$, $\widetilde H_\varepsilon$, $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ on compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces. In particular, study their asymptotic behavior as $\varepsilon\to 0$, their invariance (or lack thereof) under isometries, rotations, and smooth deformations of the underlying set $M$, and determine to what extent the leading-order asymptotic
$$H_\varepsilon(\mu)\sim d\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\cdot \mu(X)$$
(observed when $M=Q^d\subset\mathbb R^d$ is the unit cube with $\mu$ the Lebesgue measure) persists when $Q^d$ is embedded and rotated inside a larger space $X^n$, $n>d$, or otherwise deformed.

Consider the incompressible Euler equations on a smooth compact domain (or the torus) $\mathbb{T}^d$:
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla) u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
with initial data $u(0,\cdot)=u_0$ in some Banach space $X$ of divergence-free vector fields (e.g. $L^2$ or $H^s$). For a bounded set $K\subset X$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the Kolmogorov $\varepsilon$-entropy of $K$ is
$$H_\varepsilon(K) := \log_2 N_\varepsilon(K),$$
where $N_\varepsilon(K)$ is the minimal number of balls of radius $\varepsilon$ (in the metric of $X$) needed to cover $K$. Given a bounded family $\mathcal{F}_0 \subset X$ of initial data, let $\mathcal{F}_t$ denote the set of solutions at time $t$ obtained by evolving each element of $\mathcal{F}_0$ under the Euler flow.

The Euler equations formally preserve a Hamiltonian structure and admit a Liouville-type (volume-preserving) phase-space description, which by analogy with finite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems would suggest conservation of $\varepsilon$-entropy under the flow. Nevertheless, numerical and theoretical observations indicate that
$$H_\varepsilon(\mathcal{F}_t) < H_\varepsilon(\mathcal{F}_0) \qquad \text{for } t > 0$$
can occur for natural choices of $\mathcal{F}_0$ and $\varepsilon$.

Problem: Provide a rigorous mathematical explanation of this phenomenon of $\varepsilon$-entropy decrease in time for ensembles of solutions of the Euler equations, reconciling it with the underlying Hamiltonian and Liouville-type structure of ideal incompressible fluid dynamics.

Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation for an ideal fluid on a surface $M$ (for concreteness, take $M$ to be the two-torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or the two-sphere $S^2$), written in vorticity form as
$$\partial_t \omega + \{\psi, \omega\} = 0, \qquad \omega = \Delta \psi,$$
where $\omega: M \to \mathbb{R}$ is the vorticity, $\psi$ is the stream function, $\Delta$ is the Laplace–Beltrami operator, and $\{f,g\} = \partial_x f\,\partial_y g - \partial_y f\,\partial_x g$ is the canonical Poisson bracket on $M$. This system is an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system on the dual of the Lie algebra $\mathrm{SVect}(M)$ of divergence-free vector fields on $M$, equipped with the Lie–Poisson structure, and its Hamiltonian is the kinetic energy $H(\omega) = \tfrac12 \int_M |\nabla \psi|^2$.

Although the system possesses an infinite family of Casimir invariants (the moments $\int_M f(\omega)\,d\mu$ for any smooth $f$) and admits a formal Lax representation arising automatically from its Euler–Poincaré structure, no Lax pair depending nontrivially on a spectral parameter is known, and the existence of such a representation (or of action–angle coordinates) is not established.

Problem. Formulate a precise reasonable notion of integrability for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems—for instance, one of:
(a) algebraic-geometric integrability arising from a Lax pair with a nontrivial spectral parameter;
(b) the existence of a complete set of functionally independent Poisson-commuting first integrals giving an invariant foliation by Lagrangian tori in a suitable functional-analytic sense;
(c) integrability in the sense of meromorphic/real-analytic first integrals along a generic invariant submanifold (in the spirit of Ziglin–Morales-Ramis or Melnikov-type obstructions applied to periodic orbits and saddle separatrices of the Euler flow)—

and prove that the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is not integrable in that sense. Equivalently, exhibit a rigorous obstruction (e.g. nontrivial monodromy of variational equations along a periodic solution, a nonvanishing Melnikov integral for a heteroclinic/homoclinic connection of stationary solutions, or a differential-Galois obstruction) that rules out integrability of the 2D Euler equation.

Let $N$ be a closed non-orientable smooth surface (e.g. the real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$ or the Klein bottle) endowed with an area form $\mu$ (defined locally up to sign, i.e. a density). The group $\mathrm{SDiff}(N,\mu)$ of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of $N$ acts on its Lie algebra of divergence-free vector fields, and dually on the space of vorticity functions (more precisely, pseudo-functions / twisted densities adapted to non-orientability). A system of $n$ point vortices on $N$ with strengths $\Gamma_1,\dots,\Gamma_n\in\mathbb{R}$ is the Hamiltonian dynamical system on (a desingularization of) $N^n$ obtained by lifting to the orientable double cover $\widetilde N \to N$ and using the Green's function of the Laplacian on $\widetilde N$ together with the deck involution, producing equations of motion for the positions $x_1,\dots,x_n\in N$ governed by a Hamiltonian of Kirchhoff–Routh type.

Solve the following:

(a) Determine the smallest number $n$ of point vortices for which the system on $N$ fails to be Liouville-integrable, and exhibit explicit non-integrable examples for $N=\mathbb{RP}^2$ and $N=$ Klein bottle, together with proofs of non-integrability (e.g. via Melnikov, symbolic dynamics, or topological entropy arguments).

(b) Describe the full set of Casimir invariants for the natural Lie–Poisson structure on the dual of the Lie algebra of $\mathrm{SDiff}(N,\mu)$ for a closed non-orientable surface $N$, in analogy with the generalized enstrophies and circulations known in the orientable case.

(c) Construct finite-dimensional Lie-algebra approximations of $\mathrm{SDiff}(N,\mu)$ for non-orientable $N$ (analogous to the $\mathfrak{su}(n)$-type approximations of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the sphere and torus), and prove a suitable convergence statement.

Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian 3-manifold, and consider the incompressible Euler equation
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
for a time-dependent divergence-free vector field $u(t,\cdot)$ on $M$, tangent to $\partial M$ if any. For a fixed regularity class (e.g. $C^k$ with non-integer $k$ sufficiently large, or a suitable Sobolev space) on the space $\mathcal{X}$ of divergence-free vector fields on $M$, call a solution $u(t,\cdot)$ a wandering solution if there exists an open neighborhood $U\subset\mathcal{X}$ of the initial datum $u(0,\cdot)$ and a time $T>0$ such that $u(t,\cdot)\notin U$ for all $t\ge T$ (equivalently, the trajectory eventually leaves a neighborhood of its initial datum and never returns).

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem is generally regarded as open. Only partial results are available: using KAM-theoretic methods, Khesin, Kuksin and Peralta-Salas (and subsequent work) established non-mixing and non-transitivity of the 3D Euler flow in suitable C^k topologies for prescribed helicity and large energy, both globally and locally near typical steady states on S^3. These results constitute the only known progress toward the existence of wandering solutions in 3D, analogous to the 2D results of Nadirashvili and Shnirelman, but a direct construction of wandering solutions for the 3D Euler equation has not been achieved.

Let $(M,g)$ be a closed Riemannian 3-manifold and consider the incompressible Euler equation on $M$:
$$\partial_t u + \nabla_u u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
acting on the space $\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ of divergence-free vector fields of class $C^k$. Let $\Phi_t^E:\mathcal{X}^k(M)\to\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ denote the (locally defined) Euler flow.

The flow is said to be transitive on a set $U\subset\mathcal{X}^k(M)$ if for every nonempty open $V_1,V_2\subset U$ there exists $t\ge 0$ with $\Phi_t^E(V_1)\cap V_2\ne\emptyset$, and it is said to be mixing if for any two nonempty open sets $V_1,V_2$ one has $\Phi_t^E(V_1)\cap V_2\ne\emptyset$ for all sufficiently large $t$.

Existing KAM-based arguments establish non-transitivity and non-mixing of the 3D Euler flow only under restrictions on the regularity index $k$ (typically $k>4$ and non-integer, sufficient to apply KAM theory to the Lagrangian flow of steady states).

Problem. Remove these smoothness restrictions: prove non-transitivity and non-mixing of the incompressible Euler equation on closed Riemannian 3-manifolds for the $C^k$ topology in full generality (in particular, for all relevant integer values of $k$ and for low-regularity classes not currently covered by KAM methods).

Let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $H:M\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth Hamiltonian. Assume the Hamiltonian system defined by $H$ is Liouville integrable: there exist $n$ smooth functions $f_1=H,f_2,\dots,f_n:M\to\mathbb{R}$ that pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$ for all $i,j$, and are functionally independent (i.e., $df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_n\neq 0$) on an open dense subset of $M$. Let
$$\Sigma\;=\;\{\,x\in M\;:\;df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_n\,(x)=0\,\}$$
denote the singular set on which the integrals fail to be functionally independent. The Hamiltonian flow of $H$ preserves $\Sigma$ and each connected component of its strata.

Investigate the dynamical complexity of the Hamiltonian flow restricted to $\Sigma$:

(a) Describe what constraints Liouville integrability imposes on the dynamics on $\Sigma$ (and on its individual smooth strata).

(b) Determine whether the restricted dynamics on $\Sigma$ can exhibit chaotic behavior — for instance, positive topological entropy, a horseshoe, or a hyperbolic invariant set with a dense orbit — even when $\Sigma$ is a "tiny" (low-dimensional, measure-zero) submanifold of $M$.

(c) If chaos is possible, exhibit an explicit smooth ($C^\infty$ or real-analytic) example of a Liouville integrable system on a compact symplectic manifold whose restriction to the singular locus $\Sigma$ has positive topological entropy; if it is impossible, prove the corresponding rigidity theorem.

Consider stationary solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on R^3 (or a Riemannian 3-manifold), i.e., divergence-free vector fields v satisfying (v · ∇)v = −∇p for some pressure function p. Two classes of such fields are of particular interest:

(i) Fields v whose Bernoulli function b = p + |v|^2/2 is nonconstant; by Arnold's structure theorem, away from critical points of b the trajectories of v lie on the level sets {b = const}, which are unions of tori and cylinders, giving such fields a "topologically tame" structure.

(ii) Beltrami fields, i.e., divergence-free vector fields satisfying curl v = λ v for some nonzero constant λ; these have constant Bernoulli function and can exhibit arbitrarily complicated topology. In particular, given any finite link L ⊂ R^3 and any nonzero λ ∈ R, there exists a C^∞ diffeomorphism of R^3 arbitrarily close to the identity in any C^m norm whose image of L is a set of vortex lines of some Beltrami field with eigenvalue λ.

This produces an apparent paradox: a "generic" steady Euler field looks like type (i) and is topologically simple, yet the subclass of Beltrami fields (type (ii)) realizes arbitrarily complicated topology of vortex lines.

Problem. Provide a mathematical explanation of this paradox by formulating an appropriate, natural notion of genericity for steady three-dimensional Euler fields under which:
(a) a typical steady Euler field is topologically tame (its trajectories lie on a regular family of two-dimensional level surfaces of the Bernoulli function), and
(b) the rich topological complexity exhibited by Beltrami fields is consistently accounted for within this notion of typicality.

Specify the function space, topology, and measure-theoretic or Baire-category sense in which "generic" is to be understood, and prove that the proposed notion yields these two properties.

Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian 3-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{V}(M)$ denote the space of smooth divergence-free vector fields on $M$ that are tangent to the boundary. For $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$, define its energy by
$$E(v) = \int_M \|v(x)\|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}(x),$$
and its helicity by
$$\mathcal{H}(v) = \int_M \langle v, \operatorname{curl}^{-1} v \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol},$$
where $\operatorname{curl}^{-1} v$ is a vector potential $A$ with $\operatorname{curl} A = v$. Arnold's classical inequality states that there exists a constant $C(M) > 0$ such that $E(v) \geq C(M)\, |\mathcal{H}(v)|$ for all $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$.

Construct a sequence of functionals $\{I_n : \mathcal{V}(M) \to \mathbb{R}\}_{n \geq 1}$, with $I_1 = \mathcal{H}$, having the following properties:

(i) each $I_n$ is invariant under the action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ (i.e., is a higher-order helicity-type invariant);

(ii) for every $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$ and every $n \geq 1$, if $I_1(v) = I_2(v) = \cdots = I_{n-1}(v) = 0$ but $I_n(v) \neq 0$, then there exists a constant $C_n(M) > 0$ (independent of $v$) and an exponent $\alpha_n > 0$ such that
$$E(v) \geq C_n(M)\, |I_n(v)|^{\alpha_n}.$$

In particular, vanishing of all lower invariants forces the first nonzero invariant to bound the energy of the field from below.

$$\mathcal{H}(v) = \int_M \langle v, \operatorname{curl}^{-1} v \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol},$$
where $\operatorname{curl}^{-1} v$ is a vector potential $A$ with $\operatorname{curl} A = v$. Arnold's classical inequality states that there exists a constant $C(M) > 0$ such that $E(v) \geq C(M)\, |\mathcal{H}(v)|$ for all $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$.

Construct a sequence of functionals $\{I_n : \mathcal{V}(M) \to \mathbb{R}\}_{n \geq 1}$, with $I_1 = \mathcal{H}$, having the following properties:

(i) each $I_n$ is invariant under the action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ (i.e., is a higher-order helicity-type invariant);

(ii) for every $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$ and every $n \geq 1$, if $I_1(v) = I_2(v) = \cdots = I_{n-1}(v) = 0$ but $I_n(v) \neq 0$, then there exists a constant $C_n(M) > 0$ (independent of $v$) and an exponent $\alpha_n > 0$ such that
$$E(v) \geq C_n(M)\, |I_n(v)|^{\alpha_n}.$$

In particular, vanishing of all lower invariants forces the first nonzero invariant to bound the energy of the field from below.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The problem, originating in Arnold–Khesin's topological hydrodynamics, remains open in full generality. Partial progress exists: cubic ("third-order") asymptotic helicity-type invariants and certain higher analogs of the asymptotic Hopf invariant have been constructed (e.g., Bodnar/Komendarczyk-Vela-Vick), and a related rigidity result shows helicity is the only regular integral invariant under mild assumptions. However, no general hierarchy giving energy lower bounds when lower invariants vanish has been established.

representations.normalized:
Consider the three-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
   i ψ_t + Δψ + |ψ|^2 ψ = 0,   ψ : ℝ_t × ℝ^3 → ℂ,
and the one-dimensional cubic NLS equation
   i φ_t + φ_{xx} + |φ|^2 φ = 0,   φ : ℝ_t × ℝ → ℂ.

It is known that the 1D NLS arises from the dynamics of a vortex filament in ℝ^3 governed by the localized induction approximation (LIA) (the binormal flow γ_t = γ_s × γ_{ss}) via the Hasimoto transformation, which produces a 1D NLS for the complex function ψ(s,t) = κ(s,t) exp(i ∫^s τ(s',t) ds') built from the curvature κ and torsion τ of the filament.

(a) Construct a direct reduction of the 3D NLS equation to the 1D NLS equation by considering singular solutions of the 3D NLS supported on a time-dependent one-dimensional submanifold (curve) γ(·,t) ⊂ ℝ^3, expressing the resulting 1D evolution along γ as the 1D cubic NLS, without passing through the LIA / binormal flow / Hasimoto transformation.

(b) Analogously, consider the compressible Euler equations on ℝ^3 for a velocity field u and density ρ:
   ∂_t (ρ u) + ∇·(ρ u ⊗ u) + ∇p(ρ) = 0,   ∂_t ρ + ∇·(ρ u) = 0.
Construct a reduction of this 3D system to an effective one-dimensional evolution by restricting to singular solutions whose support (e.g. mass or vorticity concentration) lies on a moving one-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^3, and identify the resulting equations governing the motion of that submanifold and of the data carried along it.

Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote a shape space of smooth closed hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (for instance, the space $\mathrm{Emb}(M,\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ of unparametrized embeddings of a closed manifold $M$), and consider on $\mathcal{S}$ the family of nonlocal Riemannian metrics of fractional Sobolev order $H^{-1/2}$ that arise naturally in hydrodynamics: namely, the metrics induced on the space of dynamic free boundaries or on the space of vortex sheets by the kinetic energy of the surrounding incompressible fluid (where, for a normal velocity field $a$ on a hypersurface $\Gamma$, the squared norm is $\|a\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}^2 = \int_\Gamma a\, \mathcal{N}^{-1} a\, dS$ with $\mathcal{N}$ the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, or analogously a vortex-sheet kinetic-energy norm).

Develop the differential geometry of $(\mathcal{S}, g_{H^{-1/2}})$: in particular, determine the geodesic equation, the Levi-Civita connection, sectional curvature, completeness properties (metric and geodesic), existence of minimizing geodesics, the structure of the exponential map, and the relationship of these geodesics to the free-boundary Euler equations and to the Birkhoff–Rott vortex-sheet evolution.

Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold. Consider the space of complex wave functions $\Psi: M \to \mathbb{C}$ of fixed $L^2$-norm, and the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ of the space of smooth probability densities on $M$. The Madelung transform $\Psi = \sqrt{\rho}\, e^{i\theta/\hbar}$ is known, on the open set of nowhere-vanishing wave functions, to define (after quotienting by the constant phase $S^1$-action) a symplectomorphism and indeed a Kähler map from this space to $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$, where the wave-function side carries the Fubini–Study Kähler structure and the density side carries the structure induced by the Fisher–Rao information metric. Moreover, on this regular stratum the inverse Madelung map admits an interpretation as a momentum map for the action of a certain semidirect product group $G \ltimes C^\infty(M, \mathbb{R})$ (the diffeomorphism group acting on smooth functions) on the space of wave functions.

(a) Extend the symplectomorphism and Kähler-map properties of the Madelung transform to the full space of smooth wave functions on $M$, including those that are allowed to vanish on subsets of $M$ (with arbitrary zero set, possibly of positive codimension), giving a precise description of the geometric structures and the regularity needed across the zero locus.

(b) In this extended framework, give a momentum-map interpretation, with respect to the semidirect product group action above, that accounts for the discrepancy in the quantization condition $\oint d\theta \in 2\pi\hbar\,\mathbb{Z}$ around zeros (nodes) of the wave function: explain in momentum-map terms why and when this integrality condition must hold, thereby resolving the controversy over whether the Madelung hydrodynamic formulation requires the phase $\theta$ to be globally single-valued modulo $2\pi\hbar$.

The Madelung transform has been shown to be a symplectomorphism and Kähler map on the regular stratum (nowhere-vanishing wave functions), with a momentum-map interpretation for a semidirect product group action (Khesin–Misiołek–Modin, and Fusca). Setting. Consider the hydrodynamic pilot-wave system describing a millimetric droplet bouncing on the surface of a vertically vibrated fluid bath above the Faraday threshold. In a standard model, the in-plane position $X(t)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ of the droplet satisfies a stroboscopic equation of motion of the form
$$ m\ddot X(t) + \gamma \dot X(t) = -\nabla h(X(t),t), $$
where the underlying wave field $h(x,t)$ is generated by the cumulative impacts of the droplet,
$$ h(x,t) = \sum_{n: t_n\le t} A\, e^{-(t-t_n)/T_F}\, W\!\big(|x-X(t_n)|\big), $$
with $W$ a Bessel-type Faraday wave kernel of wavelength $\lambda_F$, $T_F$ a memory time, and $\{t_n\}$ the bouncing times.

Separately, recall the Madelung transform: a wavefunction $\psi(x,t) = \sqrt{\rho(x,t)}\, e^{iS(x,t)/\hbar}$ solving the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\psi + V\psi$ is equivalent to the hydrodynamic system
$$ \partial_t \rho + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho\, v) = 0, \qquad m(\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v) = -\nabla\!\left(V + Q[\rho]\right), $$
with $v = \nabla S/m$ and quantum potential $Q[\rho] = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,\Delta\sqrt{\rho}/\sqrt{\rho}$.

Problem. Derive, by a combination of (i) a multi-scale averaging procedure applied to the fast bouncing/Faraday oscillations of the droplet–wave dynamics described above, and (ii) the Madelung transform, an effective continuum description of the long-time statistics of the droplet position whose evolution coincides with (or rigorously approximates) that of a Schrödinger-type equation for an emergent wavefunction $\psi$. In particular:

(a) Identify a small parameter $\varepsilon$ (e.g. ratio of Faraday period to memory time, or ratio of de Broglie-like wavelength to bath wavelength) and perform an averaging of the droplet equation over the fast time scale to obtain a closed evolution for the slowly-varying density $\rho(x,t)$ and mean velocity $v(x,t)$ of the droplet.

(b) Show that the averaged system can be put, via the inverse Madelung transform $\psi = \sqrt{\rho}\,e^{iS/\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}}$, into the form of a Schrödinger equation with an effective Planck constant $\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}$ expressible in terms of the physical parameters $(m,\gamma,A,T_F,\lambda_F)$, and identify the effective potential induced by external boundaries or applied forces.

(c) Establish in what regime (memory, impact phase, geometry) this droplet–quantum-particle correspondence is exact, and quantify the corrections beyond that regime.

The proposed derivation—obtaining a Schrödinger-type description of bouncing-droplet dynamics by combining multi-scale averaging with the Madelung transform—does not appear to have been carried out rigorously. Partial correspondences (e.g., the Durey–Milewski–Bush statistical correspondence between droplet position distributions and time-averaged wave fields, and analogies via de Broglie's double-solution / quantum thermostat) are established in limited regimes, and recent work extends these statistical correspondences empirically, but a complete averaging-plus-Madelung derivation of the droplet–quantum particle correspondence is still being sought.

representations.normalized:
Consider an infinite mechanical cascade model — a Hamiltonian system of infinitely many coupled mechanical degrees of freedom (for example, an infinite chain of nonlinearly coupled oscillators or rotators arranged on a hierarchy of scales) intended as a finite-dimensional toy model for the energy cascade in turbulent fluids. In such models, a sustained transfer of energy from injection scales to dissipation scales is typically enforced by inserting, by hand, an explicit linear friction (damping) term on the small-scale modes.

Problem. Identify a mathematically natural mechanism, intrinsic to the conservative Hamiltonian dynamics of an infinite mechanical cascade of this type, by which energy is effectively dissipated (i.e. transported irreversibly to arbitrarily small scales and removed from any fixed finite-scale window) without postulating an explicit friction term in the equations of motion. Equivalently, construct an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian cascade model and prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, energy escapes to infinity in mode space as t → ∞, thereby reproducing dissipative behaviour on each finite collection of modes purely from the conservative dynamics.

representations.normalized:
Consider the following idealized mechanical "chamber-and-damper" apparatus intended to model an energy cascade. The device consists of a finite collection of coupled chambers, indexed by i, each equipped with three positive real parameters: an integer mode number n_i (interpreted as a characteristic wavenumber or number of internal degrees of freedom), a mass parameter m_i, and a damping (or coupling) coefficient r_i. The dynamics among the chambers are designed so that energy injected at one scale is transferred, through the chain of couplings, toward chambers with smaller n_i (a large-scale, or "inverse," cascade), in a manner formally analogous to inverse energy cascade phenomena.

(a) Determine whether a mechanism of this type can be made to faithfully describe energy cascades occurring in real (viscous, three-dimensional) hydrodynamics.

(b) Decide whether one can explicitly choose the parameters {n_i}, {m_i}, {r_i} so that the apparatus actually exhibits the intended cascade behavior, and exhibit such a choice if it exists.

(c) Establish a rigorous link between such a mechanical device and a heat-engine-type model, in particular constructing an analogue of Maxwell's demon within this framework.

(d) Most importantly, construct an analogue of this mechanism within the dynamics of a two-dimensional ideal (Euler) incompressible fluid on a bounded domain or torus, and use it to give a mathematically rigorous mechanism producing inverse energy cascade in 2D ideal hydrodynamics.

Consider deterministic compartmental epidemic models with standard incidence, a linear birth term b(N)=Λ N (Λ>0), one susceptible compartment S, one removed/immunized compartment R, and an n-dimensional vector I=(I_1,…,I_n) of disease compartments. The dynamics in the SIR-PH framework are specified by:

• a sub-generator matrix A∈ℝ^{n×n} (the PH transition matrix between infectious phases, with A1≤0),
• a nonnegative matrix B∈ℝ^{n×n} encoding the forces of infection generated by each infectious phase,
• a nonnegative vector δ∈ℝ^n of disease-induced mortality rates,
• constants γ_r≥0 (loss of immunity rate) and γ_s≥0 (vaccination rate from S to R),
• a probability vector α (initial distribution among infectious phases at infection).

Writing N=S+R+1·I and scaling variables (s,i,r)=(S/N,I/N,R/N), one obtains a system of ODEs of the form (3.5):

ds/dt = Λ(1−s) − s(αᵀ·B i) + γ_r r − γ_s s + Φ_s · s(δᵀ i),
di/dt = α s(αᵀ·B i) (rewriting with B) + Aᵀ i − Λ i + Φ_i · i(δᵀ i) − δ∘i terms,
dr/dt = γ_s s − γ_r r − Λ r − (−A1)ᵀ_recov i + Φ_r · r(δᵀ i),

where Φ_s,Φ_i,Φ_r∈{0,1} are switches. Define three submodels:
(SM) scaled model: Φ_s=Φ_i=Φ_r=1,
(FA) first approximation: Φ_s=Φ_i=Φ_r=0,
(IA) intermediate approximation: Φ_s=Φ_r=1, Φ_i=0.

Let R_0 denote the basic reproduction number computed by the next-generation method from this system. A biologically feasible endemic equilibrium is a fixed point (s*,i*,r*) of the chosen submodel with s*,r*≥0, i*>0 componentwise, and s*+r*+1·i*≤1 (or =1 after scaling).

Question. For each of the three classes SM, FA, and IA, does the condition R_0>1 always imply the existence and uniqueness of a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium with positive disease components, for every admissible choice of parameters (Λ, A, B, δ, γ_r, γ_s, α) and every dimension n≥1?

representations.normalized:
Consider a SIR-PH epidemic model defined as follows. Let the population be split into a susceptible compartment $S$, a vector of "disease" (infectious/exposed) compartments $\mathbf{I}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ governed by a phase-type structure, and a removed compartment $R$. The disease compartments follow $\dot{\mathbf{I}} = (\boldsymbol{\beta}^\top \mathbf{I})\,S\,\boldsymbol{\alpha} + \mathbf{I}^\top A$, where $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ with $\sum_i\alpha_i=1$ is the initial distribution among disease states, $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ is a vector of infection rates, and $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is a sub-generator (Markovian transition matrix among disease states with absorption). The full SIR-PH system also incorporates:
- a linear birth rate (constant inflow into $S$),
- natural mortality at rate $\mu>0$ for every compartment,
- vaccination of susceptibles (transferring mass into $R$) and loss of immunity (transferring mass from $R$ into $S$),
- disease-induced mortality from the $\mathbf{I}$ compartments (an extra removal rate vector $\boldsymbol{\nu}\ge 0$),
- vaccination-induced mortality.

Define the basic reproduction number $R_0$ via the next-generation matrix construction of van den Driessche and Watmough applied to this model. A disease-free equilibrium (DFE) is an equilibrium with $\mathbf{I}=0$; an endemic equilibrium (EE) is an equilibrium with $\mathbf{I}\ne 0$ whose coordinates are biologically feasible (all non-negative).

Consider also two simplifications used in the literature:
- The SIR-PH-FA approximation, in which the total population is replaced by its equilibrium value in the force-of-infection term (frequency-dependent transmission with fixed total population $N$).
- The SIR-PH-IA approximation, an "incidence approximation" obtained by linearizing certain mass-action terms around the DFE.

Question. Is the following statement true: for every SIR-PH model (and likewise for every SIR-PH-FA and SIR-PH-IA approximation) with parameters as above, whenever $R_0>1$ and a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium exists, that endemic equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture that $R_0>1$ implies local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium for SIR-PH models (and their FA/IA approximations) is stated explicitly as an open problem. It has been verified in numerous special cases via Routh–Hurwitz or Lyapunov methods, but no general proof or counterexample appears to have been published; subsequent literature on SIR-PH models still treats it as conjectural.

representations.normalized:
Consider the following compartmental epidemic model with susceptibles $s$, exposed $e$, infectious $i$, and removed $r$ compartments, governed by the ODE system

$$\begin{aligned}
 s' &= \Lambda - \beta_i\, s\, i - (\Lambda + \gamma_s)\, s + \gamma_r\, r,\\
 e' &= \beta_i\, s\, i - (\Lambda + \gamma_e)\, e,\\
 i' &= \gamma_e\, e - (\Lambda + \gamma + \delta)\, i,\\
 r' &= \gamma\, i + \gamma_s\, s - (\Lambda + \gamma_r)\, r,
\end{aligned}$$

with parameters $\Lambda>0$ (linear birth rate, also acting as natural death rate), $\beta_i>0$ (infection rate from $i$), $\gamma_e>0$ (progression rate from $e$ to $i$), $\gamma>0$ (recovery rate), $\delta\ge 0$ (disease-induced death rate), $\gamma_s\ge 0$ (vaccination rate of susceptibles), and $\gamma_r\ge 0$ (loss of immunity rate). Define
$$R = \frac{\beta_i\, \gamma_e}{(\Lambda+\gamma_e)(\Lambda+\gamma+\delta)}, \qquad s_{\rm dfe} = \frac{\Lambda}{\Lambda+\gamma_s}, \qquad R_0 = s_{\rm dfe}\, R.$$

The disease-free equilibrium (DFE) is the equilibrium with $e=i=0$. It is known to be locally asymptotically stable when $R_0<1$, and globally asymptotically stable when $R\le 1$ (via, e.g., the Lyapunov function $V(e,i)=\gamma_e\, e+(\gamma_e+\Lambda)\, i$).

Question: In the parameter regime $R_0<1<R$, is the disease-free equilibrium globally asymptotically stable on the biologically relevant invariant region? If so, exhibit a Lyapunov function (in the variables $s,e,i,r$) yielding the most effective proof of global asymptotic stability.
