Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $f \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_d$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d \ge 1$.

Define the Waring rank $R_V(f)$ to be the minimal integer $r$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_1$ with
$$ f = \ell_1^d + \ell_2^d + \cdots + \ell_r^d. $$
Define the Chow rank $R_{Ch}(f)$ to be the minimal integer $s$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_{i,j} \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_1$ ($1\le i\le s,\,1\le j\le d$) with
$$ f = \sum_{i=1}^{s} \prod_{j=1}^{d} \ell_{i,j}. $$

The border Waring rank $\underline{R}_V(f)$ is the smallest $r$ such that $f$ lies in the Zariski closure of the set of degree-$d$ forms of Waring rank at most $r$; equivalently, the smallest $r$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_i(\varepsilon)$ depending polynomially on $\varepsilon$ with
$$ f = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \sum_{i=1}^{r} \ell_i(\varepsilon)^d $$
(or, equivalently, $\varepsilon^N f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{r} \ell_i(\varepsilon,x)^d$ modulo $\varepsilon^{N+1}$ for some $N$). The border Chow rank $\underline{R}_{Ch}(f)$ is defined analogously, replacing $d$-th powers $\ell_i^d$ by products $\prod_{j=1}^{d}\ell_{i,j}$.

Let
$$ \mathcal{V}_{\text{Waring}} = \{\,f : \underline{R}_V(f) < \infty \text{ with bound polynomial in the input size}\,\}, \qquad \mathcal{V}_{\text{Chow}} = \{\,f : \underline{R}_{Ch}(f) < \infty \text{ with bound polynomial in the input size}\,\} $$
be the corresponding complexity classes of polynomial sequences with polynomially bounded border Waring rank and border Chow rank, respectively.

(a) Determine whether $\mathcal{V}_{\text{Waring}} \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\text{Chow}}$.

(b) More modestly, prove non-trivial upper bounds for $\underline{R}_V(f)$ in terms of $\underline{R}_{Ch}(f)$ (or vice versa) for an arbitrary degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomial $f$.

representations.normalized:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and let $r \ge 1$. Consider the space $V^{\otimes d}$ (or, more generally, the affine space of tensors/polynomials computed by width-$r$ algebraic branching programs over $V$). An algebraic branching program (ABP) of width $r$ computing a polynomial $f$ is a directed acyclic layered graph with a source and a sink, in which each edge is labelled by an affine linear form in the variables of $V$ and each internal layer has at most $r$ vertices; the polynomial computed is the sum over source-to-sink paths of the product of the edge labels. Equivalently, width-$r$ ABPs of length $d$ compute the (1,1)-entry of an iterated product $A_1 A_2 \cdots A_d$ of $r \times r$ matrices whose entries are affine linear forms.

Define the variety
$$\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V} \;:=\; \overline{\{\, f \in \mathrm{Sym}^d V^* : f \text{ is computed by some width-}r \text{ ABP over } V\,\}} \;\subseteq\; \mathrm{Sym}^d V^*,$$
where the closure is taken in the Zariski topology. The group $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ acts naturally on $\mathrm{Sym}^d V^*$, and the coordinate ring $\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}]$ decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-modules indexed by partitions $\lambda$, with multiplicities $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$.

A representation-theoretic obstruction to a polynomial $g \in \mathrm{Sym}^d V^*$ lying in $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ is a partition $\lambda$ such that the multiplicity of the irreducible $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-module $S_\lambda V^*$ in the coordinate ring of the $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-orbit closure of $g$ strictly exceeds $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$.

Problem. Develop and carry out the geometric complexity theory (GCT) program for the variety $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$: determine, or give effectively computable bounds on, the multiplicities $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$ for all partitions $\lambda$, and use these to exhibit representation-theoretic obstructions separating explicit polynomial families (such as the permanent or other hard polynomials) from $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ for suitable values of $r$.

The GCT program for the iterated matrix multiplication / small-width ABP variety remains an active open research direction. Geometric and representation-theoretic properties of IMM have been investigated (e.g. its symmetry group, dual variety, and Jacobian loci), and occurrence obstructions have been studied — with the Occurrence Obstruction Conjecture for permanent vs. determinant having been refuted, in part via results showing that partitions occurring in the IMM coordinate ring also occur for the permanent. However, no full implementation of the GCT obstruction framework for $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ yielding super-polynomial VP vs. VNP-type lower bounds is known.

Let Γ = (V, E) be a finite simple graph with vertex set V = {1, …, n} and edge set E. Fix a bond dimension m_e ∈ ℕ for each edge e ∈ E and a local (physical) dimension d_v ∈ ℕ for each vertex v ∈ V. For each vertex v, let H_v = ℂ^{d_v} and for each edge e ∈ E incident to v, let B_{v,e} = ℂ^{m_e}. Form the vector space
   A_v = H_v ⊗ ⨂_{e ∋ v} B_{v,e}.
A tensor T_v ∈ A_v at each vertex v can be contracted along the edges of Γ: for each edge e = {u, v} ∈ E, pair the tensor factor B_{u,e} = ℂ^{m_e} with B_{v,e} = ℂ^{m_e} via the standard bilinear pairing. The contraction yields a tensor
   κ_Γ(T_1, …, T_n) ∈ H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n.
The tensor network variety TNS^Γ_{m,n} is defined as the Zariski closure in H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n of the image of the contraction map
   κ_Γ : A_1 × ⋯ × A_n → H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n,  (T_1, …, T_n) ↦ κ_Γ(T_1, …, T_n).

Problem. Determine an explicit system of polynomial equations defining the variety TNS^Γ_{m,n} as a subvariety of H_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ H_n. If necessary, restrict attention to specific classes of graphs Γ (for example, cycles, trees, or regular lattices) and/or to particular assignments of the bond dimensions (m_e)_{e ∈ E} and local dimensions (d_v)_{v ∈ V}.

Fix integers $d, D \geq 2$ and $n \geq 1$. For matrices $A_1, \dots, A_d \in \mathrm{Mat}_{D \times D}(\mathbb{C})$, define the uniform (translation-invariant) matrix product state with periodic boundary conditions as the tensor
$$T(A_1,\dots,A_d) \;=\; \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_n=1}^{d} \operatorname{tr}(A_{i_1} A_{i_2} \cdots A_{i_n})\, e_{i_1} \otimes e_{i_2} \otimes \cdots \otimes e_{i_n} \;\in\; (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes n},$$
where $\{e_1,\dots,e_d\}$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{C}^d$. Let $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n} \subseteq (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes n}$ denote the Zariski closure of the image of the map $(A_1,\dots,A_d) \mapsto T(A_1,\dots,A_d)$, viewed as an algebraic variety.

Recall that the trace algebra is the ring of $\mathrm{GL}_D$-invariant polynomial functions on $\mathrm{Mat}_{D\times D}(\mathbb{C})^{\oplus d}$ under simultaneous conjugation, generated by traces of words in the matrices $A_1,\dots,A_d$ (by results of Procesi and Sibirskii), with relations described by the trace ideal.

Problem: Investigate the geometry of the variety $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n}$ — including its dimension, singular locus, identifiability properties, and ideal of defining equations — and develop systematic methods, based on the structure of the trace algebra and the relations among trace monomials, for producing families of polynomial equations vanishing on $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n}$.

Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and let $T \in \mathbb{F}^{n_1} \otimes \mathbb{F}^{n_2} \otimes \mathbb{F}^{n_3}$ be a 3-tensor. The subrank $Q(T)$ is defined as the largest integer $r$ such that the diagonal tensor $\langle r \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^{r} e_i \otimes e_i \otimes e_i$ can be obtained from $T$ by applying linear maps to each of the three factors; equivalently, $Q(T) \geq r$ iff there exist linear maps $A_j : \mathbb{F}^{n_j} \to \mathbb{F}^r$ ($j=1,2,3$) such that $(A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes A_3)(T) = \langle r \rangle$. The border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ is the largest $r$ such that $\langle r \rangle$ lies in the Zariski closure of the orbit $\{(A_1 \otimes A_2 \otimes A_3)(T) : A_j \in \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb{F}^{n_j}, \mathbb{F}^r)\}$ (working over an algebraically closed field, or in the corresponding topological sense over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$).

Known upper bounds on $Q(T)$ and $\underline{Q}(T)$ typically proceed indirectly: one bounds the subrank from above by another rank-type invariant of $T$ (for example, by the slice rank, analytic rank, geometric rank, partition rank, G-stable rank, or similar quantities) which is itself easier to control.

Problem: Develop a genuinely intrinsic method for proving upper bounds on the subrank $Q(T)$ and the border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ of a tensor $T$ that does not proceed by first upper-bounding $Q(T)$ or $\underline{Q}(T)$ by another rank notion of $T$.

Let $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ be a $d$-way tensor over the complex numbers. The subrank $Q(T)$ is the largest integer $r$ such that the diagonal tensor $\langle r \rangle := \sum_{i=1}^r e_i^{\otimes d}$ can be obtained from $T$ by applying linear maps $A_1, \ldots, A_d : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^r$ in each tensor factor, i.e., $(A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d)\, T = \langle r \rangle$. The border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ is the largest integer $r$ such that $\langle r \rangle$ lies in the Euclidean (equivalently Zariski) closure of the set of tensors obtainable from $T$ in this way; equivalently, $\underline{Q}(T) \geq r$ if there exist families of linear maps $A_i(\varepsilon)$ depending polynomially on $\varepsilon$ with $\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0}(A_1(\varepsilon) \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d(\varepsilon))\,T = \langle r \rangle$.

(a) Determine the exact value of the border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ for a generic tensor $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$, as a function of $n$ and $d$.

(b) Give explicit (algebraic or geometric) conditions on a tensor $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ that characterize when $\underline{Q}(T)$ is strictly greater than this generic value.

Background and setup. Consider the n-qubit Hilbert space (ℂ²)^⊗n. The (pure) stabilizer states are the states obtained from |0⟩^⊗n by applying elements of the Clifford group; equivalently, they are the joint +1-eigenstates of maximal abelian subgroups of the n-qubit Pauli group (up to phases). The (exact) stabilizer rank χ(|ψ⟩) of a state |ψ⟩ ∈ (ℂ²)^⊗n is the smallest integer r such that there exist stabilizer states |s_1⟩, …, |s_r⟩ and complex coefficients c_1, …, c_r with
   |ψ⟩ = Σ_{i=1}^{r} c_i |s_i⟩.

The magic state is |T⟩ = cos(π/8)|0⟩ + e^{iπ/4} sin(π/8)|1⟩, and the n-fold tensor product |T⟩^⊗n is the canonical family used to study stabilizer rank.

Problem. Exhibit an explicit family of n-qubit quantum states |ψ_n⟩ (for example |T⟩^⊗n) and prove that
   χ(|ψ_n⟩) = ω(n),
i.e., establish a super-linear lower bound on the exact stabilizer rank of an explicit sequence of n-qubit states.

Let $n\ge 1$ and consider the $n$-qubit Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_n=(\mathbb{C}^2)^{\otimes n}$. A stabilizer state in $\mathcal{H}_n$ is a unit vector (up to scalar) of the form $U|0\rangle^{\otimes n}$ where $U$ is an element of the $n$-qubit Clifford group; equivalently, it is a joint eigenvector of a maximal abelian subgroup of the Pauli group on $n$ qubits. Denote by $\mathrm{Stab}_n\subset\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{H}_n)$ the (finite) set of stabilizer states. For a vector $v\in\mathcal{H}_n$, the stabilizer rank of $v$ is
$$\chi(v)=\min\Bigl\{r\;:\;v=\sum_{i=1}^r c_i\,s_i,\ c_i\in\mathbb{C},\ s_i\in\mathrm{Stab}_n\Bigr\}.$$

Now fix a degree $d\ge 1$ and consider instead the space $S^d\mathbb{C}^m$ of symmetric tensors of order $d$ on $\mathbb{C}^m$, embedded in the appropriate $n$-qubit (or qudit) tensor space via the standard symmetrization. Define the generic stabilizer rank
$$\mathrm{stabR}_d := \min\bigl\{r\;:\; \text{a generic point of } S^d\mathbb{C}^m \text{ lies in the linear span of } r \text{ stabilizer states}\bigr\},$$
i.e. the least integer $r$ such that the $r$-th secant-like variety obtained as the linear span of $r$ stabilizer states fills (a Zariski-dense subset of) the symmetric space.

Problem. Establish non-trivial lower bounds on $\mathrm{stabR}_d$ as a function of $d$ (and $m$); in particular, prove a lower bound that grows faster than any bound obtainable from elementary dimension-counting arguments.

Consider the following two information-theoretic privacy settings.

(1) Private Read-Update-Write (PRUW). A data-storage system consists of N non-colluding databases, each storing M submodels (sections) of equal size L over a finite field. A user wishes to (a) download exactly one chosen submodel indexed by θ ∈ {1,...,M}, (b) compute a local update to that submodel, and (c) upload the update back so that the corresponding stored submodel is correctly modified, while every other stored submodel is unchanged. The privacy requirement is that, from the queries, answers, and uploaded symbols observed by any single database, no information is revealed about the index θ or about the values of the downloaded and uploaded symbols. Define the reading cost D as the expected number of bits downloaded per database normalized by L, the writing cost U as the expected number of bits uploaded per database normalized by L, and the total communication cost as C = D + U.

(2) PSU-based Federated Submodel Learning (FSL). A central server stores a model partitioned into M submodels. In each training round, a set of clients each selects a private subset of submodels to update. Using a combination of Private Set Union (PSU) and Symmetric Private Information Retrieval (SPIR), the protocol must ensure that the server learns only the union (or the aggregate of updates over that union) of the submodels collectively updated by the clients, and nothing about any individual client's chosen subset or its specific contribution; clients similarly learn nothing about the other clients' selections. Define analogous per-round communication costs (download + upload, normalized appropriately).

Problem. Establish tight converse (impossibility) bounds on the achievable reading cost, writing cost, and total communication cost for PRUW, and on the analogous communication costs for PSU-based FSL, that match the best known achievable schemes. Equivalently, determine the capacity (the infimum of the total normalized communication cost over all valid schemes) of PRUW and of PSU-based FSL.

Consider a distributed storage system consisting of N non-colluding servers, each storing (coded) copies of a database organized into M sections (submodels). A client wishes to perform a private read-update-write (PRUW) operation: in each round the client (i) downloads the content of a chosen section θ ∈ {1,…,M}, (ii) computes an update, and (iii) writes the update back to section θ, while satisfying:

  (R1) Private reading: each individual server learns nothing about θ from the queries used to read.
  (R2) Private writing: each individual server learns nothing about θ from the uploaded update, and learns nothing about the value of the update itself.
  (R3) Storage consistency: after the write, the stored database equals the previous database with section θ replaced by its updated value.

In the federated submodel learning (FSL) variant, multiple clients participate; the scheme is additionally required to satisfy client-side privacy via private set union (PSU) combined with symmetric PIR (SPIR): the servers should learn only the union of submodel indices updated by the set of clients (or the aggregate of updates to those submodels), and nothing about any individual client's chosen index or update.

Now introduce adversarial parties: a subset A of up to a (out of N) servers may be Byzantine, returning arbitrarily corrupted responses and arbitrarily deviating from the protocol, and an external eavesdropper may observe the transmissions to/from up to e servers. 

Problem: Design PRUW schemes, and PSU+SPIR–based private FSL schemes, that simultaneously
  (a) preserve properties (R1)–(R3) (and, for FSL, client-side privacy as above) against any T-subset of colluding honest-but-curious servers,
  (b) allow the client(s) to correctly recover the desired reads and produce correct updates to the database despite the actions of any a Byzantine servers,
  (c) guarantee that an eavesdropper observing any e of the communication links learns nothing (in the information-theoretic sense) about θ, the read content, or the update,
and characterize the optimal read and write communication rates (capacities) of such schemes as functions of (N, T, a, e, M).

Setup. Consider a distributed storage system in which a database is replicated (or coded) across $N$ non-colluding servers. Each server stores a model partitioned into $M$ disjoint sections (submodels). A single-client Private Read-Update-Write (PRUW) protocol allows a client to (i) privately download the contents of a chosen section $\theta \in \{1,\dots,M\}$, (ii) compute an update locally, and (iii) upload the update back to the same section, subject to the following requirements:
- Privacy: no server (or any allowed colluding subset) learns the index $\theta$ of the section read or written.
- Security: no server learns the values downloaded or the values of the update uploaded.
- Correctness: after the protocol, the chosen section is correctly updated at all servers, and the client correctly recovers the requested section's contents.

The communication cost is measured as the total number of symbols exchanged between the client(s) and the servers per unit of information read/written.

Problem. Generalize the PRUW model to a multi-client setting in which $K \geq 2$ clients simultaneously interact with the $N$ servers. Concretely, design a protocol satisfying:
1. Each client $k \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ privately reads from a chosen section $\theta_k$ and privately writes an update to that section, with the same privacy, security, and correctness guarantees as in the single-client PRUW model (extended to apply jointly to the group of clients, so that the multi-set $\{\theta_1,\dots,\theta_K\}$ and all update/read values remain hidden from any non-colluding subset of servers).
2. The protocol combines (aggregates or jointly encodes) queries, answers, and/or updates across the $K$ clients so as to achieve a strictly smaller total communication cost (per client, or in aggregate) than $K$ independent executions of the best known single-client PRUW protocol.

Determine whether such a multi-client PRUW protocol exists, and characterize the optimal achievable read and write communication costs as functions of $N$, $M$, and $K$ (and any colluding parameters).

Setup. Consider a federated submodel learning (FSL) system in which a global machine learning model is partitioned into M disjoint submodels W_1, …, W_M, each W_i consisting of L parameters taking values in a finite field F_q. The submodels are stored across N non-colluding databases using a (possibly coded) storage scheme. Users participate in training as follows: a user with locally available training data relevant to a subset S ⊆ {1, …, M} of the submodels wishes to (a) download the current values of all submodels W_i for i ∈ S (the read phase) and (b) upload an additive update Δ_i ∈ F_q^L to each W_i for i ∈ S so that the storage is updated to W_i + Δ_i (the write phase).

Privacy requirement (Private Read–Update–Write, PRUW). The protocol must guarantee that, from the messages exchanged with any single database, the database learns nothing (in the information-theoretic sense) about: (i) the index set S of submodels the user accesses, and (ii) the values of the uploaded updates {Δ_i : i ∈ S}.

Cost. Let C_read(|S|) and C_write(|S|) denote, respectively, the total number of symbols of F_q downloaded and uploaded by the user during the read and write phases of a PRUW protocol that serves a request of size |S|. Let C_PRUW^single denote the read+write communication cost of the best known PRUW protocol that handles a single submodel (|S| = 1).

Question. Does there exist a PRUW protocol that, when used by a single user to read and update |S| submodels simultaneously, achieves total read+write communication cost strictly less than |S| · C_PRUW^single — i.e., strictly less than the cost of running the single-submodel PRUW protocol |S| separate times — while still satisfying the information-theoretic privacy requirements above? Equivalently, characterize the optimal per-submodel communication rate (or capacity region) for simultaneous PRUW of |S| submodels and determine whether it improves upon the |S|-fold repetition baseline.

Existing PRUW literature (communication-efficient PRUW with/without sparsification, rate–distortion tradeoffs, heterogeneous databases, storage-constrained databases) all addresses the single-submodel-per-user setting. No published work was found that designs or characterizes the capacity of simultaneous PRUW for a user requesting multiple submodels at once, so the question of whether this beats |S|-fold repetition appears to remain open.

Consider the problem of Private Read–Update–Write (PRUW) in federated learning / federated submodel learning with top-r sparsification, defined as follows. A model consisting of M submodels is stored, in a coded fashion, across N non-colluding databases. In each round, a client (i) downloads (reads) a fraction r' of the parameters of one desired submodel — the "most significant" parameters according to a sparsification rule — and (ii) uploads (writes) updates to a fraction r of the parameters of that submodel. Communication cost is measured by the read rate R_R = L/D and write rate R_W = L/U, where L is the number of symbols of useful information, and D, U are the total numbers of symbols downloaded and uploaded per round, respectively.

In the standard information-theoretic privacy formulation, the mutual information between (a) the index of the desired submodel, (b) the indices (positions) of the sparse parameters/updates, and (c) the values of those updates, on one side, and all information observed by any individual database, on the other side, is required to be exactly zero. Existing rate–privacy–storage tradeoffs only relax the zero-leakage requirement on the indices of the sparse updates, which has limited impact on the communication rate.

Problem: Formulate and characterize the rate–privacy tradeoff for PRUW with top-r sparsification when privacy is relaxed via a differential-privacy-style constraint that simultaneously permits a prescribed amount of information leakage about (1) the index of the desired submodel, (2) the indices of the selected sparse parameters/updates, and (3) the values of the selected updates/parameters. Specifically, determine the optimal achievable read and write communication rates (R_R, R_W) as functions of the allowed leakage parameters (e.g., (ε, δ)-DP budgets or analogous mutual-information bounds) for each of the three categories of information, and exhibit explicit schemes attaining these rates.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Existing work on PRUW with sparsification addresses information-theoretic privacy and a rate–distortion or rate–privacy–storage tradeoff that allows leakage only on the indices of sparse updates. No published result was found that characterizes the rate–privacy tradeoff under a differential-privacy-style relaxation permitting leakage on the desired submodel index and the values of selected updates/parameters; this is posed as a future research direction and appears unresolved.

Consider a private epidemiological data collection system involving three classes of parties: a set of users, a set of N non-colluding databases, and a single data collector. The system stores epidemiological records distributed across the N databases. The protocol proceeds in rounds with two phases:

(Reading phase.) The data collector privately retrieves aggregated information from the databases concerning a chosen statistic, without revealing to any single database which statistic is being queried.

(Writing phase.) Each user privately uploads an update (e.g., an individual epidemiological record or an update to a stored value) to a chosen section/index of the distributed storage across the N databases, in such a way that no single database learns
 (a) the index of the section that is being updated, nor
 (b) the value of the update being written.

For one round of the writing phase, define the writing cost (the users' upload cost) as the total number of symbols (normalized by the size L of one section's update vector, as L → ∞) that the users must transmit to the N databases in order to perform one private update while satisfying the above privacy constraints together with the correctness constraint that, after the writing phase, each database stores the correct (updated) function of the section's contents.

Problem. Determine the information-theoretically optimal (minimum achievable) writing cost in this three-party private epidemiological data collection setting, as a function of the number of databases N and the relevant storage/code parameters, and exhibit a scheme that attains this minimum together with a matching converse.

Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth manifold of dimension at least $2$, and let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ denote the space of real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $M$, endowed with its natural Polish topology. Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$; this defines an equivalence relation $E_{\mathrm{tc}}$ on $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$.

(a) Does there exist a classification of the elements of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants? More precisely, is there a Polish (or standard Borel) space $Y$ and a Borel map $\Phi \colon \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M) \to Y$ such that $\Phi(f) = \Phi(g)$ if and only if $f$ and $g$ are topologically conjugate?

(b) Is the equivalence relation $E_{\mathrm{tc}}$ a Borel subset of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M) \times \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$?
representations.original:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth manifold of dimension at least $2$, and let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ denote the space of real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $M$, endowed with its natural Polish topology. Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$; this defines an equivalence relation $E_{\mathrm{tc}}$ on $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$.

(a) Does there exist a classification of the elements of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants? More precisely, is there a Polish (or standard Borel) space $Y$ and a Borel map $\Phi \colon \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M) \to Y$ such that $\Phi(f) = \Phi(g)$ if and only if $f$ and $g$ are topologically conjugate?

(b) Is the equivalence relation $E_{\mathrm{tc}}$ a Borel subset of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M) \times \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Anti-classification results in the smooth category (Foreman–Gorodetski and Foreman–Weiss) show that for closed manifolds of dimension ≥ 2 the topological/measure-isomorphism conjugacy relation on smooth diffeomorphisms is not Borel. In the real-analytic category, Banerjee–Kunde extended such anti-classification (for measure-isomorphism) to real-analytic diffeomorphisms of the 2-torus, and Goncharuk obtained anti-classification results for real-analytic flows on the 2-torus. However, the question for topological conjugacy on $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)$ for general closed manifolds $M$ with $\dim M \ge 2$ does not appear to be fully settled in the literature.

Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ denote the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ ($r\ge 1$), endowed with the $C^r$ topology (a Polish space). A diffeomorphism $f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ is called Kupka–Smale if (i) every periodic point of $f$ is hyperbolic, and (ii) for every pair of periodic points $p,q$ of $f$, the stable manifold $W^s(p)$ and the unstable manifold $W^u(q)$ intersect transversely. Let $\mathrm{KS}(M)\subset\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ denote the set of Kupka–Smale diffeomorphisms, with the induced Polish topology. Define the topological conjugacy relation on $\mathrm{KS}(M)$ by
$$f\sim_{\mathrm{top}} g \iff \exists\,h\in\mathrm{Homeo}(M)\ \text{with}\ h\circ f = g\circ h.$$

Answer the following:
(a) Does there exist a complete classification of $(\mathrm{KS}(M),\sim_{\mathrm{top}})$ by Borel-measurable invariants taking values in a standard Borel space — i.e., a Borel map $\Phi:\mathrm{KS}(M)\to X$ into a standard Borel space $X$ such that $f\sim_{\mathrm{top}} g$ if and only if $\Phi(f)=\Phi(g)$?
(b) Is $\sim_{\mathrm{top}}$, viewed as a subset of $\mathrm{KS}(M)\times\mathrm{KS}(M)$, a Borel set?

status_assertions.value: open_status:partially_solved

Recent anti-classification work shows that on closed manifolds of dimension at least 5, topological conjugacy on $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is not a Borel equivalence relation, suggesting strong obstructions to a Borel classification by complete invariants. However, the question as posed specifically for the Kupka–Smale subspace (and for low-dimensional manifolds) does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature, so it remains at least partially open.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with $\dim M \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$ denote the space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $M$, equipped with the $C^\infty$ topology (a Polish space). Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$; this defines an equivalence relation $\sim_{tc}$ on $\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$. An equivalence relation $E$ on a Polish space $X$ is called Borel if $E \subseteq X \times X$ is a Borel subset of the product.

Question: Does there exist a subset $U \subseteq \mathrm{Diff}^\infty(M)$ which is either open and dense, or a dense $G_\delta$ set, such that the restriction of $\sim_{tc}$ to $U$ (viewed as a subset of $U \times U$) is Borel?

Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$-diffeomorphisms of $M$. A diffeomorphism $f\in\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is said to satisfy Smale's Axiom A if its non-wandering set $\Omega(f)$ is hyperbolic and the periodic points of $f$ are dense in $\Omega(f)$. Two diffeomorphisms $f,g\in\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h\colon M\to M$ with $h\circ f = g\circ h$. This determines an equivalence relation $\cong_{TC}$ on the Borel subset $A(M)\subseteq\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ of Axiom A diffeomorphisms.

Determine the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the equivalence relation $\cong_{TC}$ on $A(M)$ in the sense of Borel reducibility: in particular, locate this equivalence relation within the hierarchy of Borel/analytic equivalence relations (e.g., whether it is Borel, classifiable by countable structures, reducible to an orbit equivalence relation of a Polish group action, or universal among such relations).

Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ (with the $C^\infty$ topology). A diffeomorphism $f \in \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is called structurally stable if there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $f$ in $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ such that for every $g \in U$ there is a homeomorphism $h : M \to M$ with $h \circ f = g \circ h$. Two diffeomorphisms $f, g \in \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ are topologically conjugate, written $f \sim_{\mathrm{top}} g$, if there exists a homeomorphism $h : M \to M$ such that $h \circ f = g \circ h$.

Let
$$C = \{ f \in \mathrm{Diff}(M) : f \text{ is topologically conjugate to some structurally stable diffeomorphism} \},$$
and let $E$ denote the equivalence relation $\sim_{\mathrm{top}}$ restricted to $C \times C$.

Recall that an equivalence relation $E$ on a standard Borel space $X$ is Borel reducible to equality on a standard Borel space $Y$ (written $E \leq_B {=}_Y$) if there is a Borel function $\varphi : X \to Y$ such that for all $x, x' \in X$, $x\, E\, x'$ if and only if $\varphi(x) = \varphi(x')$.

Question: Is $E$ Borel reducible to equality?

Let $C$ denote the Cantor space (a compact, metrizable, totally disconnected, perfect topological space). A Cantor dynamical system is a pair $(C,T)$ where $T\colon C\to C$ is a homeomorphism. Such a system is called minimal if every orbit $\{T^n(x):n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in $C$. Two Cantor dynamical systems $(C,T)$ and $(C,S)$ are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h\colon C\to C$ such that $h\circ T=S\circ h$.

The space $H(C)$ of all homeomorphisms of $C$, equipped with the uniform convergence topology, is a Polish space, and the set $M(C)\subseteq H(C)$ of minimal homeomorphisms is a Borel (in fact, $G_\delta$) subset. Topological conjugacy defines an equivalence relation $\sim_c$ on $M(C)$, viewed as a subset of $M(C)\times M(C)$.

Question: Is $\sim_c$ a Borel subset of $M(C)\times M(C)$?

Background and definitions. Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with the discrete topology, and let $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ be the space of bi-infinite sequences over $A$ with the product topology, on which the shift map $\sigma:A^{\mathbb{Z}}\to A^{\mathbb{Z}}$, $\sigma(x)(n)=x(n+1)$, acts as a homeomorphism. A subshift is a nonempty closed subset $X\subseteq A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\sigma(X)=X$. A subshift $X$ is called minimal if it has no proper nonempty closed shift-invariant subset; equivalently, every $\sigma$-orbit in $X$ is dense in $X$. Two subshifts $(X,\sigma)$ and $(Y,\sigma)$ (possibly over different finite alphabets) are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:X\to Y$ with $h\circ\sigma=\sigma\circ h$.

Fix a way of coding minimal subshifts (over varying finite alphabets) as elements of a standard Borel space $\mathcal{M}$ — for example, by coding each minimal subshift via its language, viewed as a closed subset of $\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\bigcup_{n\geq 1}\{1,\dots,k\}^n$. Let $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ be the equivalence relation on $\mathcal{M}$ given by topological conjugacy. Then $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ is a countable Borel equivalence relation.

Recall that a countable Borel equivalence relation $E$ on a standard Borel space $X$ is hyperfinite if $E=\bigcup_n F_n$ where $F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots$ is an increasing sequence of Borel equivalence relations each having finite classes. A countable Borel equivalence relation $E_\infty$ is universal if every countable Borel equivalence relation $F$ Borel reduces to $E_\infty$, i.e., there is a Borel map $f$ with $x\,F\,y\iff f(x)\,E_\infty\,f(y)$.

Question. Is $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ hyperfinite, or is it a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?

Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite set of finite words over $A$. The (two-sided) subshift of finite type determined by $\mathcal{F}$ is the set
$$X_{\mathcal F}=\{x\in A^{\mathbb Z}: \text{no word from }\mathcal F\text{ occurs in }x\},$$
equipped with the product topology and the shift map $\sigma:X_{\mathcal F}\to X_{\mathcal F}$ defined by $(\sigma x)_n=x_{n+1}$. Two such subshifts $(X,\sigma_X)$ and $(Y,\sigma_Y)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:X\to Y$ with $h\circ\sigma_X=\sigma_Y\circ h$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input two finite presentations (i.e., the alphabets $A,B$ and finite forbidden-word lists $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$) of subshifts of finite type $X_{\mathcal F}\subseteq A^{\mathbb Z}$ and $X_{\mathcal G}\subseteq B^{\mathbb Z}$, decides whether $X_{\mathcal F}$ and $X_{\mathcal G}$ are topologically conjugate?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The decidability of topological conjugacy for two-sided one-dimensional subshifts of finite type is a long-standing open problem in symbolic dynamics, prominently listed in Boyle's open-problems survey. Partial results exist: conjugacy is decidable for one-sided SFTs and for tree-shifts of finite type, and "direct conjugacy" via N-block presentations is decidable; the multidimensional case has hardness results. The general two-sided question remains open.

Background. A Borel dynamical system is a pair $(X,T)$ where $X$ is a standard Borel space and $T:X\to X$ is a Borel automorphism. Two Borel systems $(X,T)$ and $(Y,S)$ are said to be almost Borel isomorphic modulo a class $\mathcal N$ of "negligible" invariant Borel sets if there exist invariant Borel sets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$ with $X\setminus X_0,\,Y\setminus Y_0\in\mathcal N$ and a Borel bijection $\phi:X_0\to Y_0$ with $\phi\circ T=S\circ\phi$. For a Borel system, the topological entropy refers to the supremum of Kolmogorov–Sinai (metric) entropies $h_\mu(T)$ taken over all $T$-invariant Borel probability measures $\mu$, and the metric entropy refers to $h_\mu(T)$ for a specified invariant measure class.

There is a known almost Borel classification theorem for sufficiently regular (e.g.\ smooth) dynamical systems in which one discards sets that are universally null (negligible for every invariant probability measure) and the invariant under consideration is the topological entropy; this classification realizes such systems, up to almost Borel isomorphism, as universal models built from Bernoulli shifts of prescribed entropies.

Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, modulo equality $\mu$-almost everywhere, endowed with the weak topology. A transformation $T \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ is called a $K$-automorphism if there exists a sub-$\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{K} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ such that $T\mathcal{K} \supseteq \mathcal{K}$, $\bigvee_{n\geq 0} T^n\mathcal{K} = \mathcal{B}$ (mod $\mu$), and $\bigcap_{n\geq 0} T^{-n}\mathcal{K}$ is the trivial $\sigma$-algebra. Let $K \subseteq \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ be the set of $K$-automorphisms; it is a Borel subset. Define the measure-isomorphism equivalence relation $\cong$ on $K$ by $S \cong T$ if and only if there exists $\varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ with $\varphi S \varphi^{-1} = T$.

(a) Is the equivalence relation $\cong$ on $K$ a Borel subset of $K \times K$?

(b) Is $\cong\!\upharpoonright\! K$ Borel reducible to an action of $S_\infty$ (the Polish group of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$)? That is, does there exist a Borel function $f: K \to Y$, where $Y$ is a standard Borel $S_\infty$-space, such that $S \cong T$ if and only if $f(S)$ and $f(T)$ lie in the same $S_\infty$-orbit?

Let $([0,1], \lambda)$ denote the unit interval equipped with Lebesgue measure. Let $\mathrm{MPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ be the Polish group of (equivalence classes mod null sets of) invertible measure-preserving transformations of $([0,1],\lambda)$, endowed with the weak topology, and let $\mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda) \subseteq \mathrm{MPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ be the subset of ergodic transformations. Two transformations $S, T \in \mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ are said to be measure-isomorphic, written $S \cong T$, if there exists $\varphi \in \mathrm{MPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ such that $\varphi \circ S = T \circ \varphi$ almost everywhere; this defines an analytic equivalence relation on $\mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda)$.

Recall that for analytic equivalence relations $E$ on a Polish space $X$ and $F$ on a Polish space $Y$, $E$ is Borel reducible to $F$, written $E \le_B F$, if there exists a Borel map $f \colon X \to Y$ such that $x \mathrel{E} x' \iff f(x) \mathrel{F} f(x')$. The relations $E$ and $F$ are Borel bi-reducible, $E \sim_B F$, when $E \le_B F$ and $F \le_B E$. An equivalence relation is called a maximal (or universal) orbit equivalence relation induced by a Polish group action if every orbit equivalence relation arising from a continuous action of a Polish group on a Polish space Borel reduces to it; such a maximal relation exists and is unique up to Borel bi-reducibility (e.g., realized by the action of the homeomorphism group of $[0,1]^{\mathbb{N}}$ on a suitable space).

Question: Is the measure-isomorphism equivalence relation on $\mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ Borel bi-reducible with the maximal orbit equivalence relation induced by a Polish group action?

Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish space of ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, equipped with the weak topology. Two transformations $T,S \in \mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if there exist measurable sets $A \subseteq X$ (positive measure, $T$-sweeping out) and $B \subseteq X$ (positive measure, $S$-sweeping out) such that the induced transformations $T_A$ and $S_B$ are measure-theoretically isomorphic (equivalently, $T$ and $S$ have measurably isomorphic suspension flows up to a time change). This defines an analytic equivalence relation $E_K$ on $\mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$.

Recall the framework of Borel reducibility: for analytic equivalence relations $E$ on a Polish space $X$ and $F$ on a Polish space $Y$, one writes $E \leq_B F$ if there is a Borel function $f : X \to Y$ such that $x E x' \iff f(x) F f(x')$. An equivalence relation $E$ is said to be classifiable by an $S_\infty$-action (where $S_\infty$ is the Polish group of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$) if $E \leq_B F$ for some orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of $S_\infty$ on a Polish space; equivalently, $E$ is Borel reducible to the isomorphism relation on countable structures in some countable language.

Determine the precise location of the Kakutani equivalence relation $E_K$ in the Borel-reducibility hierarchy of analytic equivalence relations. In particular, decide whether $E_K$ is Borel reducible to an orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of $S_\infty$.

For a continuous self-map $f : X \to X$ of a compact metric space, the topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$ is defined in the usual way. A topological factor of $(X,f)$ is a pair $(Y,g)$ with $g : Y \to Y$ continuous on a compact metric space together with a continuous surjection $\pi : X \to Y$ satisfying $\pi \circ f = g \circ \pi$. The factor is called trivial if $|Y| = 1$. The map $f$ is said to have completely positive entropy if every non-trivial topological factor of $(X,f)$ has strictly positive topological entropy.

Define
$$\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n) := \{ f \in C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n) : f \text{ has completely positive entropy} \}.$$

Determine the descriptive set-theoretic complexity of $\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n)$ as a subset of the Polish space $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n)$. In particular, locate this set precisely within the Borel/projective hierarchy (e.g., determine whether it is Borel, and if not, whether it is complete coanalytic).

Such a measure $\mu$ is said to be fully supported if $\operatorname{supp}(\mu) = \mathbb{T}^2$.

Question: Is it true that for every smooth topologically mixing map $f \in C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^2, \mathbb{T}^2)$, every measure of maximal entropy of $f$ is fully supported?

Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, endowed with the weak topology. Two transformations $T,S\in\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if there exist measurable sets $A,B\subseteq X$ of positive measure such that the induced transformation $T_A$ on $A$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to the induced transformation $S_B$ on $B$ (where $T_A(x)$ is defined as $T^{n(x)}(x)$ with $n(x)$ the first return time of $x$ to $A$, and analogously for $S_B$). This defines an equivalence relation $\mathcal{K}$ on $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ whose equivalence classes are called Kakutani equivalence classes.

(a) For which (if any) Kakutani equivalence classes $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}\subseteq\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ is $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}$ a Borel subset of $\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$?

(b) Whenever such a class is Borel, determine the descriptive set-theoretic complexity of the measure-theoretic isomorphism equivalence relation $\cong$ (where $T\cong S$ iff there exists $\varphi\in\mathrm{MPT}(X,\mu)$ with $\varphi T=S\varphi$) restricted to $[T]_{\mathcal{K}}$, in the sense of Borel reducibility among Borel/analytic equivalence relations.

Let $X$ be the Polish space of continuous actions of $F_2$ on the Cantor space (equivalently, the space of pairs of homeomorphisms of the Cantor space, with the topology inherited from the homeomorphism group). For each action $\alpha \in X$ and each $\alpha$-invariant Borel probability measure, one obtains a measure-preserving action of $F_2$ on a standard probability space. Call an action $\alpha \in X$ "Bernoulli-isomorphic" if there exists an $\alpha$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ such that the measure-preserving system $(\alpha, \mu)$ is measure-theoretically isomorphic to some Bernoulli shift action of $F_2$ on a standard probability space $(K^{F_2}, \nu^{F_2})$.

Let $X = \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Z}^2}$ with the natural shift action of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, and let $X_2 \subseteq X$ denote the free part of this action (i.e. the Borel set of points with trivial stabilizer). Write $\sigma$ for the restricted $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action on $X_2$. Let $X_H \subseteq (\mathbb{Z}^2)^{\mathbb{Z}}$ denote the Polish space of directed bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$, i.e. bijections $p:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $p(n+1)-p(n)$ is a unit vector for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$; equip $X_H$ with the natural $\mathbb{Z}^2$-action by translation (shifting the image by a vector in $\mathbb{Z}^2$), also denoted $\sigma$.

Assume there exists a Borel $\mathbb{Z}^2$-equivariant map $\Phi : (X_2,\sigma) \to (X_H,\sigma)$. Such a map induces a Borel $\mathbb{Z}$-action $T_\Phi$ on $X_2$ defined by following the Hamiltonian path: for $x\in X_2$, $T_\Phi(x) = \sigma_{v(x)}(x)$, where $v(x) = \Phi(x)(1)-\Phi(x)(0) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$. Every $\sigma$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $X_2$ is then $T_\Phi$-invariant, and ergodicity is preserved. Let $M_e$ denote the set of ergodic $\sigma$-invariant Borel probability measures on $X_2$.

Question: Can $\Phi$ be chosen so that for all $\mu,\nu \in M_e$, the measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^2$-systems $(X_2,\mu,\sigma)$ and $(X_2,\nu,\sigma)$ are measurably conjugate if and only if the measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}$-systems $(X_2,\mu,T_\Phi)$ and $(X_2,\nu,T_\Phi)$ are measurably conjugate?

Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard atomless probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving automorphisms of $(X,\mu)$ modulo equality almost everywhere, equipped with the weak topology. Consider the conjugation action of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ on itself, $(g,h)\mapsto g h g^{-1}$, and let $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ be the orbit equivalence relation it induces on $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$.

Recall that for Borel equivalence relations $E$ and $F$ on standard Borel spaces $Y$ and $Z$, $E$ is Borel reducible to $F$ (written $E\le_B F$) if there is a Borel map $f:Y\to Z$ such that $y_1\mathbin{E}y_2 \iff f(y_1)\mathbin{F}f(y_2)$. An orbit equivalence relation $F$ (induced by a Borel action of a Polish group on a standard Borel space) is called a complete orbit equivalence relation if $E\le_B F$ for every orbit equivalence relation $E$ arising from a Borel action of a Polish group on a standard Borel space.

Question: Is $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ a complete orbit equivalence relation?

Consider the conjugacy equivalence relations
- $\sim_{\mathrm{Aut}}$ on $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$: $S \sim_{\mathrm{Aut}} T$ iff there exists $R \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ with $RSR^{-1} = T$;

Question: Does $\sim_{\mathrm{Aut}}$ Borel reduce to $\sim_{[T_0]}$? That is, is there a Borel map $f:\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu) \to [T_0]$ with $S \sim_{\mathrm{Aut}} T \iff f(S) \sim_{[T_0]} f(T)$? Does the analogous Borel reducibility hold when both relations are restricted to ergodic transformations?

Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard atomless probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving automorphisms of $(X,\mu)$ (modulo null sets), equipped with the weak topology. The group $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ acts on itself by conjugation: $g\cdot T = gTg^{-1}$.

Recall the following notion (due to Allison and Panagiotopoulos): a continuous action of a Polish group $G$ on a Polish space $Y$ is called \emph{unbalanced} if there is no Borel-definable way to assign, in a $G$-invariant manner, points of a Polish space carrying a Polish group action with a compatible bi-invariant metric; more precisely, the orbit equivalence relation $E^Y_G$ is not Borel reducible to any orbit equivalence relation induced by a continuous action of a Polish group admitting a compatible two-sided invariant metric. (Equivalently, the action exhibits a generic "unbalanced" dynamical obstruction in the sense of the games-orbits-play framework.)

Questions:
(a) Is the conjugation action of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ on itself unbalanced?
(b) If yes, does this remain true when the action is restricted to the set of ergodic measure-preserving transformations (which is a $G_\delta$ invariant subset of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$)?

Let $G$ be a Polish group (a topological group whose underlying space is separable and completely metrizable) acting continuously on a compact Polish space $X$. Define the topological full group of this action to be the group of all homeomorphisms $h \colon X \to X$ for which there exists an open cover $X = U_1 \cup \cdots \cup U_n$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $h(x) = g_i \cdot x$ for every $x \in U_i$ and every $i$; equip this group with its natural Polish group topology.

Recall that a subset $A$ of a topological group $H$ is coarsely bounded (in the sense of Rosendal) if $A$ has finite diameter with respect to every continuous left-invariant pseudometric on $H$, equivalently, if every continuous isometric action of $H$ on a metric space has bounded $A$-orbits. The group $H$ itself is called coarsely bounded if $H$ is a coarsely bounded subset of itself.

Investigate the structure of the topological full groups arising in this way, with special emphasis on the case $G = \mathbb{R}$:

1. Characterize when such a topological full group is coarsely bounded.
2. Characterize when such a topological full group admits a dense finitely generated subgroup.
3. Determine, up to isomorphism, how many topological full groups arise in this manner.
4. Provide a classification of the continuous actions by homeomorphisms of such topological full groups on compact Polish spaces.

Let $(I,\lambda)$ denote the unit interval equipped with Lebesgue measure, and for each integer $n\ge 1$ let $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ denote the $n$-dimensional torus equipped with Lebesgue measure. Denote by $\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$ the standard Borel space of Lebesgue measure-preserving automorphisms of $I$ that have finite Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, and by $\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ the standard Borel space of $C^\infty$ Lebesgue measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^n$.

Does there exist a Borel measurable map
$$G:\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)\;\longrightarrow\;\bigsqcup_{n\ge 1}\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$$
such that for every $T\in\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$, if $G(T)\in\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ then the measure-preserving systems $(I,\lambda,T)$ and $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n,G(T))$ are measure-theoretically isomorphic?

The question, attributed to F. Rodriguez Hertz, concerns a Borel-uniform version of the smooth realization problem. The general smooth realization problem for finite-entropy systems is a well-known open problem in ergodic theory, and no Borel selector of the kind asked for appears in the literature. Searches reveal only partial smooth realization results (e.g., Gerber–Katok pseudo-Anosov constructions, slow-entropy realizations for commuting transformations) but no resolution of this Borel-map version.

Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ be an invertible measure-preserving dynamical system on a standard probability space. Recall:

- Two measure-preserving systems $(X,\mu,T)$ and $(Y,\nu,S)$ are said to be *measure isomorphic* if there exist full-measure invariant subsets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$ and a measurable bijection $\phi:X_0\to Y_0$ with $\phi_*\mu=\nu$ and $\phi\circ T=S\circ\phi$ on $X_0$.
- Two systems are *Kakutani equivalent* if each is measure isomorphic to a measurable induced (first-return) transformation of the other on some positive-measure subset; equivalently, they admit isomorphic suspension flows up to time change.
- A measure-preserving system $(X,\mu,T)$ is said to be *smoothly realizable on the torus* (isomorphically) if there exist $d\geq 1$, a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $f:\mathbb{T}^d\to\mathbb{T}^d$, and an $f$-invariant Borel probability measure $\nu$ on $\mathbb{T}^d$ such that $(\mathbb{T}^d,\nu,f)$ is measure isomorphic to $(X,\mu,T)$.
- It is said to be *Kakutani realizable on the torus* if such an $f$ exists with $(\mathbb{T}^d,\nu,f)$ Kakutani equivalent to $(X,\mu,T)$.

Question: If a measure-preserving dynamical system on a standard probability space is Kakutani realizable by a smooth diffeomorphism of some torus equipped with an invariant Borel probability measure, must it also be isomorphically realizable by a smooth diffeomorphism of some torus with an invariant Borel probability measure?

Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group and let $F \curvearrowright (X,\mu)$ be a measure-preserving action on a standard probability space, i.e., a Borel action of $F$ on a standard Borel space $X$ preserving a Borel probability measure $\mu$. A topological model of this action is a continuous action $F \curvearrowright Y$ on a compact metrizable space $Y$ together with an $F$-invariant Borel probability measure $
u$ on $Y$ such that the systems $(X,\mu,F)$ and $(Y,
u,F)$ are measurably isomorphic. The topological model $(Y,F)$ is called uniquely ergodic if $
u$ is the unique $F$-invariant Borel probability measure on $Y$.

Question: Does every measure-preserving action of a free group on a standard probability space admit a uniquely ergodic topological model?

Work in the setting of Borel dynamics. A Borel dynamical system is a pair (X,T) where X is a standard Borel space and T:X→X is a Borel automorphism. For an invariant Borel probability measure μ on (X,T), let h_μ(T) denote the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. A Borel system (Y,S) is said to embed into (X,T) on a μ-full set if there is a Borel injection π:Y'→X, defined on a T-invariant Borel set Y'⊆Y with μ(Y')=1, that conjugates S|_{Y'} to T|_{π(Y')}.

Following Hochman, call a free Borel system (X,T) universal if for every free Borel system (Y,S) and every S-invariant ergodic Borel probability measure μ on Y with h_μ(S) strictly less than the Borel entropy h(X,T) := sup{h_ν(T) : ν an ergodic T-invariant Borel probability measure on X}, the system (Y,S) embeds into (X,T) on a μ-full set. More generally, for t∈(0,∞], call (X,T) t-universal if it is free, carries no ergodic invariant measure of entropy ≥t, and contains an s-universal subsystem for every s<t.

Problem. Characterize, as broadly as possible, the families of Borel (respectively topological or smooth) dynamical systems that are universal in this sense. In particular, identify natural dynamical, geometric, or combinatorial properties (e.g., specification-type conditions, hyperbolicity, partial hyperbolicity, expansiveness) that imply universality, and determine which classes of systems—beyond mixing shifts of finite type, mixing sofic shifts, mixing positive-recurrent countable-state Markov chains, β-shifts, synchronized subshifts, and Axiom A diffeomorphisms restricted to their basic sets—are universal.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is a broad research program in Borel/topological dynamics initiated by Hochman (building on Krieger's generator theorem). Universality has been established for several specific classes (mixing SFTs, mixing sofic shifts, mixing positive-recurrent countable-state Markov chains, β-shifts, synchronized subshifts, Axiom A diffeomorphisms; also systems with the weak specification property, by Burguet and others). However, a complete characterization of which families are universal remains open, with ongoing research extending universality to broader classes.

For a real number $R \geq 1$, let $B(R) = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : \|x\| \leq R\}$ denote the closed disc of radius $R$ centered at the origin in the Euclidean plane, and define
$$N(R) = \#\{\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : \lambda \in B(R)\},$$
the number of integer lattice points contained in $B(R)$. The area of $B(R)$ equals $\pi R^2$. Define the error term
$$E(R) = N(R) - \pi R^2.$$
Prove or disprove: for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$$E(R) = O_\varepsilon\!\left(R^{1/2 + \varepsilon}\right) \quad \text{as } R \to \infty.$$
Equivalently, show that the discrepancy between the lattice-point count and the area of the disc is bounded, up to arbitrarily small power factors, by the square-root scale $R^{1/2}$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Hardy's conjecture for the Gauss circle problem remains a famous open problem. The best known upper bound on the error term, due to Huxley (2003), is $O(R^{131/208+\varepsilon})$ with $131/208 \approx 0.6298$, far from the conjectured $1/2$. The conjectured lower bound exponent of $1/2$ matches known $\Omega$-results (Hardy, Soundararajan) up to log factors, but the upper bound remains unproved.

Let $B(R)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:\|x\|\le R\}$ and let $\mathcal{L}(R)=\mathbb{Z}^2\cap\{x:|\,\|x\|-R\,|\le \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\}$ be the set of integer lattice points lying in the closed annulus of width $\sqrt2$ centered on the circle of radius $R$. Order the points of $\mathcal{L}(R)$ as $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{K(R)}$ by increasing polar angle (with indices taken cyclically modulo $K(R)$), where $K(R)=|\mathcal{L}(R)|$. For each lattice point $\lambda$, let $A_R(\lambda)$ denote the area of the intersection of $B(R)$ with the closed unit square centered at $\lambda$ (with sides parallel to the coordinate axes).

For each fixed integer $k\ge 1$, define the limiting correlation (assumed to exist)
$$C_k \;=\; \lim_{R\to\infty}\frac{1}{K(R)}\sum_{j=1}^{K(R)}\Bigl(A_R(\lambda_j)\,A_R(\lambda_{j+k})-\tfrac{1}{4}\Bigr).$$

Prove or disprove: $\displaystyle\lim_{k\to\infty} C_k = 0.$

For $R>0$ and $\lambda>0$, consider the annulus $\mathcal{A}_R(\lambda) := \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : R^2 \leq |x|^2 \leq R^2 + \sqrt{\lambda}\}$, and for each lattice point $v \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ define the rescaled intersection area
$$A_R(\lambda; v) := \mathrm{Area}\bigl((v + [-1/2,1/2]^2) \cap \mathcal{A}_R(\lambda)\bigr) \cdot (\text{normalization})$$
so that $A_R(\lambda_j)$ records, in a fixed normalization, the area of intersection between a unit square centred at a lattice point of squared norm $\lambda_j$ and a thin annular strip of radius $\sim R$.

Define the random-model object $A_\infty(r,\theta)$ as the area of intersection between the unit square $[-1/2,1/2]^2$ and the half-plane region cut out by the line at signed perpendicular distance $r$ from its centre at angle $\theta$ (i.e., $\{x \in [-1/2,1/2]^2 : x\cdot(\cos\theta,\sin\theta) \leq r\}$).

Let $(r,\theta,r')$ be uniformly distributed on $[-1/\sqrt 2, 1/\sqrt 2] \times [0,2\pi) \times [-1/\sqrt 2, 1/\sqrt 2]$, and set
$$(Y_1, Y_2) := \bigl(A_\infty(r,\theta),\, A_\infty(r',\theta)\bigr).$$

Let $\theta \in [0, 2\pi)$ be a fixed angle and let $r \in \mathbb{R}$ be a shift parameter. Consider the tilted-and-shifted semi-infinite rectangle
$$R_{r,\theta} = \{(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : (x,y) = r\,(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) + s\,(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) + t\,(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta),\ s \geq 0,\ t \in [-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}]\},$$
i.e. an infinite strip of width $\sqrt{2}$ along the direction $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, starting at the offset $r$ along that direction. Enumerate the lattice points $\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \dots$ of $\mathbb{Z}^2 \cap R_{r,\theta}$ in increasing order of their projection $\langle \kappa_\ell, (\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\rangle$ onto the long side of the rectangle. Let
$$p_\ell(r,\theta) = \langle \kappa_\ell, (-\sin\theta, \cos\theta)\rangle \in I := [-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}]$$
denote the projection of $\kappa_\ell$ onto the short side.

It is known that for a set of $\theta$ of full measure (those whose direction is badly approximable by rationals), the sequence $\{p_\ell(r,\theta)\}_{\ell}$ is equidistributed in $I$ on average over $\ell$.

Problem. For generic $\theta$, prove (or disprove) equidistribution of $p_\ell(r,\theta)$ in $I$ without averaging over the index $\ell$, by instead exploiting averaging over the shift parameter $r$. Concretely: show that for almost every $\theta$, there exists a set of shifts $r$ of full density along which, for each fixed $\ell$, the values $p_\ell(r,\theta)$ become equidistributed in $I$ as $r$ varies.

Let $R \geq 2$ be a large real parameter and consider the thin annulus
$$\Gamma_R = \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : R - 1 \leq |x| \leq R + 1 \}.$$
For each lattice point $\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \cap \Gamma_R$, write its polar coordinates as $\lambda = (|\lambda|\cos\theta_\lambda, |\lambda|\sin\theta_\lambda)$, and set $r_\lambda = |\lambda| - R$ (the signed radial distance to the circle of radius $R$).

For an interval $I \subset [-1,1]$ and an arc $[c,d] \subset \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ of length $|d - c|$, define
$$N(R; I, [c,d]) = \#\{ \lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \cap \Gamma_R : \theta_\lambda \bmod 2\pi \in [c,d],\ r_\lambda \in I \}.$$
It is known that an asymptotic formula
$$N(R; I, [c,d]) \sim \frac{|d-c|\,|I|}{2\pi} \cdot R \qquad (R \to \infty)$$
holds uniformly in such intervals provided the sector length satisfies $|d-c| \geq R^{-1/2+o(1)}$ (equivalently, the arclength on the circle is at least $R^{1/2+o(1)}$).

Problem: Establish the same asymptotic for a wider range of shorter sector lengths $|d - c|$, i.e., extend the asymptotic to $|d-c| \geq R^{-1/2 - \delta}$ for some $\delta > 0$ (or as far below the threshold $R^{-1/2}$ as possible).

$$s^+(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i^2, \qquad s^-(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i < 0} \lambda_i^2.$$

(a) Prove or disprove: if $G$ is connected, then
$$\min\{s^+(G),\, s^-(G)\} \;\geq\; n - 1.$$

(b) (Stronger form.) Prove or disprove: if $G$ is an arbitrary graph having exactly $\kappa$ connected components, then
$$\min\{s^+(G),\, s^-(G)\} \;\geq\; n - \kappa.$$

The conjecture remains open in general. It has been verified for several graph classes (bipartite, regular, complete multipartite, line/claw-free graphs, graphs with small order after blow-up). Recent partial progress includes Shengtong Zhang's 2024 result establishing $\min\{s^+(G), s^-(G)\} \geq n - \gamma(G) \geq n/2$ (where $\gamma$ is the domination number), and a 2025 preprint resolving the claw-free case via a "gluing lemma". The inequality is the Elphick–Wocjan conjecture (2018), a spectral strengthening of Turán's theorem. It has been verified for several classes (triangle-free graphs, weakly perfect graphs, Kneser graphs, conference graphs, certain strongly regular and Ramanujan graphs, and almost all graphs), and no counterexamples have been found computationally up to 40 vertices, but the conjecture remains open in general as of recent works (2024–2025).

Let H be a 3-uniform hypergraph on n vertices, i.e., V(H) is a finite set of size n and E(H) is a collection of 3-element subsets of V(H). The shadow (2-section) of H is the simple graph G on the same vertex set V(H) in which two distinct vertices u,v are adjacent if and only if {u,v} is contained in some edge of H. Call H planar if its shadow graph is planar.

The spectral radius ρ(H) of H is defined as the spectral radius of its adjacency tensor A(H), namely the largest value λ for which there exists a nonnegative, nonzero vector x ∈ R^n with (A(H) x^2)_i = λ x_i^2 for every i ∈ V(H), where (A(H) x^2)_i = Σ_{{i,j,k} ∈ E(H)} 2 x_j x_k.

For graphs F and G on disjoint vertex sets, the join F ∨ G is the graph obtained from the disjoint union of F and G by adding every edge between V(F) and V(G). Let K_2 denote the complete graph on 2 vertices and P_{n-2} the path on n-2 vertices. Let H* denote the unique 3-uniform hypergraph on n vertices whose shadow equals K_2 ∨ P_{n-2} and whose edge set consists of all triples {u,v,w} ⊆ V that span a triangle in K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}.

Prove or disprove: there exists n_0 such that for every integer n ≥ n_0, among all planar 3-uniform hypergraphs on n vertices, H* is the unique hypergraph attaining the maximum value of ρ(·).

The spectral radius ρ(H) of H is defined as the spectral radius of its adjacency tensor A(H), namely the largest value λ for which there exists a nonnegative, nonzero vector x ∈ R^n with (A(H) x^2)_i = λ x_i^2 for every i ∈ V(H), where (A(H) x^2)_i = Σ_{{i,j,k} ∈ E(H)} 2 x_j x_k.

For graphs F and G on disjoint vertex sets, the join F ∨ G is the graph obtained from the disjoint union of F and G by adding every edge between V(F) and V(G). Let K_2 denote the complete graph on 2 vertices and P_{n-2} the path on n-2 vertices. Let H* denote the unique 3-uniform hypergraph on n vertices whose shadow equals K_2 ∨ P_{n-2} and whose edge set consists of all triples {u,v,w} ⊆ V that span a triangle in K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}.

Prove or disprove: there exists n_0 such that for every integer n ≥ n_0, among all planar 3-uniform hypergraphs on n vertices, H* is the unique hypergraph attaining the maximum value of ρ(·).

Let G be a finite, simple, connected graph on n ≥ 2 vertices with minimum degree δ. The toughness of G is defined by
  t(G) = min { |S| / c(G − S) : S ⊆ V(G), c(G − S) ≥ 2 },
where c(H) denotes the number of connected components of a graph H, and the minimum is over all vertex subsets S whose removal disconnects G (with t(G) = +∞ for complete graphs). Let L(G) = D(G) − A(G) be the Laplacian matrix of G, where D(G) is the diagonal degree matrix and A(G) is the adjacency matrix, and let its eigenvalues be ordered as
  μ_1 ≥ μ_2 ≥ … ≥ μ_{n−1} ≥ μ_n = 0.

Prove or disprove: for every such connected non-complete graph G,
  t(G) ≥ μ_{n−1} / (μ_1 − δ).

Background and definitions.

A graph $F$ is called color-critical if there exists an edge $e \in E(F)$ such that $\chi(F-e) < \chi(F)$, where $\chi$ denotes the chromatic number. For an integer $r \ge 2$ and an integer $n \ge r$, let $T_{n,r}$ denote the Turán graph: the complete $r$-partite graph on $n$ vertices whose part sizes differ by at most one. Write $t_r(n) = e(T_{n,r})$.

Mubayi's theorem (supersaturation form). Let $F$ be a color-critical graph with $\chi(F) = r+1 \ge 3$. There exists $n_0 = n_0(F)$ such that for every integer $q$ with $1 \le q \le n/2$ and every $n \ge n_0$, every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with
$$e(G) \ge t_r(n) - q + 1$$
contains at least $q \cdot c(F,n)$ copies of $F$, where $c(F,n)$ denotes the minimum number of copies of $F$ that an edge of $T_{n,r}$ can be added to obtain (the standard Mubayi counting function). Equality is achieved by adding $q-1$ edges inside one part of $T_{n,r}$.

Let $\lambda(G)$ denote the spectral radius (largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix) of a graph $G$.

Problem.

(i) (General spectral Mubayi.) Establish a spectral analogue of Mubayi's theorem. Specifically, for a color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F) = r+1 \ge 3$, determine the smallest function $\phi(F,n,q)$ such that for every integer $q$ with $1 \le q \le n/2$ and every sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with
$$\lambda(G) \ge \lambda(T_{n,r}) - \phi(F,n,q)$$
contains at least $q \cdot c(F,n)$ copies of $F$, and characterize the extremal graphs.

(ii) (Critical case $q=1$.) For each of the following specific color-critical graphs $F$, determine the sharp threshold $\lambda^\ast(F,n)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\lambda(G) > \lambda^\ast(F,n)$ contains strictly more copies of $F$ than the minimum supersaturation count (equivalently, more than $c(F,n)$ copies), and identify all extremal graphs:
  (a) $F$ is the triangle $K_3$;
  (b) $F$ is a clique $K_{r+1}$ with $r \ge 3$;
  (c) $F$ is a book $B_k$ (the graph consisting of $k$ triangles sharing a common edge);
  (d) $F$ is an odd cycle $C_{2k+1}$ with $k \ge 2$;
  (e) $F$ is an even wheel $W_{2k}$ (the join of a vertex with $C_{2k}$).

Significant progress has been made. A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a finite simple graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a function called a signature (or edge signing). The adjacency matrix $A(G,\sigma)$ of $(G,\sigma)$ is the symmetric $|V|\times|V|$ matrix with entries $A(G,\sigma)_{uv}=\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise. The spectral radius $\rho(G,\sigma)$ is the largest absolute value of an eigenvalue of $A(G,\sigma)$.

Let $G$ be a nontrivial graph (i.e., having at least one edge) with maximum degree $\Delta$. Does there always exist a signature $\sigma:E(G)\to\{+1,-1\}$ such that
$$\rho(G,\sigma) < 2\sqrt{\Delta-1}\,?$$

For a subset $U \subseteq \{0,1\}^d$, let $Q_d[U]$ denote the subgraph of $Q_d$ induced by $U$, and let $\lambda_1(Q_d[U])$ denote its largest eigenvalue (i.e., the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix). For each integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le 2^d$, determine
$$f(d,m) := \max\{\lambda_1(Q_d[U]) : U \subseteq \{0,1\}^d,\ |U| = m\}.$$
That is, find a closed-form expression (or sharp characterization) for the maximum possible largest eigenvalue of an induced subgraph of $Q_d$ on exactly $m$ vertices, together with the extremal sets $U$ achieving this maximum.

The problem (attributed to Fink, with a weaker form by Friedman–Tillich) appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: Bollobás and Lee showed that for an induced subgraph on $n \le d$ vertices with $n \ge 105$, the largest eigenvalue is at most $\sqrt{n-1}$, achieved by stars; and Hamming balls of radius $o(d)$ achieve a largest eigenvalue within $1+o(1)$ of the conjectured maximum. Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices with edge set $E(G)$, and let $e(G)=|E(G)|$. Denote by $\mu_1(G)\ge\mu_2(G)\ge\cdots\ge\mu_n(G)=0$ the eigenvalues of the Laplacian matrix $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix and $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees. For each integer $k$ with $1\le k\le n$, set
$$S_k(G)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mu_i(G).$$

For integers $k\ge 1$, $r\ge 1$, $s\ge 0$ with $n=k+r+s$, define the graph $G_{k,r,s}$ as follows. Its vertex set is partitioned into three parts: a clique $K_k$ on $k$ vertices, an independent set $I_r$ on $r$ vertices, and an independent set $I_s=\{v_1,\dots,v_s\}$ on $s$ vertices. Every vertex of $I_r$ is adjacent to every vertex of $K_k$, and there are no edges between $I_r$ and $I_s$ nor inside $I_r$ or $I_s$. For each $v_i\in I_s$, its neighborhood $N(v_i)$ is a proper subset of $V(K_k)$, and the neighborhoods are nested: $N(v_{i+1})\subseteq N(v_i)$ for $1\le i\le s-1$.

Prove or disprove: for every graph $G$ of order $n$ and every $k\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}$,
$$S_k(G)\;\le\;e(G)+\binom{k+1}{2},$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong G_{k,r,s}$ for some $r\ge 1$ and $s\ge 0$.

Define the two median eigenvalues of $G$ as $\lambda_H(G) = \lambda_{\lceil n/2 \rceil}(G)$ and $\lambda_L(G) = \lambda_{\lceil (n+1)/2 \rceil}(G)$, and define the HL-index of $G$ by
\[ R(G) = \max\bigl(|\lambda_H(G)|,\ |\lambda_L(G)|\bigr). \]
A graph is called subcubic if every vertex has degree at most $3$, and planar if it can be embedded in the plane without edge crossings.

Prove or disprove: for every planar subcubic graph $G$, one has $R(G) \le 1$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The conjecture (due to Mohar) appears to still be open in general. It is known that R(G) ≤ √2 for every subcubic graph (Mohar), with equality only for the Heawood graph, and recent work has verified Mohar's conjecture for K₄-minor-free subcubic graphs and other sparse subclasses, but the full planar case remains unresolved as of recent (2024–2025) papers.

Let $G$ be a simple connected graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A(G)$. By the Perron–Frobenius theorem, $A(G)$ has a unique (up to positive scaling) positive unit eigenvector $x = (x_1,\dots,x_n)$ associated with its largest eigenvalue; this $x$ is called the principal eigenvector of $G$. Normalize $x$ so that $\|x\|_2 = 1$ (Euclidean unit norm), and define the $\ell_1$-norm of the principal eigenvector by $\|x\|_1 = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i$.

For $n \ge 7$, let $P_{n-3}\cdot K_4$ denote the lollipop graph obtained from a complete graph $K_4$ and a path $P_{n-3}$ on $n-3$ vertices by identifying one endpoint of the path with a single vertex of $K_4$ (so the resulting graph has $n$ vertices and is connected).

Prove or disprove: among all connected graphs on $n$ vertices, the lollipop graph $P_{n-3}\cdot K_4$ uniquely minimizes the $\ell_1$-norm $\|x\|_1$ of its principal eigenvector.

A spherical orbifold is a quotient $S^n/\Gamma$ of the round $n$-sphere $S^n$ (with its standard constant-curvature-$1$ Riemannian metric) by a finite subgroup $\Gamma$ of the isometry group $O(n+1)$, equipped with the induced Riemannian orbifold structure. The Laplace–Beltrami operator on such an orbifold has a discrete spectrum consisting of nonnegative real eigenvalues, each occurring with finite multiplicity. Call two spherical orbifolds eigenvalue equivalent if the underlying sets of distinct Laplace eigenvalues coincide (i.e., they have identical spectra after multiplicities are ignored). The Riemannian volume of $S^n/\Gamma$ is $\mathrm{vol}(S^n)/|\Gamma|$.

Question: Do there exist two spherical orbifolds (in some dimension $n$) that are eigenvalue equivalent in the above sense but have different Riemannian volumes?

representations.normalized:
A spherical orbifold of dimension d is a quotient S^d/Γ, where S^d denotes the unit round sphere in R^{d+1} and Γ is a finite subgroup of the orthogonal group O(d+1) acting on S^d. Two such orbifolds are said to be Laplace-isospectral if the Laplace–Beltrami operators on their smooth parts have the same spectrum (with multiplicities), and they are isometric if there is a volume- and metric-preserving bijection between them; equivalently, S^d/Γ and S^d/Γ' are isometric iff Γ and Γ' are conjugate in O(d+1). The volume of S^d/Γ equals vol(S^d)/|Γ|.

For each integer d ≥ 2, determine
   V(d) := sup { vol(S^d/Γ) : there exist finite subgroups Γ, Γ' ⊂ O(d+1) such that S^d/Γ and S^d/Γ' are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric },
or equivalently, determine the smallest possible order of Γ admitting such an isospectral non-isometric partner in dimension d.

The problem is generally open. It has been conjectured that the largest-volume isospectral non-isometric pairs of spherical space forms are lens spaces, and this conjecture has been verified in dimensions n ≡ 2,3,4,5,6,7 (mod 9). Known constructions yield lower bounds such as vol(S^d)/8 (using almost-conjugate (Z/2Z)^3 subgroups) and vol(S^{2n-1})/11 in infinitely many odd dimensions, but the exact maximum is not known in general.

A Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is determined spectrally by the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of its Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions. Two closed Riemannian manifolds are called Laplace-isospectral if these spectra coincide, and isometric if there exists a smooth distance-preserving bijection between them.

A compact simply connected Riemannian symmetric space is irreducible if it is not isometric to a Riemannian product of two lower-dimensional symmetric spaces. Such spaces are classified by É. Cartan.

Determine the complete list of compact simply connected irreducible Riemannian symmetric spaces $\widetilde M$ with the following property: there exist two closed Riemannian manifolds $M_1$ and $M_2$, both of which are quotients $\widetilde M/\Gamma_i$ by finite groups $\Gamma_i$ of isometries acting freely on $\widetilde M$, such that $M_1$ and $M_2$ are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric.

A spherical space form is a Riemannian manifold of the form $\Gamma\backslash S^n$, where $S^n$ is the unit round sphere of dimension $n$ and $\Gamma$ is a finite subgroup of $O(n+1)$ acting freely on $S^n$ by isometries, equipped with the quotient metric. A lens space is a spherical space form of odd dimension $2m-1$ obtained as $L\backslash S^{2m-1}$ for some cyclic subgroup $L$ of $O(2m)$ acting freely.

Fix a dimension $n \geq 2$. Among all unordered pairs $(M_1, M_2)$ of $n$-dimensional spherical space forms which are isospectral but not isometric, suppose that the common volume $\mathrm{vol}(M_1) = \mathrm{vol}(M_2)$ attains the maximum possible value over all such pairs (assuming such a maximum is attained in dimension $n$).

Question: Must every such volume-maximizing pair consist of two lens spaces?

Let $q\ge 2$ be an integer and let $\varphi$ denote Euler's totient function. A $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens space with fundamental group of order $q$ is the quotient $L = S^{2n-1}/\Gamma$, where $S^{2n-1}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is the unit sphere and $\Gamma\cong\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ acts freely on $S^{2n-1}$ by an isometry of the form $(z_1,\dots,z_n)\mapsto(\zeta^{s_1}z_1,\dots,\zeta^{s_n}z_n)$, where $\zeta = e^{2\pi i/q}$ and $s_1,\dots,s_n$ are integers coprime to $q$. Two such lens spaces are called isospectral if the spectra of their Laplace–Beltrami operators (acting on smooth functions, with multiplicities) coincide, and isometric if there is a Riemannian isometry between them.

Question: Suppose $n\equiv -1\pmod{\varphi(q)/2}$. Does there exist a pair of $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens spaces with fundamental group of order $q$ which are isospectral but not isometric?

Two subgroups $H_1$ and $H_2$ of a compact Lie group $G$ are called almost conjugate (or Gassmann equivalent) if there exists a bijection $\varphi : H_1 \to H_2$ such that for every $h \in H_1$, the element $\varphi(h)$ is conjugate to $h$ in $G$; equivalently, for every conjugacy class $C \subset G$ one has $|C \cap H_1| = |C \cap H_2|$. They are conjugate if there exists $g \in G$ with $g H_1 g^{-1} = H_2$.

Determine, for each of the compact Lie groups $\mathrm{SU}(3)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(2) \cong \mathrm{Spin}(5)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(3)$, and the exceptional group $G_2$, whether it contains a pair of finite subgroups that are almost conjugate but not conjugate.

A compact Riemannian symmetric space is said to be of group type if it is isometric to a compact connected Lie group G equipped with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric (so the isometric symmetric space structure is given by left and right translations).
