A lens space is defined as follows. Fix integers $n\ge 1$ and $q\ge 2$, and choose integers $p_1,\dots,p_n$ coprime to $q$. Let $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/q}$ and let the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ act on the unit sphere $S^{2n-1}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ by
$$k\cdot (z_1,\dots,z_n) = (\zeta^{kp_1}z_1,\dots,\zeta^{kp_n}z_n).$$
This action is free and isometric with respect to the round metric, and the quotient $L(q;p_1,\dots,p_n)=S^{2n-1}/(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$ is a closed Riemannian manifold, called a lens space. Two lens spaces are isospectral if their Laplace–Beltrami operators on functions have the same eigenvalue spectrum (with multiplicities), and they are isometric if they are isometric as Riemannian manifolds. A lens space $L$ is called spectrally unique within the family of lens spaces (of given dimension $2n-1$ and fundamental-group order $q$) if every lens space isospectral to $L$ is in fact isometric to $L$.

Question: Is a generic lens space spectrally unique? That is, does there exist a natural notion of genericity in the parameter family $\{L(q;p_1,\dots,p_n)\}$ such that, for a generic choice of parameters, the lens space $L(q;p_1,\dots,p_n)$ admits no non-isometric isospectral partner among lens spaces?

A spherical space form is a closed Riemannian manifold of the form $S^n/\Gamma$, where $S^n$ is the unit round $n$-sphere and $\Gamma \subset O(n+1)$ is a finite subgroup acting freely on $S^n$, equipped with the metric induced from the round metric on $S^n$. The length spectrum of $(M,g)$ is the set of lengths of all closed geodesics in $M$, counted with appropriate multiplicities. The wave trace is a tempered distribution on $\mathbb{R}$ whose singular support, by the Poisson relation, is contained in the length spectrum of $(M,g) \cup \{0\}$.

Determine the precise relationship between the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum of a spherical space form. In particular, decide to what extent the Laplace spectrum of $S^n/\Gamma$ determines its length spectrum, and to what extent the length spectrum determines (or constrains) the Laplace spectrum. Equivalently, establish whether the Poisson relation is an equality for every spherical space form, i.e. whether the singular support of the wave trace coincides with $\{0\} \cup \{\pm L : L \text{ is the length of a closed geodesic in } S^n/\Gamma\}$.

Let $M$ be a closed (or finite-volume) hyperbolic manifold, i.e. a complete Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Two such manifolds $M_1$ and $M_2$ are said to be:

(a) isospectral if the Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions has the same spectrum (counted with multiplicities) on $M_1$ and on $M_2$;

(b) strongly isospectral if, for every natural elliptic differential operator $D$ that is canonically associated to the Riemannian structure and acts on sections of a natural vector bundle (for example the Hodge Laplacian on $p$-forms for each $p$, the Dirac operator when applicable, or any operator obtained by the Sunada-type construction from a representation of the isometry group of a common Riemannian cover), the spectra of $D$ on $M_1$ and on $M_2$ coincide.

Equivalently, in the locally symmetric setting $M_i = \Gamma_i \backslash \mathbb{H}^n$, strong isospectrality requires that for every finite-dimensional representation $\tau$ of the maximal compact subgroup $K = \mathrm{SO}(n)$ of $G = \mathrm{SO}(n,1)^\circ$, the spectra of the corresponding Bochner-type Laplacian on the bundle $\Gamma_i \backslash (G \times_K V_\tau)$ agree for $i = 1, 2$.

Question: Do there exist a pair of hyperbolic manifolds $M_1, M_2$ that are isospectral in the sense of (a) but not strongly isospectral in the sense of (b)?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

Standard constructions of isospectral hyperbolic manifolds (Sunada's method, Vignéras' arithmetic constructions, Garoufalidis–Reid examples) all produce strongly isospectral pairs, since they yield representation-equivalent subgroups of a common cover. A web search did not surface any construction or proof in the literature producing isospectral hyperbolic manifolds that fail to be strongly isospectral, nor a proof that none exist; the question appears to remain open.

Consider a low-earth-orbit (LEO) mega-constellation of N satellites, each at altitude h, equipped with a phased-array antenna producing K narrow spot beams of half-power beamwidth θ_b and employing a frequency-reuse pattern designed to maximize downlink area spectral efficiency for communications (not geolocation). Let a ground user at position x ∈ R^3 receive signals from the subset S(x) ⊆ {1,…,N} of satellites whose beams illuminate x at a given time, and let the received signal from satellite i carry a known reference waveform from which one can estimate time-of-arrival τ_i, carrier-Doppler f_i, and possibly angle-of-arrival, subject to clock biases and ephemeris uncertainty.

Formulate and analyze a positioning framework for x that simultaneously addresses the following questions:

(a) Signal and beam design. Given that narrow beams and aggressive frequency reuse minimize the number of satellites visible at x at any time and reduce beam overlap, what reference-signal structure, beam-hopping schedule, and frequency-reuse modification (compatible with the communication payload) maximize a localization performance metric such as the position error bound PEB(x) = sqrt(tr(J(x)^{-1})), where J(x) is the equivalent Fisher information matrix derived from {τ_i, f_i} over i ∈ S(x)?

(b) Geometric dilution. Characterize, as a function of beamwidth θ_b and constellation geometry, the minimum number and angular spread of simultaneously visible satellites needed to guarantee PEB(x) ≤ ε for a prescribed ε > 0, and identify constellation/beamforming parameter regimes for which this is achievable without sacrificing communications capacity below a prescribed threshold C_min.

(c) Opportunistic exploitation. When the constellation parameters cannot be altered, devise estimators that exploit communication-only signals (synchronization sequences, pilots, payload structure) to estimate {τ_i, f_i} with quantifiable Cramér–Rao-type bounds, and determine conditions on ephemeris accuracy, clock stability, and multi-epoch fusion under which the resulting localization is consistent and achieves a specified accuracy.

Provide either explicit constructions and achievability results, or impossibility/lower-bound results showing fundamental trade-offs between area spectral efficiency and the attainable localization accuracy.

LEO-based opportunistic positioning using communication mega-constellations (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper) is an active and unresolved research area as of 2026. Multiple recent works propose partial solutions (carrier-Doppler tracking, opportunistic STARLINK signal exploitation, hybrid TDOA/FDOA estimators), but no comprehensive framework jointly optimizing beam design, frequency reuse, and positioning accuracy under communication constraints has been established. The problem is widely cited as open in surveys on 6G NTN localization.

Consider a user equipment (UE) on or near the Earth's surface that wishes to establish a radio link with a low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite belonging to a non-terrestrial cellular network. To successfully close such a link, the UE must compensate for (i) the round-trip propagation delay between itself and the satellite and (ii) the Doppler frequency shift induced by the satellite's high relative velocity; both compensations require knowledge of the UE's approximate geographic position. In current cellular standards this position is supplied by an onboard Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver, but assume that the UE has no GNSS capability and that no other UE-side absolute positioning source is available.

The satellite (or the network) is assumed to know its own ephemeris (position and velocity at every time instant) and can transmit downlink reference signals with known waveforms, timing, and carrier frequency. The UE can measure features of received downlink signals (e.g., received power, time of arrival relative to its local clock, carrier-frequency offset, angle of arrival if it has multiple antennas) from one or more satellites that may pass over it, possibly at different times.

Design and rigorously analyze a standalone radio-access-technology–dependent positioning scheme — i.e., a scheme that uses only such cellular downlink/uplink measurements between the UE and satellites, with no GNSS or other external positioning input — that produces an estimate of the UE position with accuracy sufficient to enable initial timing advance and Doppler pre-compensation, and hence radio-link closure with the non-terrestrial network. In particular:

1. Identify the minimal set of measurements (number of satellites, number of time epochs, types of signal observables) needed for the UE position to be observable, given satellite ephemeris and an unknown UE clock bias and frequency offset.
2. Derive the Cramér–Rao lower bound (or an equivalent fundamental accuracy limit) on UE position estimation as a function of carrier frequency, bandwidth, signal-to-noise ratio, satellite geometry, and the number of observation epochs.
3. Determine the maximum positioning error tolerable for successful initial access (link closure) as a function of the orbital and waveform parameters, and specify regimes in which the proposed scheme meets this tolerance.

The problem of GNSS-free initial-access localization for UEs connecting to LEO-based non-terrestrial networks is an active open research area. 3GPP Release 17/18 NTN specifications still require UEs to report GNSS-derived position for initial access, and recent research papers (2023–2025) on LEO-based positioning, Doppler/delay-based UE localization, and 6G NTN initial access continue to propose partial solutions (e.g., Doppler-only, multi-satellite TDOA/FDOA schemes) but do not provide a fully standardized, validated standalone RAT-dependent positioning method that closes the radio link for GNSS-less UEs.

Consider a single low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite moving along a known orbit, used to verify the position of a ground user equipment (UE) via round-trip-time (RTT) measurements. Model the UE as a point on or near the Earth's surface with unknown horizontal position p ∈ R^2 (altitude assumed known), and let the satellite at the i-th measurement epoch be at known position s_i ∈ R^3, i = 1,…,N. The measurement model is

   r_i = ||s_i − [p; h]|| + c·b + n_i,

where b is an unknown clock-bias term, c the speed of light, and n_i ~ N(0, σ^2) independent Gaussian noise. The position error bound (PEB) is defined as PEB(p) = sqrt(tr(J(p)^{-1})), where J(p) is the Fisher information matrix of the RTT measurement model with respect to p (after marginalising or jointly estimating b). For UEs whose horizontal location lies near the projection of the satellite's orbital ground track, the geometric dilution of precision (GDOP) degenerates and PEB(p) becomes very large, so that although the median PEB over a uniform UE distribution satisfies a 10 km verification accuracy target, the mean PEB and worst-case PEB are an order of magnitude larger.

Design a single-LEO RTT-based positioning and verification procedure—comprising the choice of measurement epochs {t_i}, an estimator p̂ of p, and a verification test deciding whether a claimed location is consistent with the RTT measurements—that meets the following requirements simultaneously:

(i) the median horizontal positioning error over a uniform distribution of UEs on the visible portion of Earth is at most 10 km;

(ii) the fraction of UEs (including those located near the sub-satellite orbital track where GDOP is poor) whose horizontal positioning error exceeds 10 km is bounded by a prescribed small ε > 0;

(iii) the procedure uses only one LEO satellite (no multi-satellite fusion).

Alternatively, prove that no such procedure exists, i.e., establish a fundamental lower bound showing that for any single-LEO RTT estimator the worst-case PEB on a positive-measure set of UE locations must exceed 10 km whenever the median PEB meets the 10 km target.

The problem is posed as an open research question concerning how to mitigate severe outliers in single-LEO RTT-based location verification when geometric dilution of precision is poor. No publication was identified that resolves the question for the strict single-LEO setting; subsequent work on NTN/LEO localization typically proposes multi-LEO or hybrid solutions rather than guaranteeing the worst-case 10 km target with a single satellite.

Consider a low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite equipped with a phased-array antenna capable of forming up to B simultaneous directional beams. At any time t, let C(t) ⊆ {1,…,B} denote the subset of beams currently allocated to communication services within the satellite's nominal ground footprint, and let S(t) = {1,…,B} \ C(t) be the set of currently unused ("spare") beams. The satellite's nominal coverage cell N(t) ⊂ R^2 on the Earth's surface may shrink (for instance, when the satellite passes over a land–ocean boundary, so that the portion of N(t) over land is much smaller than over the ocean), leaving |S(t)| > 0.

Positioning reference signals (PRS) are broadcast waveforms designed so that user equipment (UE) located in a region R can estimate its position by combining time-of-arrival or carrier-phase measurements from multiple satellites. PRS waveforms are decodable at very low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), so a satellite may steer a spare beam from S(t) to illuminate a target ground region T(t) ⊂ R^2 located outside N(t).

Let U(t) ⊂ R^2 denote the set of UEs requesting positioning service at time t. For each UE u ∈ U(t), positioning accuracy depends on the geometric dilution of precision (GDOP) determined by the set of visible satellites currently transmitting PRS toward u, on the per-link SNR (which depends on beam direction, off-boresight angle, atmospheric attenuation, and slant range), and on the PRS bandwidth and integration time.

Design and analyze an opportunistic spare-beam scheduling and beam-pointing policy π that, given the satellite ephemerides, the time-varying spare-beam sets S(t), the spatial distribution of UEs U(t), and the communication-service constraints (so that beams allocated to C(t) are never preempted), assigns to each spare beam in S(t) a pointing direction (i.e. a target region T(t)) and a PRS transmission schedule, with the objectives:

(i) maximizing the expected positioning accuracy (e.g. minimizing the time- and UE-averaged position-error bound, or equivalently maximizing a Fisher-information-based utility) for UEs outside the nominal coverage N(t);
(ii) guaranteeing prescribed PRS coverage and revisit-time bounds at each location in a service area of interest; and
(iii) respecting hardware constraints, including total radiated power, beam-switching latency, and inter-beam interference.

Specifically: (a) formulate this spare-beam PRS scheduling problem as a mathematical optimization (e.g. a mixed-integer or stochastic optimal-control problem), (b) characterize its computational complexity, and (c) provide a policy with provable performance guarantees relative to the offline optimum, or establish fundamental performance limits.

Consider a cellular positioning framework (5G/6G) in which a user equipment (UE) on or near the Earth's surface receives downlink positioning reference signals (PRS) from a constellation of low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellites. Each satellite i has known time-varying position p_i(t) ∈ ℝ^3 and velocity v_i(t) ∈ ℝ^3, and transmits a carrier of nominal frequency f_c. The UE has unknown 3D position x ∈ ℝ^3, unknown clock bias b ∈ ℝ, and unknown carrier frequency offset δ ∈ ℝ. From the received signal of satellite i the UE can in principle measure the instantaneous Doppler shift
   f_i = -(f_c / c) · ⟨v_i − ẋ, (x − p_i)/‖x − p_i‖⟩ + δ + n_i,
where c is the speed of light and n_i is measurement noise. By forming frequency differences f_i − f_j (frequency-difference-of-arrival, FDOA) the unknown δ is eliminated, leaving a system of nonlinear equations in x (and possibly ẋ).

Known facts to be taken as given:
(i) Current cellular positioning signaling supports delay-/time-based observables (e.g., TDOA) but does not natively support Doppler-based observables such as FDOA.
(ii) Accurate 3D position estimation by FDOA alone is generally ill-conditioned unless at least 8 LEO satellites are simultaneously visible to the UE, a condition not always met by realistic LEO constellations.
(iii) The existing PRS waveform does not provide sufficient frequency resolution to estimate f_i with the accuracy needed for FDOA-based 3D localization.

Problem. Design a positioning scheme — comprising (a) a modified or new downlink reference-signal waveform, (b) an associated UE measurement procedure that extracts Doppler observables with quantified frequency resolution, and (c) an estimator that fuses FDOA with available delay-based observables — such that, under realistic LEO visibility (in particular, when fewer than 8 satellites are simultaneously visible), the scheme provides consistent 3D position estimates whose error is bounded in terms of receiver SNR, integration time, ephemeris uncertainty, and constellation geometry. Quantify the trade-offs between Doppler resolution, signaling overhead, and achievable localization accuracy, and prove conditions on the satellite geometry and waveform parameters under which the joint delay+FDOA estimator is identifiable and asymptotically efficient.

(i) Current cellular positioning signaling supports delay-/time-based observables (e.g., TDOA) but does not natively support Doppler-based observables such as FDOA.
(ii) Accurate 3D position estimation by FDOA alone is generally ill-conditioned unless at least 8 LEO satellites are simultaneously visible to the UE, a condition not always met by realistic LEO constellations.
(iii) The existing PRS waveform does not provide sufficient frequency resolution to estimate f_i with the accuracy needed for FDOA-based 3D localization.

Problem. Design a positioning scheme — comprising (a) a modified or new downlink reference-signal waveform, (b) an associated UE measurement procedure that extracts Doppler observables with quantified frequency resolution, and (c) an estimator that fuses FDOA with available delay-based observables — such that, under realistic LEO visibility (in particular, when fewer than 8 satellites are simultaneously visible), the scheme provides consistent 3D position estimates whose error is bounded in terms of receiver SNR, integration time, ephemeris uncertainty, and constellation geometry. Quantify the trade-offs between Doppler resolution, signaling overhead, and achievable localization accuracy, and prove conditions on the satellite geometry and waveform parameters under which the joint delay+FDOA estimator is identifiable and asymptotically efficient.

Standardization of Doppler/FDOA support in 5G/6G PRS is still under active discussion in 3GPP and the research literature; no published work provides a complete, standards-ready solution simultaneously addressing PRS redesign for Doppler resolution, sub-8-satellite 3D FDOA estimation, and integration with delay-based methods. Status appears open.

Consider a cellular positioning system in which a user equipment (UE) estimates its location from downlink positioning reference signals (PRS) transmitted by multiple transmission/reception points (TRPs). In a non-terrestrial-network (NTN) setting, the TRPs are mounted on satellites (e.g., in low Earth orbit), so that (i) propagation delays between the reference TRP and neighboring TRPs differ by amounts spanning multiple OFDM subframes, (ii) line-of-sight relative motion produces large, time-varying Doppler shifts, and (iii) maintaining radio-frequency phase coherence between TRP transmitters and the UE receiver across long observation intervals is nontrivial.

A conventional wideband PRS forces the UE to perform a correlation search over a time window of multiple subframes, which is power-intensive. The problem is to design a new downlink reference-signal scheme, suitable for standardization, with the following requirements:

1. The signal includes narrowband synchronization blocks that are quasi-co-located with the PRS in a deterministic time-frequency pattern, so that the UE can acquire timing and frequency without a wideband multi-subframe search.

2. The signal is a narrowband PRS whose resources are deployed over multiple slots in such a way that the UE can produce reliable Doppler (carrier-frequency-offset / Doppler rate) measurements in addition to time-of-arrival measurements.

3. The TRP transmitter and UE receiver are required to maintain phase coherence across the entire multi-slot transmission of the new narrowband PRS, enabling coherent combining across slots.

Specify the time-frequency resource mapping, sequence design, quasi-co-location structure, and phase-coherence requirements of such a reference signal, and analyze its time-of-arrival, Doppler, and phase-estimation performance (e.g., via Cramér–Rao bounds) under NTN-typical delay, Doppler, and oscillator-stability conditions, demonstrating that it simultaneously satisfies (1)–(3) while improving on a wideband multi-subframe PRS search.

Consider a non-terrestrial wireless network in which a user equipment (UE) on or near the Earth's surface communicates with a constellation of low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites. One satellite, designated the serving satellite, maintains a closed-loop timing- and frequency-compensation procedure with the UE: the UE pre-compensates its uplink (UL) transmissions for the propagation delay τ_s(t) and Doppler shift f_s(t) to the serving satellite so that signals arrive at that satellite aligned with its reference time–frequency grid.

Single-satellite round-trip-time (RTT) positioning estimates the UE position from the two-way time of arrival between the UE and the serving satellite. Multi-RTT positioning generalizes this by also measuring two-way times of arrival to N ≥ 2 additional LEO satellites, where the UE transmits sounding reference signals (SRS) that must be received by each of the satellites with propagation delays τ_i(t) and Doppler shifts f_i(t), i = 1,…,N, that differ from τ_s(t), f_s(t) by amounts which may exceed the tolerable delay spread and frequency offset of the underlying 5G/6G numerology.

Problem. Design a protocol and signaling scheme under which:
(i) for each non-serving satellite i, the UE momentarily adjusts its UL transmit timing by an offset Δτ_i(t) and its UL transmit frequency by an offset Δf_i(t) so that the SRS arrives at satellite i within the cyclic-prefix and subcarrier-spacing tolerances;
(ii) throughout these adjustments, the closed-loop timing- and frequency-compensation loop with the serving satellite remains valid, i.e., the serving link is not lost and subsequent UL transmissions to the serving satellite remain correctly pre-compensated;
(iii) the resulting two-way time-of-arrival measurements to the serving satellite and to the N additional satellites can be combined consistently to estimate the UE position.

Specify the offsets {Δτ_i(t), Δf_i(t)} as functions of the satellite ephemerides and UE state, the scheduling of SRS occasions across satellites, and the procedure for restoring the serving-link compensation, and prove that the resulting joint multi-RTT estimator is well-defined and feasible within standard 5G/6G physical-layer tolerances.

Consider a satellite-based positioning system in which a constellation of moving satellites broadcasts periodic positioning reference signals (PRS) to ground user equipment (UE). Let the satellites be indexed by i = 1, ..., N, with time-dependent positions p_i(t) ∈ R^3 known to a central location management function (LMF). At each time t the LMF supplies the UE with:

(a) assistance information A_i(t) describing the configuration (carrier, bandwidth, PRS sequence parameters, expected time of arrival window, Doppler pre-compensation) of every neighboring satellite i visible from the UE, and
(b) a PRS muting pattern, i.e. a binary schedule M_i(t,k) ∈ {0,1} for each satellite i and each PRS slot/symbol index k, where M_i(t,k)=1 indicates that satellite i is silent in slot k.

A UE attempting to acquire PRS from a distant satellite j experiences interference from nearby satellites; reception is feasible in slot k only if for every nearby interferer i ≠ j the slot k (suitably shifted by the differential propagation delay τ_{ij}(t) = (||p_i(t) - x_UE|| - ||p_j(t) - x_UE||)/c) is muted, i.e. M_i(t, k + ⌊τ_{ij}(t)/T_s⌋) = 1, where T_s is the symbol duration. Because satellites move, the set of nearby/distant satellites and the delays τ_{ij}(t) vary with t, so both A_i(t) and M_i(t,·) must be updated dynamically.

Problem. Design and analyze an update policy for (A_i(t), M_i(t,·))_{i=1}^N, taking the predictable satellite ephemerides as input, such that:

1. For every UE position x_UE in the service region and every time t, the assistance information A_i(t) provided to the UE is consistent with the actual configuration of every satellite i visible from x_UE.

2. For every UE x_UE and every satellite j whose PRS the UE is scheduled to measure, there exist infinitely many PRS slots k in which the interference from all other satellites (after accounting for differential delays τ_{ij}(t)) is muted, so that the PRS from j is decodable; in particular, when PRS instances of multiple satellites overlap, the serving satellite mutes adjacent symbols/slots to absorb the larger propagation delay of the distant satellite.

3. The signaling overhead (rate of updates of A_i and M_i communicated to UEs) and the fraction of muted PRS resources are minimized subject to the above feasibility constraints.

Provide a constructive scheme achieving (1)–(3), or prove impossibility/lower bounds on the achievable overhead-muting tradeoff.

Consider a positioning system in which a user equipment (UE) on or near the Earth's surface receives ranging-type signals from two heterogeneous space-based sources:

(i) a constellation of medium-earth-orbit Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) satellites, providing pseudorange, carrier-phase, and Doppler measurements relative to known broadcast ephemerides; and

(ii) a constellation of low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellites that transmit cellular-style (e.g., 5G NR) downlink signals and from which the UE (or the network) can extract time-of-arrival, carrier-phase, and/or Doppler measurements together with ephemeris information.

Two architectural modes are considered:

(A) UE-assisted mode: the UE forwards its raw GNSS and LEO measurements (with associated metadata such as timestamps, satellite identifiers, and quality indicators) to a network entity, called the Location Management Function (LMF), which computes the UE position.

(B) UE-based mode: the UE's modem itself accumulates GNSS pseudorange/Doppler measurements together with the 5G NR radio measurements obtained from LEO satellites and computes its own position.

The problem is to design, and rigorously analyze, a joint measurement-processing framework — specifying the measurement model, the state vector (including UE position, velocity, clock bias and drift, and any inter-system biases), the data-association and integrity logic, and the estimation algorithm — that:

1. fuses GNSS and LEO measurements coherently in both modes (A) and (B), accounting for differences in carrier frequency, signal structure, geometry, ephemeris accuracy, and timing reference between the two systems;

2. exploits the orbital diversity of LEO satellites (large angular rates, low altitude, strong Doppler, and complementary geometry to GNSS) to improve positioning accuracy and availability; and

3. is shown, via a quantitative performance analysis (e.g., Cramér–Rao-type bounds and/or achievable estimator performance), to outperform GNSS-only positioning in challenging environments such as dense urban canyons where a substantial fraction of GNSS line-of-sight links are blocked or affected by multipath.

Provide such a joint-processing architecture and characterize its achievable positioning accuracy as a function of the number and geometry of available GNSS and LEO satellites, the measurement noise levels, and the LOS/NLOS blockage statistics of the environment.

Let $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ denote the set of Borel probability measures on a Polish space $\mathcal{X}$. Consider a variational objective $E:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ and, for each integer $n\ge 1$, a random empirical-style approximation $E_n:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ built from $n$ i.i.d. samples (or analogous random data) drawn from an underlying data distribution. Let
$$\mu_* \in \arg\min_{\mu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} E(\mu), \qquad \mu_n \in \arg\min_{\mu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} E_n(\mu).$$

The problem is to identify abstract classes $\mathcal{C}$ of pairs $(E,(E_n)_{n\ge 1})$ such that all three of the following hold:

(i) (Consistency) For every $(E,(E_n))\in\mathcal{C}$, one has $E(\mu_n)\to E(\mu_*)$ as $n\to\infty$, in probability or almost surely.

(ii) (Quantitative rates) There exist explicit model assumptions on $(E,(E_n))$ (e.g., regularity, convexity, concentration, dimension, smoothness of densities) under which one can prove non-asymptotic bounds of the form $\mathbb{E}[E(\mu_n)-E(\mu_*)] \le r(n)$ with an explicit rate function $r(n)\to 0$.

(iii) (Practical scope) The class $\mathcal{C}$ is broad enough to encompass variational objectives on measures arising in machine learning practice, such as those used for out-of-distribution generalization, weakly supervised learning, or uncertainty quantification.

Provide such classes $\mathcal{C}$, together with proofs of (i)–(ii) and a demonstration of (iii).

Fix a positive integer $k$. For each dimension $d \geq 1$, let $D_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a (measurable) domain of Lebesgue volume $1$, and let
$$F_d^k(D_d) := \{\, f : D_d \to \mathbb{R} : \|D^\alpha f\|_\infty \le 1 \text{ for every multi-index } \alpha \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^d \text{ with } |\alpha| \le k\,\}.$$
For an algorithm $A_n$ that approximates $\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx$ using at most $n$ function evaluations of $f$, define the worst-case error
$$e(A_n, F_d^k(D_d)) := \sup_{f \in F_d^k(D_d)} \Bigl| \int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx - A_n(f) \Bigr|,$$
and let $e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) := \inf_{A_n} e(A_n, F_d^k(D_d))$ be the optimal (deterministic) $n$-th minimal worst-case error over all such algorithms.

Problem. Characterize the family of domains $D_d$ (as $d$ varies) for which there exists a constant $c_k > 0$, depending only on $k$, such that
$$e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) \le c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d} \qquad \text{for all } n, d \ge 1,$$
and for each such admissible family $\{D_d\}$ construct an explicit sequence of algorithms attaining this rate.

For integers $d,k\geq 1$, let
\[
F_d^k \;=\; \{\, f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb{R} \;:\; \|D^\alpha f\|_\infty \le 1 \text{ for every multi-index } \alpha \text{ with } |\alpha|\le k \,\}.
\]
A randomized cubature algorithm $A_n$ using at most $n$ function values is a (measurable) mapping that, given a random seed $\omega$, produces an approximation $A_n(f,\omega)$ to the integral $I(f)=\int_{[0,1]^d} f(x)\,dx$. Its worst-case randomized error on $F_d^k$ is
\[
e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,F_d^k) \;=\; \inf_{A_n}\; \sup_{f\in F_d^k}\; \bigl(\mathbb{E}\,|I(f)-A_n(f,\cdot)|^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
It is known that for some constants $C(k)$ independent of $d$ and $n$, there exist randomized algorithms achieving an upper bound of the form
\[
e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,F_d^k) \;\le\; C(k)\, d^{\,t}\, n^{-k/d-1/2},
\]
and one may take $t=(k+1)/2$.

Determine the smallest exponent $t=t(k)\ge 0$ for which an upper bound of the above form
\[
e^{\mathrm{ran}}(n,F_d^k) \;\le\; C(k)\, d^{\,t}\, n^{-k/d-1/2}
\]
holds for all $d,n\ge 1$ with some constant $C(k)$ depending only on $k$.

Setting. For each i = 1, ..., d, let F_i be a Banach space of real-valued functions on some domain D_i, continuously embedded so that point evaluations (or appropriate linear functionals) are bounded, and let S_i : F_i → R be a bounded linear functional with unit norm (think of S_i(f) = ∫ f dμ_i as a univariate integration functional). Let F_d be a suitable tensor product Banach space of F_1, ..., F_d, and let S_d = S_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S_d be the corresponding tensor-product functional on F_d. For an algorithm A_n that uses at most n linear (or function-value) evaluations to approximate S_d, the worst-case error is

  e(A_n, F_d) = sup { |S_d(f) − A_n(f)| : f ∈ F_d, ‖f‖ ≤ 1 },

and the n-th minimal worst-case error is e(n, F_d) = inf_{A_n} e(A_n, F_d).

Background (Hilbert case). When each F_i = H_i is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, the following is known: if for each i there exists a bounded linear functional on H_i with unit norm whose Riesz representer h_i is nonnegative, together with functions f_i, g_i such that the triple (h_i, f_i, g_i) is orthonormal in H_i, and a parameter α_i ∈ (0, 1] such that

  α_i · h_i = sqrt(f_i^2 + g_i^2),

then for all n ∈ N,

  e(n, F_d)^2 ≥ 1 − n · ∏_{i=1}^d (1 + α_i^2)^{−1}.

Question. Formulate and prove an analogous lower bound for the n-th minimal worst-case error of the tensor-product integration functional S_d on tensor products of Banach spaces F_i (rather than Hilbert spaces). That is, identify a structural condition on each Banach space F_i — playing the role of the orthonormal triple (h_i, f_i, g_i) and parameter α_i ∈ (0, 1] in the Hilbert setting — under which one can establish a lower bound of the form

  e(n, F_d) ≥ φ( n, α_1, ..., α_d )

for an explicit function φ exhibiting the same qualitative dependence on n and on the α_i as in the Hilbert-space inequality above (in particular forcing e(n, F_d) to remain bounded away from 0 unless n is at least of order ∏_{i=1}^d (1 + α_i^2)).

Consider one-dimensional numerical integration of a function f on the interval [0,1], i.e. approximation of the integral I(f) = ∫_0^1 f(x) dx. Two universal randomized quadrature strategies are defined as follows.

(A) Randomly shifted midpoint rule for periodic functions. Fix an integer m ≥ 1. Choose an integer n uniformly at random in {m, m+1, m+2, …, 2m}, and independently choose a shift τ uniformly at random in [0, 1/n]. Approximate I(f) by
   Q_A(f) = (1/n) ∑_{j=0}^{n-1} f( τ + (j + 1/2)/n  mod 1 ).
This algorithm is applied to 1-periodic functions f: ℝ → ℝ (extended periodically from [0,1]).

(B) Chebyshev interpolation plus Monte Carlo on the residual, for non-periodic functions. Fix m ≥ 1 and set n = 2m. Let f_m be the polynomial of degree less than m that interpolates f at the Chebyshev nodes x_i = (1 + cos((2i−1)π/(2m)))/2, i = 1,…,m. Compute I(f_m) exactly (separation of the main part). Then approximate I(f − f_m) by the simplest Monte Carlo estimator using m independent uniform samples ξ_1,…,ξ_m in [0,1]:
   Q_B(f) = I(f_m) + (1/m) ∑_{i=1}^m ( f(ξ_i) − f_m(ξ_i) ).

For standard function classes on [0,1] (e.g. Sobolev-type classes F_k^1 of functions with bounded k-th derivative, in both the periodic and non-periodic settings), give a detailed theoretical and practical comparison of the randomized algorithms Q_A and Q_B in dimension d = 1. In particular, determine and compare:
 (i) their root-mean-square errors sup_{f ∈ F} ( E |I(f) − Q(f)|^2 )^{1/2} as functions of m, including sharp constants where possible;
 (ii) the orders of optimal convergence achieved on each class, and whether either algorithm is universally (asymptotically) optimal across the scale of smoothness parameters k;
 (iii) their behavior on non-periodic vs. periodic functions, and the practical computational cost (number of function evaluations, arithmetic operations, numerical stability).

Setting. Consider multivariate numerical integration on the d-dimensional unit cube. For a class F_d of integrable real-valued functions on [0,1]^d, an algorithm A_n that uses at most n function values produces approximations A_n(f) to the integral I_d(f) = ∫_{[0,1]^d} f(x) dx. The worst-case error of A_n on F_d is

  e(A_n, F_d) = sup{ |I_d(f) − A_n(f)| : f ∈ F_d, ‖f‖_{F_d} ≤ 1 },

and the information complexity is

  n(ε, F_d) = min{ n : there exists A_n with e(A_n, F_d) ≤ ε }.

Tractability notions. The integration problem on the family {F_d}_{d≥1} is called:
 (a) polynomially tractable if there exist constants C, p, q ≥ 0 such that n(ε, F_d) ≤ C d^q ε^{−p} for all d ∈ ℕ and ε ∈ (0,1);
 (b) strongly polynomially tractable if there exist constants C, p ≥ 0 such that n(ε, F_d) ≤ C ε^{−p} for all d ∈ ℕ and ε ∈ (0,1).

Universality. A sequence of algorithms (A_n)_{n≥1} is called universal for a collection 𝒞 = {F_d^{(α)} : α ∈ A} of function classes (indexed by smoothness parameters, weights, or other a priori unknown features α) if, for every α ∈ A, the algorithms (A_n) achieve the optimal order of convergence of e(A_n, F_d^{(α)}) in n as n → ∞, without the algorithm depending on α.

Problem. Develop a theory of universality at the level of tractability rather than only at the level of convergence rate. Specifically:

 1. Formulate a precise notion of a "tractability-universal" algorithm, i.e. a single sequence (A_n) that, for every class F_d^{(α)} in a prescribed collection 𝒞, attains the same (polynomial or strong polynomial) tractability exponents as the best class-specific algorithm tailored to F_d^{(α)}.

 2. Characterize, for natural collections 𝒞 (for example, scales of isotropic Sobolev spaces H^k_d with k > d/2, classes of mixed smoothness H^{k,mix}_d, or weighted Korobov / Hilbert spaces with varying weights), whether such tractability-universal algorithms exist and, when they do, determine the optimal tractability exponents achievable simultaneously across 𝒞.

 3. Provide either explicit constructions of such universal algorithms or prove obstructions showing that tractability-universality must be strictly weaker than class-specific tractability.

Background. Let $d\ge 1$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of function classes $F\subset L_1(\Omega,\mu)$, where $(\Omega,\mu)$ is a measure space and each $F$ consists of integrable functions $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$. A (deterministic) cubature/algorithm based on $n$ function values is a map
$$Q_n(f)=\phi_n\bigl(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n)\bigr),$$
where $x_1,\dots,x_n\in\Omega$ and $\phi_n:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ (the sample points may be chosen adaptively). The worst-case error of $Q_n$ on a class $F$ is
$$e(Q_n,F)=\sup_{f\in F}\Bigl|\int_\Omega f\,d\mu-Q_n(f)\Bigr|,$$
and the $n$-th minimal error is $e_n(F)=\inf_{Q_n}e(Q_n,F)$. A sequence of algorithms $(Q_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is called \emph{universal} for the family $\mathcal{F}$ if, for every $F\in\mathcal{F}$, one has
$$e(Q_n,F)\;\asymp\;e_n(F)\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
i.e.\ $(Q_n)$ achieves the optimal order of convergence on every class $F\in\mathcal{F}$ simultaneously, without knowledge of $F$. (Analogous definitions apply in the randomized setting using expected errors.)

Known case. For $\Omega=[0,1]^d$ with Lebesgue measure, universal algorithms have been constructed for natural scales $\mathcal{F}$ of smoothness classes (e.g.\ weighted Korobov, Sobolev, and Besov classes), simultaneously attaining the optimal order on every class in the family.

Problem. Determine whether universal algorithms exist when the integration domain is not the unit cube. More precisely: exhibit a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ (or more generally a measure space) other than $[0,1]^d$, together with a natural family $\mathcal{F}$ of function classes on $\Omega$ (for instance, smoothness classes on the Euclidean ball, the sphere, the simplex, or an unbounded domain such as $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a Gaussian weight), and a sequence $(Q_n)$ of cubature rules using $n$ function values that is universal for $\mathcal{F}$ in the above sense; or prove that no such universal sequence can exist for the given family.

For integers $d,k\ge 1$ and a measurable domain $D_d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of Lebesgue volume $1$, define the smoothness class
$$F_d^k(D_d)=\{f:D_d\to\mathbb{R}\mid \|\partial^\alpha f\|_\infty\le 1\text{ for all multi-indices }\alpha\text{ with }|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
For a positive integer $n$, the (deterministic) optimal $n$-point integration error is
$$e(n,F_d^k(D_d))=\inf_{x_1,\dots,x_n\in D_d}\ \inf_{a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}}\ \sup_{f\in F_d^k(D_d)}\Big|\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(x_i)\Big|.$$
It is known that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that, for all $d,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and all volume-1 domains $D_d$,
$$e(n,F_d^k(D_d))\ \ge\ \min\!\left\{\tfrac{1}{2},\ c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d}\right\}.$$
Determine the sharp (or sharper) values of the constants $c_k$ in this lower bound. Moreover, identify the extremal domains $D_d$ of volume $1$ for which, given $k$, $d$, and $n$, the integration error $e(n,F_d^k(D_d))$ is as small as possible.

Fix an integer $d\ge 1$ and an integer $k\ge 1$. For a bounded Jordan measurable domain $D\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with Lebesgue measure $\lambda_d(D)=1$, let $F_d^k(D)$ denote the classical smoothness class consisting of all functions $f:D\to\mathbb{R}$ whose partial derivatives up to order $k$ exist and are bounded in absolute value by $1$ on $D$. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the $n$-th minimal worst-case integration error
$$e(n,F_d^k(D))\;=\;\inf_{x_1,\dots,x_n\in D,\;a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}}\;\sup_{f\in F_d^k(D)}\left|\int_D f(x)\,dx-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(x_i)\right|.$$
It is known that $e(n,F_d^k(D))\asymp n^{-k/d}$ at least for every bounded Lipschitz domain $D$.

(a) Does the limit
$$C_D\;=\;\lim_{n\to\infty} e(n,F_d^k(D))\cdot n^{k/d}$$
exist for every Jordan measurable $D$ with $\lambda_d(D)=1$ (possibly under suitable regularity assumptions on the boundary $\partial D$)?

(b) Assuming the limit exists, is the constant $C_D$ independent of the particular shape of $D$ (depending only on $d$ and $k$)?

$$\widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d)=\Bigl\{\,f\in C^2(D_d)\ \Big|\ \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \mathrm{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2},\ \mathrm{Lip}(D_\Theta f)\le d^{-1}\ \text{for every unit vector }\Theta\in S^{d-1}\,\Bigr\},$$
where $D_\Theta f$ denotes the directional derivative of $f$ in direction $\Theta$ and $\mathrm{Lip}(g)$ is the (smallest) Lipschitz constant of $g$ on $D_d$.

$$e(n,\widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d))=\inf_{\substack{x_1,\dots,x_n\in D_d\\ \phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}}}\ \sup_{f\in \widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d)}\ \Bigl|\,\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx-\phi(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n))\,\Bigr|.$$

Decide whether there exists an absolute constant $C>0$, independent of both the dimension $d$ and the domain $D_d$, such that
$$e\bigl(n,\widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d)\bigr)\ \ge\ C\,n^{-2/d}\qquad \text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N},\ d\in\mathbb{N},\ \text{and all admissible }D_d.$$

Let $d\ge 1$ and let $D_d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact, convex, orthogonally symmetric body (i.e. invariant under all orthogonal transformations of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that map $D_d$ to itself; here we take the natural symmetric body $D_d$ equal to a unit $\ell_p^d$-ball $B_p^d=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\|x\|_p\le 1\}$). Consider the class
$$\widetilde C^2(D_d)=\bigl\{f\in C^2(D_d):\ \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \|\partial_v^2 f\|_\infty\le 1\text{ for every unit vector }v\in\mathbb{R}^d\bigr\},$$
i.e. functions on $D_d$ uniformly bounded by $1$ whose second directional derivative in every direction is also uniformly bounded by $1$.

For the integration problem
$$\mathrm{INT}_d(f)=\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx,$$
define the worst-case error of an algorithm using $n$ function values as
$$e(n,d)=\inf_{x_1,\dots,x_n;\,\phi}\sup_{f\in\widetilde C^2(D_d)}\bigl|\mathrm{INT}_d(f)-\phi(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n))\bigr|,$$
where the infimum is over all (adaptive) choices of nodes and all mappings $\phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. Let $n(\varepsilon,d)$ be the minimal $n$ for which $e(n,d)\le\varepsilon$. One says the curse of dimensionality holds if there exist $\varepsilon_0>0$, $c>0$, and $\gamma>1$ such that
$$n(\varepsilon_0,d)\ge c\,\gamma^d\quad\text{for all }d\ge 1.$$

It is known that the curse of dimensionality holds when $D_d=B_p^d$ for $p\ge 2$.

Question: Does the curse of dimensionality also hold for $\widetilde C^2(B_p^d)$ when $1\le p<2$?

Let $\mathbb{T}^d = \mathbb{R}^d / \mathbb{Z}^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional torus, equipped with the normalized Lebesgue measure. For an integer $k \ge 1$, let $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ denote the Hilbert space of functions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ with dominating mixed smoothness $k$, namely the space of $f \in L_2(\mathbb{T}^d)$ whose Fourier coefficients $\hat f(\mathbf{m})$, $\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, satisfy
$$\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}^2 \;=\; \sum_{\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{Z}^d} \Big(\prod_{j=1}^d (1+|m_j|)^{2k}\Big)\, |\hat f(\mathbf{m})|^2 \;<\; \infty.$$

Consider the integration problem $I(f) = \int_{\mathbb{T}^d} f(x)\,dx$ and randomized linear quadrature rules $Q_n(f) = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(X_i)$ where the nodes $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are required to be independent and uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{T}^d$ (the coefficients $a_i$ may depend on the nodes). Define the worst-case error under iid uniform sampling by
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;=\; \inf_{a_1,\dots,a_n} \;\sup_{\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}\le 1} \;\mathbb{E}\,\big|I(f)-Q_n(f)\big|,$$
and let $e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$ denote the corresponding optimal worst-case error over all randomized algorithms using $n$ function evaluations at arbitrary (possibly adaptive) sample points.

It is known that iid uniform sampling is optimal for $L_2$-approximation in $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ with respect to the Monte Carlo (mean-square) error, and optimal up to a logarithmic factor with respect to the uniform error, which yields
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;\le\; C(d,k)\,(\log n)^{\alpha(d,k)}\, e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$$
for some exponent $\alpha(d,k)>0$.

Question: Can the logarithmic factor be removed? More precisely, does there exist a constant $C=C(d,k)$ such that
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;\le\; C\, e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$$
for all $n\ge 2$, as is known in the isotropic-smoothness setting?

$$\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}^2 \;=\; \sum_{\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{Z}^d} \Big(\prod_{j=1}^d (1+|m_j|)^{2k}\Big)\, |\hat f(\mathbf{m})|^2 \;<\; \infty.$$

Consider the integration problem $I(f) = \int_{\mathbb{T}^d} f(x)\,dx$ and randomized linear quadrature rules $Q_n(f) = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(X_i)$ where the nodes $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are required to be independent and uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{T}^d$ (the coefficients $a_i$ may depend on the nodes). Define the worst-case error under iid uniform sampling by
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;=\; \inf_{a_1,\dots,a_n} \;\sup_{\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}\le 1} \;\mathbb{E}\,\big|I(f)-Q_n(f)\big|,$$
and let $e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$ denote the corresponding optimal worst-case error over all randomized algorithms using $n$ function evaluations at arbitrary (possibly adaptive) sample points.

It is known that iid uniform sampling is optimal for $L_2$-approximation in $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ with respect to the Monte Carlo (mean-square) error, and optimal up to a logarithmic factor with respect to the uniform error, which yields
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;\le\; C(d,k)\,(\log n)^{\alpha(d,k)}\, e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$$
for some exponent $\alpha(d,k)>0$.

Question: Can the logarithmic factor be removed? More precisely, does there exist a constant $C=C(d,k)$ such that
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;\le\; C\, e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$$
for all $n\ge 2$, as is known in the isotropic-smoothness setting?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is stated as an open problem in the literature on optimal numerical integration for mixed-smoothness function spaces. Recent surveys and papers on iid sampling recovery and integration on $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ confirm that, while iid uniform points are known to be optimal up to logarithmic factors, removing the logarithmic loss for integration in this setting remains unresolved. A related result in the isotropic Sobolev case shows the logarithmic factor can be avoided except for $p=q=\infty$, but the mixed-smoothness analogue is still not established.

Background and setup. Let $F$ be a class of integrable functions on a domain $D \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ (for instance, the unit ball of a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space or a Sobolev space), equipped with a probability measure $\mu$. The integration problem is to approximate $S(f) = \int_D f\,d\mu$ for $f \in F$. A linear algorithm based on iid samples uses information of the form $(f(X_1), \dots, f(X_n))$ where $X_1, \dots, X_n$ are independent and identically distributed according to some probability measure $\nu$ on $D$ (typically $\nu = \mu$, but $\nu$ may also be chosen by the algorithm depending on $F$ but independently of $f$). The corresponding randomized worst-case error is
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(F) = \inf_{A_n,\nu} \sup_{f\in F} \bigl(\mathbb{E}\,|S(f) - A_n(f(X_1),\dots,f(X_n))|^2\bigr)^{1/2},$$
where the infimum is over all (possibly nonlinear) reconstruction maps $A_n$ and over the sampling distribution $\nu$. In contrast, the standard randomized $n$-th minimal error $e_n^{\mathrm{ran}}(F)$ allows arbitrary (adaptively chosen, not necessarily iid) sampling points.

Now consider a sequence of problems indexed by dimension $d \in \mathbb{N}$: a family $(F_d, S_d)_{d\geq 1}$, with initial error $e_0(F_d)$. For $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $d \in \mathbb{N}$ let
$$n^{\mathrm{iid}}(\varepsilon,d) = \min\{n : e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(F_d) \leq \varepsilon \cdot e_0(F_d)\}.$$
The family is called \emph{iid-polynomially tractable} if there exist constants $C, p, q \geq 0$ such that $n^{\mathrm{iid}}(\varepsilon,d) \leq C\,\varepsilon^{-p} d^q$ for all $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $d \in \mathbb{N}$, \emph{iid-strongly polynomially tractable} if this holds with $q = 0$, and \emph{iid-weakly tractable} if $\log n^{\mathrm{iid}}(\varepsilon,d)/(\varepsilon^{-1}+d) \to 0$ as $\varepsilon^{-1}+d \to \infty$. Analogous notions of polynomial, strong polynomial, and weak tractability are defined for $n^{\mathrm{ran}}(\varepsilon,d)$.

Problem. Develop a theory of iid tractability for multivariate integration (and, analogously, for $L_2$-approximation) under iid information. Specifically:

(a) Provide characterizations (necessary and sufficient conditions on the family $(F_d)$) for iid-polynomial tractability, iid-strong polynomial tractability, and iid-weak tractability.

(b) Determine how iid tractability compares to the corresponding tractability notions under optimally chosen (adaptive, non-iid) information: identify families for which the two notions coincide and families for which they differ, and quantify the gap (e.g., the loss in the exponents $p$ and $q$ when iid sampling is enforced).

(c) Exhibit explicit examples (e.g., weighted Sobolev or Korobov spaces) where iid tractability holds and examples where it fails while ordinary tractability still holds.

Let $d\ge 1$, $s\ge 1$ an integer, and $1\le p,q\le\infty$ with $s/d > (1/p - 1/q)_+$, where $(x)_+ = \max(x,0)$. Let $D_d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, and let $W_p^s(D_d)$ denote the Sobolev space of functions on $D_d$ with smoothness $s$ in $L_p$, equipped with its usual norm; let $L_q(D_d)$ be the target space.

For a set of sample points $P_n=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\subset D_d$, define the worst-case $L_q$-approximation error using only function values at $P_n$ by
$$
 e(P_n,W_p^s(D_d),L_q(D_d)) := \inf_{A_n}\ \sup_{\|f\|_{W_p^s(D_d)}\le 1}\ \|f - A_n(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n))\|_{L_q(D_d)},
$$
where the infimum is over all (possibly nonlinear) reconstruction maps $A_n:\mathbb{R}^n\to L_q(D_d)$. Let $P_n=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ consist of independent points drawn from the uniform distribution on $D_d$, and consider the (random) error $e(P_n,W_p^s(D_d),L_q(D_d))$ multiplied by the conjectured optimal rate factor $n^{\,s/d-(1/p-1/q)_+}$.

Questions:
(a) Does the limit
$$
 C(D_d,s,p,q) := \lim_{n\to\infty}\, \mathbb{E}\bigl[e(P_n,W_p^s(D_d),L_q(D_d))\bigr]\cdot n^{\,s/d-(1/p-1/q)_+}
$$
exist (in $(0,\infty)$) for every such domain $D_d$ and every admissible choice of $s,p,q$?

(b) If it exists, does $C(D_d,s,p,q)$ depend on $D_d$ only through its $d$-dimensional Lebesgue volume $|D_d|$, and not on the shape of $D_d$?

Let $D_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be an open set, and let $\rho : D_d \to [0,\infty)$ be a fixed integrable weight function such that $\int_{D_d}\rho(x)\,dx < \infty$. For an integrable function $f : D_d \to \mathbb{R}$, define the weighted integral
$$S_d(f) = \int_{D_d} f(x)\,\rho(x)\,dx.$$
A randomized cubature rule using $n$ function values has the form
$$A_n^\omega(f) = \sum_{j=1}^n a_j(\omega)\, f(x_j(\omega)),$$
where $\omega$ is a random element of some probability space, the coefficients $a_j(\omega) \in \mathbb{R}$ and the nodes $x_j(\omega) \in D_d$ are random, and we additionally allow the variant in which $x_1(\omega),\dots,x_n(\omega)$ are i.i.d. uniformly distributed in $D_d$ (assuming $D_d$ has finite Lebesgue measure). The randomized error of $A_n^\omega$ on a class $F$ of integrands is
$$e^{\mathrm{ran}}(A_n^\omega, F) = \sup_{f \in F} \left( \mathbb{E}_\omega \,|S_d(f) - A_n^\omega(f)|^2 \right)^{1/2}.$$

Call a family $(A_n^\omega)_{n \ge 1}$ *universal* if it is defined independently of the smoothness parameters of $F$ and yet, for every class $F$ in a prescribed scale of smoothness classes on $D_d$ (for instance, isotropic or mixed-smoothness Sobolev or Hölder classes), the error $e^{\mathrm{ran}}(A_n^\omega, F)$ satisfies, up to absolute constants and possibly logarithmic factors in $n$, the optimal rate known for randomized integration of $F$ on the unit cube with weight $\rho \equiv 1$.

Question: Does such a universal randomized algorithm exist for the weighted integration problem $S_d$ on a general open set $D_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with a general integrable weight $\rho$, achieving for every smoothness class in the scale the optimal randomized rate up to (at worst) additional polylogarithmic factors in $n$?

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The reducedness of the Quot scheme of points on the affine plane for all ranks r and lengths d appears to be open. Existing work (e.g., ADHM-type descriptions of Quot schemes of points on affine spaces) establishes irreducibility and reducedness in special cases but does not settle the full question. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A finite local Artinian $k$-algebra $(A, \mathfrak{m}, k)$ is called Gorenstein if its socle $\operatorname{Soc}(A) = \{a \in A : a\mathfrak{m} = 0\}$ is one-dimensional over $k$. Such an algebra $A$ corresponds to a $k$-point of the Hilbert scheme $\operatorname{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{A}^N)$ of $n = \dim_k A$ points in affine space (after a closed embedding $\operatorname{Spec} A \hookrightarrow \mathbb{A}^N$). The algebra $A$ is called smoothable if this point lies in the closure of the locus parametrizing reduced $n$-tuples of distinct points, equivalently, if $\operatorname{Spec} A$ is a flat limit of $n$ distinct reduced points.

For a local Gorenstein $k$-algebra $A$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, let $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A) = \bigoplus_{i \geq 0} \mathfrak{m}^i / \mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ be the associated graded algebra. The canonical graded Gorenstein quotient $Q(0)$ of $A$ is defined as the (unique) graded Gorenstein quotient of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A)$ whose socle degree equals that of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A)$; explicitly, $Q(0) = \operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A) / C$, where $C$ is the largest graded ideal of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A)$ not containing the top-degree socle.

Exhibit an explicit example of a nonsmoothable finite local Gorenstein $k$-algebra $A$ such that its canonical graded Gorenstein quotient $Q(0)$ is smoothable. The example should have $\dim_k A$ as small as possible.

Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parametrizing zero-dimensional subschemes of length $d$ in affine 3-space $\mathbb{A}^3$. For a local Artinian quotient $A=k[x_1,x_2,x_3]/I$ of length $d$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ and socle degree $s$ (so $\mathfrak{m}^{s+1}=0$, $\mathfrak{m}^s\neq 0$), the Hilbert function is $H(A)=(h_0,h_1,\dots,h_s)$ with $h_i=\dim_k \mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$. The algebra $A$ is called compressed if, for every $i$, $h_i$ attains the maximum value possible given $h_1$ and $s$, namely $h_i=\min\!\bigl(\binom{i+h_1-1}{h_1-1},\,\dim_k\mathrm{Soc}(A)\cdot\binom{s-i+h_1-1}{h_1-1}\bigr)$ for prescribed socle type.

Inside $\mathrm{Hilb}_{78}(\mathbb{A}^3)$, let $L_{78}$ be the locus of points corresponding to compressed local Artinian quotients of $k[x_1,x_2,x_3]$ of length $78$ with the (compressed) Hilbert function $H=(1,3,6,10,15,21,15,6,1)$ supported at a single point of $\mathbb{A}^3$ (together with the natural translations by $\mathbb{A}^3$). Inside $\mathrm{Hilb}_{96}(\mathbb{A}^3)$, let $VC_{3,96}$ be the "very compressed" locus consisting of local Artinian quotients of length $96$ whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ satisfies $\mathfrak{m}^3=0$ and which have Hilbert function $H=(1,3,6,\dots)$ truncated as $(1,3,92)$ with socle equal to $\mathfrak{m}^2$.

Question:
(a) Is $L_{78}$ an irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}_{78}(\mathbb{A}^3)$?
(b) Is $VC_{3,96}$ an irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}_{96}(\mathbb{A}^3)$?

(In either case, if the answer is yes, show further that the resulting component is generically nonreduced.)

Work over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $0$. For a finite local $k$-algebra $A$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, the Hilbert function of $A$ is the sequence $H_A(i) = \dim_k(\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1})$. Fix integers $n \geq 2$ and $r \geq 1$. A local algebra $A$ of length $d = 1 + n + r$ is said to have Hilbert function $(1,n,r)$ if $\dim_k A/\mathfrak{m} = 1$, $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2 = n$, $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}^2/\mathfrak{m}^3 = r$ and $\mathfrak{m}^3 = 0$. Such an algebra is called very compressed when its Hilbert function is $(1,n,r)$ with $r \leq \binom{n+1}{2}$ (i.e., $\mathfrak{m}^2$ is as large as possible subject to $\mathfrak{m}^3=0$ and the embedding dimension being $n$).

Let $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parameterizing length-$d$ zero-dimensional subschemes of $\mathbb{A}^n$. Inside this scheme, let $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d} \subseteq \mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ denote the closure of the locus of points corresponding to (subschemes supported at a single point and isomorphic to) very compressed local algebras with Hilbert function $(1,n,r)$, where $r = d - (1+n)$. The smoothable component is the closure of the open locus parameterizing reduced subschemes (equivalently, the unique irreducible component containing the locus of $d$ distinct points).

Assume that
$$\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{6} + 2 < r \leq \binom{n+1}{2}.$$
Determine, for each such pair $(n,d)$ with $d = 1 + n + r$, whether $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d}$ is an irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ distinct from the smoothable component, or whether $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d}$ is contained in the smoothable component.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The question is a variant of the classical Bonnet problem on surfaces realizing a prescribed mean curvature. Classical results (Bonnet, Cartan, Chern) describe continuous isometric deformations preserving principal curvatures, and Hopf's theorem forces a CMC immersion of $S^2$ into $\mathbb{R}^3$ to be a round sphere; however, the precise question—whether non-congruent isometric immersions of $S^2$ into $\mathbb{R}^3$ can share the same (non-constant) mean curvature function and what relation must hold between their induced metrics—does not appear to be settled in the literature found. Related recent rigidity results exist for star-shaped hypersurfaces in warped products and for surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$, but none directly resolves the $S^2\to\mathbb{R}^3$ case as stated. Status appears open.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\Delta(n,d)$ as $d \to \infty$ (with $n$ fixed). More precisely, determine
$$\liminf_{d\to\infty} \frac{nd - \Delta(n,d)}{d} \quad \text{and} \quad \limsup_{d\to\infty} \frac{nd - \Delta(n,d)}{d},$$
or any sharp asymptotic estimate for $(nd - \Delta(n,d))/d$.

status_assertions.value: open_status:open

The minimum dimension of irreducible components of the punctual Hilbert scheme remains an active area of research. While all smoothable components are known to have dimension at least (n-1)(d-1) (with curvilinear components achieving this bound), the question of the smallest possible component dimension across all (including elementary/non-smoothable) components for fixed n as d → ∞ has not been resolved. Recent work has constructed small elementary components for n ≥ 4, but no sharp asymptotic formula for Δ(n,d) appears to be established.

The question is connected to a long-standing conjecture of Briançon–Iarrobino on the most singular points of the Hilbert scheme of points. Recent work (2023–2025) provides conjectural criteria for the maximum tangent space dimension in three dimensions, reducing it to a problem in convex geometry, and exhibits explicit examples (e.g. in lengths 8 and 39) that disprove some earlier guesses. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parametrizing zero-dimensional closed subschemes of $\mathbb{A}^4_k$ of length $d$. Let $\mathrm{Hilb}^{\mathrm{Gor}}_d(\mathbb{A}^4) \subseteq \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ be the open locus parametrizing those subschemes $\Gamma$ whose structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_\Gamma$ is a Gorenstein $k$-algebra. Let $\mathrm{Hilb}^{\mathrm{sm}}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ denote the smoothable component, defined as the closure of the locus of reduced subschemes consisting of $d$ distinct points; this component has dimension $4d$, and a point $[\Gamma]$ on it is smooth in $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ if and only if $\dim_k T_{[\Gamma]} \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4) = 4d$.

For a point $[\Gamma] \in \mathrm{Hilb}^{\mathrm{Gor}}_d(\mathbb{A}^4) \cap \mathrm{Hilb}^{\mathrm{sm}}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$, define its surplus by
$$ s([\Gamma]) := \dim_k T_{[\Gamma]} \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4) - 4d \ \geq\ 0. $$
Two pointed schemes $(X_1, x_1)$ and $(X_2, x_2)$ are called smoothly equivalent if there exist a scheme $Y$, a point $y \in Y$, and smooth morphisms $Y \to X_1$ and $Y \to X_2$ sending $y$ to $x_1$ and $x_2$ respectively.

Problem: For small values of the surplus $s$, classify, up to smooth equivalence, the singularities of the Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^4)$ at points $[\Gamma]$ of the smoothable Gorenstein locus with $s([\Gamma]) = s$.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $n\ge 1$ and $d\ge 1$ be integers, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ denote the punctual Hilbert scheme parameterizing ideals $I\subset k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]$ (equivalently $0$-dimensional subschemes of $\mathbb{A}^n$ supported at the origin) such that $\dim_k k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]/I = d$. A point $[I]\in\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ is called curvilinear if the quotient $k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]/I$ embeds into $k[[t]]$, equivalently if $I$ contains the maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ to a power and the quotient is generated by a single element as a $k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]$-module; equivalently $\mathrm{Spec}\,k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]/I$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{Spec}\,k[t]/(t^d)$. The curvilinear locus $\mathrm{Curv}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)\subset\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ is the locally closed subset of curvilinear points. A monomial ideal is an ideal generated by monomials in $x_1,\dots,x_n$.

Question: Does every monomial ideal $I\in\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$ lie in the Zariski closure of the curvilinear locus $\mathrm{Curv}_d(\mathbb{A}^n,0)$?

Let $n,d\ge 1$ and consider the polynomial ring $S=\mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_n]$, graded in the standard way. Let $H:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ be the Hilbert function of the homogeneous coordinate ring $S/I_Z$ of a set $Z$ of $d$ general points in $\mathbb{P}^n$; equivalently $H(t)=\min(\binom{t+n}{n},d)$. Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_H$ denote Haiman–Sturmfels' multigraded Hilbert scheme parametrizing homogeneous ideals $I\subset S$ with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}(S/I)_t = H(t)$ for every $t\ge 0$.

Inside $\mathrm{Hilb}_H$ consider the two distinguished loci:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathrm{Sat}_H \subset \mathrm{Hilb}_H$: the closure of the set of points $[I]$ such that $I$ is a saturated homogeneous ideal (i.e.\ $I=I:\mathfrak{m}^{\infty}$ where $\mathfrak{m}=(x_0,\dots,x_n)$).
\item $\mathrm{Slip}_H \subset \mathrm{Hilb}_H$: the closure of the open locus parametrizing ideals $I(Z')$ of $d$ distinct reduced points $Z'\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ (the "limits of ideals of points" component).
\end{itemize}

Give an effective criterion that, for an arbitrary closed point $[I]\in\mathrm{Hilb}_H$, decides whether $[I]\in\mathrm{Sat}_H$ and whether $[I]\in\mathrm{Slip}_H$.

By a theorem of Haiman and Sturmfels, $H^h_S$ exists as a quasi-projective scheme over $k$ (projective when each $S_a$ is finite-dimensional).

Exhibit an explicit example, of as small size as possible (small $n$, simple grading group $A$, and small values of $h$), of a triple $(S, A\text{-grading}, h)$ for which the resulting multigraded Hilbert scheme $H^h_S$ is disconnected. Preferably, the example should have the property that the Hilbert function $h$ is eventually constant (i.e., there is a finitely generated submonoid containing the degrees, on which $h$ takes a constant value outside a finite set).

Let k be an algebraically closed field. Recall that a finite scheme over k is a scheme Γ = Spec A where A is a finite-dimensional k-algebra; its degree deg Γ is dim_k A. The Hilbert scheme of points Hilb_d(A^N) parameterizes finite subschemes of degree d of affine space, and its smoothable component is the closure of the locus of unions of d distinct reduced points. Embed Γ as a subscheme of some A^N (the choice does not affect what follows up to a fixed shift). The smoothability defect δ(Γ) is defined as the minimum, over all embeddings of Γ as a closed subscheme of a smoothable finite subscheme Γ' ⊂ A^N, of deg Γ' − deg Γ. (Equivalently, δ(Γ) measures how many extra points must be added to Γ to place it inside a smoothable finite scheme; δ(Γ) = 0 if and only if Γ is smoothable.)

For finite schemes Γ_1, Γ_2 over k, let Γ_1 ×_k Γ_2 = Spec(A_1 ⊗_k A_2) denote their product, and write Γ^{×n} for the n-fold product. Note deg(Γ^{×n}) = (deg Γ)^n.

Let $n, d_1, d_2, d_3, r_1, r_2$ be positive integers and let $\mathbb{A}^n$ denote affine $n$-space over an algebraically closed field $\mathbf{k}$. Consider the bilinear scheme
$$\mathrm{Bilin}^{r_1,r_2}_{d_1,d_2,d_3}(\mathbb{A}^n),$$
whose functor of points sends a $\mathbf{k}$-algebra $R$ to the set of equivalence classes of data
$$(\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{F}_2, \mathcal{F}_3,\; \pi_1, \pi_2,\; \mu),$$
where each $\mathcal{F}_i$ is a locally free quotient of $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$-modules of rank $d_i$ (with $\mathcal{F}_3$ also a quotient compatible with the structure), $\pi_1,\pi_2$ are the corresponding surjections, and
$$\mu : \mathcal{F}_1 \otimes_R \mathcal{F}_2 \longrightarrow \mathcal{F}_3$$
is an $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$-bilinear map such that the images of the natural multiplication maps factor through $\mu$ with appropriate ranks $r_1, r_2$ controlling the dimensions of the spaces of linear factorizations on each side. Equivalently, $\mathrm{Bilin}^{r_1,r_2}_{d_1,d_2,d_3}(\mathbb{A}^n)$ can be realized as a closed subscheme of an appropriate product of Quot schemes of $\mathbb{A}^n$.

Investigate the geometry of $\mathrm{Bilin}^{r_1,r_2}_{d_1,d_2,d_3}(\mathbb{A}^n)$:

(a) Determine its irreducible components. In particular, identify the component(s) parameterizing tuples of points and the totally degenerate locus, and decide for which $(n, d_1, d_2, d_3, r_1, r_2)$ the scheme is reducible.

(b) Describe its singular locus and classify the types of singularities that occur.

(c) Decide for which parameters the scheme is nonreduced, and exhibit nilpotents in the structure sheaf when they exist.

Consider a relativistic plasma described by viscous hydrodynamics whose energy–momentum tensor admits a Landau-frame decomposition
T^{μν} = ε u^μ u^ν − (P + Π) Δ^{μν} + π^{μν},
where ε is the energy density, P the equilibrium pressure, u^μ the fluid four-velocity, Δ^{μν} = g^{μν} − u^μ u^ν the spatial projector, Π the bulk-viscous pressure, and π^{μν} the (traceless, transverse) shear-stress tensor. The microscopic degrees of freedom are quarks and gluons at high temperatures and hadrons at low temperatures, with single-particle phase-space distributions
f(x,p) = f_eq(x,p) + δf_shear(x,p; π^{μν}) + δf_bulk(x,p; Π),
where the non-equilibrium corrections δf are functionals of π^{μν} and Π whose form depends on the chosen ansatz (e.g. Grad's 14-moment, Chapman–Enskog, Romatschke–Strickland).

The differential emission rate of real photons and of dileptons from such a medium is, at leading order in the electromagnetic coupling, a convolution of the partonic/hadronic matrix elements with products of the distributions f and of Bose/Fermi factors (1 ± f).

Problem. Determine, from first principles in QCD (and from the relevant hadronic effective theories in the confined phase), the exact energy- and momentum-differential emission rates
dN_γ/(d^4x d^3k)   and   dN_{ℓ⁺ℓ⁻}/(d^4x d^4q)
of photons and dileptons emitted by the plasma when it is out of local thermal equilibrium, expressed as explicit functionals of the local hydrodynamic variables (T, u^μ, π^{μν}, Π) through the underlying microscopic distributions f_eq + δf_shear + δf_bulk, in such a way that:
(i) the result is independent of the (unphysical) choice of δf-ansatz to the order in gradients considered;
(ii) it reproduces the known equilibrium rate in the limit π^{μν}, Π → 0;
(iii) it consistently accounts for the additional electromagnetic radiation associated with the entropy produced by viscous dissipation.

representations.normalized:
In high-energy hadronic collisions, prompt-photon production and Drell–Yan dilepton production are commonly described by collinear-factorized perturbative QCD formulas of the form

  E_γ dσ^{γ}/d^3 p = ∑_{a,b} ∫ dx_a dx_b f_{a/A}(x_a, μ_F) f_{b/B}(x_b, μ_F) · (E_γ dσ̂^{ab→γ X}/d^3 p)(μ_R, μ_F),

  dσ^{ℓ⁺ℓ⁻}/dM² = ∑_{a,b} ∫ dx_a dx_b f_{a/A}(x_a, μ_F) f_{b/B}(x_b, μ_F) · (dσ̂^{ab→ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ X}/dM²)(μ_R, μ_F),

where f_{a/A} are parton distribution functions of hadrons or nuclei A, B, dσ̂ are partonic cross sections computed in fixed-order perturbation theory, μ_R, μ_F are renormalization and factorization scales, p_T^γ denotes the transverse momentum of the produced photon, and M denotes the invariant mass of the produced lepton pair.

Determine, with quantitative theoretical control, the lower boundary in p_T^γ (for prompt photons) and the lower boundary in M (for Drell–Yan dileptons) below which these perturbative hard-scattering formulas cease to provide a reliable description in (i) proton–proton collisions and (ii) nucleus–nucleus collisions. In particular, characterize and compute the non-perturbative corrections that become important in the regime p_T^γ ≲ 1–5 GeV and at low dilepton invariant mass, and establish a controlled framework that extends the validity of the perturbative description (or systematically supplements it with non-perturbative contributions) into the soft regime relevant to electromagnetic probes of heavy-ion collisions.

Consider a high-energy heavy-ion collision modeled as a relativistic many-body system whose evolution passes through three successive regimes characterized by the ratio of the microscopic relaxation time τ_relax to the macroscopic evolution time τ_evolution: (i) a far-from-equilibrium free-streaming regime in which τ_relax ≫ τ_evolution and partonic constituents propagate quasi-freely; (ii) a hydrodynamization transition regime in which τ_relax ~ τ_evolution and the system rapidly approaches an effective fluid description; and (iii) a hydrodynamic regime in which τ_relax ≪ τ_evolution and viscous relativistic hydrodynamics applies. In each regime, electromagnetic radiation (real photons and dileptons, i.e. virtual photons decaying to lepton pairs) is produced from the strongly interacting medium with a rate determined by the electromagnetic current–current correlator evaluated in the appropriate underlying microscopic theory (e.g. QCD kinetic theory at weak coupling or holographic strongly-coupled gauge theory).

Existing detailed computations of pre-equilibrium photon and dilepton production assume a conformal, boost-invariant, transversely homogeneous 0+1-dimensional background, in which all fields depend only on proper time and the system has exact longitudinal boost invariance and no transverse spatial dependence.

Develop a framework that:
(a) defines and computes the differential photon and dilepton production rates dN/(d^4x d^3k) (or d^4k) consistently as functions of spacetime and momentum across the free-streaming, hydrodynamization, and hydrodynamic regimes, with matching conditions ensuring continuity of the rate and of the underlying current–current correlator across regime boundaries; and
(b) extends the computation beyond the conformal boost-invariant 0+1-dimensional approximation to backgrounds with transverse inhomogeneities (and, more generally, non-conformal, non-boost-invariant 3+1-dimensional evolution), producing event-by-event predictions for photon and dilepton spectra integrated over the full spacetime history of the collision.

Provide explicit calculational schemes (within QCD kinetic theory, holographic methods, or hybrid approaches) realizing (a) and (b), and quantify the resulting electromagnetic yields and their dependence on the initial-state transverse profile.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and fix positive integers $n$, $d$, and $r$. Consider the Quot scheme $\mathrm{Quot}_{n,d}^r := \mathrm{Quot}(\mathcal{O}^{\oplus r}_{\mathbb{A}^n}, d)$ parametrizing quotients $\mathcal{O}^{\oplus r}_{\mathbb{A}^n} \twoheadrightarrow Q$ where $Q$ is a coherent sheaf of length $d$ supported at the origin (equivalently, finite-length quotient modules of $k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]^{\oplus r}$ of dimension $d$ over $k$). The principal component $\mathrm{Quot}_{n,d}^{r,\mathrm{prin}}$ is defined as the closure of the locus of quotients $Q$ corresponding to $r$-tuples of ideals (or, equivalently, the closure of the locus of quotients whose annihilator defines a reduced subscheme of $d$ distinct points, suitably interpreted) — i.e. the smoothable component.

For a finite-length quotient $M$ of $k[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]^{\oplus r}$ with Hilbert function $h_M(i) = \dim_k M_i$, set $h_M^{\max}(i) := \min\bigl(r \binom{n+i-1}{i},\, d - \sum_{j<i} h_M(j)\bigr)$, the maximum possible value of $h_M(i)$ given the previous values. The quotient $M$ is called very compressed if $h_M(i) = h_M^{\max}(i)$ for every $i \geq 0$. Let $\mathrm{VC}^r_{n,d} \subseteq \mathrm{Quot}_{n,d}^r$ denote the locally closed locus of very compressed quotients.

Question: Determine whether, for all triples $(n,d,r)$ outside a finite explicit exceptional set, the following alternative holds:
$$\mathrm{VC}^r_{n,d} \subseteq \mathrm{Quot}_{n,d}^{r,\mathrm{prin}} \quad \text{or} \quad \overline{\mathrm{VC}^r_{n,d}} \text{ is an irreducible component of } \mathrm{Quot}_{n,d}^r.$$

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $S = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables, and let $T = k[y_1,\dots,y_n]$ act on $S$ by contraction (partial differentiation). For a form $F \in S$ of degree $j$, define the apolar (annihilator) ideal $\mathrm{Ann}(F) = \{\partial \in T : \partial \circ F = 0\} \subseteq T$, and consider the zero-dimensional Gorenstein subscheme $\Gamma = \mathrm{Spec}(T/\mathrm{Ann}(F)) \subseteq \mathbb{A}^n$ of some length $d$. The Hilbert scheme of points $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ then has a point $[\Gamma]$. An irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ is called elementary if its general point parameterizes a scheme supported at a single point.

Fix an even integer $j > 2$. For a general form $F$ of degree $j$ in $n$ variables, determine for which pairs $(j,n)$ the point $[\Gamma]$ lies on a unique elementary irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ which is moreover everywhere nonreduced. As a weaker version: exhibit at least one pair $(j,n)$ with even $j > 2$ for which this conclusion holds.

representations.normalized:
Consider relativistic heavy-ion collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair in the range relevant to the RHIC beam energy scan and to the HADES and FAIR fixed-target programs (roughly a few GeV up to a few tens of GeV), where the quark–gluon plasma (QGP) phase, if formed, occupies a small fraction of the total space-time evolution relative to a prolonged and complex pre-equilibrium stage and an extended hadronic phase, and where perturbative hard-process calculations are unreliable because of the modest center-of-mass energy. The system is modeled by a multistage description (initial state, pre-equilibrium, viscous relativistic hydrodynamics with an equation of state p(T,μ_B) and transport coefficients such as shear viscosity η/s(T,μ_B) and bulk viscosity ζ/s(T,μ_B) depending on temperature T and baryon chemical potential μ_B, followed by hadronic transport), in which thermal photons and dileptons are emitted at all stages with rates determined by the in-medium electromagnetic spectral function ρ_EM(ω,k;T,μ_B).

Formulate a quantitative framework that determines:
(a) which inclusive and differential photon and dilepton observables (e.g., transverse-momentum spectra, invariant-mass spectra dN/dM, elliptic and triangular flow coefficients v_n(p_T) and v_n(M), polarization observables) carry distinguishable sensitivity to the early, pre-equilibrium stage of the collision as opposed to the hydrodynamic and hadronic stages;
(b) how these observables constrain the (T, μ_B) dependence of the equation of state and of the transport coefficients η/s(T,μ_B) and ζ/s(T,μ_B) in the finite-μ_B regime accessed at lower collision energies; and
(c) how to handle the diminished reliability of hard-process (prompt photon, Drell–Yan) baselines at these energies within such a framework.

Specifically, identify or construct photon/dilepton observables (or combinations thereof) whose theoretical predictions, computed within a hydrodynamic-based multistage model with prescribed ρ_EM, are demonstrably more sensitive to the early-stage dynamics and to the finite-μ_B equation of state and transport coefficients than to uncertainties in the hadronic-phase emission and the missing hard-process contribution.
